SERVICE PROCEDURES

Repainting 

Before repainting, determine the overall condition of the existing 
paint. 

Horizontal surfaces usually show the greatest surface deterioration. 
Carefully inspect thehood (16612) and roof panel (50202) to determine the 
overall condition of the paint. 

Clean the areas to be inspected and look carefully for any signs of 
surface deterioration or any other form of film breakdown. Check for cracking 
or humidity blistering. In particular, note the gloss level. Low gloss 
indicates surface irregularities caused by such defects as checking or 
blistering. 

Look for evidence of brittleness, poor adhesion or excessive chipping. 
If in doubt about the condition of the paint, scrape the finish slightly with 
a penknife or apply a piece of 50.8 mm (2 inch) masking tape to the finish 
surface and pull the tape off at a 90 degree angle and examine further. 

If a complete repainting job is necessary, plan a painting sequence. 
This provides continuity and avoids dry joint overlaps which cause unnecessary 
work before spraying.

Some state and local governments have specific health and safety 
regulations which recommend the use of a special breathing apparatus when 
using finishing materials containing toxic products.

 Respray Sequence, Methodical 

Once the difficult access areas have been sprayed, begin painting the 
roof panel at the C-pillar, along the drip rail to the front body pillar 
(02500). Then paint from the rail inward toward the roof panel center.

Move to the opposite side of the body and pick up the wet paint edge by 
applying the paint from the center of the roof panel. Continue outward and 
along the drip rail to the front body pillar and finish the roof panel by 
spraying the C-pillar.

Extend the coat application down the C-pillar, then paint the entire 
body side including the front doors (20124) and fender quarter. 

Move across to the front cowl, hood and top of the opposite front 
fender (16005). 

Continue down the front fender and along the body side to include the 
front door, quarter panel and C-pillar. 

Paint the luggage compartment door (40110) and back panels.

 Drying Paint Repair Work 

Remove or cover radiator grille (8200). Also cover parking lamps 
(13200), rear lamps (13404) and outside rear view mirrors (17682) when drying 
the vehicle at approximately 60°C (140° F). 

Monitor the temperature of the passenger compartment. If the vehicle is 
equipped with a radio tape player and/or digital audio compact disc player, do 
not allow the temperature to exceed 60°C (140°
F). 

Latch front doors only to the first catch to avoid distortion of the 
weatherstrips.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Rattle Elimination 

Foreign objects such as nuts, bolts or small pieces of body deadener in 
the door wells, pillars and quarter trim panels (31012) often cause rattles. 
Check door wells carefully by striking the underside of the front doors 
(20124) with a rubber mallet. 

Inspect all bolts and screws periodically. If tightening the bolts and 
screws located on such assemblies as the front door, hood and luggage 
compartment door hinges does not stop the rattles, the trouble is probably 
caused by misalignment.

Weatherstripping and anti-squeak material that has slipped out of 
position may cause rattles and squeaks. Apply additional Weatherstrip Adhesive 
E8AZ-19552-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M2G14-A.

ADJUSTMENTS

Body Service � Collision Damage Repair 

 NOTE: Perform major body straightening operations with body panels at room 
temperature. 

To perform any major body service effectively, always use Ford 
replacement parts. They are identical in size, shape and strength to the 
original parts. Follow the service procedures as described.

 NOTE: Follow all instructions concerning the location of structural members 
in load-bearing areas. 

The structural members are positioned to suit the shape and 
installation of the mechanical components fitted, such as engine, 
transmission, suspension and other components. 

To avoid a possible reduction in strength and safety, restrict service 
to structural members on collision-damaged vehicles. To preserve the strength 
of the panel, dismantle the panels at the original joints. Use an assembly aid 
for service operations such as replacing longitudinal members and inner fender 
panels. Using an aid makes sure of satisfactory service and adherence to the 
specified dimensions. 

If service is properly performed, all service procedures using 
replacement panels and members will result in the same standards of strength 
while maintaining operational safety.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Underbody

 NOTE: In geographic areas where heavy concentrations of road salt or other 
corrosive materials are used for snow removal or road dust control, flush and 
inspect the complete underside of the vehicle at least twice a year.

Give particular attention to cleaning out underbody members and drain 
holes where dirt and other foreign materials may have collected.

================================================================================
PAGE 1641
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 01-01: Underbody

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Body Misalignment Check

 CAUTION: Never apply heat to the bumper energy absorbers. Heat could cause the 
material inside the absorbers to expand and flow out of the absorbers or crack 
the metal housing. Always remove the absorbers before performing body frame 
service near them. Never use a bumper energy absorber for pulling. 

 CAUTION: Never apply excessive heat to bumper surface. Heat could cause the 
bumper to distort. 

 CAUTION: When collecting exhaust fumes in service area, never attach a metal 
collector to the exhaust tail pipe as the heat could damage the bumper. 

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to correct any serious misalignment with one 
pulling/pushing operation. Damage to structure could occur. 

To align or square up a body, take two opposite diagonal measurements 
between the front, center or rear pillars. Take the measurements between 
reference points, such as crease lines or weld joints, which are diagonally 
opposite each other on the two pillars being measured. Since all measurements 
should be made from the bare metal, remove all interior trim from the points 
being checked. Refer to Section 01-05 . 

Align each section proportionately until the proper dimensions are 
obtained. Refer to the Underbody Dimensions illustration.

Due to the design and construction of the unibody vehicle, it is 
important to monitor the upper body structure while making any corrections to 
the underbody structure.

Rough out badly damaged areas before taking measurements for squaring 
up the unibody body. Remove the glass to prevent breakage. Refer to Section 01-11 . In severe cases, reinforcement brackets and other inner construction 
parts may have to be removed or cut to permit restoration of the outer shell 
and pillars without excessive strain on the parts.

In cases of severe or sharp bends, it may be necessary to use heat. 
Never heat the area to more than 650°C (1200°
F). Always use temperature-indicating crayons when applying heat to any part.

All body welding should be done with a Rotunda Synergic Wire Welder 
164-R3527 or equivalent with welding wire meeting AWS-E-70-S-6 specification.

ADJUSTMENTS

Unibody Repairs 

 CAUTION: Disconnect battery ground cable (14301) before using any electric 
welding equipment to prevent damage to electrical components. Refer to Section 14-01 . 

 CAUTION: If heat is needed to straighten a unibody member, keep the temperature 
below 650°C (1200°F). Excessive heat may 
weaken the metal in the unibody members and cause permanent damage. Always use 
temperature-indicating crayons when applying heat to any part. 

 NOTE: Heat should be kept to a minimum area so that the hardness of the metal 
will not be affected.

MIG welding equipment should be used for all unibody welding.

When a reinforcement is to be welded to a unibody side member, run the 
welds lengthwise along the side of the reinforcements.

If a damaged unibody member is to be replaced, use the same method of 
attachment as on the original member. New bolts, required for replacement 
parts, should be of the same specification as the original bolts.

================================================================================
PAGE 1644
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 01-01: Underbody

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment, Unitized Body 

 CAUTION: In cases of severe or sharp bends, it may be necessary to use heat. Any 
attempt to cold-straighten a severely bent bracket may cause ruptures of the 
welds and may also cause cracks in the bent part. Never heat the area to more 
than 650°C (1200°F). Always use 
temperature-indicating crayons when applying heat to any part. 

 CAUTION: Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301) before using any electric 
welding equipment to prevent damage to electrical components. Refer to Section 14-01 . 

 NOTE: Heat and the use of heavy-duty repair equipment must be carefully 
controlled because of the difference in the gauge of the metal used in the 
construction of a unitized body and the stress points in a unitized body. It 
is possible to pull damaged areas back into alignment with the use of modern 
collision repair equipment without heating the metal.

Unibody misalignment can affect front and rear wheel alignment, the 
operation of the suspension parts and drivetrain operation. Window glass 
cracks, door and window opening concerns and air or water leaks at the doors 
are often caused by improperly tightened bolts and unibody misalignment.

All the dimensions are detailed to the centerline of existing holes in 
the underbody assembly. Once the unibody is aligned, the other operations can 
be performed as described.

Inspect all unibody structural members for cracks, twists or bends. 
Check all welded connections for cracks. Inspect support brackets for 
looseness. Perform any necessary service or make replacements, as required.

================================================================================
PAGE 1645
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 01-01: Underbody

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Welding

 CAUTION: Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301) before using any electrical 
welding equipment to prevent damage to electrical components. Refer to Section 14-01 . 

Perform all welding using Rotunda Synergic Wire Welder 164-R3527 or 
equivalent with welding wire meeting AWS-E70S-6 specification.

When repairing a flange, drill or punch 5 mm (0.2 inch) holes in one 
side of the flange and MIG weld and add filler material.

Varying factors determine panel thickness, panel design, 
cross-sectionals and sizes, joining method, welding method and welding 
locations during manufacturing. In order to apply the most suitable repair 
method, it is most important to have a thorough understanding of the body 
design, concept and construction.

In a unibody, the structural elements supporting the transmission and 
suspension are secured to the unibody. Every structural member and outer panel 
is designed to offer the maximum protection in the event of a collision. It is 
very important that a repaired part meet the same standards as the original 
equipment. 

It is essential that repair welds, particularly on load-bearing parts 
or parts contributing to the strength of the assembly, are equivalent to the 
originals in number, size, type and strength.

 Steel Components, Low-Alloy 

 CAUTION: Disconnect the battery ground cable before using any electric welding 
equipment to prevent damage to electrical components. Refer to Section 14-01 . 

 NOTE: All welding should be done with a Rotunda Synergic Wire Welder 
164-R3527 or equivalent with welding wire meeting AWS-E-70S-6 specification. 

Do not use oxyacetylene when welding any high-tensile or high-strength, 
low-alloy steel components. Use only MIG welding. During MIG welding, use a 
temperature-indicating crayon to make sure the temperature does not exceed 650°
C (1200°F). Always use 
temperature-indicating crayons when applying heat to any part. 

Replace spot-welded components with the same number of MIG plug welds, 
using puddle welding techniques to weld the compartments.

Use MIG welding when welding high-strength, high-tensile or 
conventional mild steel. Use 0.8 mm or 0.9 mm diameter wire meeting 
AWS-E-70S-6 specification. MIG welding is also known as gas metal arc welding 
(GMAW).

When cutting salvage or repairable components, use a grinding disc, air 
chisel, reciprocating saw, Plasma Cutting System - 30 Amp 164-R3526 or 
equivalent.

Radiator Grille

Thunderbird vehicles do not use a conventional radiator grille.

Cougar's radiator grille (8200) is attached to hood (16612). It allows

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hood Latch 

 Removal 

From inside the vehicle, release the hood (16612). 

Disengage hood auxiliary catch hook (16892) at radiator support hood 
seal (16A238) and at hood latch (16700). 

Remove the two hood latch assembly retaining bolts. Remove hood latch 
control handle and cable retainer screw. Disengage cable and remove hood latch. 

 Installation 

Thread terminal end of cable into hood latch assembly return spring. 

Rotate cable through latch lever V-slot, position cable retainer to 
hood latch and install screw to retain. 

Position hood latch and install two retaining screws. Tighten to 10-14 Nm
 (89-123 lb-in). Adjust hood latch to check for primary and 
secondary engagement and tighten retaining bolts. 

Slide hood auxiliary catch hook into radiator support hood seal and 
hood latch.

Close hood and verify correct hood latch adjustment and hood to fender 
margins.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Radiator Grille Opening Panel Reinforcement

 Removal 

Remove PARK/TURN signal lamps. Refer to Section 17-01 . 

On Cougar, remove radiator grille (8200).

Disconnect headlamp wiring. 

Lift up on hood latch link and disengage from slot in radiator grille 
opening panel (8190).

Remove front bumper cover (17D957). Refer to Section 01-19 . 

Remove secondary hood latch bracket. 

Remove two retaining screws at hood latch support (16707). 

Remove two (one each side) retaining screws at side mounting brackets. 

Remove four (two each side) retaining screws at RH and LH ends of 
radiator grille opening panel reinforcement (8A284). 

Remove two (one each side) retaining screws at upper corner of radiator 
grille opening panel reinforcement to front fender (16005). 

Remove radiator grille opening panel reinforcement from vehicle and 
remove headlamps (13008). 

 Installation 

Install headlamps to panel. Refer to Section 17-01 . 

Position radiator grille opening panel reinforcement to vehicle and 
align locator to slot in hood latch support. 

Install two (one each side) retaining screws at upper corners of 
radiator grille opening panel reinforcement to front fender. Tighten to 8-20 Nm
 (71-177 lb-in).

Install two (one each side) retaining screws at hood latch support.

Check and adjust alignment of hood (16612) to headlamps if required. 

Install four retaining screws (two each side) at RH and LH ends of 
radiator grille opening panel reinforcement to fender brace. 

Install two (one each side) retaining screws to side radiator grille 
opening panel brackets (8B455). 

Install front bumper cover. Refer to Section 01-19 . 

Install secondary hood latch bracket. 

Install PARK/TURN signal lamps. Refer to Section 17-01 .

ADJUSTMENTS

Hood Alignment 

The hood (16612) can be adjusted fore-and-aft and side-to-side by 
loosening six (three each side) hood hinge-to-body retaining bolts. Close hood 
and adjust as required. Tighten the rear hood hinge-to-body retaining bolts to 
7-11 Nm (62-97 lb-ft). Open hood and tighten the remaining 
two retaining bolts to 9-14 Nm (80-123 lb-in). 

To raise or lower the hood, remove cowl vent screens (018A16). Loosen 
the hood hinge pivot bolt and raise or lower the hood as necessary. After 
adjustment is made, tighten pivot bolt to 9-14 Nm (80-123 
lb-in). Then replace cowl vent screens.

================================================================================
PAGE 1666
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 01-02: Body Panels, Front End

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Hood Bumpers 

Hood bumpers, located on the top LH and the top RH surface of the 
radiator support, can be adjusted up and down to provide a level surface 
alignment of the hood (16612) with the front fenders (16005). To make sure 
that the rear corners of the hood are pulled down snugly against the rear hood 
bumpers and/or seals, it may be necessary to adjust the hood latch (16700) 
accordingly. Adjust the bumpers on each side of the radiator support to 
eliminate any looseness of the hood when latched.

================================================================================
PAGE 1667
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 01-02: Body Panels, Front End

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Hood Latch 

Before adjusting the hood latch (16700), make sure that the hood latch 
is properly aligned. The hood latch can be moved side-to-side to align it with 
the opening in the hood inner panel and up and down to obtain a flush fit with 
the front fenders (16005).

Loosen the hood latch retaining bolts until they are just loose enough 
to move the hood latch.

Move the hood latch side-to-side to align it with the opening in the 
hood inner panel. 

Loosen the locknuts on the two hood bumpers and lower the bumpers. 

Move the hood latch up or down as required to obtain a flush fit 
between the top of the hood (16612) and front fenders when an upward pressure 
is applied to the front of the hood. Tighten the hood latch retaining screws 
to 10-14 Nm (89-123 lb-in). 

Raise the two hood bumpers to eliminate any looseness at the front of 
the hood when closed. Secure the hood bumper locknuts.

Open and close hood several times to check operation. 

If correct latch position is not obtainable, remove two locating pins 
from latch assembly by tapping them into the radiator support. (They will 
eventually fall from the vehicle.) Then follow Hood Alignment procedure. 

If hood closing efforts and inside hood latch control handle and cable 
(16916) efforts are too high, adjust the hood hinge (16796) assembly upwards 
and/or the hood bumpers downwards.

 Removal 

 NOTE: A second person is required for this procedure.

Support the front door (20124).

Section 01-03: Doors and Luggage Compartment Door

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Weatherstrips 

Door opening weatherstrips are mechanically retained. No adhesive is 
required for retention. 

 Door, Front 

 Removal 

Remove front door scuff plate (13208). Loosen required front door trim 
panels (23942). Refer to Section 01-05 . 

Pull front door opening weatherstrip (20708) off weld flange around 
door opening. 

Pull roof side rail weatherstrip (51222) off weld flange across top of 
door opening. Peel the adhesive-backed seal from the B-pillar and remove 
pushpin with pliers. 

To remove front door lower weatherstrip (20758), start from either end 
of the door-mounted front door lower weatherstrip. Using a flat-blade 
screwdriver, pry retaining pins from door inner panel and remove front door 
lower weatherstrip. 

 Installation 

Inspect the front door opening weatherstrip and roof side rail 
weatherstrip mounting flanges for distortion. Correct any distortions by using 
locking-type pliers or a pair of hammers. Clean remaining adhesive from 
B-pillar using Extra Strength Tar and Road Oil Remover B7A-19520-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M5B106-A. 

Starting at upper corner of B-pillar and continuing down A-pillar, 
install roof side rail weatherstrip on mounting flanges.

 NOTE: Cover unused attachment holes with butyl tape before installing roof 
side rail weatherstrip. 

Peel adhesive protecting tape off roof side rail weatherstrip. Apply 
roof side rail weatherstrip along B-pillar approximately 3.175 mm (1/8 inch) 
from window. 

To install front door lower weatherstrip, align nylon pushpins in seal 
with holes in front door (20124). Install pins from front to rear. Make sure 
pushpins are fully engaged. 

Install front door scuff plate and tighten front door trim panel. Refer 
to Section 01-05 . 

To install front door opening weatherstrip, push weatherstrip onto weld 
flange starting at the lower A-post continuing around the opening clockwise to 
the bottom of the B-pillar.

Position seal ends on rocker flange and butt ends together, working 
excess length along rocker.

(20124) in the desired direction.

Loosen the door hinge bolts just enough to permit movement of the front 
door with a padded pry bar. 

Move the front door the necessary distance. Tighten the hinge bolts to 
25-35 Nm (19-25 lb-ft). Check front door fit to be sure there

latch striker tapping plate alignment for proper front door closing. 

The front door and quarter window glass (29710) must be checked to 
verify proper alignment to the roof rail and vertical weatherstrips. Refer to 
 Section 01-11 .

 Striker, Door Latch 

 NOTE: Adjust the door latch striker after the door is properly adjusted. 
Refer to door alignment procedure in this section. Do not adjust door latch 
striker to correct door sag.

The latch striker is moved vertically and horizontally to align striker 
and latch. The striker will move 6.3 mm (0.25 inch) in any direction on 
B-pillar. The striker must be shimmed to move fore and aft to provide striker 
clearance.

To check striker clearance:

Clean latch and striker and apply a thin coat of dark grease such as 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or XG-1-K or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B to striker.

Open and close door to produce measurable pattern in grease.

Using Torx® Drive Bit Set D79P-2100-T or equivalent, 
reposition striker as required to allow easy and secure door closure. Install 
no more than one shim between striker and B-pillar to adjust fore and aft 
clearance.

Tighten striker assembly to 35-45 Nm (26-33 lb-ft).

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Torsion Bar, Luggage Compartment 

Open the luggage compartment door (40110) and note the pop-up distance. 
The luggage compartment door should have adequate finger clearance. 

If luggage compartment door does not have adequate finger clearance, 
luggage compartment door hinge torsion bar tension should be increased. 

If the luggage compartment door pops open with more force than is 
desired, luggage compartment door hinge torsion bar tension can be decreased. 

 WARNING: SAFETY GLASSES MUST BE WORN WHEN PERFORMING THIS OPERATION. 

 WARNING: USE CARE WHEN ADJUSTING THE TORSION BAR AS IT IS UNDER TENSION AND 
COULD SPRING OUT OF CONTROL IF NOT HANDLED PROPERLY. 

Support the luggage compartment door in the full-open position before 
adjusting the luggage compartment door/tailgate hinge torsion bar (44891).

To adjust luggage compartment door/tailgate hinge torsion bar, use a 
tool designed to safely perform the adjustment (such as the one described in 
Torsion Bar Loading). Move luggage compartment door hinge torsion bar end to 
another position (notch) to increase or decrease tension. 

Adjust one luggage compartment door/tailgate hinge torsion bar and 
check the adjustment before adjusting the other torsion bar. 

After torsion bar adjustment, the difference in position of the torsion 
bar ends, between the RH and LH side, must not be more than one slot.

LUBRICATION

Lubricant

 Weatherstrip � Door and Roof Side Rail 

Use Silicone Lubricant C0AZ-19553-AA (jelly) or D7AZ-19553-AA (spray) 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A on the door and window 
weatherstrips. It is recommended that silicone lubricant be applied to the 
weatherstrips whenever necessary. Silicone lubricant helps avoid weatherstrip 
squeaks and retards excess weatherstrip wear from chafing between the door 
glass upper frame and the weatherstrip. It also helps to retain door window 
alignment by reducing friction between the glass frame and the rubber 
weatherstrip. 

 Hinge, Door 

Use Multi-Purpose Grease Spray F5AZ-19G209-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESR-M1C159-A to lubricate door hinges. 

[FIGURE: N6585C.gif]

 Hinge, Luggage Compartment Door 

Use Multi-Purpose Grease Spray F5AZ-19G209-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESR-M1C159-A to lubricate luggage compartment door hinges 
(42700). Apply an even coat to all movable hinge surfaces when a binding 
condition occurs.

Section 01-05: Trim, Interior

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Trim, Interior

This section covers removal and installation of the interior mouldings 
and trim components. 

In most instances, one component overlaps another component. 

When this condition is found, it will be necessary to loosen or remove 
the overlapping components before removal of the desired components. 

The interior trim has the following features:

The RH front door trim panel (23942) and LH front door trim panel 
(23943) are covered with either vinyl or cloth. 

Floor carpet (13000) covers the floor and cargo areas. 

The package tray trim panel (46668) is made of fiberboard. 

The remaining panels are plastic. 

Many of the interior trim panels use concealed fasteners. The 
installation procedures show the location of each fastener.

Section 01-09: Mirrors, Rear View

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Mirror, Outside Rear View

 Power 

The outside power rear view mirrors include the following features:

The outside rear view mirror motor (17D696) can be serviced separately.

The outside rear view mirror glass (17K707) can also be serviced 
separately.

The outside rear view mirror control (17B676) is located on the LH 
front door trim panel finish panel (23712). 

One outside rear view mirror control operates both RH and LH outside 
rear view mirrors (17682). 

Moving the outside rear view mirror control to the LH or RH position 
controls the appropriate outside rear view mirror requiring adjustment.

The outside rear view mirror control is designed to tilt the mirror up, 
down, left or right by pressing the push button on the arrow indicating the 
desired direction.

[FIGURE: AN0674A.gif]

1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 01-09: Mirrors, Rear View

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Mirror, Inside Rear View

 Manual 

The inside rear view mirror (17700) consists of a mirror and housing 
assembly that mounts to an inside rear view mirror bracket (17698) at the 
upper center of the windshield glass (03100). The inside rear view mirror 
bracket is affixed to the windshield glass with a two-part epoxy. 

The inside rear view mirror can be adjusted in any direction. The 
inside rear view mirror can also be changed from day to night position to 
reduce the glare from the headlamps of vehicles in the rear. 

Move the tab toward you for the night position and away from you for 
the day position. The special swivel bracket allows the inside rear view 
mirror to move up or down and from side to side.

 Mirror, Inside Rear View 

[FIGURE: N12639A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

3

Inside Rear View Mirror Bracket

4

�

Mirror Assembly Slot (Part of 17698)

5

17700

Inside Rear View Mirror

 Automatic Dimming 

The automatic dimming inside rear view mirror has the following 
characteristics:

It will change from normal to non-glare when glare reaches the inside 
rear view mirror.

The inside rear view mirror functions mainly at night with limited 
function at dusk or dawn.

From non-glare, the inside rear view mirror will return to normal after 
a short delay. The delay starts when glare goes away, and prevents excessive 
changing of the inside rear view mirror as traffic moves behind and around the 
vehicle or on rolling hills and curves.

The sensitivity of the inside rear view mirror is adjusted automatically.

The automatic dimming inside rear view mirror measures the brightness 
of the light from the rear of the vehicle. It automatically makes a correction 
in the glare.

The inside rear view mirror may be turned off by pushing the switch to 
the OFF position.

There are two light sensors (photocells) in this inside rear view mirror.

The sensor that detects rear glare is located inside a window in the 
upper RH corner of the inside rear view mirror.

The second light sensor, which determines outside light level, is 
located on the backside of the inside rear view mirror case.

One important safety feature is that the mirror automatically locks in 
the normal state whenever the transmission is placed in REVERSE. This feature 
ensures a bright, clear view in the inside rear view mirror when backing up.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Mirrors, Rear View

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's concern by operating the outside rear view mirror 
(17682) to duplicate the condition.

Inspect the components of the power rear view mirror system to 
determine if any of the following mechanical or electrical conditions are 
present:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged outside rear view mirrors or inside rear view mirror.

Damaged outside rear view mirror control.

Damaged transmission range sensor.

Open fuse junction panel fuse:

INT LPS Fuse 4 (10A).

TURN SIGNAL Fuse (10A)

Damage to wiring harness.

Loose or corroded connections.

Flex the harness and connectors at the outside rear view mirror control 
as well as the outside rear view mirrors and inside rear view mirror (if 
equipped with automatic dimming inside rear view mirror). Look for obvious 
signs of opens or shorts.

If the inspection reveals obvious concerns that can be readily 
identified, service as required. 

If the concerns remain after the inspection, determine the symptoms and 
go to the Symptom Chart.

 Symptom Chart � Mirrors, Rear View 

Refer to the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual for the 
connector numbers cited in the pinpoint tests.

Use Rotunda Digital Volt-Ohmmeter 014-00407 or equivalent to perform 
pinpoint tests.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mirror Bracket, Inside Rear View 

 Removal 

Remove inside rear view mirror (17700) as described. Mark location of 
inside rear view mirror bracket (17698) on outside of windshield glass (03100).

Apply low heat from Rotunda Master Heat Gun 107-R0301 or equivalent 
until inside rear view mirror windshield pad (17A720) softens. Peel inside 
rear view mirror bracket off the windshield glass. 

 Mirror Bracket, Inside Rear View 

[FIGURE: N12639A.gif]

 Installation 

Make sure windshield glass, inside rear view mirror bracket and 
adhesive kit (Rearview Mirror Adhesive D9AZ-19554-CA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESB-M2G176-A) are at least at room temperature: 18°
C (64.4°F). 

If windshield glass is being replaced, locate and mark inside rear view 
mirror mounting bracket location on the outside surface of the windshield 
glass. 

Thoroughly clean bonding surfaces of windshield glass and inside rear 
view mirror bracket to remove old adhesive. Use mild abrasive cleaner on 
windshield glass and fine sandpaper on inside rear view mirror bracket to 
lightly roughen surface. Wipe clean with alcohol-moistened cloth. 

Crush accelerator vial (part of Rearview Mirror Adhesive D9AZ-19554-CA 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M2G176-A) and apply accelerator 
to bonding surface of inside rear view mirror bracket and windshield glass. 
Let dry for three minutes. 

Apply two drops of Rearview Mirror Adhesive D9AZ-19554-CA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESB-M2G176-A to the mounting surface of the inside 
rear view mirror bracket. Using a clean toothpick or wooden match, quickly 
spread the adhesive evenly over the mounting surface of the inside rear view 
mirror bracket. 

Quickly position the inside rear view mirror bracket on windshield 
glass. The 9.5 mm (3/8 inch) circular recess in the inside rear view mirror 
bracket must be toward the inside of the passenger compartment. Press and hold 
the inside rear view mirror bracket firmly against the windshield glass for 
one minute. 

Allow the bond to set for five minutes. Remove any excess bonding 
material from the windshield glass with an alcohol-moistened cloth.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seat Tracks, Manual 

Manual seat tracks have the following features: 

The front seat cushion extension handle (603A86) is located at the 
front of the seat. 

Pulling the front seat cushion extension handle allows forward or 
rearward movement of the seat assembly. 

Manual front seat tracks (61705) are retained to the front floor pan 
(11135) in the following manner: 

Studs with nut and washer assemblies are used at both rear positions 
and at the front outboard position. 

A bolt and washer assembly is used at the front inboard position. 

The nuts and screws retaining the front seat tracks are removed from 
inside the vehicle.

================================================================================
PAGE 1720
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seats, Front

 Power, Six-Way 

The six-way power seat system provides horizontal, vertical and tilt 
adjustments. It consists of the following components: 

seat regulator control switch (14A701) 

seat regulator motor (14547) 

vertical gear drives and horizontal rack-and-pinion drives

The mechanical portion of the front seat track (61705) in the 
horizontal drive has the following features: 

It consists of a rack-and-pinion drive on each track. 

The pinion housing and seat regulator motor is mounted to the movable 
section of the track. 

When the seat regulator control switch is actuated, the center armature 
is energized and the horizontal drive units are activated. 

The seat is then moved forward or rearward by the pinion gears 
traveling in a rack on each lower track section. 

In the vertical drive, worm gear and sector gear mechanisms are used. 
The drive units are located in the front and rear of the transmission case and 
operate in the following manner: 

When the seat regulator control switch is actuated, the front and rear 
armatures are energized simultaneously and the vertical drive units are 
activated. 

The seat is then moved up or down by the sector gears. 

When the front tilt portion of seat regulator control switch is 
actuated, the front armature drives the front vertical worm gear and moves the 
seat to the desired position. 

When the rear tilt portion of seat regulator control switch is 
actuated, the rear armature drives the rear vertical worm gear and moves the 
seat to the desired position. 

The transmission and seat regulator motors are serviced only as an 
assembly. 

The seat regulator control switch assembly is serviced separately. 

 Circuit Protection 

The power seat circuit is protected by the 20-amp SEAT/LOCK circuit 
breaker in the fuse junction panel.

PAGE 1721
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Latch, Seat Back

The front seat back latch (62648) system has the following features:

The modular front seat back latch mechanism is located on the outboard 
rear corner of the front seat assembly. 

This mechanism also provides seat back pivot. 

The front seat back latch is used on all bucket seat applications. 

The seat back is folded forward for rear seat entry or exit by pushing 
the seat back forward. 

The front seat back latch remains unlocked with normal usage. It locks 
only during vehicle deceleration (emergency stopping or upon impact) or on 
steep downhill grades. 

A manual (override) front seat back latch handle knob (62762) is 
provided only to help unlock the front seat back latch. 

The following safety precautions must be observed:

Proper front seat back latch function in emergency situations requires 
that the seat back be in its full rearward normal position and against the 
rearward stops in the front seat back latch assembly. 

The area behind the seat must be kept clear at all times to allow full 
rearward travel of the seat back. 

Rear seat passengers should not lean on the front seat backs while the 
vehicle is in motion. The forward force on the seat back from the rear 
passenger in an emergency situation may prevent proper operation of the 
inertia front seat back latch mechanism. 

 NOTE: The front seat back latch handle knob is not reusable. If it is 
removed, it must be replaced with a new front seat back latch handle knob. 

 NOTE: If the front seat back latch is removed for any reason, it must be 
installed as described in Removal and Installation. 

 NOTE: If a front seat back latch assembly or component is non-functional or 
damaged, the entire front seat back latch assembly must be replaced. Under no 
circumstances are inertia front seat back latch components to be replaced or 
serviced as individual components.

Front seat back latch operates as follows:

To adjust reclining front seat to a tilt position, lift up and hold the 
lever located on the lower side of the seat. Lean against the seat back to 
tilt it backward. 

To return the seat back, lift handle and remove body pressure from the 
seat back. The springs will return the seat to an upright position. When the 
desired degree of tilt is reached, lock the seat in position by releasing the 
lever. 

The manual front seat back latch recliner system is also modular and 
does not require adjustments. Do not lubricate the front seat back latch 
system. Lubricating the mechanism will adversely affect free rotation of the 
locking arms.

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lumbar Support System

 NOTE: Front seat armature support is available on Cougar 30th anniversary 
vehicle.

The front seat back pad adjuster system consists of the following 
components: 

Seat regulator control switch (14A701). 

A lumbar front seat back pad adjuster (65500). 

Two front seat armatures (65578).

A front seat back pad adjusting pump (65530). 

Seat back control wiring (14B719).

Front seat adjusting motor drive tube (618B62)

Front seat back pad adjusting hose (65528).

The system operates as follows: 

During the inflate mode, the front seat back pad adjusting pump pumps 
air through a hose to the lumbar or bolster seat back control switch and 
housing check valve.

The air is then routed through a separate hose to the lumbar or bolster 
support front seat back pad adjusters located in the seat back. 

The bolster support front seat back pad adjusters actuate a 
spring-loaded front seat armature which articulates the bolster inward when 
inflated. 

Except for front seat back pad adjusters, all components are generally 
located at or under the front seat cushion frame and spring.

 CAUTION: The longer nipple on the seat control switch (located at the center of 
the switch body) should always be connected to the hose leading to the lumbar 
front seat back pad adjuster. The shorter nipple on the switch body connects 
to the front seat back pad adjusting pump outlet. If this order is reversed, 
the lumbar front seat back pad adjuster will not hold air pressure. 

The seat control switch performs three functions: 

Turns front seat back pad adjusting pump on. 

Acts as a one-way check valve for air passage to lumbar and bolster 
front seat back pad adjusters. Once inflated, the seat control switch is 
returned to its normal mode and the check valve closes. This maintains air 
pressure in the front seat back pad adjuster. 

When deflated, the check valve in the seat control switch opens to 
deflate the lumbar or bolster front seat back pad adjuster. The spring loaded 
front seat armature then returns to its retracted position. In this mode, the 
front seat back pad adjusting pump does not operate.

The front seat head rest guide rod sleeves (610A16) are retained in the

Front seat head rest guide rod sleeves contain a removable spring that 
permits the positioning of the front seat back head restraint.

 Removal

Remove retaining pins and front seat track to floor insulators (61748).

Remove front seat track retaining bolts.

Disconnect wiring harness.

Remove seat from vehicle.

Seat Track, Power � Six-Way 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Use care when handling a seat and track assembly. Dropping the assembly

buckle end bolts to front seat track. Tighten bolt to 30-43 Nm
 (23-31 lb-ft). Refer to Section 01-20A .

Connect the seat regulator control switch to the front seat track 
assembly at the connectors. 

Install seat assembly as described. Connect the seat regulator motor 
connector and the seat sensor switch connector. 

Check operation of the seat.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Latch, Seat Back � Front

 NOTE: If the front seat back latch (62648) assembly does not pass the 
following procedure, the entire front seat back latch assembly must be 
replaced. Service of the front seat back latch components is not acceptable 
and should not be attempted. Refer to Cleaning and Inspection .

Remove seat as described.

With seat and track assembly removed from vehicle and positioned on a 
flat surface,grasp only the seat cushion, and slowly tilt the seat assembly 
forward enough to cause the seat back to tilt forward by gravity.

The front seat back latch should engage at this point (11 degrees from 
original position), restricting the seat back from tilting to its full forward 
position.

If front seat back latch does not operate as described, replace front 
seat back latch assembly.

 Removal 

Remove seat and track assembly as described. 

Remove front seat back latch handle knob (62762) and bezel and discard. 

Disengage front seat cushion cover (62900) as required to gain access 
to front front seat back latch-to-front seat cushion frame and spring 
retaining bolts as described. Remove bolts. 

Disengage front seat back cover (64416) as required to gain access to 
bolts retaining front seat back latch assembly to front seat back frame 
(61018) as described. Remove bolts . 

[FIGURE: AR0793A.gif]

 Installation 

Position front seat back latch assembly to front seat back frame .

Install front seat back cover as described. 

Attach front seat back latch to front seat cushion frame and spring 
(63100) with front seat back latch-to-seat cushion frame and spring assembly 
bolts. Tighten bolts to 44-60 Nm (33-44 lb-ft). 

Install front seat cushion side shield (62186). 

Install new front seat back latch handle knob and bezel.

Check front seat back latch for proper operation before installing in 
vehicle.

Install seat and track assembly in vehicle as described. 

Check front seat track (61705), front seat back latch and safety belts 
for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Head Restraints

 Removal 

Unscrew front seat head rest guide rod retainers (610A18). 

Pull up on front seat back head restraint (611A08). Compress foam in 
area of front seat head rest guide rod sleeves (610A16). 

Remove front seat back head restraint positioning springs. Pull front 
seat back head restraint up and out. 

[FIGURE: R4199F.gif]

 Installation 

Compress foam in front seat head rest guide rod sleeve area. Install 
positioning springs on sleeves. 

Slide front seat head rest guide rod retainer onto front seat back head 
restraint posts.

Insert front seat back head restraint posts into front seat head rest 
guide rod sleeve and push down to engage positioning spring. 

Tighten front seat head rest guide rod retainer onto front seat head 
rest guide rod sleeve.

 NOTE: Head restraint must operate smoothly throughout its range of travel, 
must remain in any fixed position, and must not be freely removable from the 
seat back. If any of these conditions are not met, check for proper 
installation of positioning spring onto sleeve. 

Adjust head restraint assembly by applying hand pressure, either up or 
down, to center area of head restraint.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Latch, Manual

The front seat back latch system is modular so it does not require 
customer or dealer adjustments or maintenance. Do not lubricate the front seat 
back latch (62648) system. Lubricating the mechanism will adversely affect 
free rotation of the locking arms.

The only authorized service permitted on the inertia and manual front 
seat back latch mechanism are the following: 

tightening of all retaining bolts to specification. 

replacement (in entirety) of a damaged or non-functional front seat 
back latch assembly. 

removal of any foreign material, such as tie straps, pieces of foam and 
trim.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Window, Heated Back

A series of grid lines are baked onto the back window glass (42006). 
The grid lines consist of two layers:

Power for the back window glass grids and the indicator is supplied 
directly from the battery through Fuse 14FL (40A) in the power distribution 
box which protects the circuit.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Switch and Light, Heated Back Window 

The heated back window switch and light (18C621): 

is mounted on the instrument panel (04320). 

operates with the ignition key in RUN. 

has a rocker switch spring-loaded to center position to turn the system 
on or off. 

has a timer-controlled relay that turns off automatically after approx 
imately 10 minutes of operation. If more than 10 minutes are required, the 
heated back window switch and light can be reactivated for another 10 minutes 
by pushing the rocker switch momentarily to the ON position. This operation 
can be repeated as required. 

The heated back window switch and light operates as follows:

When the heated back window switch and light is pushed to the ON 
position, the normally open contacts in the control are electrically closed. 

This provides power from battery to the back window glass grids and the 
indicator, triggering the timing circuit. 

This contact will remain closed until: 

the timer turns it off 

the heated back window switch and light is pushed momentarily to the 
OFF position 

the ignition switch is turned to the OFF position. 

This circuit is protected by RUN Fuse (5A) in the fuse junction panel 
(14A067).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Window Regulator, Power

 Removal 

 WARNING: IF THE FRONT DOOR POWER WINDOW REGULATOR COUNTERBALANCE SPRING MUST BE 
REMOVED OR REPLACED FOR ANY REASON, MAKE SURE THAT THE FRONT DOOR POWER WINDOW 
REGULATOR ARMS ARE IN A FIXED POSITION PRIOR TO REMOVAL TO PREVENT POSSIBLE 
INJURY DURING C-SPRING UNWIND. 

Remove front door trim panel (23942) and front door trim shield 
(237A04). Refer to Section 01-05 . 

Lower front door window glass (21410) to access holes in door inner 
panel. Remove two nut and washer assemblies retaining front door window glass 
to front door window channel bracket (23288). 

Prop the front door window glass in the full-up position. 

Disconnect body main wiring (14A005). 

Remove two nut and washer assemblies retaining window regulator 
equalizer arm bracket (23230). 

Remove the three rivets and one nut and washer assembly retaining front 
door window regulator (23200) to door inner panel as follows: 

Remove the center pin from each rivet with a drift punch. 

Using a 6 mm drill, drill out the rest of the rivet using care not to 
enlarge the sheet metal retaining holes. 

Remove front door window regulator through door access hole. 

 Installation 

With front door window glass in full-up position, install front door 
window regulator through access hole in door inner panel. 

Position front door window regulator to door inner panel and install 
three rivets and one nut and washer assembly. 

Install window regulator equalizer arm bracket to front door window 
regulator and loosely assemble with two nut and washer assemblies. 

Install front door window channel bracket to front door window glass 
and secure with two nut and washer assemblies. Tighten nut and washer 
assemblies to 10-14 Nm (89-123 lb-in). 

Connect body main wiring. 

Lower front door window glass approximately 75 mm (3 inches) from 
full-up position. 

With front door (20124) open, place hands on each side of front door 
window glass and pull front door window glass fully into front door glass top 
run (21596). 

Apply a downward pressure on the window regulator equalizer arm bracket 
and tighten two nuts and washer assemblies. Tighten to 10-14 Nm
 (89-123 lb-in). 

Cycle front door window glass to verify proper operation. 

Install front door trim panel and front door trim shield. Refer to 
 Section 01-05 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Windshield Glass

 Removal 

Remove windshield wiper arms and blades. Refer to Section 01-16 .

 WARNING: SAFETY GLASSES AND GLOVES MUST BE WORN. 

Remove windshield outside moulding (03144) as described.

Remove visors and drop headliner near windshield opening down to avoid 
cutting headliner during windshield removal. Place a small block of suitable 
material between headliner and roof to act as a spacer. Remove windshield 
garnish moulding (03606) as required.

Remove LH and RH cowl vent screens. Refer to Section 01-02 .

Remove inside rear view mirror (17700). Refer to Section 01-09 .

 CAUTION: Use care to avoid damage to the instrument panel. 

 NOTE: A long-bladed knife is needed to cut two rows of urethane along bottom 
of windshield glass (03100).

Use Rotunda Knife With Offset Blade 107-R1511, Rotunda Interior Auto 
Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalent to cut adhesive. Refer to 
manufacturer's instructions when using tool.

 Rotunda Knife With Offset Blade 

[FIGURE: N6999C.gif]

 Rotunda Interior Auto Glass Cut-Out Knife 

[FIGURE: N9628C.gif]

Remove windshield and moulding assemblies from vehicle using suitable 
suction tool.

Trim remaining urethane on pinch weld to within 1 to 1.5 mm (0.04 to 
0.06 inch) thickness with utility knife or razor blade. When completed, 
surface should be smooth and free of cuts and contamination.

[FIGURE: N10128A.gif]

Check pinch weld sealing area for damaged sheet metal, rust or foreign 
objects which may have caused, or may cause, glass breakage. Service metal as 
required.

 Installation 

 NOTE: A minimum of 10 minutes is required for primer surface to dry.

If painted sheet metal has been exposed anywhere along the flange, use 
the supplied wool applicator and apply Urethane Metal Primer or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G234-C to windshield pinch weld.

Place windshield and moulding assembly on a low, stable work surface, 
inside up.

Clean windshield with ammonia-based glass cleaner.

 NOTE: Wipe off Urethane Glass Prep or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
WSB-M5B280-C2 immediately after application because it flash dries. Prep 
application must be applied twice.

Using a clean wool applicator, wipe inside glass edge with Urethane 
Glass Prep or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSB-M5B280-C2, 21 mm (0.8 
inch) wide along top and sides and 70 mm (2.75 inch) wide along the bottom. 
Wipe off glass prep and repeat prep application.

Install foam dam (with self-adhesive backing) on pinch weld about 9.0 
mm (0.35 inch) from edge of windshield glass. At bottom of windshield glass, 
install 50 mm (2 inches) from bottom edge of windshield glass. 

Properly align windshield glass to body.

Place windshield glass into opening. Center it top and bottom, 
side-to-side (adjust lower glass stops if necessary).

Using masking tape or crayon, make alignment marks at points on four 
sides of both glass and window opening.

Remove windshield glass and moulding assemblies from vehicle and place 
it back on work table.

Thoroughly shake and stir Urethane Glass Primer or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSB-M2G314-B to make sure of uniform pigment mixing.

 NOTE: Allow a minimum of five minutes for glass primer to dry.

Using a clean wool applicator, apply primer to inside glass edge 16 mm 
(0.6 inch) wide along top and sides and 70 mm (2.75 inches) wide along bottom.

 NOTE: Leave a door window slightly open until adhesive is cured.

 NOTE: Apply new urethane on top of existing material on pinch weld.

Apply an even bead of urethane WSB-M2G316-B around entire sheet metal 
pinch weld next to windshield moulding retaining leg. The bead should be 
triangular in shape, 16 mm (0.625 inch) high and 8 mm (0.33 inch) at base. 
Apply two rows of urethane along cowl top.

Install windshield assembly onto vehicle. This must be done before 
adhesive skins over.

Install retainers and moulding (29700).

Remove spacer and install headliner, visors, windshield wiper arms, 
blades, and windshield garnish moulding.

Install cowl vent screens. Refer to Section 01-02 .

 CAUTION: Use only urethane for service of air and water leaks in urethane set 
windshield. 

 CAUTION: When replacing urethane installed glass parts, the vehicle should not 
be driven until the urethane has cured. At temperatures above 13°
C (55°F) and relative humidities above 50%, 
adequate cure time is typically 12 to 24 hours (less at higher temperatures 
and lower humidities). See detailed instructions provided by the urethane 
manufacturer. Inadequate or improper curing may adversely affect the retention 
of the windshield.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Back Window Glass

 Removal 

Disconnect rear window defroster wires.

 WARNING: SAFETY GLASSES AND GLOVES MUST BE WORN. 

Remove interior garnish mouldings and drop headliner near back window 
to avoid cutting headliner during back window removal. Place a small block of 
suitable material between headliner and roof to act as a spacer.

 CAUTION: Use care to avoid damage to the rear package tray cover panel. 

Use Rotunda Knife with Offset Blade 107-R1511 and Rotunda Interior Auto 
Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalents to cut adhesive. Refer to 
manufacturer's instructions when using tool.

 Rotunda Knife with Offset Blade 

[FIGURE: N6999C.gif]

 Rotunda Interior Auto Glass Cut-Out Knife 

[FIGURE: N9628C.gif]

Remove back window glass (42006) and moulding assemblies from vehicle 
using suitable suction tool.

Trim remaining urethane on pinch weld to within 1 and 1.5 mm (0.04 and 
0.06 inch) thickness with utility knife or razor blade. When completed, 
surface should be smooth and free of cuts and contamination.

[FIGURE: N10128A.gif]

Check pinch weld sealing area for damaged sheet metal, rust or foreign 
objects which may have caused, or may cause, glass breakage. Service metal as 
required.

 Installation 

 NOTE: A minimum of 10 minutes is required for primer surface to dry.

If painted sheet metal has been exposed anywhere along the pinch weld, 
use the supplied wool applicator and apply Urethane Metal Primer or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G234-C to rear window pinch weld.

 NOTE: If a new back window glass is to be installed, attach new moulding to 
edge of glass starting at top center working out, then down pillars and around 
lower corners.

Place back window and moulding assembly on a low stable work surface, 
inside up.

Install foam dam (with self-adhesive backing) inside edge of pinch weld.

Clean back window with ammonia-based glass cleaner.

 NOTE: Wipe off Urethane Glass Prep or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
WSB-M5B280-C2 immediately after application because it flash dries. Prep 
application must be applied twice.

Using a clean wool applicator, wipe inside glass edge with Urethane 
Glass Prep or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSB-M5B280-C2, 12.7 mm 
(0.8 inch) wide along top and sides 30 mm (1.2 inches) wide along bottom. Wipe 
off glass prep and repeat application.

Properly align back window glass to body.

Place back window glass into opening. Center it top and bottom, 
side-to-side (adjust lower glass stops, if necessary).

Using masking tape or crayon, make alignment marks at points on four 
sides of both glass and window opening.

Remove back window glass and moulding assemblies from vehicle and place 
it back on work table.

Thoroughly shake and stir Urethane Glass Primer or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSB-M2G314-B to make sure of uniform pigment mixing.

 NOTE: Allow a minimum of five minutes for glass primer to dry.

Using a clean wool applicator, apply primer to inside glass edge 12.7 
mm (0.8 inch) wide along top and sides and 30 mm (1.2 inches) wide along bottom.

 NOTE: Leave a door window slightly open until adhesive is cured.

 NOTE: Apply new urethane on top of existing material in pinch weld.

Apply an even bead of Urethane or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
WSB-M2G316-B around entire sheet metal flange next to back window moulding 
retaining leg. The bead should be triangular in shape 16 mm (0.625 inch) high 
and 8 mm (0.33 inch) at base. Apply two rows of urethane along cowl top.

 CAUTION: When replacing urethane installed glass parts, the vehicle should not 
be driven until the urethane has cured. At temperatures above 13°
C (55°F) and relative humidities above 50%, 
adequate cure time is typically 12 to 24 hours (less at higher temperatures 
and lower humidities). See detailed instructions provided by the urethane 
manufacturer. Inadequate or improper curing may adversely affect the retention 
of the back window glass. 

Install back window glass onto vehicle, taking care to align marks on 
glass to marks on body. This must be done before adhesive skins over.

Reconnect rear window defroster wires.

Remove spacer and install headliner. Install retainers and back window 
upper garnish moulding (42430).

Apply tape from top and sides of Cougar back window glass to roof to 
hold back window glass in place until urethane cures.

 CAUTION: Use only urethane for service of air and water leaks in urethane-set 
back windows, or deterioration of urethane may result. 

Check installation for air and water leaks in urethane seal.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Window Regulator Electric Drive

 Removal 

Raise the front door window glass (21410) to the full-up position if 
possible. If the front door window glass cannot be raised and is in a 
partially down position, it must be supported so that it will not fall into 
the door when the window regulator electric drive (23394) is removed. 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove front door trim panel (23942) and front door trim shield 
(237A04). Refer to Section 01-05 . 

Disconnect window regulator safety relay switch wiring (14A200). 

Position the body main wiring (14A005) out of the way. Using a 19 mm 
(3/4 inch) hole saw with a 1/4 inch pilot, drill three holes at the existing 
drill dimples located on the door inner panel adjacent to the window regulator 
electric drive. 

 WARNING: IF THE FRONT DOOR POWER WINDOW REGULATOR COUNTERBALANCE SPRING MUST BE 
REMOVED OR REPLACED FOR ANY REASON, MAKE SURE THAT THE FRONT DOOR POWER WINDOW 
REGULATOR ARMS ARE IN A FIXED POSITION PRIOR TO REMOVAL TO PREVENT POSSIBLE 
INJURY DURING C-SPRING UNWIND. 

Remove the three retaining screws and disengage the window regulator 
electric drive from the front door window regulator (23200). 

 Window Regulator Electric Drive 

[FIGURE: AN0331A.gif]

 Installation 

Position the window regulator electric drive to the front door window 
regulator and install the three screws snug, not tight.

Connect the body main wiring at the connector and cycle the window 
regulator electric drive to verify gear engagement. After the gears are 
engaged, tighten the three window regulator electric drive retaining screws to 
6-10 Nm (54-88 lb-in). 

Install the front door trim panel and front door trim shield. Refer to 
 Section 01-05 . 

Connect battery ground cable. 

Check the drain holes at the bottom of the front doors (20124) to make 
sure that each is open to prevent water build-up over the window regulator 
electric drive.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Door Glass Top Run

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Removal of front door glass top run (21596) is recommended only if 
damage occurs to the front door glass top run. Due to fragile make-up of the 
component, unnecessary removal may cause damage and/or breaks in the aluminum 
or the light gauge steel carrier insert within the rubber seal of the front 
door glass top run. 

Remove the following components: 

inside rear view mirror mounting hole cover (17K709)

front door belt line outside weatherstrip (21452) and front door belt 
line inside weatherstrip (21456)

front door glass top run retainer screw 

front door window glass (21410)

outside rear view mirror (17682)

To remove front door glass top run, carefully pull front door glass top 
run off window opening pinch weld and remove through window opening. 

 Door Glass Run Retainer 

[FIGURE: AN0332B.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The front door glass top run requires very critical and special 
handling. The front door glass top run must be handled by the center section 
only, never by front or rear legs. The front door glass top runs must be 
handled in a manner that prevents damage to the A- and B-pillar corners. 

 NOTE: Apply lubricant meeting Ford specification ESB-M99C109-A or equivalent 
to front door glass top run.

 NOTE: This procedure requires two people, one inserting the front leg of the 
front door glass top run and another person holding the remainder of front 
door glass top run at center section to prevent bending. After the front 
(A-pillar section) and the rear (B-pillar section) of the front door glass top 
run is inserted into the front door (20124), the front door glass top run is 
installed as described in the following procedure: 

Locate moulded B-pillar corner of front door glass top run from pinch 
weld flange to upper corner of door frame. 

Apply hand pressure to front door glass top run from belt line area of 
B-pillar and push front door glass top run upward (vertically) into corner. 
Make sure front door glass top run is fully flush with sheet metal. 

While applying upward pressure along B-pillar, install front door glass 
top run onto door frame pinch weld along B-pillar starting from top and moving 
downward. Use hand pressure to make sure front door glass top run is flush 
with outer door panel sheet metal. 

Use hand pressure from center to upper door frame area. Push front door 
glass top run rearward along pinch weld flange into B-pillar upper corner. 
Make sure front door glass top run is flush with outer door panel sheet metal 
at corner. 

While applying hand pressure rearward, install front door glass top run 
onto door frame pinch weld along upper door frame starting from B-pillar and 
point to A-pillar. 

Use hand pressure from lower A-pillar leg of front door glass top run 
and push front door glass top run upward (vertically) into corner. Make sure 
front door glass top run is fully flush with outside sheet metal. 

While applying upward hand pressure along A-pillar, install front door 
glass top run onto door frame pinch weld. Use hand pressure to fully seat 
front door glass top run. Make sure front door glass top run leg is fully 
seated. 

Install front door glass top run to door inner panel with screw and 
washer assembly. Tighten to 10-14 Nm (89-123 lb-in). 

Install front door trim panel (23942) and front door trim shield 
(237A04). Refer to Section 01-05 .

 Door Glass Top Run 

[FIGURE: AN0333A.gif]

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Grid Wire, Back Window Glass � Method I

A single break or any breaks that total 25 mm (1 inch) in one grid 
cannot be serviced. The back window glass (42006) must be replaced. For breaks 
less than 25 mm (1 inch) long, use the following procedure:

 NOTE: If the first layer of the heated back window grid (brown) is damaged or 
missing, it will be necessary to apply brown Acrylic Lacquer Touch-Up Paint 
AL81-5477-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M2P100-B on the glass 
prior to applying the Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A. 

Inoperative grid wires on back window glass should be repaired by using 
Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M4J58-A. 

 Surface Preparation 

 CAUTION: Do not use scrapers, sharp instruments, or abrasive cleaners on the 
interior surface of the back window glass, as this may cause damage to the 
grid lines. 

The vehicle should be brought inside and warmed to 16°
C (60°F) or above. 

Clean the entire grid line service area with Ultra Clear Spray Glass 
Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P5-A to 
remove all dirt, wax, grease, oil or other foreign matter. It is important 
that the service area be clean and dry. 

 Mixing 

 NOTE: The bottle of Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A and touch-up paint (if needed) must be 
at room temperature. Shake bottle for at least one minute for thorough mixing. 
Shake frequently during use. 

 Application 

Mark location of break on the outside of the back window glass. 

Using cellulose tape, mask off the area directly above and below grid 
break. The break area should be at the center of the mask and tape gap must be 
no wider than the existing grid line. 

[FIGURE: K3787E.gif]

 NOTE: If the brown layer of the grid is not broken or missing, apply only the 
Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M4J58-A to the break. 

Apply the repair coating in several smooth, continuous strokes 
(allowing three to five minutes drying time between coats) across the break 
area using the brush applicator in the cap. Extend the service coating at 
least 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) on both sides of the break area. 

If both brown and silver layers of the grid are broken or missing, 
apply a coating of the Dark Walnut Metallic Acrylic Lacquer Touch-Up Paint 
AL815858-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M2P100-B across the 
break area first. Two coats may be necessary to obtain the proper color. Allow 
the touch-up paint to dry. Then apply three coats of grid repair compound 
allowing three to five minutes drying time between coats. The coating of the 
grid repair compound should extend at least 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) on both sides 
of the break area. 

 CAUTION: Be careful not to damage grid line with the razor blade. If this 
occurs, additional service may be necessary. 

Allow to dry for five minutes then remove the mask. 

After removing the mask, check the outside appearance of the grid 
service area. If the repair compound is visible above or below the grid, this 
excess should be removed. This can be done by placing a single-edge razor 
blade on the back window glass parallel to grid and gently scraping toward 
grid. 

 Curing 

The service coating will air-dry in approximately one minute and can be 
energized within three minutes. Optimum hardness and adhesion occurs after 
approximately 24 hours. At that time, the serviced area may be cleaned with a 
mild window cleaner.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Grid Wire, Back Window Glass � Method II

Use a rear window defroster service kit to service pigtail connections, 
and grid line breaks. 

The service kit is available from:

Marketing East Company

No.10 Liberty Street

North Andover, Massachusetts 01845

Telephone: (978) 689-9565

Any break in the grid longer than 25 mm (1 inch) cannot be serviced. The 
back window glass (42006) must be replaced. For breaks less than 25 mm (1 
inch) long, use the following procedure:

 Surface Preparation 

The vehicle should be brought inside and warmed to 16°
C (60°F) or above.

 CAUTION: Do not use scrapers, sharp instruments or abrasive cleaners on the 
interior surface of the back window glass as this may cause damage to grid 
lines. 

Clean entire grid line service area with Ultra-Clear Spray Glass 
Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P5-A to 
remove all dirt, wax, grease, oil or other foreign matter. It is important 
that service area be clean and dry.

 Application 

Mark location of break on outside of back window glass.

[FIGURE: N12581A.gif]

Place masking tape (provided in kit) over break in grid wire, aligning 
holes in masking tape with grid wire.

Prepare service kit two-part epoxy.

Check expiration date of package. If hardener has crystallized, place 
package in hot water until the hardener softens.

Remove plastic clamp from package separating resin and hardener.

Knead package until resin and hardener are thoroughly mixed.

Cut corner of package to open.

Apply two-part epoxy, with stick provided, to wire grid through cut-out 
in masking tape.

[FIGURE: N12582A.gif]

Carefully remove masking tape from grid wire service area.

 NOTE: Care should be taken while using heat gun around interior trim.

Using Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent, heat grid wire service 
area for one to two minutes.

[FIGURE: N12583A.gif]

 NOTE: Heated back window is now operational.

 Two-part epoxy will thoroughly cure in 24 hours. Start engine, turn 
heated back window switch and light (18C621) on, and leave on for five 
minutes. Inspect grid wire service area.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Lead Window Terminal Service � Method I

 NOTE: There are two methods for servicing terminal separation from glass 
and/or grid breaks. Method I involves soldering the terminal to the glass and 
Method II uses an epoxy adhesive. Also, grid line service procedures are 
different.

Allow the back window glass (42006) to warm up to room temperature for 
one half hour to an hour. 

Clean the bus bar in the area to be serviced, using fine steel wool 
(3/0 to 4/0 grade). 

Restore the area where the bus bar terminal was originally attached by 
applying three coats of Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A. Allow approximately 10 
minutes drying time between coats. 

Working as quickly as possible to avoid overheating the back window 
glass, tin the bus bar with solder in the area where the terminal will be 
reattached. 

Using Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent or heat lamp, preheat the 
back window glass in the solder area to 67°C-83°
C (120°F-150°F) just prior 
to soldering on the terminal. 

Position the terminal on the bus bar in the area that was tinned and 
hold it in place with an ice pick or screwdriver. 

[FIGURE: L2447F.gif]

 CAUTION: To avoid damaging the bus bar, remove the soldering gun or iron as soon 
as the solder flows. 

Apply soldering heat to the pad of the terminal until the solder flows. 

Start the vehicle. Turn the heated back window switch and light 
(18C621) ON and leave it on for five minutes. Inspect the terminal and apply 
Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M4J58-A to the required area.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Lead Window Terminal Service � Method II

Use a rear window defroster service kit to service pigtail connections, 
and grid line breaks. 

The service kit is available from:

Marketing East Company

No.10 Liberty Street

North Andover, Massachusetts 01845

Telephone: (978) 689-9565

Allow back window glass (42006) to warm up to room temperature for one 
half-hour to an hour.

Clean bus bar in area to be serviced using fine steel wool (3/0 to 4/0 
grade).

[FIGURE: N12577A.gif]

Apply masking tape to bus bar around bus bar terminal location.

Prepare service kit two-part epoxy.

Check expiration date of package. If hardener has crystallized, place 
package in hot water until the hardener softens.

Remove plastic clamp from package separating resin and hardener.

Knead package until resin and hardener are thoroughly mixed.

Cut corner of package to open.

Apply two-part epoxy, with stick provided, to bus bar terminal location 
of bus bar.

Using a screwdriver, position bus bar terminal to bus bar.

[FIGURE: N12578A.gif]

 NOTE: Care should be taken while using heat gun around interior trim.

Using Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent, heat bus bar terminal 
and two-part epoxy for one to two minutes while holding bus bar terminal in 
position.

[FIGURE: N12579A.gif]

Carefully remove masking tape.

Carefully install wire to terminal. Heated back window is now 
operational. Two-part epoxy will thoroughly cure in 24 hours.

[FIGURE: N12580A.gif]

Start engine, turn heated back window switch and light (18C621) on, and 
leave it on for five minutes. Inspect bus bar terminal service area.

LUBRICATION

Window Regulator

The front door power window regulator minus motor (23208) should be 
well lubricated to provide ease of operation. The regulator should be 
lubricated whenever the front door glass top run (21596) is removed or 
excessive effort is required to operate the windows. Lubricate entire surface 
prior to assembly with Multi-Purpose Grease (spray) D7AZ-19584-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M1C106-B and ESR-MC159-A. To 
lubricate the regulator, apply an even coating of Multi-Purpose Grease (tube) 
DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M1C93-A and 
ESR-MC159-A to the window regulator arm rollers (23240), shafts and entire 
length of the window regulator equalizer arm brackets (23230) as illustrated 
by the shaded areas. 

[FIGURE: N12584A.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

Door Window Glass 

 Height Stop Adjustment 

Remove front door trim panel (23942) and front door trim shield 
(237A04). Refer to Section 01-05 . 

Lower front door window glass (21410) approximately 75 mm (3 inches) 
from full-up position. 

Loosen nut and washer assemblies retaining the window regulator 
equalizer arm bracket (23230) to door inner panel. 

Loosen nut and washer assembly retaining door window glass inner 
stabilizer (22380). 

With front door (20124) open, place hands on each side of front door 
window glass and pull front door window glass fully into front door glass top 
run (21596) at B-pillar. 

Apply a downward pressure on the window regulator equalizer arm bracket 
and tighten nut and washer to 10-14 Nm (89-123 lb-in). 

Set door window glass inner stabilizer so that it is slightly touching 
front door window glass and tighten nut and washer assembly to 10-14 Nm
 (89-123 lb-in). 

Cycle front door window glass to verify proper operation.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Panel

The instrument panel (04320) features a separate instrument panel 
reinforcement (04545) and houses the controls for most of the vehicle's 
electrical systems. 

The RH side of the instrument panel contains:

the glove compartment (06010).

the passenger side air bag module (044A74).

The center of the instrument panel supports:

the radio chassis (18806).

the A/C control (19980).

the clock.

the ashtray assembly (including cigar lighter)

The LH side of the instrument panel frames the steering column tube 
(3514) and houses:

the instrument cluster (10849).

the instrument panel finish panel (044D70).

The instrument panel reinforcement is serviced as part of the 
instrument panel and is not available separately.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cigar Lighter and Ash Receptacle

An ash receptacle (30702) and cigar lighter knob and element (15052) 
are located in the instrument panel (04320).

The cigar lighter knob and element has a low-resistance heating coil 
which operates much like the coil used in a portable heater:

When the cigar lighter knob and element is pushed completely in, the 
circuit is closed and current flows through the heating coil to the ground. 

When sufficient heat is generated, the cigar lighter knob and element 
will overcome the spring pressure of the bimetal retaining fingers and be 
released.
