IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Pistons and Connecting Rods 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Cylinder Ridge Reamer

T64L-6011-EA

 Removal 

Drain engine cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Remove upper intake manifold (9424) and lower intake manifold as 
described. 

Remove cylinder heads (6049) as described. 

Remove oil pan (6675) as described. 

Before removing piston (6108), inspect top of each cylinder bore. If a 
ridge has formed at the top of the cylinder, it must be removed before piston 
removal. Remove ridge as follows: 

Turn crankshaft (6303) until piston to be removed is at bottom of 
cylinder bore. 

Place a clean shop cloth over piston head to collect cuttings. 

Remove ridge using Cylinder Ridge Reamer T64L-6011-EA. Never cut into 
ring travel area more than 0.8 mm (0.031 inch) when removing ridge. 

Turn crankshaft until piston to be removed is at the low point of its 
travel. 

If more than one piston is being removed, identify the piston and 
connecting rod caps by numbering 1 through 3 from front to rear on RH bank and 
4 through 6 from front to rear on LH bank. This will make sure each component 
is installed in its original position during assembly. 

Remove connecting rod cap retaining nuts and cap. 

Install ignition wire spark plug boots over connecting rod cap studs 
and push piston out through the top of the cylinder blocks (6010). Use care to 
prevent damage to bearing surfaces. 

Install connecting rod cap and hold in position with cap retaining nuts. 

If piston is to be disassembled, refer to Subassemblies .

Inspect cylinder bore. If new piston rings are to be installed on the
piston, a cross-hatch pattern should be obvious on the cylinder bore wall. 

If honing is required, remove glaze from cylinder bore wall using 
spring-loaded hone. Follow manufacturer's instructions when using this type of 
equipment. 

After honing, thoroughly clean cylinder bore using a detergent and 
water solution. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Lightly oil all retaining bolt and stud threads before installation 
except those specifying special sealant. 

Lubricate cylinder bore wall and piston with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A. 

Install ignition wire spark plug boots or suitable protection on 
connecting rod (6200). 

 CAUTION: As piston is tapped into bore with a hammer handle, guideconnecting rod 
onto crankshaft journal to avoid damage to bearing surfaces. 

 NOTE: Install pistons in the same cylinders from which they were removed or 
to which they were fitted. If a connecting rod is transposed from one cylinder 
blocks or cylinder to another, new connecting rod bearings (6211) should be 
fitted and connecting rod should be numbered to correspond with new cylinder 
number. 

Install piston with notch in piston dome facing the front of engine, 
using Piston Ring Compressor D81L-6002-C or equivalent. 

Check connecting rod bearing clearances. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

Lubricate bearing surfaces with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A. 

Make sure connecting rod is seated on crankshaft journal. Install 
connecting rod cap and tighten retaining bolts as follows: 

Tighten to 20-25 Nm (15-18 lb-ft).

Tighten to 40-45 Nm (30-33 lb-ft). 

Rotate an additional 90-120 degrees.

If necessary, check connecting rod side clearance as described in 
 Section 03-00 . 

Install oil pump screen cover and tube (6622) with a new oil pump inlet 
tube gasket (6626) and tighten retainers as follows:

 Tighten oil pump screen cover and tube cylinder block bolts to 20-30 Nm
 (15-22 lb-ft). 

Tighten oil pump screen cover and tube support bracket retaining nut to 
40-55 Nm (30-40 lb-ft).

Install oil pan as described. 

Check piston deck clearance and bore clearance as shown. 

 Piston and Connecting Rod 

[FIGURE: AA1007A.gif]

Install cylinder heads as described. 

Install lower intake manifold and upper intake manifold as described. 

Fill crankcase with the correct amount of clean engine oil meeting Ford 
specification WSS-M2C153-F.

Fill cooling system with the specified engine coolant. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Start engine and check for oil and coolant leaks.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Connecting Rod Bearings 

The connecting rod bearings (6211) are a selective fit to provide the 
necessary clearance. Refer to Section 03-00 to measure clearance and select 
the proper connecting rod bearings. 

 Removal 

Remove spark plugs (12405) as described in Section 03-07A . 

Remove oil pan (6675) as described. 

Turn crankshaft (6303) until connecting rod (6200) from which the 
connecting rod bearings are to be removed is at the lowest point of travel. 

Remove connecting rod cap and connecting rod bearing. 

 CAUTION: Tape or place old ignition wire spark plug boots over connecting rod 
bolts to avoid damage to crankshaft journal during service. 

Remove upper connecting rod bearing. Push piston (6108) up into 
cylinder block bore slightly to provide clearance for removal. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Contaminants allowed to remain on the connecting rod, cap or connecting 
rod bearings can distort connecting rod bearings or damage crankshaft journals. 

 NOTE: Lightly oil bolt and stud threads before installation.

Thoroughly clean connecting rod bearings, connecting rod cap and 
connecting rod. 

Clean crankshaft journal and lubricate with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A. 

Install upper connecting rod bearing in the connecting rod and pull 
connecting rod down until connecting rod seats on crankshaft. 

When installing connecting rod bearings, make sure tab on connecting 
rod bearings engages slot in connecting rod and that connecting rod bearing is 
fully seated in connecting rod. 

Install lower connecting rod bearing in connecting rod cap and 
lubricate bearing surface with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A. 

Install connecting rod cap and retaining bolts as follows: 

Tighten bolts to 20-25 Nm (15-18 lb-ft).

Tighten bolts to 40-45 Nm (30-33 lb-ft). 

Rotate an additional 90-120 degrees.

Install oil pan as described. 

Install spark plugs as described in Section 03-07A .

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Crankshaft Rear Oil Seal 

 NOTE: A one-piece crankshaft rear oil seal (6701) is used for replacement on 
all engines. If replacement is necessary, this type of crankshaft rear oil 
seal MUST BE used. The complete crankshaft rear oil seal can be replaced 
without removing the crankshaft (6303).

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Jet Plug Remover

T77L-9533-B

Rear Main Seal Replacer

T82L-6701-A

 Removal 

Remove transmission. Refer to Section 07-01 .

 CAUTION: Avoid scratching or damaging oil seal surface or possible engine oil 
leakage may occur. 

Using a sharp awl, punch one hole into the crankshaft rear oil seal 
metal surface between lip and cylinder blocks (6010). 

Screw in the threaded end of Jet Plug Remover T77L-9533-B. Use the jet 
plug remover to remove crankshaft rear oil seal. 

 Installation 

Position crankshaft rear oil seal on Rear Main Seal Replacer 
T82L-6701-A. Position tool and crankshaft rear oil seal to rear of cylinder 
blocks. 

Alternate bolt tightening to seat crankshaft rear oil seal properly. 
(Two bolts are supplied with Rear Main Seal Replacer T82L-6701-A. Engine 
flywheel bolts may be used if necessary.)

Install transmission. Refer to Section 07-01 .

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Camshaft Rear Bearing Cover 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Impact Slide Hammer

T50T-100-A

Impact Slide Hammer

T59L-100-B

 Removal 

Remove transmission. Refer to Section 07-01 . 

Remove flywheel (6375) as described. 

Remove engine rear plate (7007). 

Using a sharp chisel or punch and hammer, cut a hole in center of 
camshaft rear bearing cover (6266). 

Remove camshaft rear bearing cover using Impact Slide Hammer T59L-100-B 
or T50T-100-A. The camshaft rear bearing cover can also be pried from bore 
using a large punch. Use care to prevent damage to camshaft rear bearing cover 
bore. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Prior to installing a camshaft rear bearing cover, the camshaft rear 
bearing cover bore should be inspected for any damage that would interfere 
with proper sealing of the camshaft rear bearing cover. If the bore is 
damaged, it will be necessary to true the surface by boring for the next 
specified oversize camshaft rear bearing cover. Oversize camshaft rear bearing 
covers are identified by the OS stamped in the flat located on cup side of 
camshaft rear bearing cover. 

 NOTE: Apply a light coating of Perfect-Seal Sealing Compound B5A-19554-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A to seal 
camshaft rear bearing cover before installation. 

Install camshaft rear bearing cover using suitable driver. 

Install engine rear plate. 

Install flywheel as described. 

Install transmission. Refer to Section 07-01 .

Lower vehicle.

specification WSS-M2C153-F.

Start engine and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft Bearings 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Camshaft Bearing Set

T65L-6250-A

 Removal 

Remove engine from vehicle as described. 

Remove flywheel (6375) and engine rear plate (7007). 

Remove camshaft (6250) as described. Loosen lower intake manifold bolts. 

Remove crankshaft (6303) as described, and push pistons (6108) to top 
of cylinder bore. 

Remove camshaft rear bearing cover (6266) from rear of cylinder blocks 
(6010). 

Select proper size expanding collet and back-up nut and assemble on 
expanding mandrel from Camshaft Bearing Set T65L-6250-A. With expanding collet 
collapsed, install collet assembly in camshaft bearing (6261). Tighten back-up 
nut on expanding mandrel until collet fits camshaft bearing. 

Assemble puller screw and extension if necessary, and install on 
expanding mandrel. Wrap a cloth around threads of puller screw to protect 
front bearing or journal. Tighten pulling nut against thrust bearing and 
pulling plate to remove camshaft bearing. Hold a wrench on end of puller screw 
to prevent it from turning. 

Repeat this procedure for each camshaft bearing. To remove front 
camshaft bearing, install puller screw from rear of cylinder blocks. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Failure to use correct expanding collet can cause severe camshaft 
bearing damage. Make sure front camshaft bearing is installed at specified 
distance below front face of cylinder blocks. 

 NOTE: Camshaft bearings are available refinished to size for standard and 
0.38 mm (0.015 inch) undersize journal diameters. The camshaft bearings are 
not interchangeable from one bore to another. 

Position new camshaft bearings at bearing bores with oil holes aligned 
with holes in cylinder blocks. Press camshaft bearings in place using Camshaft 
Bearing Set T65L-6250-A. Center pulling plate and puller screw to avoid damage 
to camshaft bearing. 

Install camshaft rear bearing cover as described. 

Install crankshaft as described. 

Retighten lower intake manifold bolts as described. 

Install camshaft as described. 

Install engine rear plate and flywheel as described. 

Install engine in vehicle as described.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Crankshaft 

 Removal 

Remove engine from vehicle as described. 

Mount engine in a suitable work stand. Drain crankcase and cylinder 
block cooling jackets. 

Disconnect ignition wire from the spark plugs (12405). Refer to Section 03-07A .

Remove spark plugs. Refer to Section 03-07A .

Remove oil pan (6675) and oil pump screen cover and tube (6622). 

Remove engine front cover (6019) and water pump (8501) as an assembly. 

Remove camshaft position sensor drive gear. 

Remove crankshaft sprocket (6306), camshaft sprocket (6256) and timing 
chain. 

Remove flywheel (6375) and engine rear plate (7007) as described. 

Remove connecting rod caps. Turn crankshaft (6303) as necessary to 
position connecting rod (6200) in the low point of travel before removing 
connecting rod cap. 

Push piston (6108) up into cylinder block bore after removing 
connecting rod cap. Make sure crankshaft journals are not damaged. 

Each connecting rod cap should be identified so it can be installed in 
its original position during assembly. 

Remove crankshaft main bearing caps. 

 NOTE: Handle crankshaft with care to prevent possible damage to finished 
bearing surfaces. 

Carefully lift crankshaft out of cylinder blocks (6010) to prevent 
damage to bearing surfaces. 

Remove crankshaft rear oil seal (6701) and discard. 

 CAUTION: Because the crankshaft incorporates deep rolling of the main journal 
fillets, journal refinishing is limited to 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) undersize 
standard journal dimensions. Further crankshaft main journal refinishing may 
result in fatigue failure of the crankshaft. 

Refer to Section 03-00 for crankshaft cleaning, inspection and 
refinishing.

Tighten in two steps: Tighten to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft), 
tighten an additional 115-125 degrees.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Contaminants on a bearing surface will cause damage to the crankshaft 
journals. 

 NOTE: Lightly oil all bolts and stud threads before installation. 

Make sure all crankshaft bearing surfaces and crankshaft main bearings 
(6333) are clean. 

If crankshaft main bearing journals have been refinished to definite 
undersize, remove crankshaft main bearings from cylinder blocks and main 
bearing caps. 

Loosen the lower intake manifold retaining bolts and support brackets 
prior to installing crankshaft main bearings or measuring bearing clearances. 

Install new crankshaft main bearings. Make sure tabs on crankshaft main 
bearings engage slots in the main cap and cylinder blocks. 

Make sure crankshaft rear oil seal groove in cylinder blocks is clean. 

Carefully lower crankshaft into position in cylinder blocks. Be careful 
not to damage crankshaft thrust main bearing (6337). 

Make sure crankshaft rear oil seal groove in rear main bearing cap is 
clean. 

 NOTE: Prior to applying sealer, clean sealing surfaces with Metal Parts 
Cleaner F4AZ-19A536-RA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M5B392-A, 
to remove all residues that may interfere with the sealers ability to adhere.

 NOTE: When using silicone sealer, assembly must occur within 15 minutes after 
sealer application. After this time, the sealer may start to set-up and its 
sealing effectiveness may be reduced. 

Apply a 3 mm (0.125 inch) bead of Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESB-M4G92-A and ESE-M4G195-A to rear 
main bearing cap-to-cylinder block parting line. 

Lubricate bearing surfaces with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A. Install main bearing 
caps and retaining bolts. 

Tighten main bearing cap retaining bolts as follows: 

Wedge a prybar between cylinder block web and crankshaft cheek in front 
of the No. 3 crankshaft main bearing. 

Do not jam the prybar into position. Carefully tap on the prybar until 
it holds crankshaft toward front of engine. 

Tighten main bearing cap retaining bolts in two steps in sequence 
shown: tighten to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft), tighten an additional 
115-125 degrees.

Remove prybar. 

Check crankshaft end play as described in Section 03-00 . 

Install crankshaft rear oil seal as described. 

If crankshaft connecting rod journals have been refinished to a 
definite undersize, remove connecting rod bearings (6211) from connecting rods 
and connecting rod caps. 

Install new connecting rod bearings. Make sure tabs on connecting rod 
bearings securely engage the slots inconnecting rod and cap. 

Rotate cylinder blocks as necessary to bring each crankshaft throw to 
lowest point of travel. Pull piston downward until connecting rod bearing 
seats on crankshaft and install connecting rod caps. 

Check connecting rod clearance. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

As each clearance check is completed, lubricate bearing surfaces with 
Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A before installing connecting rod cap. 

Tighten retaining bolts in three steps:

Tighten to 20-25 Nm (15-18 lb-ft).

Tighten to 40-45 Nm (30-33 lb-ft).

Tighten an additional 90-120 degrees.

Install timing chain and engine front cover with water pump as 
described. 

Install camshaft position sensor (CMP sensor) (6B288) as described in 
 Section 03-14 . 

Install oil pan as described. 

Install engine rear plate and flywheel as described. 

Install spark plugs. Refer to Section 03-07A .

Connect ignition wires to spark plugs. Refer to Section 03-07A .

Install engine in the vehicle as described.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Engine 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Crankshaft Damper Remover

T58P-6316-D

Front Cover Seal Replacer

T70P-6B070-B

Spark Plug Wire Remover

T74P-6666-A

Damper/Front Cover Seal Replacer

T82L-6316-A

Vibration Damper Remover Adapter

T82L-6316-B

Cylinder Ridge Reamer

T64L-6011-EA

 Disassembly 

Before starting disassembly, remove accessories and any emission 
control equipment which is not directly attached to the engine. 

Remove flywheel (6375) and engine rear plate (7007). 

Remove intake manifolds (9424). 

 NOTE: When LH exhaust manifold (9430) is removed, note location of oil level 
indicator tube support bracket.

Remove LH and RH exhaust manifolds.

Disconnect front evaporative emission hose and remove the following 
positive crankcase ventilation system components: 

Front and rear crankcase ventilation tube (6758).

Positive crankcase ventilation valve (PCV valve) (6A666).

Disconnect water bypass tube (8548) and water bypass hose (8597) at 
lower intake manifold. Remove heater water outlet tube retaining bolts and 
heater water outlet tube (18663) from water pump (8501).

 NOTE: When removing an ignition wire from a spark plug (12405), use Spark 
Plug Wire Remover T74P-6666-A. Grasp and twist boot back and forth on spark 
plug insulator to free boot. Use tool to pull boot from spark plug. Do not 
pull on ignition wire directly or it may become separated from connector 
inside boot.

Disconnect ignition wires from spark plugs. Refer to Section 03-07A .

Remove the following components: 

throttle body (9E926) and throttle body gasket (TB gasket) (9E936) 

EGR valve (EGR valve) (9D475) 

upper intake manifold and intake manifold upper gasket (9H486) 

fuel injectors (9F593) and fuel injection supply manifold (9F792) 

 NOTE: If the crankshaft pulley and vibration damper have to be separated, 
mark the damper and pulley so that they may be reassembled in the same 
relative position. This is important as the damper and pulley are initially 
balanced as an assembly. 

 NOTE: If the crankshaft damper is being replaced, check if the original 
damper has balance pins installed. If so, new balance pins (E0SZ-6A328-A or 
equivalent) must be installed on the new damper in the same position as the 
original damper. The crankshaft pulley (new or original) must also be 
installed in the same relative position as originally installed. 

Remove crankshaft pulley and vibration damper. Use Crankshaft Damper 
Remover T58P-6316-D and Vibration Damper Remover Adapter T82L-6316-B to remove 
vibration damper. 

Remove hold-down clamp (12270) and camshaft position sensor (CMP 
sensor) (6B288) and housing. 

Remove valve covers (6582). 

 CAUTION: Do not damage machined sealing surfaces or possible leakage may occur. 

 NOTE: Before attempting to remove lower intake manifold, break seal between 
lowerintake manifold and cylinder blocks (6010). Wedge a large prybar between 
lower intake manifold and cylinder blocks. Pry downward on prybar using lug on 
water pump as a leverage point.

Remove lower intake manifold and intake manifold gasket (9439). Discard 
intake intake manifold gasket and end seals. 

Remove spark plugs. 

Remove rocker arms (6564) and push rods (6565). The location of each 
rocker arm, push rod and rocker arm seat (6A528) should be noted. When engine 
is assembled, each component should be installed in its original position. 

Remove cylinder heads (6049). Discard cylinder head retaining bolts. 
Remove and discard head gaskets (6051). 

Remove tappet guide plates and retainers (6K564) and valve tappets 
(6500). 

The location of each valve tappet should be identified. When engine is 
assembled, each valve tappet should be installed in its original position. If 
valve tappets are stuck in bores due to excessive varnish or gum deposits, it 
may be necessary to use a magnet or a claw-type tool to aid removal. When 
using a remover tool, rotate valve tappet back and forth to loosen it from any 
gum or varnish that may have formed on valve tappet. 

Remove oil bypass filter (6714).

Remove oil pan (6675). 

Remove oil pump screen cover and tube (6622) . Discard oil pump inlet 
tube gasket (6626). 

Remove water pump and engine front cover (6019) as an assembly. Remove 
and discard engine front cover gasket.

After removing engine front cover, remove camshaft sprocket retaining 
bolt and washer from end of camshaft (6250). 

 CAUTION: Do not damage finished areas on crankshaft (6303) and crankshaft 
sprocket (6306). 

 NOTE: If crankshaft sprocket is difficult to remove, it can be loosened by 
prying using two large prybars. 

Remove distributor drive gear (6255). Remove camshaft sprocket (6256), 
crankshaft sprocket and timing chain at the same time. 

[FIGURE: A6677E.gif]

Remove timing chain vibration damper (6284) from front of cylinder 
blocks. (This requires pulling back on ratcheting mechanism and then 
installing pin through hole in bracket to relieve tension.)

Remove camshaft thrust plate (6269).

 CAUTION: Do not damage camshaft bearing surfaces or engine damage may occur. 

Remove camshaft. 

If necessary, remove camshaft rear bearing cover (6266) from back of 
engine. 

 CAUTION: Never cut into ring travel area in excess of 0.794 mm (0.0325 inch) or 
damage to piston rings or cylinder blocks may occur. 

 NOTE: Before removing pistons (6108), inspect top of cylinder bores. If 
necessary, remove ridge and/or carbon deposits from each cylinder using 
Rotunda Cylinder Ridge Reamer 014-00292 or equivalent. Before ridge or 
deposits are removed, turn crankshaft until piston is at bottom of its stroke. 
Cover piston with a clean shop towel to collect cuttings. After cutting 
operation, turn crankshaft until piston is at top of its stroke and remove 
shop towel with cuttings. 

Remove connecting rod caps and pistons.

[FIGURE: A6673E.gif]

The location of each piston, connecting rod bearings (6211) and 
connecting rod cap should be noted. When engine is assembled, each component 
should be installed in its original position. 

Remove main bearing caps and crankshaft. The location of crankshaft 
main bearings (6333) should be identified. When engine is assembled, each 
crankshaft main bearing should be installed in its original position. 

For cleaning purposes, oil gallery and cooling jacket plugs can be 
removed.

Tighten in two steps: tighten to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft), 
tighten an additional 115-125 degrees.

 Assembly 

 NOTE: During engine assembly, silicone sealer will be applied to many 
components before installation. When the sealant is applied, the component 
should be installed within 15 minutes. After this time, the sealant begins to 
set-up and its sealing effectiveness can be reduced. 

 NOTE: Lightly oil all retaining bolt and stud threads before installation 
except those specifying special sealant. 

If removed, install oil gallery and cooling jacket plugs. Tighten plugs 
to specification. 

Before installation, coat plug threads with Pipe Sealant with Teflon®
 D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
WSK-M2G350-A2. 

To provide clearance for camshaft sprocket, oil gallery plugs on front 
of engine must be threaded below machined surface. 

Install crankshaft as follows: 

Install crankshaft main bearings in cylinder blocks. Note that third 
crankshaft main bearing from front is the crankshaft thrust main bearing 
(6337). 

Lubricate crankshaft main bearings with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A and 
carefully lower crankshaft into place. Use care to prevent damage to bearing 
surfaces. 

 NOTE: Prior to applying sealer, clean sealing surfaces with Metal Surface 
Cleaner F4AZ-19A536-RA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M5B392-A, 
to remove all residues that may interfere with the sealers ability to adhere.

Apply a 3 mm (0.125 inch) bead of Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-BA or AA 
or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESB-M4G92-A and ESE-M4G195-A to 
cylinder block rear main bearing cap parting line. 

Install crankshaft main bearings in main bearing caps and install caps. 
Note that caps are numbered with triangles. Cap No. 1 is located at the front 
of engine with triangle facing front of engine. 

Install main bearing cap retaining bolts. 

 CAUTION: Do not jam prybar into place. Tap into position only enough to hold 
crankshaft forward while cap bolts are tightened. 
Before tightening main bearing cap retaining bolts, wedge a large 
prybar between cylinder block web and crankshaft cheek located in front of No. 
3 crankshaft main bearing. 

Tighten main bearing cap retaining bolts in two steps: tighten to 50 Nm
 (37 lb-ft), tighten an additional 115-125 degrees.

Check crankshaft end play. Refer to Section 03-00 .

Install pistons as follows: 

Install connecting rod bearings in connecting rods (6200) and 
connecting rod caps. 

 NOTE: Lubricate piston and cylinder walls with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A before 
installation. 

 NOTE: Scratching of crankshaft journal can be prevented by covering 
connecting rod bolts with ignition wire spark plug boots or flexible hose. 

Install pistons using Piston Ring Compressor D81L-6002-C or equivalent. 
The notch in piston dome must face the front of engine.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Subassemblies 

 Cylinder Head 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Valve Spring Compressor

T81P-6513-A

 Disassembly 

Remove rocker arm seat retaining bolts, rocker arm seats (6A528) and 
rocker arms (6564). 

Remove exhaust manifolds (9430) if required, and spark plugs (12405). 

Clean carbon out of cylinder head combustion chambers before removing 
valves. 

Compress valve spring (6513) using Valve Spring Compressor T81P-6513-A. 
Remove valve spring retainer keys (6518) and release valve springs. 

Remove valve spring retainer (6514), valve stem seal (6571) and valve. 
Discard valve stem seals and identify all valve parts from the disassembled 
cylinder and note whether they are intake or exhaust. 

[FIGURE: A6719E.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

6507

Intake Valve

2

6505

Exhaust Valve

Lower Valve Spring Retainer

4

Valve Stem Seal

5

Valve Spring

6

Upper Valve Spring Retainer

7

6518

Valve Spring Retainer Key

8

6049

Cylinder Head

Clean, inspect and service cylinder head (6049) as required or prepare 
to transfer all usable parts to a new cylinder head. 

 Assembly 

All valves, valve stem seals and valve guides are to be lubricated with 
Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A. Apply Multi-Purpose Grease D0AZ-19584-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M1C93-A and ESR-M1C159-A to valve 
tips before installation. 

Install each valve in port from which it was removed or to which it was 
fitted. 

 NOTE: Due to different leakage rates between intake and exhaust valve stems, 
valve stem seals must not be interchanged. 

Install exhaust valve stem seal. Make sure valve stem seal is bottomed 
on guide. 

Install intake valve stem seal. Valve stem seal must be bottomed on 
guide. 

Install lower valve spring retainer. 

Install valve spring over valve and then install upper valve spring 
retainer. Compress valve spring and install valve spring retainer keys. 

 CAUTION: Do not install the spacers unless necessary. Use of spacers in excess 
of recommendations will result in over-stressing valve springs and overloading 
camshaft lobes which could lead to valve spring breakage and/or worn camshaft 
lobes. 

Measure assembled height of valve spring from top of lower valve spring 
retainer to underside of upper valve spring retainer with dividers. Check 
dividers against a scale. If assembled height is greater than specification, 
install necessary 0.79 mm (0.030 inch) thick spacer(s) between cylinder head 
spring pad and lower valve spring retainer to bring assembled height to 
recommended specification. 

 CAUTION: Do not tighten bolts. The bolts must be loose 
enough to allow rocker arm to be rotated to side. 

Position rocker arms and rocker arm seats on cylinder heads and install 
rocker arm seat retaining bolts.

Install exhaust manifold, if removed, and spark plugs. 

 Pistons, Piston Pins and Rings 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Piston Pin Remover/Replacer

T68P-6135-A

 Disassembly 

Remove connecting rod bearings (6211) from connecting rod (6200) and 
cap. 

Remove piston rings using a suitable piston ring expander. 

Mark piston (6108) to ensure assembly with same connecting rod and 
installation in same cylinders from which they were removed. 

Using an arbor press and Piston Pin Remover and Replacer T68P-6135-A, 
press piston pin (6135) from piston and connecting rod. 

[FIGURE: A8121C.gif]

 Assembly 

Check the fit of a new piston in the cylinder bore before assembling 
piston and piston pin to connecting rod. Refer to Section 03-00 .

The piston pin bore of a connecting rod and diameter of piston pin must 
be within specification. Refer to Specifications .

Apply light coat of clean engine oil to all parts. 

Start piston pin in piston and connecting rod (this may require a very 
light tap with a mallet). Using an Arbor Press and Piston Pin Remover and 
Replacer T68P-6135-A, press piston pin through piston until the piston pin is 
centered. 

[FIGURE: A8122C.gif]

Check end gaps of all piston rings. It must be within specification. 
Follow instructions contained on piston ring package and install piston rings. 
 Refer to Section 03-00 .

Check piston ring side clearance of compression rings with Feeler Gauge 
D81L-4201-A or equivalent by inserting it between piston ring and its lower 
land. This gauge should slide freely around entire piston ring circumference 
without binding. Any wear that occurs will form a step at inner portion of 
lower land. If lower lands have high steps, piston should be replaced. 

Make sure connecting rod bearings and bearing bore in connecting rod 
and cap are clean. Foreign material under connecting rod bearings will distort 
connecting rod bearings and cause a failure. Install connecting rod bearings in 
connecting rod and cap with tangs fitting in slots provided. 

 Oil Pump 

 Disassembly 

If necessary, remove oil bypass filter (6714). 

Remove oil pump and filter body (6603) to engine front cover retaining 
bolts and remove oil pump and filter body from engine front cover (6019). 

Lift pump gears out of pocket in oil pump and filter body. 

Remove oil pump body seal (6C639) and discard. 

Clean sealing surfaces of engine front cover and oil pump and filter 
body.

Using a straightedge and feeler gauge, measure across mounting surface 
of engine front cover for wear or warpage.

If surface is out of flat by more than 0.04 mm (0.0016 inch), replace 
the engine front cover as described.

 Assembly 

 CAUTION: Failure to properly coat the oil pump gears may result in failure of 
the pump to prime when engine is started. Do not use chassis lubricants. 

Lightly pack gear pocket with petroleum jelly or coat all gear surfaces 
with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A. 

Install gears in oil pump and filter body pocket. Make sure petroleum 
jelly fills all voids between gears and pockets. 

Position oil pump body seal. Install oil pump and filter body to engine 
front cover using alignment dowels on engine front cover. 

Tighten oil pump and filter body retaining bolts to 23-32 Nm
 (17-23 lb-ft) for M8 bolts and 8-11 Nm 
(71-97 lb-in) for M6 bolts. 

 Oil Pressure Relief Valve 

 Removal 

After drilling a hole through valve plug, remove plug with a slide 
hammer or by prying. 

Remove spring and pressure relief valve from bore. 

 Inspection 

Thoroughly clean pressure relief valve bore and pressure relief valve 
to remove any metal chips which may have entered bore as a result of drilling 
operation. 

Inspect pressure relief valve and valve bore for wear, scoring or 
galling. If inspection determines part(s) to be unserviceable, replace 
pressure relief valve and/or oil pump and filter body. 

Check clearance between pressure relief valve and bore. The valve 
should slip into bore without side play or binding. 

Check spring for signs of fatigue or collapse. 

 Installation 

Lubricate pressure relief valve with clean engine oil and install in 
bore. The end with smaller diameter goes in first. 

Position spring in bore. 

Install a new plug. The plug can be tapped into bore using a 
plastic-tipped hammer. Make sure plug is 0-0.25 mm (0-0.010 inch) below 
machined surface. 

 Oil Pump Intermediate Shaft 

 Removal 

Remove camshaft position sensor (CMP sensor) (12126) and camshaft 
position sensor housing as described in Section 03-14 .

Separate oil pump intermediate shaft (6A618) from camshaft position 
sensor housing shaft. 

 Installation 

Push lock ring end of oil pump intermediate shaft into camshaft 
position sensor housing shaft.

 NOTE: Install camshaft position sensor housing and oil pump intermediate 
shaft as an assembly, making sure that end of oil pump intermediate shaft is 
seated in oil pump drive gear. 

Install oil pump intermediate shaft and camshaft position sensor as 
described in Section 03-14 .

Install hold-down clamp (12270). Tighten to 20-30 Nm 
(15-22 lb-ft). 

 Cylinder Block Assembly 

 Disassembly 

Mount the engine in a workstand and remove all parts not furnished with 
the new cylinder blocks (6010) following the procedures in Removal and 
Installation. 

Remove the cylinder head to block dowels (6A008) and the cylinder 
block drain plugs. 

Remove the used cylinder blocks from the workstand. 

 Assembly 

Clean the gasket and seal surfaces of all serviceable parts and 
assemblies. 

Position the new cylinder blocks in a work stand and install the 
cylinder head to block dowels and cylinder block drain plugs. 

Transfer all serviceable parts removed from the used cylinder blocks. 

Check all assembly clearances and correct as necessary. 

 Cylinder Block, Bare 

Before replacing a cylinder blocks, determine if it is serviceable. If 
so, make the necessary service. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

 Disassembly 

Completely disassemble the used engine following the procedures in Removal and Installation. 

Remember to ridge ream the cylinder bores before removing pistons. 

Remove the cylinder head to block dowels and the cylinder block drain 
plugs. 

 Assembly 

Clean the gasket and seal surfaces of all serviceable parts and 
assemblies. 

Position the new cylinder blocks in a work stand and install the 
cylinder head to block dowels and the cylinder block drain plugs. 

Transfer all serviceable parts removed from the used cylinder blocks 
following the procedures in Removal and Installation. 

Check all assembly clearances and correct as necessary.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine

 WARNING: DO NOT OPERATE THE ENGINE WITH THE HOOD OPEN UNTIL THE FAN HAS BEEN 
FIRST EXAMINED FOR POSSIBLE CRACKS AND SEPARATION. 

The 4.6L (2V) (281 CID) is a V-8 engine with the following: 

single overhead camshafts (6250) (OHC). 

two valves per cylinder. 

sequential multiport fuel injection (SFI). 

composite intake manifold (9424). 

aluminum cylinder heads (6049). 

a cast-iron, 90-degree V cylinder blocks (6010). 

The electronic ignition system has two ignition coils (12029). This 
high energy ignition system is required for fast-burn combustion.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Induction System

Sequential multiport fuel injection (SFI) provides the fuel/air mixture 
needed.

Eight solenoid-operated fuel injectors, mounted in the intake manifold 
(9424), meter fuel into the air intake stream in accordance with engine demand.

The eight fuel injectors are:

positioned so that their tips direct fuel just ahead of the engine 
intake valves (6507).

connected in parallel with the fuel pressure regulator.

Fuel:

is supplied from the fuel tank (9002) by a high-pressure electric fuel 
pump (9350), mounted in the fuel tank.

is filtered and sent to the fuel injection supply manifold (9F792).

A fuel pressure regulator (9C968) on this fuel injection supply 
manifold controls the fuel delivery pressure at a constant 269 kPa (39 psi).

Excess fuel supplied by the fuel pump, but not needed by the engine, is 
returned to the fuel tank via a fuel return line.

Section 03-01B: Engine, 4.6L (2V)

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Crankshaft

The crankshaft (6303): 

is supported on the bottom of the cylinder blocks (6010) by five 
steel-backed, over-plated aluminum crankshaft main bearings (6333). 

connects with the camshafts (6250) by two sprockets and two timing 
chains.

The crankshaft thrust main bearing (6337) and crankshaft thrust washer 
(6334) limits crankshaft end play and absorbs thrust loads applied to the 
crankshaft ends.

Camshaft

The camshafts (6250) are individually chain-driven. There is an 
automatic hydraulic timing chain tensioner (6L266) on each timing chain.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Valve Train

The configuration of the valve train consists of a hydraulic valve 
tappet (6500) providing automatic lash adjustment. 

The camshaft lobe transfers its up-and-down motion to the rocker arms 
(6564). 

The camshafts (6250) are seated in journal bores on top of the cylinder 
head (6049).

The valves are arranged alternately: intake valve (6507)/exhaust valve 
(6505).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Lubrication System 

The lubrication system of the 4.6L (2V) engine is designed to provide 
optimum oil flow to critical components of the engine throughout its entire 
operating range. 

 Engine Lubrication System

Oil Drain to Sump (Part of 6010)

Oil is drawn into the oil pump (6600) through the oil pump screen cover 
and tube (6622) in the sump. 

Oil is pumped through the oil bypass filter (6714) on the left front 
side of the cylinder blocks (6010). 

Oil enters the main oil gallery where it is distributed to the 
crankshaft main journals, and to both cylinder heads (6049). 

From the crankshaft main journals, the oil is routed through 
cross-drilled passages in the crankshaft (6303) to the crankpins for 
connecting rod bearing lubrication. 

Controlled leakage through the crankshaft main bearings (6333) and 
connecting rod bearings (6211) is distributed radially outward to cool and 
lubricate the cylinder walls as well as the entire connecting rod (6200), 
piston (6108) and piston ring assemblies. 

The left cylinder head is fed from a drilling into the lateral supply 
passage feeding the main gallery at the front of the cylinder blocks. 

The right cylinder head is fed from a drilling into the rear of the 
main gallery. 

Main gallery pressure is reduced as it enters the cylinder head 
galleries through the use of fixed serviceable orifices located at the upper 
part of the feed passages. 

This reduced pressure in the cylinder head galleries feeds the following:

camshaft journals

valve tappets (6500)

hydraulic timing chain tensioners (6L266)

The cam lobes and rocker arms (6564) are lubricated by splash created 
through valve train operation. 

 Oil Pump 

The oil pump has the following characteristics: 

It is a positive displacement, internal gear pump using top seal rotors. 

It is mounted on the front face of the cylinder blocks. 

The inner rotor is piloted on the crankshaft post and is driven through 
flats on the crankshaft. 

System pressure is limited by an integral, internally vented relief 
valve which directs the bypass oil back to the inlet side of the oil pump. 

Oil pump displacement has been selected to provide adequate volume to 
ensure proper oil pressure both at hot idle and maximum speed. 

Relief valve calibration protects the system from excessive pressure 
during high viscosity conditions, yet is designed to provide adequate 
lubrication under high temperature and high speed conditions. 

 Oil Pan 

The oil pan (6675):

is a stamped steel component which is fastened to the bottom of the 
cylinder blocks.

acts as a reservoir holding lubrication that is pumped through the 
engine by the oil pump after start up.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Cooling System 

The engine coolant: 

flows through the radiator tubes, cooled by air passing over the 
cooling fins (assisted by the cooling fan as necessary). 

is then circulated from the radiator outlet tank (8054) through the 
radiator coolant recovery reservoir (8A080) which is pressurized to 
continuously separate the air from the cooling system.

flows from the radiator coolant recovery reservoir through the engine, 
heater core (18476) and water pump (8501), then returns to the radiator (8005) 
through the water hose connection (8592).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Drive Belt System

The 4.6L (2V) OHC engine is equipped with a serpentine drive belt 
(8620) to ensure maximum life. When replacing the drive belt, it should be of 
the same type as originally installed.

Engines are equipped with an automatic drive belt tensioner (6B209) 
that will not require any drive belt tension adjustment for the life of the 
drive belt.

A loose drive belt will result in slippage which may cause a noise 
complaint or improper accessory operation.

a loose drive belt may result in operational problems, such as the 
generator not delivering proper charge, etc.

Refer to Section 03-05 for service procedures.

Section 03-01B: Engine, 4.6L (2V)

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Valve Cover and Gasket

 RH Side 

 Removal 

Disconnect negative battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove air cleaner outlet tube (9B659). 

Disconnect 42-pin connector and 8-pin connector leading to the mass air 
flow sensor (MAF sensor) (12B579) and intake air temperature sensor (IAT 
sensor) (12A697).

Remove nut retaining A/C line to the RH front fender apron (16054).

Lift A/C line and feed the 42-pin connector under the line. Position 
42-pin connector out of the way.

Relieve fuel system pressure and disconnect fuel lines. Refer to 
 Section 10-01 .

 CAUTION: Do not pull on the ignition wires, as ignition wire may separate from 
the connector in the ignition wire boot. 

Disconnect ignition wires from spark plugs (12405). Refer to Section 03-07B .

Remove ignition wires and ignition wire separators (12297) from valve 
cover studs and position ignition wires out of the way. 

Remove positive crankcase ventilation valve (PCV valve) (6A666) from 
crankcase ventilation grommet (6A892) and position out of the way. 

Remove bolts and stud bolts retaining valve cover (6582) to cylinder 
head (6049). Remove valve cover. 

 Installation 

Position and glue new valve cover gasket (6584) into valve cover. Use 
Gasket and Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M11P17-A and ESE-M2G52-A. 

 NOTE: Remove all traces of dirt, oil or previously applied sealant from the 
sealing surfaces. Clean all sealing surfaces with Metal Surface Cleaner 
F4AZ-19A536-RA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-MSB392-A. Sealing 
surfaces must be clean and dry before applying sealant.

 NOTE: Install valve covers and retainers no more than four minutes after 
applying sealer.

Apply Silicone Gasket and Sealer F6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6 in both places where engine front cover 
(6019) meets cylinder head. 

Install valve cover gaskets, valve covers, bolts and stud bolts. 
Tighten stud bolts and bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) no 
more than four minutes after applying sealer. 

Install positive crankcase ventilation valve into crankcase ventilation 
grommet. 

Install ignition wire separators on studs and connect ignition wires to 
spark plugs. Refer to Section 03-07B .

Connect fuel lines. Refer to Section 10-01 .

Position and connect 42-pin connector and 8-pin connector.

Position A/C line and install retaining nut.

Connect battery ground cable. 

Start engine and check for leaks. 

 LH Side 

 Removal 

Remove air cleaner outlet tube. 

Disconnect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Disconnect speed control actuator cable (9A825) from throttle body 
(9E926). Position speed control actuator cable out of the way. 

Disconnect fuel charging wiring (9D930) from the electronic variable 
orifice sensor and oil pressure sensor (9278). Position fuel charging wiring 
out of way. 

 CAUTION: Do not pull on the ignition wire as ignition wire may separate from the 
connector in the ignition wire boot. 

Disconnect ignition wires from spark plugs. Refer to Section 03-07B .

Remove ignition wires and ignition wire separators from studs and 
position ignition wires out of the way. 

Remove bolts and stud bolts retaining valve cover to cylinder head. 
Remove valve cover. 

[FIGURE: AA0636A.gif]

 Installation 

Remove all traces of dirt, oil or previously applied sealants from the 
engine front cover and cylinder head sealing surfaces. Sealing surfaces must 
be clean and dry before applying sealant.

Position and glue new valve cover gasket onto valve cover. Use Gasket 
and Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B meeting Ford specifications ESR-M11P17-A and 
ESE-M2G52-A.

 NOTE: Prior to applying sealer, clean sealing surfaces with Metal Surface 
Cleaner F4AZ-19A536-RA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M5B392-A, 
to remove all residues that may interfere with the sealer's ability to adhere. 

 NOTE: Install valve cover and retainers no more than four minutes after 
applying sealer.

Apply Silicone Gasket and Sealer F6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6 in both places where engine front cover meets 
cylinder head. 

Install valve cover gaskets, valve covers, bolts and studs bolts. 
Tighten stud bolts and bolts to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in) no 
later than four minutes after applying sealer. 

Install ignition wire separators on studs and connect ignition wires to 
spark plugs. Refer to Section 03-07B .

Position and connect fuel charging wiring to the electronic variable 
orifice sensor and oil pressure sensor. 

Position and connect speed control actuator cable. 

Connect battery ground cable. 

Start engine and check for leaks.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Rocker Arm

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Valve Spring Spacer

T91P-6565-AH

Valve Spring Compressor

T91P-6565-A

 Removal 

Remove valve covers (6582) as described. 

Position piston (6108) of cylinder being serviced at the bottom of its 
stroke and camshaft lobe at base circle. 

 CAUTION: If Valve Spring Spacer T91P-6565-AH is not used, valve spring retainer 
(6514) will hit valve stem seal (6571) resulting in damage to the valve stem 
seal. 

Install Valve Spring Spacer T91P-6565-AH between valve spring coils to 
prevent valve stem seal damage. 

Install Valve Spring Compressor T91P-6565-A under camshaft (6250) and 
on top of valve spring retainer. 

[FIGURE: A15052C.gif]

Compress valve spring (6513) and remove rocker arm (6564). 

Remove Valve Spring Compressor T91P-6565-A and Valve Spring Spacer 
T91P-6565-AH.

Repeat Steps 2 through 6 until all necessary rocker arms are removed. 

 Installation 

Apply clean engine oil to valve stem and tip, rocker arm contact 
surfaces and valve tappet. 

Install Valve Spring Spacer T91P-6565-AH between valve spring coils. 

 NOTE: Piston must be at the bottom of its stroke and camshaft at base circle. 

Compress valve spring using Valve Spring Compressor T91P-6565-A and 
install rocker arm. 

Remove valve spring compressor and spacer. 

Repeat Steps 1 through 4 until all rocker arms are installed. 

Install valve cover, as described. 

Start engine and check for leaks.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Valve Tappet, Hydraulic

 Removal 

Remove rocker arms (6564) as described.

Remove valve tappets (6500) from cylinder heads (6049).

Clean and inspect valve tappets as described in Section 03-00 .

 Installation 

Apply clean engine oil to valve stem and tip, rocker arm roller contact 
surfaces and valve tappets and cylinder head valve tappet bore.

 NOTE: Valve tappets must have no more than 1.5 mm (0.059 inch) of plunger 
travel prior to installation.

Install valve tappets into cylinder heads.

Install rocker arms as described.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Valve Spring, Retainer and Valve Stem Seal 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Valve Spring Spacer

T91P-6565-AH

Valve Spring Compressor

T91P-6565-A

Valve Stem Seal Replacer

T91P-6571-A

 Removal 

Remove valve covers (6582) and rocker arms (6564) as described. 

Remove spark plug (12405) from applicable cylinder. Refer to Section 03-07B .

Position piston (6108) at top of stroke with both exhaust valve (6505) 
and intake valve (6507) closed. 

 NOTE: Failure of air pressure to hold the exhaust valve and intake valve 
closed while performing the following steps is an indication of valve and/or 
valve seat damage and requires removal of cylinder head (6049). 

Install an air line with an adapter in the spark plug hole and turn air 
supply on. 

Install Valve Spring Spacer T91P-6565-AH between valve spring coils. 

Compress valve spring (6513) using Valve Spring Compressor T91P-6565-A. 

[FIGURE: A15052C.gif]

 CAUTION: If air pressure has forced the piston to the bottom of the cylinder, 
any loss of air pressure will allow the valve(s) to fall into the cylinder. A 
rubber band, tape or string wrapped around the end of the valve stem will 
prevent this from happening and still allow enough travel to check the valve 
for binds and excessive guide-to-valve stem clearance. 

Remove valve spring retainer keys (6518), valve spring retainer (6514) 
and valve spring. 

Using locking pliers remove valve stem seal (6571). 

Repeat Steps 2 through 8 until all necessary valve stem seals are 
removed. 

[FIGURE: A13630B.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Piston must be at top dead center (TDC) of cylinder being serviced. 

Remove air pressure from spark plug adapter. Inspect the valve stem for 
damage. Rotate the valve and check the valve stem tip for eccentric movement 
during rotation. Move the valve up and down through normal travel in the valve 
guide and check the stem for binds. 

 CAUTION: If the valve has been damaged, it will be necessary to remove the 
cylinder head for service. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

If the condition of the valve is satisfactory, apply clean engine oil 
to the valve stem and hold the valve closed. Apply the air pressure within the 
cylinder. 

Install new valve stem seal using Valve Stem Seal Replacer T91P-6571-A. 

[FIGURE: A24777A.gif]

Position valve spring and valve spring retainer over valve stem. 

Install Valve Spring Spacer T91P-6565-AH between valve spring coils. 

Compress valve spring using Valve Spring Compressor T91P-6565-A and 
install valve spring retainer key. 

Remove valve spring compressor and spacer. 

Turn air supply OFF and remove adapter from spark plug hole. 

Install spark plug. 

Install rocker arms and valve covers as described. 

Start engine and check for leaks.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Crankshaft Pulley/Crankshaft Front Oil Seal

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Crankshaft Damper Remover

T58P-6316-D

Front Cover Seal Remover

T74P-6700-A

Crankshaft Seal Replacer/Cover Aligner

T88T-6701-A

Crankshaft Damper Replacer

T74P-6316-B

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Release drive belt tensioner (6B209) and remove drive belt (8620). 
Refer to Section 03-05 . 

Raise vehicle on hoist. 

Remove crankshaft pulley bolt (6A340) and crankshaft pulley retaining 
washer (6378) from crankshaft (6303). 

Install Crankshaft Damper Remover T58P-6316-D on crankshaft pulley 
(6312) and pull crankshaft pulley from crankshaft. 

[FIGURE: A13668B.gif]

Using Front Cover Seal Remover T74P-6700-A, remove crankshaft front 
seal (6700). 

 Installation 

Lubricate seal bore in engine front cover (6019) and seal lip with 
clean engine oil. 

Using Crankshaft Seal Replacer/Cover Aligner T88T-6701-A, install 
crankshaft front seal. 

[FIGURE: A14815E.gif]

Using Crankshaft Damper Replacer T74P-6316-B, install crankshaft pulley. 

 NOTE: Prior to applying sealer, clean sealing surfaces with Metal Surface 
Cleaner F4AZ-19A536-RA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M5B392-A, 
to remove all residues that may interfere with the sealer's ability to adhere. 

Apply Silicone Gasket and Sealant F6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6 to end of keyway of crankshaft pulley as 
shown. 

[FIGURE: A18921B.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure key on crankshaft aligns with keyway of crankshaft pulley. 

Install crankshaft pulley bolt and crankshaft pulley retaining washer. 
Tighten in four steps:

Tighten to 90 Nm (67 lb-ft).

Loosen bolt one full turn.

Tighten bolt to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft).

Tighten an additional 90 degrees.

[FIGURE: A13662B.gif]

Lower vehicle. 

Install drive belt. Refer to Section 03-05 . 

Connect battery ground cable. 

Start engine and check for leaks.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Engine Front Cover 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Crankshaft Damper Remover

T58P-6316-D

Crankshaft Damper Replacer

T74P-6316-B

Front Cover Seal Remover

T74P-6700-A

Fuel Pressure Gauge

T80L-9974-B

Crankshaft Seal Installer/Aligner

T88T-6701-A

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Drain the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Remove the upper radiator hose (8260).

Remove the cooling fan (8600) and the fan shroud (8146). Refer to 
 Section 03-03 .

Disconnect the idle air control (IAC) tube from the throttle body 
induction tube and the positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) vent tube from the 
LH valve cover (6582). Loosen the induction tube clamp at the throttle body 
(9E926). Remove the air cleaner (9601) and induction tube assembly.

Loosen the water pump pulley bolts. Remove the serpentine belt (8620).

Remove the water pump pulley (8509).

Remove the serpentine belt idler pulley from the engine front cover 
(6019).

Remove the LH ignition coil retainers and position the ignition coil 
(12029) aside.

Remove the power steering pump reservoir (3A697).

Remove the battery cable support bracket from the power steering pump 
reservoir bracket and position it aside. Disconnect the cylinder 
identification (CID) sensor from the front of the cylinder head (6049).

Remove the power steering pump reservoir bracket from the front of the 
cylinder head (6049).

Disconnect the RH ignition coil connectors, exhaust gas recirculation 
vacuum regulator (EVR) connectors, and vacuum harness. Remove the EVR with the 
bracket.

Remove the RH ignition coil bracket retainers and position the ignition 
coil (12029) out of the way.

Install three bolts to the crankshaft pulley. Use a pry bar between the 
bolts to hold the crankshaft (6303) and remove the crankshaft pulley retaining 
bolt.

[FIGURE: A13668B.gif]

Remove the crankshaft pulley, using Crankshaft Damper Remover 
T58P-6316-D.

Install tool T74P-6700-A to the front engine seal and remove the seal 
from the engine front cover (6019).

Raise the vehicle. Refer to Section 00-02 .

Disconnect the pressure line and bracket, the electrical connector at 
the pump, and the oil pressure sending unit (9278). Remove the power steering 
pump retainers and position the power steering pump aside (3A674). Cap the 
line and the power steering pump (3A674).

Remove the battery cable support brackets from the front of the engine 
and position them aside.

Remove the oil pressure sending unit (9278) and the power steering 
wiring harness locator.

Remove the four front oil pan retaining bolts.

Disconnect the crankshaft position sensor (CPS) connector.

Lower the vehicle. Refer to Section 00-02 .

Remove the oil level indicator tube mount from the valve cover stud and 
position aside.

Disconnect the engine harness and the spark plug wire holders from the 
LH valve cover (6582) and position them away from the valve cover (6582). 
Disconnect the spark plug wires (12280) from the spark plugs (12405) and 
position them aside. Remove the throttle cable from the throttle body (9E926) 
and position it aside.

Remove the LH valve cover (6582).

Disconnect the PCV valve assembly from the RH valve cover (6582) and 
position it away from the valve cover (6582).

Disconnect the engine harness and spark plug wire holders from the RH 
valve cover (6582) and position them away from the valve cover (6582). 
Disconnect the spark plug wires (12280) from the spark plugs (12405) and 
position them aside. Disconnect the vacuum line from the throttle body (9E926) 
and the RH shock tower.

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY TUBES WILL REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME 
AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. THIS PRESSURE MUST BE RELIEVED BEFORE SERVICING THE 
FUEL SYSTEM; OTHERWISE, PERSONAL INJURY OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE COULD OCCUR. 
A VALVE IS PROVIDED ON THE FUEL INJECTION SUPPLY MANIFOLD FOR THIS PURPOSE. 

Connect Fuel Pressure Gauge T80L-9974-B to the fuel pressure relief 
valve on the fuel injection supply manifold. Open the manual valve on the 
gauge to relieve fuel system pressure. Remove the safety clips and disconnect 
the fuel lines, using tool D87L-9280-A (3/8 inch tube) or D87L-9280-B (1/2 
inch tube). Remove the fuel pressure gauge.

Disconnect the 40-pin connector and position it aside.

Remove the RH valve cover (6582).

Remove the remaining engine front cover retaining bolts and remove the 
engine front cover (6019).

 CAUTION: Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes, power abrasive discs, or other 
abrasive means to clean the sealing surfaces. 

Remove and discard all gaskets and clean the gasket surfaces. Clean the 
gasket sealing surfaces with Metal Surface Cleaner F4AZ-19A536-RA (or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M5B392-A). Allow the cleaner to 
thoroughly dry.

Clean the valve covers (6582) and the engine front cover (6019).

 Installation 

[FIGURE: A25166A.gif]

Install a new gasket to the engine front cover (6019). Apply Silicone 
Gasket and Sealant F7AZ-19554-EA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
WSE-M4G323-A6 to the locations where the cylinder heads (6049) and the oil pan 
(6675) attach to the cylinder block (6010).

[FIGURE: AA0627A.gif]

Install the engine front cover (6019) to the engine and tighten the 
retaining bolts to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft).

Using Gasket and Trim Adhesive F3AZ-19B508-B (or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESR-M11P17-A and ESE-M2G52-A), glue new valve cover gaskets 
onto the valve covers (6582). Apply Silicone Gasket and Sealant F7AZ-19554-EA 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6 in the two locations 
where the engine front cover (6019) attaches to the cylinder heads (6049). 
Position the valve covers to the engine. Install and tighten the retaining 
bolts to 10 Nm (89 lb-in).

 NOTE: Lubricate the front engine cover (6582) and the inner lip of the front 
engine seal with engine oil, prior to installation.

Install a new front engine seal to the engine front cover (6019), using 
Seal Replacer/Cover Aligner T88T-6701-A1, Plate T88T-6701-A2, and Crankshaft 
Damper Replacer T74P-6316-B.

Install the oil level indicator tube mount to the valve cover stud. 
Tighten the nut to 10 Nm (89 lb-in).

Raise the vehicle.

Drain the engine oil.

Install and tighten the four oil pan-to-engine front cover bolts. 
Tighten the bolts in the following sequence:

Tighten to 20 Nm (15 lb-ft).

Tighten 60 degrees further.

Connect the CPS connector.

Install the battery cable support brackets to the lower engine front 
cover studded bolts. Tighten the nuts to 11 Nm (8 lb-ft).

Connect the power steering pump (3A674) and oil pressure sending unit 
harness locator.

Install the power steering pump (3A674). Tighten the retaining bolts to 
25 Nm (18 lb-ft). Connect the power steering pressure (PSP) 
switch connector to the power steering pump (3A674) and the oil pressure 
sending unit connector.

Remove the protective cap from the power steering pressure line fitting 
and install a new Teflon® seal using the Teflon Seal 
Replacer Set D90P-3517-A. Install the power steering line to the power 
steering pump (3A674) and tighten the line fitting to 20 Nm 
(15 lb-ft). Install the bracket to the line and the power steering pump (3A674)

Lower the vehicle.

[FIGURE: A18921B.gif]

Apply a small amount of Silicone Gasket and Sealant F6AZ-19562-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6 to the keyway area of the 
crankshaft pulley. Install the crankshaft pulley using Crankshaft Damper 
Installer T74P-6316-B and Centering Adapter T88T-6701-A2. Remove the 
crankshaft damper installer from the crankshaft (6303). Tighten the damper 
retaining bolt, using the following sequence:

Tighten to 90 Nm (66 lb-ft).

Loosen one full turn.

Tighten to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft).

Tighten 90 degrees further.

Install the water pump pulley (8509). Tighten the bolts to 25 Nm
 (18 lb-ft).

Install the serpentine belt idler pulley to the engine front cover 
(6019). Tighten the bolt to 25 Nm (18 lb-ft).

Install the serpentine belt (8620).

Connect the engine harness and spark plug wire holders to the LH valve 
cover studs. Connect the spark plug wires (12280) to the spark plugs (12405). 
Install the throttle cable to the throttle body (9E926).

Install the power steering pump reservoir mounting bracket to the LH 
cylinder head (6049). Tighten the retaining bolts to 25 Nm 
(18 lb-ft). Connect the CID sensor to the cylinder head (6049).

Install the battery cable support to the power steering bracket. 
Tighten the bolt to 25 Nm (8 lb-ft). Install the power 
steering pump reservoir (3A697) and hoses to the mounting bracket. Tighten the 
bolts to 8 Nm (71 lb-in).

Install the LH ignition coil (12029). Tighten the bolts to 7 Nm
 (62 lb-in).

Connect the engine harness and spark plug wire holders to the RH valve 
cover studs. Connect the spark plug wires (12280) to the spark plugs (12405).

Install the vacuum line to the throttle body (9E926) and RH shock tower.

Lubricate the O-rings with clean engine oil.

Connect the fuel lines and install the safety clips.

Connect the 40-pin connector.

Connect the PCV valve assembly to the RH valve cover.

Install the RH ignition coil (12029) and bracket assembly. Connect the 
connectors. Tighten the bolts to 25 Nm (18 lb-ft).

Install the EVR assembly. Tighten the nut to 15 Nm (11 
lb-ft).

Connect the ignition coil (12029) and the EVR connectors. Route and 
install the vacuum harness.

Install the cooling fan motor and shroud assembly. Refer to Section 03-03 . Connect the cooling fan motor electrical connector. Tighten the bolts 
to 9 Nm (80 lb-in).

Install the upper radiator hose (8260) to the radiator (8005).

Install the induction tube to the throttle body air box and securely 
tighten the clamps. Connect the PCV vent tube and the IAC clean air tube. 
Install the PCV vent tube to the LH valve cover.

Connect the battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Fill the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Fill the engine with oil.

Fill the power steering system.

Start the engine and check for leaks.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Camshaft Timing Chains and Tensioners 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Cam Positioning Tool

T91P-6256-A

Cam Positioning Tool Adapters

T92P-6256-A

Crankshaft Holding Tool

T93P-6303-A

 Removal 

 CAUTION: At no time, when the timing chain(s) are removed and the cylinder heads 
(6049) are installed, may the crankshaft (6303) and/or camshafts (6250) be 
rotated. Failure to follow these directions will result in valve and/or piston 
damage. 

 NOTE: Because this is not a free-wheeling engine, if it has "jumped time," 
there will be damage to the valves and/or pistons (6108) and will require the 
removal of the cylinder heads. The camshaft sprockets (6256) should only be 
disassembled from the camshafts when one of the components is to be replaced. 

Remove valve covers (6582), oil pan (6675) and engine front cover 
(6019) as described. 

Remove crankshaft position sensor pulse wheel. 

Rotate engine to No. 1 top dead center (TDC). 

[FIGURE: A14820B.gif]

 NOTE: This will prevent accidental rotation of the camshafts. 

 NOTE: Cam Positioning Tool Adapters T92P-6256-A and Cam Positioning Tool 
T91P-6256-A must be installed on camshaft to prevent camshaft 
from rotating.

Install Cam Positioning Tool Adapters T92P-6256-A and Cam Positioning 
Tool T91P-6256-A on flats of camshafts. 

[FIGURE: AA0628A.gif]

Remove two bolts retaining RH timing chain tensioner (6L266) to 
cylinder head and remove timing chain tensioner. 

Remove RH timing chain tensioner arm (6L253). 

Remove two bolts retaining RH timing chain guide (6K297) to cylinder 
head and remove timing chain guide. 

Remove RH timing chain from camshaft sprocket and crankshaft sprockets 
(6306). 

 NOTE: Cam Positioning Tool Adapters T92P-6256-A and Cam Positioning Tool 
T91P-6256-A must be installed on camshaft to prevent 
camshaft from rotating. 

Remove two bolts retaining LH timing chain tensioner to cylinder head 
and remove timing chain tensioner. 

Remove LH timing chain tensioner arm. 

Remove two bolts retaining LH timing chain guide to cylinder head and 
remove timing chain guide. 

Remove LH timing chain from camshaft sprocket and crankshaft sprocket. 

If necessary, remove camshaft sprockets and crankshaft sprockets as 
described. 

 CAUTION: Do not rotate crankshaft and/or camshafts. Engine damage may occur. 

Inspect the plastic running face on timing chain tensioner arms and 
timing chain guides. If worn or damaged, remove and clean oil pan and oil pump 
screen cover and tube (6622). 

 Installation 

 NOTE: If engine has "jumped time," make sure that all repairs to engine 
components and/or valve train have been made. Then rotate engine 
counterclockwise 45 degrees. This will position all pistons below top of deck 
face. Install cylinder heads as described. 

 NOTE: Cam Positioning Tool Adapters T92P-6256-A and Cam Positioning Tool 
T91P-6256-A must be installed on camshafts to prevent 
camshafts from rotating. 

Install timing chain guides (both sides). Install timing chain guide 
retaining bolts. Tighten to 8-12 Nm (71-106 lb-in). 

If removed, position LH camshaft sprocket spacer (6265) and sprocket on 
camshaft. 

Install washer and camshaft sprocket retaining bolt. Do not tighten at 
this time. 

If removed, position RH camshaft sprocket spacer and sprocket on 
camshaft. 

Install washer and camshaft sprocket retaining bolt. Do not tighten at 
this time.

 NOTE: Steps 2 through 11 will install only one camshaft. If both camshafts

 (71-106 lb-in). 

 Installation Sequence 

[FIGURE: A14817D.gif]

spring. Rotate camshaft as necessary until all rocker arms are installed.

valve spring retainer. Install valve tappet (6500). 

Compress valve spring far enough to install rocker arm. 

Repeat Steps 8 through 10 until all rocker arms are installed. Remove 
Valve Spring Spacer from valve spring. 

 CAUTION: Crankshaft must only be rotated in the clockwise direction and only as 
far as top dead center (TDC). 

 NOTE: This will position crankshaft at top dead center (TDC). 

Rotate crankshaft clockwise 45 degrees. 

[FIGURE: A13658B.gif]

 CAUTION: Timing chain procedures must be followed exactly or damage to valves or 
pistons will result. 

Install timing chains as described.

as necessary. 

 NOTE: Prior to applying sealer, clean sealing surfaces with Metal Surface 
Cleaner F4AZ-19A536-RA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M5B392-A, 
to remove all residues that may interfere with the sealer's ability to adhere. 

Apply a 8-12 mm (0.32-0.47 inch) bead of Silicone Gasket and Sealant 
F6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6 in 
locations shown.

Water Pump 

 Removal 

Drain engine cooling system, remove cooling fan motor/fan blade (8600) 
and fan shroud (8146) assembly. Refer to Section 03-03 . 

Release drive belt tensioner (6B209) and remove drive belt (8620). 
Refer to Section 03-05 . 

Remove four bolts retaining water pump pulley (8509) to water pump 
(8501) and remove water pump pulley. 

Remove four bolts retaining water pump to engine (6007) and remove 
water pump. 

[FIGURE: A14810D.gif]

 Installation 

Replace O-ring type water pump housing gasket (8507) and clean sealing 
surface of cylinder blocks (6010). 

Lubricate water pump housing gasket with Ford Premium Cooling System 
Fluid E2FZ-19549-AA (in Canada, Motorcraft CXC-8-B) or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESE-M97B44-A. 

Position water pump on engine and install four retaining bolts. Tighten 
to 20-30 Nm (15-22 lb-ft). 

Position water pump pulley on water pump and install four retaining 
bolts. Tighten bolts to 20-30 Nm (15-22 lb-ft). 

Install drive belt. Refer to Section 03-05 . 

Install cooling fan motor/fan blade, fan shroud assembly and fill 
engine cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 . 

Check for leaks.

Intake Manifold 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Drain engine cooling system. 

Relieve fuel system pressure and disconnect fuel lines. Refer to 
 Section 10-01 . 

Remove air cleaner outlet tube (9B659). Refer to Section 03-12 .

Release drive belt tensioner (6B209) and remove drive belt (8620). 
Refer to Section 03-05 . 

 CAUTION: Do not pull on ignition wire as wire may separate from the connector in 
the ignition wire boot. 

Disconnect all ignition wires from spark plugs (12405). Refer to 
 Section 03-07B .

Disconnect ignition wires and ignition wire separators (12297) from 
valve cover stud bolts. 

Disconnect fuel charging wiring (9D930) from both ignition coils 
(12029) and camshaft position sensor (CMP sensor) (6B288). 

Remove four bolts retaining ignition coil to ignition coil brackets. 

Disconnect generator wiring harness from junction block at front fender 
apron (16054) and from generator (GEN) (10300). 

Remove four bolts retaining generator mounting bracket (10153) to 
intake manifold (9424). 

Remove bolts retaining generator to cylinder blocks (6010) and remove 
generator. 

Raise vehicle on a hoist. 

Disconnect fuel charging wiring from the oil pressure sensor (9278) and 
electronic variable orifice sensor and position fuel charging wiring out of 
the way. 

Disconnect EGR valve to exhaust manifold tube (9D477) from RH exhaust 
manifold (9430). 

Lower vehicle. 

Disconnect accelerator cable (9A758) and speed control actuator cable 
(9A825) from throttle body (9E926).

Remove accelerator cable bracket (9723) from intake manifold and 
position out of the way. 

Disconnect vacuum hose from throttle body adapter vacuum port. 

Disconnect heater water hose (18472). 

 NOTE: Two water outlet connection retaining bolts also retain intake manifold. 

Remove two bolts retaining water hose connection (8592) to intake 
manifold and position upper radiator hose (8260) and water hose connection out 
of the way. 

Remove the remaining nine bolts retaining intake manifold to cylinder 
heads (6049) and remove intake manifold.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Exhaust Manifold 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

On LH exhaust manifold (9430), remove bolt retaining oil level 
indicator tube (6754). 

Raise vehicle on hoist. 

Disconnect fuel charging wiring (9D930) from heated oxygen sensors 
(HO2S) (9F472). 

Remove EGR valve to exhaust manifold tube line nut from RH exhaust 
manifold and remove EGR valve to exhaust manifold tube (9D477). 

Disconnect three way catalytic converter (TWC) (5E212) from RH and LH 
exhaust manifold. Refer to Section 09-00 .

Lower three way catalytic converter and secure to crossmember with wire 
in positions shown. 

[FIGURE: A13631B.gif]

For LH exhaust manifold, disconnect the steering shaft and position out 
of the way. Refer to Section 11-04 . 

Remove eight nuts retaining LH exhaust manifold and remove LH exhaust 
manifold and two exhaust manifold gaskets (9448).

[FIGURE: A14805C.gif]

For RH exhaust manifold, remove eight nuts retaining exhaust manifold to 
cylinder head (6049) and studs and remove RH exhaust manifold and exhaust 
manifold gasket. 

 Installation 

If RH exhaust manifold is being replaced, transfer EGR valve tube to 
manifold connector (9F485) and tighten to 45-65 Nm (34-47 
lb-ft). 

Clean mating surfaces of exhaust manifolds and cylinder heads. 

Position exhaust manifold gasket and LH exhaust manifold to cylinder 
head and studs and install eight retaining nuts. Tighten in sequence to 18-22 Nm
 (14-16 lb-ft). 

 Installation Sequence 

[FIGURE: AA0637A.gif]

Position two exhaust manifold gaskets and LH exhaust manifold to 
cylinder head and studs and install eight retaining nuts. Tighten in sequence 
to 18-22 Nm (14-16 lb-ft). Refer to above illustration. 

Position and connect steering shaft. Refer to Section 11-04 .

 NOTE: Loosen line nut at EGR valve (EGR valve) (9D475) prior to installing 
assembly into vehicle. This will allow enough movement to align EGR valve 
retaining bolts. 

Position and connect EGR valve to exhaust manifold tube to exhaust 
manifold. Tighten line nut to 35-45 Nm (26-33 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: Two through bolts required on LH front engine support insulator (6038) 
and one through bolt required on RH front engine support insulator. 

 NOTE: Make sure exhaust system clears No. 3 crossmember. Adjust as necessary. 

Remove wire and position three way catalytic converter. Install four 
nuts and tighten to 27-41 Nm (20-30 lb-ft). 

Connect fuel charging wiring to heated oxygen sensors. 

Lower vehicle. 

Connect battery ground cable. 

Start engine and check for exhaust leaks.

If removed, position oil pump screen cover and tube on oil pump and

 (71-106 lb-in). Tighten oil pump screen cover and 
tube-to-main bearing stud spacer bolt to 20-30 Nm (15-22 
lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: AA0759A.gif]

 NOTE: Prior to applying sealer, clean sealing surfaces with Metal Surface 
Cleaner F4AZ-19A536-RA or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSE-M5B392-A, 
to remove all residues that may interfere with the sealer's ability to adhere. 

Apply Silicone Gasket and Sealant F6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting

than four minutes after applying sealer.
