ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment, Front 

Do not attempt to check and adjust wheel alignment without first making 
a preliminary inspection of the front end parts.

Check all the factors of wheel alignment except the turning angle 
before making any adjustments. Check the turning angle only after caster, 
camber and toe have been adjusted to specification. Check the wheel alignment 
under the following curb load conditions: 

Oil level and radiator (8005) filled to specification.

Spare tire, wheel, jack and jack handle in position.

Front seats in rearmost position.

All other loading removed.

All tires inflated to specified pressure (cold).

All excessive mud, dirt and road deposit accumulation removed from 
chassis and underbody.

Refer to Specifications for wheel alignment specifications. 

Adjusting the camber affects caster and toe. Adjusting the caster 
affects toe. The recommended adjustment sequence is to first set camber, set 
caster, and then set toe. Prior to resetting toe, camber should always be 
checked and reset if necessary. 

The front suspension is fully adjustable for caster, camber and toe. 

After the front-wheel alignment factors have been checked, make the 
necessary adjustments. Do not attempt to adjust front-wheel alignment by 
bending the suspension or steering parts.

 Equipment Installation 

Equipment used for wheel alignment inspection must be accurate and 
capable of 4-wheel alignment. All wheel alignment readings must be performed 
on an alignment rack level to within 1.59 mm (0.0625 inch) side-to-side and 
front-to-rear. The instrumentation used must have a means of compensating for 
wheel runout. 

Install the wheel alignment equipment on the vehicle and follow the 
installation and inspection instructions provided by the manufacturer. 

 Caster 

The caster is the forward or rearward tilt of the top of the front 
wheel spindle (3105). If the top of the front wheel spindle tilts to the rear, 
caster is positive. For correct caster angle, refer to Specifications . 

Caster is adjusted by moving the front suspension lower arm strut 
(3468) relative to the front sub-frame (5C145). Loosen the nuts securing the 
front suspension lower arm strut to the front sub-frame and adjust the caster 
by turning the nuts in the appropriate direction until the desired setting is 
achieved. The setting should be locked by holding the rear nut used to adjust 
and tightening the opposite front nut to 140-160 Nm (104-118 
lb-ft). 

The maximum caster difference (side-to-side) is shown in Specifications. 

[FIGURE: F1216C.gif]

 Camber 

Camber is the amount that the centerline of the wheel is tilted inward 
or outward from the true vertical. If the top of the wheel is tilted outward, 
away from the vehicle, the camber is positive. If the top of the wheel is 
tilted inward, toward the vehicle, the camber is negative. For correct camber 
angle, refer to Specifications . 

The maximum camber difference (side-to-side) is shown in Specifications. 

 Toe 

 NOTE: Toe should only be checked and adjusted after the caster and camber 
have been adjusted to specification. 

Toe-in and toe-out is the difference in the distance between the 
extreme front and extreme rear of the tires. Toe-in occurs when the dimension 
taken at the front of the tires is less than that taken at the rear of the 
tires � positive toe. Toe-out occurs when the dimension taken at the 
front of the tires is greater than that taken at the rear of the tires �
 negative toe. 

Start the engine and move the steering wheel back and forth several 
times until it is in the straight-ahead or centered position so the power 
steering control valve will be in the center (neutral) position. Lock the 
steering wheel in place using a steering wheel holder. 

 NOTE: Whenever the jam nuts are loosened for toe adjustment, the nut and tie 
rod ends (3A130) must be cleaned and lubricated and the jam nut tightened to 
58-67 Nm (43-49 lb-ft). 

Adjust the LH and RH tie rod end lengths until each wheel has one-half 
of the desired total toe specification. 

[FIGURE: F1640F.gif]

For correct toe setting, refer to Specifications . 

 Reference Definitions 

[FIGURE: F7804B.gif]

 Wheel/Tire Runout 

Check wheel and tire runout with the tires inflated to the normal load 
inflation pressure. To provide accurate results, make the checks with a dial 
indicator or Rotunda Radial Runout Gauge 007-0056A or equivalent immediately 
after the road test. If time is allowed to pass between the road test and the 
runout checks, the tires may develop slight flat spots, which can affect the 
accuracy of the tire runout checks. 

Measure tire radial runout at the center and outside ribs of the tread 
face. It may be necessary to put tape on the tire tread to keep the dial 
indicator roller from falling into tread block grooves in the tread. Measure 
the lateral runout just above the letters identifying the tire size. 

Measure wheel radial runout at the wheel rim along the inside edge of 
the flange. 

 Tire Lead 

"Lead" is the movement or wander of the vehicle from a straight path on 
a level road with no pressure on the steering wheel. 

Lead is usually caused by: 

Incorrect wheel alignment.

Uneven brake adjustment.

Uneven or incorrect tire inflation pressures.

Damaged or worn tire construction.

The way a tire is constructed can produce tire lead. An example of this 
is placement of the radial belts. Off-center belts on a radial tire can cause 
the tire to develop a side force while rolling straight down the road. If one 
side of the tire is a little larger diameter than the other, the tire will 
tend to roll to one side. This will develop a side force which can produce 
tire lead.

 Bearing, Front Wheel 

The front wheel bearings are pregreased, sealed and require no 
scheduled maintenance. The front wheel bearings are preset and cannot be 
adjusted. If a bearing is disassembled for any reason, the wheel hub (1104) 
assembly must be replaced.

Front wheel bearings that need replacing may be indicated by a noise 
that occurs only when turning. To diagnose the front wheel bearings: 

Road test the vehicle on a smooth road. Make sharp turns to the right 
and left.

If the vehicle makes noises on right turns, the left wheel bearing may 
need to be replaced. 

If the vehicle makes noises on left turns, the right wheel bearing may 
need to be replaced. 

If wheel bearing noise is heard on either right or left turns, the 
wheel hub assembly on the suspected side should be removed and inspected.

Spin the tire quickly by hand and make sure the tire turns smoothly 
without noise from the wheel bearing.

Remove the wheel and front disc brake caliper (2B121). Refer to Section 06-03 .

Position Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent 
against the wheel hub, then push and pull the wheel hub. Measure the end play 
of the wheel hub assembly. There should be no perceptible end play. If there 
is perceptible end play, replace the wheel hubs. 

 Bearing, Rear Wheel 

 NOTE: The rear wheel bearings are of a cartridge design and are pregreased, 
sealed and require no scheduled maintenance. The rear wheel bearings (1225) 
are preset and cannot be adjusted. If a bearing is disassembled for any 
reason, it must be replaced as a unit. No individual service seals, rollers or 
races are available. The hub nut torque of 255-345 Nm 
(188-254 lb-ft) restricts rear wheel bearing/wheel hub relative movement and 
maintains axial position of the rear hub (1109). Due to the importance of the 
wheel hub nut torque/tension relationship, take the following precautions 
during service: 

Since the rear wheel bearing cannot be adjusted, the rear axle wheel 
hub retainer (4B477) must not be backed off after reaching the required torque 
of 255-345 Nm (188-254 lb-ft) during installation. 

The rear axle wheel hub retainer and washer assembly must be replaced 
with a new rear axle wheel hub retainer and washer assembly whenever the rear 
axle wheel hub retainer is backed off or removed. Never reuse the rear axle 
wheel hub retainer. 

Power tools must not be used to tighten the rear axle wheel hub 
retainer or rear wheel bearing damage will result. Use a torque wrench.

The rear hub and rear wheel drive shaft and joint splines have an 
interference fit requiring special tools for disassembly. The rear axle wheel 
hub retainer can be used to accomplish assembly. Refer to Section 04-02 .

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Turning Angle, Front 

When the inside wheel is turned 20 degrees, the turning angle of the 
outside wheel should be as specified. The turning angle cannot be adjusted 
directly because it is a result of the combination of caster, camber and toe 
adjustments and should, therefore, be measured only after these adjustments 
have been made. If the turning angle does not measure to specification, check 
the suspension, front sub-frame (5C145) or steering parts for a bent condition. 

The front suspension is fully adjustable for caster, camber and toe. 
After front-wheel alignment factors have been checked, make the necessary 
adjustments. Do not attempt to adjust front wheel alignment by bending the 
suspension or steering parts.

PAGE 2297
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 04-00: Suspension � Service

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Steering Angle Check

 NOTE: Perform the steering angle check before toe-in measurement (if any 
steering angle corrections have been made). 

Check the wheel steering angles at full right and left positions. If 
the angles are not within specification, the tie rod ends (3A130) must be 
adjusted to the right or left until the steering angles are equal.

Adjustment of the tie rod end affects the centering of the steering 
wheel in the straight-ahead position. Adjustments can be fine-tuned by 
shifting the tie rod ends a small amount away from the equal angle setting. If 
the steering wheel cannot be centered with the steering angles within 
specification, check for improper assembly or installation of the following 
steering components:

power rack and pinion steering gear

steering column tube (3514)

steering wheel (3600)

Refer to Section 11-00 for steering system servicing.

Adjust the steering angles as follows:

With paint or marking pen, mark both tie rod ends, front wheel spindle 
tie rods (3280) and jam nuts in their original positions. These reference 
marks will help in equalizing right and left adjustments.

Remove the tie rod boot clips and free the boots to prevent them from 
being twisted when the front wheel spindle tie rods are turned. 

Loosen and back off the tie rod end jam nuts. 

To avoid toe-in change, turn front wheel spindle tie rod into and the 
other out of the front wheel spindle tie rods by equal amounts. This shortens 
one front wheel spindle tie rod and lengthens the other, shifting the steering 
rack right or left until the rack teeth are centered on the pinion and rack 
travel from the centered position is equal in both directions. This equalizes 
the wheel steering angles but also rotates the pinion and steering wheel.

Position the wheels straight ahead and check the steering wheel 
centering. If close to correct, shift the rack and front wheel spindle tie 
rods left or right without turning the wheels to center the steering wheel. A 
shift to the left will turn the wheel clockwise and a shift to the right will 
turn it counterclockwise as seen from the driver seat.

Verify that the wheel steering angles are still within specification. 
If not within specification, the steering wheel can be removed and shifted on 
the steering gear input worm gear and rack (3524) to center it.

ADJUSTMENTS

Steering Pull/Drift

 NOTE: Side-to-side ride height variation can cause side-to-side camber 
variation.

 NOTE: When trying to correct for pull/drift refer to the following conditions.

Vehicle will pull/drift:

toward the side with the most positive camber.

toward the side with the least positive caster. 

toward the low side if vehicle is leaning.

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment, Rear

The recommended adjustment sequence for rear alignment is to set 
chamber and then toe. Toe should be rechecked prior to final tightening. 

 Toe, Rear 

Rear toe is set by rotating a cam bolt at the inner pivot of the rear 
suspension arm and bushing (5500). Loosen the nut securing the adjustment and 
set toe by rotating the head of the bolt. Lock the adjustment by holding the 
bolt and tightening the nut to 225-275 Nm (166-202 lb-ft). 

 Camber, Rear 

Camber is adjusted by rotating a cam bolt at the inner pivot of the 
rear suspension arm and bushing. Loosen the nut securing the adjustment and 
set camber by rotating the head of the bolt. Lock the adjustment by holding 
the bolt and tightening the nut to 133 Nm (99 lb-ft).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension 

The front suspension is a long spindle, short and long arm design. The 
design consists of:

short upperfront suspension arm bushing joint (3085). 

longfront suspension lower arm strut (3468).

front shock absorber (18124).

front coil spring (5310).

front stabilizer bar (5482),lower suspension arm stabilizer bar 
insulator (5493), andstabilizer bar link (5K484).

================================================================================
PAGE 2303
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Components 

Hot forged A-frame upper front suspension arm bushing joint (3085) with 
lubed for life, low friction, integral ball joint. 

Hot forged front suspension lower arm (3079) with lubed for life, 
tension loaded, low friction front suspension lower arm ball joint (3050). 

High efficiency 1:1 ratio front stabilizer bar (5482) with zero 
compliance double ball joint stabilizer bar links (5K484), upset rings to 
limit lateral movement and tapered link attachments for increased reliability. 

Hot forged, one-piece front wheel spindle (3105) with integral caliper 
anchor plates. 

Rivetedfront disc brake rotor shields (2K005). 

Variable rate front coil springs (5310). 

Cold formed double isolated front suspension lower arm strut (3468).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Component Replacement

The following front suspension components may be replaced either 
individually or as an assembly:

Front shock absorber (18124), front coil spring (5310) and front shock 
absorber mounting bracket (18183) may be replaced individually. It is not 
necessary to replace front shock absorbers in pairs.

Front suspension lower arm (3079), front suspension lower arm ball 
joint (3050) and front suspension lower arm mounting bolt bushing (3069) may 
be replaced individually.

Front wheel hub (1104) may be replaced individually.

Front wheel bearings are not serviceable. If damaged, the wheel hub 
must be replaced. 

Front suspension lower arm strut (3468) and front suspension lower arm 
rear strut bushing (3B271)/front suspension lower arm strut rear bushing 
(3A225) may be replaced individually.

Front wheel spindle (3105) may be replaced individually.

Front suspension arm bushing joint (3085) and upper ball joint must be 
replaced as an assembly.

Front stabilizer bar (5482), lower suspension arm stabilizer bar 
insulator (5493) and stabilizer bar link (5K484) may be replaced individually.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fasteners, Suspension 

 CAUTION: All front suspension fasteners are important attaching parts in that 
they could affect the performance of vital parts and systems, and/or could 
result in major service expense. Any part must be replaced with one of the 
same part number or with an exact equivalent part if replacement becomes 
necessary. Do not use a replacement part of lesser quality or substitute 
design. Torque values must be used as specified during assembly for proper 
retention of this part. 

Never attempt to heat, quench or straighten any front suspension part. 
Replace with a new part.

PAGE 2306
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Shock Absorber

 NOTE: The front shock absorber (18124) is part of the front shock absorber 
and spring assembly and requires disassembly of the front suspension in order 
to replace.

The front shock absorbers provide motion and force and damping between 
the sprung and unsprung masses of the vehicle when traveling over irregular 
road surfaces. 

The front shock absorber consists of a twin tube gas-pressurized 
structure providing damping in both the rebound (UP) and compression (DOWN) 
directions. This damping is accomplished by driving a dual (rebound and 
compression) acting piston through a fluid environment. The motion resistant 
forces are controlled by a velocity sensitive variable orifice piston assembly 
within the front shock absorber.

================================================================================

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheel Bearing and Wheel Hub 

Each front wheel is bolted to a wheel hub (1104) and bearing assembly. 
The front wheel bearing is an integral part of the wheel hub assembly and is 
serviced as a wheel hub assembly. A front axle wheel hub retainer (3B477) 
retains the wheel hub assembly to the front wheel spindle (3105) assembly.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Spindle

 Removal 

Raise vehicle on hoist. 

Remove tire and wheel assembly. 

Mark front disc brake rotor (1125) and lug bolt (1107) sofront disc 
brake rotor can be installed in the same position as original for rotor 
runout. 

Remove disc brake caliper (2B120) and front disc brake rotor. Refer to 
 Section 06-03 . Support disc brake caliper with wire. 

[FIGURE: F5206C.gif]

Remove wheel hub (1104) assembly as described. 

Remove front brake anti-lock sensor (2C204) and position out of the way. 

Remove tie rod end cotter pin and loosen castellated nut. Separate tie 
rod end from front wheel spindle (3105) using Tie Rod End Remover TOOL-3290-D 
or equivalent. Remove nut. 

[FIGURE: F5207D.gif]

 CAUTION: Use extreme care to avoid damage to the ball joint seal. If seal is 
damaged, replace the stabilizer bar link (5K484) assembly. 

 Remove stabilizer bar link at front wheel spindle using Ball Joint 
Remover D88L-3006-A or equivalent. 

[FIGURE: F7821E.gif]

Separate front suspension lower arm ball joint (3050) from front wheel 
spindle. Loosen nut and rap front wheel spindle with hammer. Remove nut and 
discard. 

Remove and discard upper front wheel spindle to upper front suspension 
arm ball joint bolt and nut. Spread slot slightly and remove front wheel 
spindle from front suspension lower arm ball joint and vehicle. 

 Installation 

Position front wheel spindle on front suspension lower arm (3079) and 
attach front suspension lower arm to front wheel spindle. 

Install new nut on front suspension lower arm ball joint. Tighten to 
113-153 Nm (84-112 lb-ft). 

Install wheel hub and bearing assembly as described. Tighten new front 
axle wheel hub retainer (3B477) to 255-345 Nm (188-254 
lb-ft). Install new front hub cap grease seal (1N135).

Install front disc brake rotor and disc brake caliper assembly. Refer 
to Section 06-03 . 

Install front brake anti-lock sensor. Refer to Section 06-09 . 

Install stabilizer bar link to front wheel spindle. Tighten retaining 
nut to 40-55 Nm (30-40 lb-ft). 

Attach tie rod end (3A130) and nut. Tighten nut to 53-73 Nm
 (39-53 lb-ft). Continue to tighten until a slot in nut 
lines up with hole through stud. Install new cotter pin. 

Install tire and wheel assembly. Tighten lug nuts (1012) to 115-142 Nm
 (85-104 lb-ft). Do not use power tools, use torque wrench.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring and Shock Assembly

 Removal 

Remove plastic front shock absorber strut cover cup (18A179) at front 
shock absorber mounting bracket (18183). 

Remove three upper shock retaining nuts and shock absorber housing seal 
(18T003) from mounting studs in engine compartment. 

Raise vehicle on a hoist. 

Remove tire and wheel assembly. 

Remove lower shock mounting bolt and nut. 

Remove nut at stabilizer bar link upper mounting stud. 

 CAUTION: Use extreme care to avoid damage to the ball joint seal. If seal is 
damaged, replace the stabilizer bar link (5K484) assembly. 

Separate stabilizer bar link from front wheel spindle (3105) using Ball 
Joint Remover D88L-3006-A or equivalent. 

Support front suspension lower arm (3079) assembly with HI-Lift Jack 
014-00210 or equivalent. 

[FIGURE: AF0313A.gif]

Raise front suspension lower arm and front wheel spindle with jack until 
stabilizer bar link can be completely separated from front wheel spindle. 
Position stabilizer bar link out of the way. 

Remove front wheel spindle to upper front suspension arm ball joint 
retaining nut and bolt. Discard nut and bolt. 

Lower jack to separate front wheel spindle from upper front suspension 
lower arm ball joint (3050). Do not allow front wheel spindle to hang free. 
Support it with wire or other means. 

Lower support for front suspension lower arm and remove front shock 
absorber mount and spring assembly from vehicle. 

[FIGURE: F5204C.gif]

 Installation 

Position front shock absorber spring and upper mount assembly over 
front suspension lower arm. Insert lower shock bolt into front suspension 
lower arm. 

Using transmission jack or similar device, raise front suspension lower 
arm and front shock absorber (18124) into position. Align upper shock mounting 
studs with holes. 

Remove wire supporting front wheel spindle and position front wheel 
spindle to upper front suspension lower arm. Raise lower front suspension 
lower arm using jack and attach front wheel spindle to upper front suspension 
arm ball joint. 

Install new front suspension arm bushing to front wheel spindle 
retaining bolt (from front of vehicle) and nut. Tighten nut to 68-92 Nm
 (51-67 lb-ft). 

Position stabilizer bar link and lower front wheel spindle assembly 
until stabilizer bar link can be installed. 

Install nut on stabilizer bar link stud. Tighten to 40-55 Nm
 (30-40 lb-ft). 

Remove jack from front suspension lower arm. 

Install lower shock nut. Do not tighten at this time. 

Install tire and wheel assembly. Tighten lug nuts (1012) to 115-142 Nm
 (85-104 lb-ft). Do not use power tools, use torque wrench. 

Lower vehicle, making sure upper shock mounting studs are aligned with 
holes. 

Install shock absorber housing seal and three nuts to upper mounting 
studs. Tighten to 22-31 Nm (17-22 lb-ft). 

Install plastic front shock absorber strut cover cup. 

 CAUTION: To prevent front suspension lower arm strut bushing wind-up, lower 
shock nut must be tightened with vehicle weight on wheels. 

Position vehicle on "drive on" hoist or alignment rack. Neutralize 
front suspension lower arm strut bushings (3A140) by pushing down on front of 
vehicle and releasing . Then tighten lower front shock absorber nut to 170-230 Nm
 (126-169 lb-ft).

Strut, Lower Arm

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Arm, Lower 

 Removal 

Raise vehicle. 

Remove tire and wheel assembly. 

Loosen front suspension lower arm ball joint nut three or four turns. 

Rap front wheel spindle (3105) to separate front suspension arm bushing 
joint (3085). Leave nut attached. 

Support front wheel spindle by wire or other means to prevent excessive 
sagging of upper front suspension arm bushing joint. 

Mark position of camber adjustment cam. 

 CAUTION: Do not hold front suspension lower arm strut (3468) or damage surface 
in area shown. 

 Remove nut retaining front suspension lower arm strut to front 
suspension arm bushing joint and discard. Hold front suspension lower arm 
strut by flats with wrench while turning nut. 

[FIGURE: F5208D.gif]

Remove lower shock bolt and nut. 

Remove and mark pivot (camber) bolt and nut location. 

Remove nut at front suspension lower arm ball joint (3050) and remove 
front suspension lower arm (3079). 

 Installation 

Position lower front suspension lower arm in vehicle. Loosely install 
and align pivot (camber) bolt and new nut. 

Install front suspension lower arm strut washer and insulators and 
loosely install front suspension lower arm strut to front suspension lower arm 
attaching nut. 

Loosely install new front suspension lower arm ball joint nut. 

Install lower shock bolt and nut. Do not tighten at this time. 

Tighten front suspension lower arm ball joint nut to 113-153 Nm
 (84-112 lb-ft). 

 CAUTION: Do not hold front suspension lower arm strut or damage surface in area 
shown. 

Tighten front suspension lower arm strut to front suspension lower arm 
nut to 113-153 Nm (84-112 lb-ft). 

Remove wire or other support holding front wheel spindle. 

Install tire and wheel assembly. Tighten lug nuts (1012) to 115-142 Nm
 (85-104 lb-ft). Do not use power tools, use torque wrench. 

Lower vehicle. 

 CAUTION: To prevent front suspension lower arm strut bushing wind-up, lower 
front shock absorber nut must be tightened with vehicle weight on wheel. 

Position vehicle on "drive-on" hoist or alignment rack. Push down on 
front of vehicle and release to neutralize suspension. Tighten lower shock nut 
to 170-230 Nm (126-169 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: If lower front suspension lower arm is replaced, front wheel alignment 
must be checked. 

Align camber marks at pivot bolt. Tighten nut to 113-153 Nm
 (84-112 lb-ft). 

Check wheel alignment. Refer to Section 04-00 .

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Bearings, Front 

The wheel bearings are of a hub unit design and are pregreased, sealed 
and require no scheduled maintenance. The bearings are preset and cannot be 
adjusted. If a front wheel bearing replacement is required for any repair, the 
wheel hub (1104) and bearings must be replaced as an assembly. The front wheel 
bearings cannot be disassembled from the wheel hub and serviced separately. No 
individual service seals, roller or races are available. The front axle wheel 
hub retainer (3B477) torque of 255-345 Nm (188-254 lb-ft) 
restricts front wheel bearing relative movement and maintains axial position 
of the wheel hub. Due to the importance of the front axle wheel hub retainer 
torque/tension relationship take the following precautions during service: 

Since the front wheel bearing cannot be adjusted, the front axle wheel 
hub retainer and washer must not be backed off after reaching the required 
torque of 255-345 Nm (188-254 lb-ft) during installation. 

The front axle wheel hub retainer must be replaced with a new front 
axle wheel hub retainer whenever the front axle wheel hub retainer is backed 
off or removed. Never reuse the front axle wheel hub retainer. 

Impact-type tools must not be used to tighten the front axle wheel hub 
retainer or bearing damage will result. Use a torque wrench.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension 

The rear suspension system has the following characteristics:

It is fully independent and is mounted on a rubber-isolated subframe. 

Large rear suspension arm and bushings (5500) (H-arm configuration) are 
used to oppose torque reaction on braking and acceleration. 

A rear suspension compensator link (5A972) controls toe-out during 
braking. 

The stamped rear suspension arm and bushing provides camber control. 

The variable-rate rear spring (5560) is mounted between the rear 
suspension arm and bushing and the body. 

A rear suspension jounce bumper (5K570) is located inside the rear 
shock absorber (18125). 

A rear stabilizer bar (5A772) is standard on all models. 

Permanent mould cast aluminum rear wheel knuckle (5A969):

carries the rear suspension loads. 

connects the upperrear suspension arm and bushing and lower rear 
suspension arm and bushing .

houses the rear wheel bearing (1225).

provides mounts for the brakes.

================================================================================
PAGE 2328
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 04-02: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Rear

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Components

 Inspection 

Start diagnosis of possible suspension concerns with a thorough 
inspection of vehicle. Include all suspension components and mounting points 
to identify any that are worn, damaged or loose. 

 Rear Spring 

Elastomeric insulators are used on either end for improved isolation. 

Although the rear springs (5560) are mounted in the same manner on all 
models, unique spring load/rate provisions are used to suit the particular 
model. 

Camber adjustment is available at the inboard pivot attachment through 
an internal-to the rear-spring upper retaining seat arrangement. 

Toe angle can be adjusted at the rear suspension arm and bushing (5500) 
inboard of the rearward pivot attachment to the sub-frame using eccentric rear 
suspension arm adjusting cam kits (5K751) on either side of the bushings. 

Refer to Section 04-00 for rear camber or toe alignment procedures. 

 Wheel Bearings 

The rear wheel bearings (1225) are of a cartridge design and are 
pregreased, sealed and require no scheduled maintenance. The rear wheel 
bearings are preset and cannot be adjusted. If a bearing is disassembled for 
any reason, it must be replaced as a unit. No individual service seals, 
rollers or races are available. The rear axle wheel hub retainer torque of 
255-345 Nm (188-254 lb-ft) restricts rear wheel bearing/wheel 
hub relative movement and maintains axial position of the rear hub (1109). Due 
to the importance of the wheel hub nut torque/tension relationship, take the 
following precautions during service: 

Since the rear wheel bearing cannot be adjusted, the rear axle wheel 
hub retainer (4B477) must not be backed off after reaching the required torque 
of 255-345 Nm (188-254 lb-ft) during installation. 

The rear axle wheel hub retainer and washer assembly must be replaced 
with a new rear axle wheel hub retainer and washer assembly whenever it is 
backed off or removed. Never reuse the rear axle wheel hub retainer. 

Power tools must not be used to tighten the rear axle wheel hub 
retainer or rear wheel bearing damage will result. 

The wheel hub and rear wheel drive shaft and joint splines have an 
interference fit requiring special tools for disassembly. The rear axle wheel 
hub retainer can be used to accomplish assembly. Use a torque wrench.

 Shock Absorber 

The rear shock absorber (18125):

provides motion and force damping between the sprung and unsprung 
masses of the vehicle when traveling over irregular road surfaces.

provides positive jounce and rebound over travel stops. 

consists of a twin-tube, gas-pressurized structure providing damping in 
both the rebound (up) and the compression (down) directions. 

This damping is accomplished by driving a dual (rebound and 
compression) acting piston through a fluid environment. The motion-resistant 
forces are controlled by a velocity-sensitive variable orifice piston assembly 
within the rear shock absorber. 

 Stabilizer Bar 

The rear stabilizer bar (5A772):

aids in control of suspension and restricts body roll.

attaches to the body and rear wheel knuckle (5A969) through lower 
suspension arm stabilizer bar insulators (5493) and rear stabilizer bar link 
and bushings (5C488).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Component Replacement

 CAUTION: Rear suspension fasteners are important parts because they could affect 
the performance of vital components and systems and could result in major 
service expense. They must be replaced with the same part number or with an 
equivalent part if replacement becomes necessary. Do not use a replacement 
part of lesser quality or substitute design. Torque values must be used as 
specified during reassembly to ensure proper retention of this part. Never 
attempt to heat, quench or straighten any rear suspension part. Replace with a 
new part. 

The following suspension components may be replaced either individually 
or as an assembly:

Rear spring (5560) andrear spring center mounting insulator (5741) may 
be replaced individually.

Rear shock absorber (18125) may be replaced individually. It is not 
necessary to replace therear shock absorbers in pairs.

Rear hub (1109), rear wheel bearing (1225) and rear wheel knuckle 
(5A969) may be replaced individually.

Rear suspension compensator link (5A972) must be replaced as an assembly.

Rear stabilizer bar (5A772),rear stabilizer bar link and bushing (5C488),
stabilizer bar bracket (5486) andlower suspension arm stabilizer bar insulator 
(5493) may be replaced individually.

Rear suspension arm and bushings (5500) must be replaced as an assembly.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheel Assembly 

The rear wheel assembly has the following characteristics:

Each rear wheel is bolted to a rear hub (1109). 

There are two opposed and tapered roller rear wheel bearings (1225) 
(inner and outer) with grease retainer seals (inner and outer), encased in one 
single cup or cartridge. 

This rear wheel bearing is pressed into the rear wheel knuckle bore 
from the inboard side until it rests against the shoulder on the outboard 
side. 

A snap ring is installed in a groove on the inboard side of the knuckle 
bore for added bearing retention. 

A bearing dust seal is installed on the CV joint, inboard of the rear 
wheel knuckle (5A969), rear wheel bearing and rear hub. 

The rear hub is pressed into the rear wheel knuckle assembly.

The CV joint is pressed through the rear hub in the rear wheel knuckle 
assembly.

A rear axle wheel hub retainer (4B477) attaches the rear hub to the CV 
joint.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring 

 Coil 

 Removal 

Raise vehicle on hoist.

Remove rear wheel and tire assembly. Refer to Section 04-04 .

Remove rear stabilizer bar link and bushing link nuts at both ends of 
rear stabilizer bar (5A772). Rotate rear stabilizer bar up and out of the way. 

Disconnect parking brake rear cable and conduit (2A635) at rear disc 
brake caliper (2553).

Install three Rotunda Spring Cages 164-R3555 or equivalent torear 
spring (5560) as follows: 

Install one spring cage without an adjuster link to the inboard side 
(the innermost bend of the rear spring). 

Install two more spring cages, with adjusters, at 120 degree angles to 
the previously installed cage. 

 Spring, Rear

Approximately 120 Degrees

Place a transmission jack or suitable stand under the rear suspension 
arm and bushing (5500) as far outboard as possible. 

[FIGURE: F5168B.gif]

Support the rear wheel knuckle (5A969) assembly by wiring the rear 
suspension arm and bushing to the body. 

[FIGURE: F5169B.gif]

Remove lower rear shock absorber mounting bolt, washer and nut. 

[FIGURE: F5170C.gif]

 NOTE: Rear suspension arm and bushing must not be lowered until pivot bolts 
are loose. Do not attempt to remove plastic cap on front pivot nut. 

Loosen both inboard pivot bolts on rear suspension arm and bushing.

Remove two bolts and nuts retaining rear suspension arm and bushing to 
rear wheel knuckle.

Lower the rear suspension arm and bushing by lowering jack. Make sure 
spring cages are properly seated on rear spring as rear suspension arm and 
bushing is dropped. 

[FIGURE: AF0411A.gif]

Remove jack, lowerrear suspension arm and bushing fully by hand and 
remove rear spring with cages in place. 

[FIGURE: F5172B.gif]

Remove rear spring center mounting insulators (5741) if necessary. 

[FIGURE: F5173B.gif]

If spring cages are to be removed for installation of rear spring, use 
Coil Spring Compressor D78P-5310-A or equivalent to compress rear spring and 
remove cages. Rear spring center mounting insulator should be installed on 
rear spring before installing rear spring in tool to prevent slippage of 
plates. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Compress rear spring with rear spring center mounting insulators 
installed to prevent plates from slipping. 

If a new rear spring is to be installed, it must first be compressed 
and caged. If original rear spring was removed with Rotunda Spring Cages 
164-R3555 or equivalent, duplicate the positions of the cages on the new rear 
spring. Install cages by first compressing rear spring in Coil Spring 
Compressor D78P-5310-A or equivalent. 

If original rear spring was broken, compress new rear spring in Coil 
Spring Compressor D78P-5310-A or equivalent and install three spring cages in 
positions shown under Removal, Step 5. If original length of rear spring is 
not known, such as when replacing a broken rear spring, compress rear spring 
to approximately 267 mm (10.5 inches) overall length (not including rubber 
rear spring center mounting insulators).

[FIGURE: F5174C.gif]

Install rear spring center mounting insulators if removed. 

 NOTE: Short cage (without adjuster) must be inboard. Spring pigtails may be 
in any position. 

Install rear spring, with cages in place, onto upper and rear 
suspension arm and bushings. 

Position two jackstands under front bumper reinforcement to prevent 
rear of vehicle from lifting off hoist. 

Position jack under rear suspension arm and bushing and raise rear 
suspension arm and bushing up to rear wheel knuckle bores. Make sure spring 
seats properly. Install bolts and nuts retaining rear suspension arm and 
bushing to rear wheel knuckle . Tighten nuts to 149-201 Nm 
(110-148 lb-ft). 

Remove wire supporting rear wheel knuckle, rear disc brake caliper 
(2552) and rear suspension arm and bushing. 

Install lower shock absorber mount bolt washer and nut. While holding 
bolt, tighten nut to 128-172 Nm (95-126 lb-ft). 

Remove jack and jackstands. 

Remove spring cages. 

Connect parking brake rear cable and conduit at rear disc brake caliper.

Install rear stabilizer bar link and bushing (5C488) and retaining nuts 
at both ends of rear stabilizer bar. 

Install rear wheel and tire assembly. 

Lower vehicle. 

Drive vehicle onto alignment rack. 

Set rear suspension arm adjusting cam kit (5K751) to mark made at time 
of removal. 

Tighten front rear suspension arm and bushing-to-rear sub-frame nut to 
225-275 Nm (166-202 lb-ft). Tighten rear lower rear 
suspension arm and bushing-to-sub-frame nut to 192-259 Nm 
(142-191 lb-ft). 

Check rear wheel toe setting and adjust as necessary.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Shock Absorber 

 Removal 

 WARNING: THESE VEHICLES ARE EQUIPPED WITH GAS-PRESSURIZED SHOCK ABSORBERS WHICH 
WILL EXTEND UNASSISTED. DO NOT APPLY HEAT OR FLAME TO THE SHOCK ABSORBER TUBE 
DURING REMOVAL. 

 CAUTION: The rear shock absorbers (18125) act as the rebound stops for the rear 
suspension. When rear shock absorbers are removed, the rear suspension arm and 
bushings (5500) must be restrained to prevent damage to these components. The 
best method for rear shock absorber removal is to use a drive-on hoist or 
alignment pit. 

Position vehicle on drive-on hoist or alignment pit, or use an 
equivalent method of supporting the vehicle on its suspension. 

Remove all upper retaining parts from inside luggage compartment. 

Remove bolt and nut at rear suspension arm and bushing.

 NOTE: Replace rear shock absorbers individually as required. They do not need 
to be replaced in pairs. 

Remove rear shock absorber. 

 Installation 

Properly prime the rear shock absorber to remove air from the working 
cylinder. Refer to Section 04-00 . 

Place the inner washer and insulator on the upper retaining stud. 
Position stud through shock tower mounting hole. Compress rear shock absorber 
as required and align shock absorber mounting eye for attachment.

Attach lower end of rear shock absorber. Install retaining bolt and nut 
and tighten to 128-172 Nm (95-126 lb-ft) while holding nut 
and turning bolt. 

With upper end of the rear shock absorber protruding through the body 
shock tower hole, install the washer and nut assembly.

Hub and Wheel Spindle

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

T81P-1104-A

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Do not begin procedure unless a new rear axle wheel hub retainer 
(4B477) is available. Once removed, this part cannot be reused during 
assembly. Its torque holding and retention capability is greatly diminished 
during removal. 

Remove wheel cover from wheel and tire assembly and loosen lug nuts 
(1012). 

Remove rear axle wheel hub retainer and discard.

Raise vehicle.

Remove wheel and tire assembly. Refer to Section 04-04 . 

Using needle-nose pliers, slide parking brake cable adjustment clip 
downward until front parking brake cable and conduit (2853) is free. 

[FIGURE: E8311A.gif]

Remove parking brake rear cable and conduit (2A635) from rear disc 
brake caliper (2553) (disc brakes only). 

[FIGURE: AF0037A.gif]

Remove upper and lower disc brake caliper locating pins (2B296) and 
remove rear disc brake caliper assembly from rear disc brake rotor (2C026) 
(disc brakes only). Refer to Section 06-04 . 

Carefully wire the rear disc brake caliper to brake junction bracket as 
shown (disc brakes only). 

 CAUTION: Extreme care must be taken NOT to stretch, twist or kink rear wheel 
brake hose (2A442) assembly. 

With push-on nuts removed, remove rear disc brake rotor (disc brakes) or 
brake drum (1126) (drum brakes). 

[FIGURE: F5187C.gif]

Remove three bolts retaining rear wheel disc brake shield (2C028) to
rear wheel knuckle (5A969) and remove rear wheel disc brake shield (disc 
brakes). 

Disconnect parking brake rear cable and conduit and disconnect brake 
line from wheel cylinder (drum brakes). 

Remove upper rear suspension arm and bushing nut and bolt. 

Wire upper rear suspension arm and bushing (5500) to body to prevent 
damage to rear axle shaft inner boots (4L537) when rear wheel knuckle and rear 
hub (1109) assembly is removed. 

[FIGURE: F5188B.gif]

Attach Front Hub Remover/Replacer T81P-1104-C to hub studs as shown. 
Turn wrench counterclockwise until halfshaft is free in rear hub. 

[FIGURE: F5189F.gif]

 CAUTION: Failure to mark the position will cause bushing wind up during assembly 
and can result in incorrect ride height. These conditions can cause 
misalignment and premature tire wear. 

Using a paint marker, mark the position of the rear suspension arm and 
bushing in relation to the rear wheel knuckle with the bushings in relaxed 
position. 

[FIGURE: F5190B.gif]

If rear wheel knuckle is to be replaced, note approximate angle of rear 
wheel knuckle in relaxed position by measuring distance from upper bushing to 
any convenient point on the vehicle body. 

 NOTE: When upper rear suspension arm and bushing bolt is removed from rear 
wheel knuckle, the lower arm bushings will return to the relaxed position. 

Remove nuts and bolts retaining rear suspension arm and bushing to rear 
wheel knuckle.

Remove rear wheel knuckle from halfshaft. 

[FIGURE: F5193B.gif]

 Installation 

Place rear wheel knuckle and rear hub on the halfshaft splines and 
install the lower arm-to-knuckle bolts and nuts. Position rear wheel knuckle 
so index marks on bushing (marked during removal) line up with marks on lower 
rear suspension arm and bushing. If a new rear wheel knuckle is being 
installed, set rear wheel knuckle at the approximate angle noted during 
removal before tightening bolts. 

Push rear wheel knuckle and rear hub firmly onto halfshaft. 

Install upper rear suspension arm and bushing-to-rearwheel knuckle bolt 
and nut and tighten nut to 149-201 Nm (110-148 lb-ft). 

 CAUTION: A new rear axle wheel hub retainer must be installed. Do not reuse old 
rear axle wheel hub retainer. Its torque holding and retention capability is 
greatly diminished during removal. 

Manually thread new rear axle wheel hub retainer onto halfshaft. Use a 
torque wrench to tighten to 115-142 Nm (85-104 lb-ft). Finish 
tightening to final torque in Step 17. 

[FIGURE: F5191D.gif]

Position rear wheel disc brake shield (disc brakes only) to rear wheel 
knuckle and install three retaining bolts. Tighten bolts to 30-50 Nm
 (23-36 lb-ft). Position rear brake backing plate (2212) 
(drum brakes only) to rear wheel knuckle and install four retaining bolts. 
Tighten bolts to 59-80 Nm (44-59 lb-ft). 

Attach parking brake rear cable and conduit to rear wheel cylinder 
(disc brakes). 

Install parking brake rear cable and conduit (drum brakes). 

Install rear disc brake rotor or brake drum. 

Install two new push on nuts to keep rear disc brake rotor or brake 
drum correctly oriented during assembly.

[FIGURE: F5192C.gif]

Install rear disc brake caliper assembly over rear disc brake rotor 
with the outer brake shoe and lining (2001) against disc brake rotor braking 
surface. This prevents pinching the piston boot between the inner brake shoe 
and lining and piston (disc brakes only). Refer to Section 06-04 . 

Install disc brake caliper locating pins (disc brakes) and tighten to 
98-132 Nm (73-97 lb-ft). 

Install parking brake rear cable and conduit on rear disc brake caliper 
(disc brakes). 

[FIGURE: AF0037A.gif]

Install brake cable adjustment clip. Refer to Section 06-05 . 

On drum brakes, bleed brakes. Refer to Section 06-06 . 

Install wheel and tire assembly. 

Lower vehicle and set parking brake. 

Using a torque wrench, tighten rear axle wheel hub retainer to 255-345 Nm
 (188-254 lb-ft).

Install wheel cover.

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Bearing 

The rear wheel bearings (1225) are of a cartridge design and are 
pregreased, sealed and require no scheduled maintenance. The rear wheel 
bearings are preset and cannot be adjusted. If a bearing is disassembled for 
any reason, it must be replaced as a unit. No individual service seals, 
rollers or races are available. The rear axle wheel hub retainer (4B477) nut 
torque of 255-345 Nm (188-254 lb-ft) restricts rear wheel 
bearing/wheel hub relative movement and maintains axial position of the rear 
hub (1109). Due to the importance of the wheel hub nut torque/tension 
relationship, take the following precautions during service: 

Since the rear wheel bearing cannot be adjusted, the rear axle wheel 
hub retainer must not be backed off after reaching the required torque of 
255-345 Nm (188-254 lb-ft) during installation. 

The rear axle wheel hub retainer and washer assembly must be replaced 
with a new rear axle wheel hub retainer and washer assembly whenever the rear 
axle wheel hub retainer is backed off or removed. Never reuse the rear axle 
wheel hub retainer. 

Power tools must not be used to tighten the rear axle wheel hub 
retainer or rear wheel bearing damage will result. Use a torque wrench.

The rear hub and rear wheel drive shaft and joint splines have an 
interference fit requiring special tools for disassembly. The rear axle wheel 
hub retainer can be used to accomplish assembly. 

To remove the rear axle wheel hub retainer, apply sufficient torque to 
the rear axle wheel hub retainer to overcome the prevailing torque feature of 
the rear axle wheel hub retainer.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheel and Tire Assemblies

The factory installed tires and wheels (1007) are designed to operate 
satisfactorily with loads up to and including the full rated load capacity 
when inflated to the recommended inflation pressures. 

Correct tire pressures and driving techniques have an important 
influence on tire life. 

Heavy cornering, rapid acceleration and sharp braking increase tire 
wear.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Tires 

 WARNING: DO NOT MIX DIFFERENT TYPES OF TIRES ON THE SAME VEHICLE, SUCH AS 
RADIAL, BIAS AND BIAS-BELTED TIRES EXCEPT IN EMERGENCIES (TEMPORARY SPARE 
USAGE) BECAUSE VEHICLE HANDLING MAY BE SERIOUSLY AFFECTED AND MAY RESULT IN 
LOSS OF CONTROL. 

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to vehicle, do not use tire chains on vehicles 
equipped with P225/60R16-97V tires. 

When replacing tires, only tires of the size, speed rating, load range 
and construction type originally installed on the vehicle are recommended. Use 
of any other tire size or type may seriously affect the following:

ride 

handling 

speedometer/odometer calibration 

vehicle ground clearance 

tire clearance to the body and chassis 

Consider the following when replacing tires: 

To achieve best all around vehicle performance, tires of different 
construction should not be mixed on the same vehicle. 

It is recommended new tires be installed in pairs on the same axle. 

When replacing only one tire, it should be paired with the tire having 
the most tread to equalize braking traction. 

Snow tires should be of a size and type equivalent to other tires on 
the vehicle as recommended on the tire decal.

Lug Nuts 

 NOTE: Aluminum wheels (1007) and several steel wheels must use special

All vehicles have metric (M-12) lug nuts. Replacement lug nuts must be

the word METRIC stamped on the top of the lug nut. 

[FIGURE: F7808A.gif]

 Anti-Theft 

Aluminum wheels are equipped with anti-theft lug nuts (one per wheel) 
installed during vehicle pre-delivery.

The key is attached to the wheel lug nut wrench stowed with the spare 
tire.

To allow vehicle service in the event the customer's key has been 
misplaced, a Rotunda Master Service Tool Set 164-R3104 or equivalent is 
available at most Ford and Lincoln/Mercury dealer service departments. The 
lock manufacturer can be contacted at 1-800-669-8788 if a master key set is 
not available.

The key has a circular keyway that is matched to the female slot in the 
anti-theft lug nut.

Remove or install the anti-theft lug nut as follows:

 CAUTION: Make sure the key is held square to thelug nuts. If the key is on an 
angle, it may damage the key and the anti-theft lug nuts. DO NOT use a power 
impact wrench on the wheel hub bolt nut key. 

Insert the key into the slot of the lug nut.

Place the wheel lug nut wrench on the key.

While applying pressure on the key, remove or install the lug nut.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

To maximize tire performance, inspect the tires for signs of improper 
inflation and uneven wear which may indicate a need for balancing, rotation or 
front suspension alignment. 

Tires should also be checked frequently for cuts, stone bruises, 
abrasions, blisters and for objects that may have become embedded in the 
tread. More frequent inspections are recommended when rapid or extreme 
temperature changes occur or where road surfaces are rough or occasionally 
littered with debris. 

As a further visible check of tire condition, tread wear indicators are 
moulded into the bottom of the tread grooves. The tire should be replaced when 
these indicator bands become visible. 

 Road Test 

 NOTE: A complete road test procedure is provided in Section 00-04 . 

A tire vibration diagnostic procedure always begins with a road test. 
The road test and customer interview (if available) will provide much of the 
information needed to find the source of a vibration. 

During the road test, drive the vehicle on a road that is smooth and 
free of undulations. If vibration is apparent, note and record the following: 

the speed at which the vibration occurs 

what type of vibration occurs in each speed range � 
mechanical or audible 

how the vibration is affected by changes in vehicle speed, engine 
speed, and engine torque 

type of vibration � sensitivity: torque sensitive, 
vehicle speed sensitive, or engine speed sensitive 

The following explanations help isolate the source of the vibration. 

 Torque Sensitive 

The condition can be improved or made worse by accelerating, 
decelerating, coasting, maintaining a steady vehicle speed or applying engine 
torque.

 Vehicle Speed Sensitive 

The vibration always occurs at the same vehicle speed and is not 
affected by engine torque, engine speed or the transmission gear selected.

 Engine Speed Sensitive 

The vibration occurs at varying vehicle speeds when a different 
transmission gear is selected. It can sometimes be isolated by increasing or 
decreasing engine speed with the transmission in NEUTRAL or by stall testing 
with the transmission in gear. If the condition is engine-speed sensitive, the 
cause is probably not related to the tires. 

If the road test indicates that there is tire whine, but no shake or 
vibration, the noise originates with the contact between the tire and the road 
surface. 

A thumping noise usually means the tire is flat or has soft spots that 
make a noise as they contact the roadway. Tire whine can be distinguished from 
axle noise. Axle noise diminishes or changes according to load or speed. Tire 
whine remains the same over a range of speeds. 

 CAUTION: Be sure to deflate tires to their proper pressures after this check is 
completed. Over-inflated tires will adversely affect vehicle handling. 

To verify that the tire noise is not associated with shake or 
vibration, inflate the tires one at a time to 345 kPa (50 psi) and check for a 
change in the sound.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel and Tire 

 WARNING: NEVER RUN THE ENGINE WITH ONE WHEEL OFF THE GROUND, SUCH AS WHEN 
CHANGING A TIRE. THE WHEEL STILL ON THE GROUND COULD CAUSE THE VEHICLE TO 
MOVE. 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Do not use heat to loosen a frozen wheel because heat can shorten the 
life of the wheel and damage the wheel bearings. 

Remove wheel cover applique (1137). Loosen, but do not remove, lug nuts 
(1012). 

 CAUTION: To prevent damage, never use differential carries as a lift point. 

Raise vehicle until the tire clears the floor.

Remove lug nuts. Pull the wheel (1007) off the hub. 

If corrosion has formed around the center pilot hole so the wheel 
cannot be removed by hand, use a wheel puller to remove the frozen wheel. 

 Installation 

Clean all dirt and corrosion from the hub mounting surface and center 
pilot hole of the wheel. Apply a thin film of Disc Brake Caliper Slide Grease 
D7AZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C172-A to the 
pilot flange to reduce corrosion. 

Place wheel on the rear hub (1109). Install lug nuts. Tighten them 
alternately to draw the wheel evenly against the hub. Install wheel cover 
applique.

Lower vehicle. Tighten the lug nuts to 115-142 Nm 
(85-104 lb-ft). 

Lower vehicle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Covers

 NOTE: A Phillips-head screwdriver is required for the installation of the 
wheel cover. However, the wheel (1007) may be removed from the vehicle without 
removing the wheel cover (1130). Only the wheel cover applique (1137) of the 
wheel cover needs to be removed. 

 Removal 

Pry the center wheel cover applique from the wheel cover using the 
wheel lug wrench provided with the vehicle. 

The wheel, with the wheel cover still attached, may now be removed from 
the vehicle by removing the five lug nuts (1012). 

If the tire needs to be removed from the wheel, first remove the five 
screws, using a Phillips-head screwdriver, and pull the wheel cover off of the 
wheel. 

 Installation 

Insert wheel ornament screw anchors (1A100) provided into the square 
slots on the wheel. 

Align the valve hole in the wheel cover with the valve stem and install 
the wheel cover into the wheel. 

Align the holes in the wheel cover mounting pads with the center holes 
in the wheel ornament screw anchor.

 NOTE: Do not use power tools for wheel cover installation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Replacement 

Wheels (1007)must be replaced when they are bent, dented, heavily 
rusted, have air leaks (aluminum wheels can, in most cases, be serviced using 
the procedure under Cleaning and Inspection) or elongated wheel lug bolt holes 
or have excessive lateral or radial runout. Wheels with a lateral or radial 
runout greater than the recommended specification may cause an objectionable, 
high-speed vehicle vibration.

Replacement wheels must be equal to the original equipment wheels in 
load capacity, diameter, width, offset and mounting configuration. An improper 
wheel may affect wheel bearing life, ground and tire clearance or speedometer 
and odometer calibrations.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Wheels

Inspect the lug nuts (1012)and tighten to 115-142 Nm 
(85-104 lb-ft). Loose lug nutscan cause shimmy and vibration and may also 
distort the stud holes in the wheels (1007). 

Make sure wheelsand hub are clean. Stones wedged between the wheeland 
rotor or rear drum or lumps of mud and grease can unbalance the wheel. 

Check for wheel damage. Wobble or shimmy caused by a damaged wheelwill 
eventually damage the bearings. Inspect the rims for dents that could leak 
air. 

Inspect the front wheel hub (1104)and front wheel bearings whenever the 
wheel hubsare removed or at regular inspection intervals. 

 Steel 

Rim bead seats (steel wheels only) should be cleaned with a wire brush 
or coarse steel wool to remove lubricants, old rubber and light rust. 

 Aluminum 

 CAUTION: Do not use steel wool, abrasive-type cleaner or strong detergents 
containing highly alkaline or caustic agents as damage to the protective 
coating and discoloration may result. 

 NOTE: Automatic car wash tire brushes may damage aluminum and styled road 
wheel protective coatings. Before using such a service, be sure abrasive-type 
brushes are not being used.

Aluminum wheel rim bead seats should be cleaned with a non-abrasive 
cleaner to remove tire mounting lubricants and old rubber. Before mounting or 
dismounting a tire, the bead area should be well lubricated with a rubber 
lubricant meeting Ford specification ESR-M99B135-A. 

 Mounting Area 

Corrosion buildup can result in wheels sticking to the axle or rotor 
flange after extensive service. To prevent this from recurring once the wheels 
are removed, use the following procedure: 

Clean the axle/rotor flange and wheel bore of corrosion with a wire 
brush, steel wool or other suitable material. 

Coat wheel bore with Disc Brake Caliper Slide Grease D7AZ-19590-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C172-A. Do not apply grease to 
wheel hub bolt nut seats or wheel studs. 

Install wheel on vehicle and tighten lug nuts to 115-142 Nm
 (85-104 lb-ft).

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Leaks 

Wheel services that use welding or peening are not approved. An inner 
tube is not an acceptable service for leaky wheels or tires.

If the air pressure in an aluminum wheel (1007) is found to be low, the 
following procedure should be performed before considering wheel replacement.

Remove the tire and wheel assembly and inspect the wheel for structural 
damage. If none exists, go to Step 2. If the wheel is damaged, replacewheel.

With the tire mounted on the wheel, locate the air leak using a water 
bath or equivalent method and mark the location. Check the complete wheel for 
possible additional leaks. When leaks are marked, dismount the tire marking 
the valve location on the tire for proper indexing. 

On the tire side of the wheel, thoroughly clean the leaking area with 
Professional Choke and Linkage Cleaner E8AZ-19A501-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESR-M14P10-A or use sandpaper of approximately 80-grit to 
remove all contamination. Using the sandpaper, score the surface of the wheel 
to improve adhesion of the sealer. Adequate area around the leak should be 
prepared to make sure of covering the leak. If the valve stem is close to the 
area, remove it. 

Use a clean cloth to remove all cleaner or sanding dust. 

 NOTE: Do not use a torch containing oxyacetylene. 

Heat the prepared area with Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent or 
propane torch until Aluminum Wheel Repair Compound E7AZ-19544-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M4G280-A flows. Apply the hot melt material 
over the prepared area using a liberal flow and wiping action to ensure 
coverage of the leaking area. Service is most effective when heat is applied 
to the brake side of the rim and sealer is melted by heat in the metal. 

 Tire Side of Wheel 

[FIGURE: F4854G.gif]

 Brake Side of Wheel 

[FIGURE: F4855H.gif]

Apply only enough heat to melt the sealer and then remove heat source. 
After servicing the leak, allow the wheel to cool until it can be handled 
safely. 

 CAUTION: Use caution when mounting the tire so as not to damage the sealer. 

Index and assemble tire and wheel. Inflate tire to the recommended 
pressure as indicated on the tire pressure decal. 

Repeat Step 2 to verify service. 

When the service is completed, balance the assembly and install on 
vehicle.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Straightening Wheels, Rims or Components

Do not heat wheels (1007) in an attempt to soften them for 
straightening to repair damage from striking curbs, etc. The special alloy 
used in these wheels is heat-treated, and uncontrolled heating from welding 
affects the properties of the material. Do not weld the wheels for any reason.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Maintenance and Protection in Corrosive Environments 

Aluminum wheels (1007) have a protective coating to resist corrosion. 
Care should be taken to avoid damaging the wheel or corrosion may occur. 
Washing them (do not use highly alkaline cleaning agents) when washing the 
rest of the vehicle will be enough to keep wheels looking good for many years. 
Certain environments, as created by some operations, can lead to corrosion. 
Some of these are salt, chloride compounds used for snow removal, dust control 
and highly alkaline materials. When these conditions are encountered, the 
following practice is recommended: 

Clean frequently with steam or high-pressure water from a hose. Use of 
a mild detergent will speed up the cleaning process. 

When tires are removed, the entire wheel should be cleaned and 
inspected. For maximum protection, there are various types of coatings which 
give good results. The following procedure is suggested: 

 Surface Preparation 

Remove all the soil and oil from the wheel surface with either 
high-pressure steam or solvent. A suitable solvent would be mineral spirits. 

Remove any adherent soil or oxidation products by using a soft bristle 
brush. 

Clean the surface again with solvent, using mineral spirits to remove 
loose products.

PAGE 2364
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 04-04: Wheels and Tires

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Wheel Maintenance 

 During Tire Inspection 

Check all metal surfaces thoroughly while making tire inspections, 
including areas on inboard side of wheel (1007). Watch for: 

excessive rust or corrosion build-up.

cracks in metal.

bent flanges, resulting from road obstructions.

loose, missing or damaged lug nuts (1012).

bent or stripped lug bolts (1107).

 WARNING: EXCESSIVELY CORRODED OR CRACKED WHEELS CAN BE DANGEROUS. DEFLATE TIRES 
PRIOR TO REMOVAL FROM THE WHEELS. 

Remove damaged rims or wheels. 

Mark damaged or hazardous areas with chalk so that part will be removed 
from service. 

Coat wheel pilot area with Disc Brake Caliper Slide Grease D7AZ-19590-A 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C172-A. Do not apply grease to 
Lug nut seats or lug bolts.

Replace parts as required. 

Inflate tires only to recommended air pressures. 

Check the lug nut torque and retighten the lug nuts as described.

 During Tire Changes 

 WARNING: ALLOYS OR METAL SURFACES WITH CRACKS ARE VERY DANGEROUS. THESE 
COMPONENTS COULD FAIL WITHOUT WARNING DURING INFLATION OR LATER ON THE VEHICLE 
CAUSING LOSS OF CONTROL OR PERSONAL INJURY. DESTROY ALL PARTS THAT ARE 
CRACKED. 

 WARNING: AFTERMARKET AEROSOL TIRE SEALANTS ARE EXTREMELY FLAMMABLE. ALWAYS 
QUESTION CUSTOMER TO MAKE SURE THESE PRODUCTS HAVE NOT BEEN USED. 

 WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT REPLACEMENTS ARE MADE WITH THE PROPER SIZES AND TYPES OF 
WHEELS. FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH THIS WARNING MAY RESULT IN EQUIPMENT FAILURE 
AND POSSIBLE INJURY. 

Check all metal surfaces. Watch particularly for the following items: 

cracks in the rim bead seat or drop well radii areas; these are caused 
by deep rim tool marks, overloading and overinflating tires or using larger 
than recommended tire sizes. 

cracks in the wheel disc, between the stud holes or hand holes; these 
are caused by loose lug nuts, improper installation procedures or the use of 
incorrect sizes or types of attaching parts. 

Replace the parts as necessary. 

Thoroughly remove rust, dirt and other foreign materials from all 
surfaces. Hand or electric wire brushes, sand blasting or chemical baths may 
be used. Bead seat areas of rim should be free of rust and rubber deposits. 
This is especially important for drop-center tubeless rims because the bead 
seat is the air-sealing element. 

Paint rim by brush or spray with a fast-drying metal primer. Surfaces 
should be clean and dry prior to painting. Make sure bare metal areas on the 
outside or tire side of rim are covered. This is especially important on 
drop-center tubeless rims because warm and sometimes moist air is in constant 
contact with the metal surface on the tire side of the rim. 

 NOTE: Avoid the use of any lubricant which contains water or solvent that is 
injurious to rubber such as WD40. A combination lubricant and rust-preventive 
compound is preferable such as a rubber lubricant meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1B6-A. This protective measure is of particular importance with 
drop-center tubeless rims as the air in the tire is contained by the tire-side 
rim surface. 

Lubricate the tire side of the rim base just prior to mounting tire. 

 CAUTION: When mounting a tire on a wheel, do not inflate to more than 276 kPa 
(40 psi); then deflate tire. 

 NOTE: If the tire is to be reinstalled on the same wheel, mark the tire and 
wheel so they can be reassembled in the same position. 

Inflate tire to recommended air pressure.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Tire Inflation 

 WARNING: OVER- OR UNDER-INFLATED TIRES CAN REDUCE TIRE LIFE, ADVERSELY AFFECT 
VEHICLE HANDLING AND POSSIBLY LEAD TO A SUDDEN FAILURE THAT COULD RESULT IN 
THE LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL WITHOUT WARNING. 

The tire inflation pressure is carefully calculated to give the vehicle 
satisfactory ride and steering characteristics without compromising long tire 
tread life. 

A tire chart (refer to Owner Guide for location on vehicle) gives the 
recommended cold tire inflation pressure. The cold tire inflation pressure can 
be measured after the vehicle has been parked for three hours or has been 
driven less than 5 km (3 miles). 

A higher tire inflation pressure than the recommended pressure can 
cause a hard ride, tire bruising, carcass damage and rapid wear at the center 
of the tire. Low tire pressure can produce tire squeal, hard steering, rim 
dents, high temperatures and rapid wear on the outer edges of the tires. 
Unequal inflation pressures in tires using the same axle can cause uneven 
braking and reduce handling.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Tire Rotation 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE TEMPORARY SPARE FOR ROTATION OR AS A REGULAR TIRE. THE 
TEMPORARY SPARE IS PROVIDED FOR TEMPORARY USE ONLY. ANY CONTINUED ROAD USE OF 
THE TEMPORARY SPARE MAY RESULT IN TIRE FAILURE, LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL AND 
POSSIBLE INJURY TO VEHICLE OCCUPANTS. 

If unusual or uneven tire wear is observed, determine the cause and 
correct the condition before rotating tire.

To equalize tire wear, tires may be rotated, but not until the cause of 
unusual or uneven tire wear is determined and corrected. 

If abnormal wear is detected, find and correct the cause and rotate the 
tires following the diagram to allow for more even wear. 

Rotate the LH rear tire to the RH front position and the RH rear to the 
LH front position. Rotate the LH front to the LH rear and RH front to the RH 
rear position.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Wheel and Tire Indexing 

When servicing wheels (1007) or tires, the following procedure for 
matching the tire and wheel must be followed to make sure that the best 
possible ride characteristics are maintained: 

When removing a worn tire from a wheel, mark the valve location on the 
tire prior to removal. 

If the original tire is to be remounted, index the valve mark on the 
tire to the valve of the original wheel. Go to Step 6. 

If a new wheel is being installed, locate the tire matching point based 
on the valve position on the original wheel relative to its matching point 
described in Step 3. 

Locate the matching point on the wheel. 

Steel wheels: There is either a chartreuse or red sticker on the 
outside rim flange or, if the sticker is missing, there will be a yellow paint 
mark in the dropwell of the tire side rim that must be re-marked to the 
outside rim flange. 

Aluminum Wheels: The matching point is at the valve stem.

Locating the matching point on a new tire: 

Many replacement tires as well as original equipment tires are marked 
for first harmonic matching to the wheel. These marks vary in type and color. 
Consult the tire dealer for details on mark identification. 

Mount the tire on the wheel and line up the chartreuse paint mark or 
sticker on the new tire sidewall or the matching point of the original tire 
with the mark on the rim of the steel wheel or the tire valve of the aluminum 
wheel. 

Inflate and balance the tire/wheel assembly.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Safety Precautions 

 WARNING: NEVER RUN THE ENGINE WITH ONE WHEEL OFF THE GROUND SUCH AS WHEN 
CHANGING A TIRE. THE WHEEL STILL ON THE GROUND COULD CAUSE THE VEHICLE TO 
MOVE. 

Follow the safety procedures described in this manual and obtain safety 
literature from the wheel and rim manufacturer, NHTSA and OSHA. If you have 
any questions, consult the distributor or manufacturer directly. 

Always remember the weakest weight-carrying component of the vehicle 
such as tire, wheel (1007), axle or bearings determines its overall maximum 
and safe load carrying capacity for the vehicle. The load-carrying 
requirements of each vehicle should also be determined before selecting the 
proper tire/wheel combination. 

When replacing tires, use the same size, load range and construction 
type (radial) as originally installed on the vehicle or a type that meets Ford 
specification for the vehicle. 

 NOTE: Use of improper replacement wheels and tires may adversely affect ride, 
handling, load carrying capacity, wheel bearing life, tire clearance to body 
and chassis components, vehicle ground clearance, vehicle width and brake 
cooling. 

When replacing wheels, use original equipment manufacturer's wheels or 
equivalent available from your Ford dealer with equivalent capacity, width, 
offset and mounting configuration as those originally installed on your 
vehicle. 

Inspect and replace damaged or corroded parts. Abuse during road 
operations or in mounting tires can cause damage that may weaken the parts. 
Parts that are excessively corroded are weakened. Always inspect for and 
replace damaged or heavily rusted parts.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Axle Identification Tag 

The plant code on the axle identification tag is the official service 
identifier. 

The axle identification tag is located under the cover-to-carrier bolt 
in the 12 o'clock position. 

The plant code for a particular axle assembly will not be duplicated. 

The plant code will not change as long as that particular axle assembly 
never undergoes an external design change. 

[FIGURE: AE0141A.gif]

If, however, an internal design change takes place in the same axle 
during the production life of the axle and that internal change affects 
interchangeability of service parts, a dash and numerical suffix will be added 
to the plant code. 

The vehicle certification label is located on the LH front door lock 
panel or door pillar. The vehicle certification label contains the axle 
identification code in the lower RH corner.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Driveshaft

 NOTE: All driveshafts (4602) are balanced. If the vehicle is to be 
undercoated, cover the driveshaft, universal joints (4635) and driveshaft 
centering socket yoke (4782) to prevent application of any undercoating 
material.

The driveshaft is a tubular shaft used to transfer engine torque from 
the transmission output shaft (7060) to the differential in the rear axle 
housing (4010), which in turn transmits torque through the halfshafts to the 
drive wheels.

The driveshaft assembly consists of the following components: 

two single Cardan universal joints 

a driveshaft slip yoke (4841) 

welded aluminum tube assembly 

driveshaft centering socket yoke

The driveshaft slip yoke permits the driveshaft to move forward and 
rearward on the transmission output shaft during drivetrain movement and 
during driveshaft removal and installation.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Driving Axle 

The rear drive axle operates as follows:

It receives power from the engine through the transmission and 
driveshaft (4602). 

The pinion gear rotates the differential case (4204) through engagement 
with the ring gear which is bolted to the differential case outer flange. 

Inside the differential case, two differential pinion gears (4215) are 
mounted on the differential pinion shaft (4211) which is pinned to the 
differential case. 

These differential pinion gears are engaged with the differential side 
gears (4236) to which the halfshafts are splined. 

The differential case then turns and rotates the halfshafts and rear 
wheels. 

When it is necessary for one wheel and halfshaft to rotate faster than 
the other, the faster-turning differential side gear causes the differential 
pinion gears to roll on the slower-turning differential side gear to allow 
differential action between the two halfshafts.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Anti-Lock

 4-Wheel 

Thunderbird and Cougar vehicles have a four-wheel anti-lock brake 
system (ABS) and traction control as an option.

The system prevents wheel lockup by automatically modulating the brake 
pressure during an emergency stop.

By not locking the wheels, the driver can maintain steering control and 
stop the vehicle in the shortest possible distance under most conditions.

The brake pedal force required to engage the ABS function may vary with 
the road surface conditions:

A dry surface requires a higher force while a slippery surface 
requires much less force.

During the ABS operation, the driver will sense a pulsation in the 
brake pedal (2455) accompanied by a slight up and down movement in the pedal 
height and a clicking sound.

The pedal effort and pedal feel during normal braking are similar to 
that of a conventional power brake system.

The rear brake anti-lock sensor indicator (2C189) is attached to the 
inner CV joint. Refer to Section 05-05 .
