DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Axle and Driveshaft

 Inspection and Verification 

Certain rear axle and driveline concerns are also common to the engine, 
transmission, wheel bearings, tires and other parts of the vehicle. For this 
reason, make sure the cause of the trouble is in the rear axle before 
adjusting, servicing or replacing any of the parts.

Rear axle concerns can be diagnosed and corrected quickly by following 
the proper procedures. Being able to perform a good diagnosis is necessary to 
eliminate guesswork and save time. 

The diagnostic material also deals with symptom analysis which aids the 
technician in discovering the original cause of a concern so repeat service 
can be avoided. However, the purpose of this section is to provide information 
on service steps of special importance. 

This section defines various possible rear axle conditions and tests 
for identifying the cause and the service procedure. The four rear axle 
conditions that will be reviewed are: 

Leakage conditions: 

rear axle drive pinion seal (4676)

pinion nut

differential seals

casting porosity 

rear axle housing vent (4022)

Vibration conditions: 

tires

driveline angle 

drive pinion stem and rear axle universal joint flange (4851)

wheel flange runout

Noise conditions: 

non-axle noise

axle noise

gear noise

chuckle

knock

clunk 

bearing noise 

chatter on corners

click at engagement

axle shaft noise

bearing rumble

Inoperative conditions: 

broken pinion stem

axle lockup

 U-Joint Inspection 

Remove driveshaft (4602). Refer to Section 05-01 .

Manipulate universal joint (4635) in each direction of rotation. If 
U-joint feels stiff or has a lumpy or gritty feel in any direction, replace 
universal joint. Refer to Section 05-01 .

 Noise Acceptability 

A gear-driven unit, especially an automotive axle, will produce a 
certain amount of noise. Some noise is acceptable and may be audible at 
certain speeds or under various driving conditions such as a newly paved 
blacktop road. The slight noise is not detrimental to operation of the axle 
and must be considered normal. 

With the Traction-Lok® limited-slip differential, 
slight chatter noise on slow turns after extended highway driving is 
acceptable and has no detrimental effect on the locking-axle function. 

 Preliminary Diagnosis 

 Question the Customer 

The preliminary diagnosis begins with the service technician asking the 
customer enough diagnostic questions, especially for conditions of noisy 
operation or vibration. 

Always ask the customer about: 

The exact nature of the symptom. If it is a vibration, how is it felt? 
If a noise, what kind? Is it high-pitched, a rumbling noise or some other 
concern? 

The driving conditions in which the symptoms occur; road speed, drive 
or coast, on turns, or on a grade only. 

Whether the condition is constant or variable. Does a noise increase in 
pitch with speed or some other factor? 

All information should be written on the service order so the 
technician will know where to start looking. The technician must be able to 
identify the concern from what is written on the order following the road 
test. 

Have the customer demonstrate the symptoms on a road test whenever 
possible. 

 Axle Diagnosis Check Sheet 

If there is enough reason to suspect an axle concern, the service 
technician should also initiate a Customer Concern Evaluation.

Record all the information related to the concern in order to diagnose 
it accurately and quickly. 

[FIGURE: AF0145A.gif]

 Road Test 

A road test is mandatory for any noise or vibration not eliminated by 
the on-hoist check of chassis components. The Customer Concern Evaluation is 
arranged to record the conditions that may be heard or felt during this test. 

The Customer Concern Evaluation lists four operating conditions or 
modes in which some axle noises come and go.

To perform a good diagnostic check, it is important to operate the 
vehicle in all modes and check off those in which the noise occurs. The modes 
are defined in the preceding chart. Write down the speed range at which both 
noise and vibration occur. On vehicles equipped with overdrive transmissions, 
evaluate rear axle noise with the transmission in DIRECT DRIVE, not in 
OVERDRIVE. Transmission noise can be mistaken for rear axle noise when in 
OVERDRIVE. 

 Analysis of Leakage 

Most rear axle leakage conditions can be corrected without a teardown. 
However, it is important to clean the leaking area enough to identify the 
exact source. 

A plugged or siezed rear axle housing vent will cause excessive flange 
yoke seal lip wear due to internal pressure buildup. When a leak occurs, check 
vent and vent tube for debris. Clean or replace as required.

Make sure the axle lubricant is just below bottom of fill hole.

 Flange Yoke Seal 

When the rear axle drive pinion seal leaks, it may be that it was not 
installed properly, or because of rough texture or damage on the seal journal 
surface. 

Any damage to the seal bore (dings, dents, gouges or other 
imperfections) will distort the seal casing and allow leakage past the outer 
edge of the rear axle drive pinion seal.

The rear axle drive pinion seal can be torn, cut or gouged if it is not 
installed carefully with the correct service tool. The spring that holds the 
rear axle drive pinion seal against the rear axle universal joint flange may 
be knocked out and allow leakage past the lip. 

The rubber lips can occasionally become hard (like plastic) with cracks 
at the oil lip contact point. The contact point on the rear axle universal 
joint flange is usually black, indicating excessive heat. Marks, nicks, gouges 
or rough surface texture on the seal journal of the rear axle universal joint 
flange will also cause leaks. Excessive seal lip wear will be noted. The rear 
axle universal joint flange should be replaced if any of these conditions 
exist. 

Metal chips or sand trapped at the sealing lip may also cause oil 
leaks. This can cause a wear groove on the rear axle universal joint flange 
and heavy seal lip wear. 

[FIGURE: E5517F.gif]

 Drive Pinion Nut 

 CAUTION: Removing the pinion nut disturbs pinion bearing preload. Refer to 
 Section 05-02A for 7.5 inch ring gear or Section 05-02B for 8.8 inch ring gear 
for removal and installation of pinion nut before performing this procedure. 

 NOTE: Be sure to follow the correct procedure for setting the bearing preload 
when the nut is installed. 

On some high-mileage units, oil may leak past the threads of the pinion 
nut. Correct the condition by installing a new nut or removing the nut and 
applying Pipe Sealant With Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G350-A2 on the threads and nut 
face. 

 Differential Seals 

Inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seals (4B416) are 
susceptible to the same kinds of damage as rear axle drive pinion seals if 
improperly installed. The seal bore must be clean and the lip handled 
carefully to avoid cutting or tearing it. Seal journal surface must be free of 
nicks, gouges and rough surface texture. 

 Casting Porosity (Holes in Casting) 

There may be a rear axle housing leak through small pockets in the 
metal. These pockets (casting leakage) are caused by gas bubbles in the 
casting process, known technically as a porous condition or porosity. 

Because there is a concern of changing the axle's NVH characteristics 
if disassembled to replace the differential case (4204), service is 
preferable. Seal the porous pocket with Devcon Aluminum Liquid F2 meeting Ford 
specification M3D35-A(E). 

[FIGURE: E6732B.gif]

 Axle Vent 

 NOTE: If rear axle housing vent cannot be cleared, it must be replaced. 

A plugged rear axle housing vent will cause excessive seal lip wear due 
to internal pressure buildup. When a leak occurs, check the rear axle housing 
vent which is located near the top of the differential housing. Make sure the 
vent hose is not kinked. Remove the vent hose from the vent nipple and make 
sure the hose is clear of dirt or other foreign materials. While hose is 
removed, pass a length of wire or small diameter Allen wrench in and out of 
the vent nipple to clean it of any dirt or foreign materials. Install vent 
hose. 

Make sure axle lubricant is level with bottom of fill hole. 

 Analysis of Vibration 

Few vibration conditions are caused by the axle. On a vibration 
concern, follow the diagnosis procedure in Section 00-04 unless there is a 
good reason to suspect the axle. 

Most vibrations in the rear end are caused by tires. 

 Traction-Lok® Differential 

 WARNING: NEVER RUN THE ENGINE WITH ONE WHEEL OFF THE GROUND. A VEHICLE EQUIPPED 
WITH A TRACTION-LOK® DIFFERENTIAL WILL ALWAYS HAVE BOTH 
WHEELS DRIVING. IF, WHILE THE VEHICLE IS BEING SERVICED, ONLY ONE WHEEL IS 
RAISED OFF THE FLOOR AND THE REAR AXLE IS DRIVEN BY THE ENGINE, THE WHEEL ON 
THE FLOOR COULD DRIVE THE VEHICLE OFF THE STAND OR JACK. BE SURE BOTH REAR 
WHEELS ARE OFF THE FLOOR. 

 Tires 

 WARNING: DO NOT BALANCE THE REAR WHEELS AND TIRES WHILE THEY ARE MOUNTED ON THE 
VEHICLE. POSSIBLE TIRE DISINTEGRATION, DIFFERENTIAL AND/OR HALFSHAFT FAILURE 
COULD RESULT, CAUSING PERSONAL INJURY AND/OR EXTENSIVE COMPONENT DAMAGE. USE 
OFF-VEHICLE WHEEL AND TIRE BALANCER ONLY. 

 CAUTION: Some vehicles are equipped with directional tires (refer to tire 
rotation arrows on tire sidewall). If a directional tire is removed for 
service, it must be remounted in its original location. 

Vibration is a definite concern with modern, high-mileage tires if they 
are not true both radially and laterally. They are more susceptible to 
vibration around the limits of radial and lateral runout of the tire and wheel 
assembly. They also require more accurate balancing. Wheel and tire runout 
checks, truing and balancing are done before looking at the axle. 

Sometimes a vibration concern can be corrected by properly rotating or 
inflating the tires. The best tires should be on the rear to minimize 
vibration. 

 Drive Pinion Stem and Rear Universal Joint Flange 

Rear axle universal joint flange runout should be checked as a 
potential cause of vibration. 

A cause of excessive rear axle universal joint flange runout is 
improper installation of the rear axle drive pinion seal. If the spring on the 
seal lip is dislodged, it will jam up and cock the rear axle universal joint 
flange. The flange should also be indexed before replacing the gearset because 
of flange runout. 

 Wheel Flange Runout 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Clutch Housing Alignment Adapter

T75L-4201-A

Runout of the wheel flange is an infrequent, but possible cause of rear 
end vibration. It is advisable to check the runout of the: 

Pilot (radial), maximum runout 0.15 mm (0.006 inch).

[FIGURE: AE0142A.gif]

Flange face (lateral), maximum runout 0.25 mm (0.010 inch). 

[FIGURE: E9142A.gif]

Bolt circle (radial), maximum runout 0.38 mm (0.015 inch). 

[FIGURE: E9143A.gif]

Refer to Section 00-04 for the checking procedures for wheel/tire 
runout. 

 Axle Noise 

The following is a glossary of axle noise terms:

Gear noise is the typical howling or whining of the ring gear and 
pinion. It can occur at various speeds and driving conditions or it can be 
continuous.

Chuckle is a particular rattling noise that sounds like a stick against 
the spokes of a spinning bicycle wheel. It occurs while decelerating from 64 
km/h (40 mph) and can usually be heard all the way to a stop. The frequency 
varies with the speed of the vehicle.

Knock is very similar to chuckle, though it may be loude

 Ring and Pinion Backlash Check 

This indicates runout conditions that will not show up in other tests. 
Remove the axle housing cover. Refer to Section 05-02A (7.5-inch ring gear) or 
 Section 05-02B (8.8-inch ring gear). Measure ring gear backlash on 30 
consecutive ring gear teeth using Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or 
equivalent. Note the variation between the high and low readings. If over 0.10 
mm (0.004 inch), replace the differential ring gear and pinion as described. 
Install the axle housing cover. 

[FIGURE: F5194C.gif]

 Ring Gear Runout Check 

If the ring gear runout check (before disassembly) exceeds 
specification, the condition may be caused by a warped ring gear, a damaged 
rear axle housing, loss of differential bearing preload or debris between the 
ring gear back face and the case flange. Perform the following steps to 
determine the cause of excessive runout. 

With the pinion removed, place differential case/gear subassembly with 
differential bearings (4221) and differential bearing cups (4222) in rear axle 
housing. 

[FIGURE: E7041B.gif]

Install 6.75 mm (0.265 inch) differential bearing shim (4067) on the LH 
side of subassembly. 

[FIGURE: AE0039A.gif]

Install the LH bearing cap finger-tight. 

[FIGURE: E7043B.gif]

Install progressively larger differential bearing shims on the RH side 
until the largest differential bearing shim selected can be assembled with a 
slight drag feel. 

[FIGURE: AE0143A.gif]

Install the RH side bearing cap. Install bearing cap bolts. Tighten to 
95-115 Nm (70-85 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: AE0228A.gif]

Rotate the assembly to make sure it rotates freely. 

[FIGURE: E7502B.gif]

Install Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent. Check 
and note ring gear runout. 

[FIGURE: E7503D.gif]

If the runout is within specification, the original 
out-of-specification runout was caused by insufficient differential bearing 
preload. If the runout exceeds specification, go to Step 9. 

Remove differential case from the rear axle housing.

[FIGURE: E7041B.gif]

Remove ring gear using a drift that will bottom in ring gear bolt 
holes. Strike at alternate holes around gear. 

[FIGURE: E6262C.gif]

Install differential case assembly in rear axle housing without ring 
gear. 

 NOTE: Ring gear and pinion are matched and must be replaced as a set.

Check differential case runout again. If the runout is now within 
limits, the ring gear was out of specification and the differential ring gear 
and pinion should be replaced. If the runout is still excessive, the 
differential case is damaged and should be replaced.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Inspection After Disassembly of Axle

 WARNING: ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GOGGLES. IF SOLVENT OR COMPRESSED AIR GETS IN EYES, 
SEVERE IRRITATION OR PERMANENT INJURY SUCH AS BLINDNESS COULD OCCUR. SEEK 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

Thoroughly clean all parts. Synthetic seals must not be cleaned, soaked 
or washed in cleaning solvents. Always use clean solvent when cleaning 
bearings. Oil the bearings immediately after cleaning to prevent rusting. 
Inspect the parts for wear or damage. Clean the inside of the carrier before 
assembly. 

When a scored differential ring gear and pinion (4209) is replaced, the 
rear axle housing (4010) should be washed thoroughly and steam-cleaned. This 
can only be done effectively if all seals and bearings have been removed from 
the rear axle housing. Inspect individual parts as follows:

 Gears 

Examine the pinion and ring gear teeth for scoring or excessive wear. 
Worn gears cannot be rebuilt to correct a noisy condition. Gear scoring is the 
result of excessive shock loading or the use of an incorrect lubricant. Scored 
gears cannot be reused. Examine the teeth and thrust surfaces of the 
differential side gears (4236). Wear on the hub of the differential side gear 
can cause a chucking noise known as chuckle when the vehicle is driven at low 
speeds. Wear of splines, thrust surfaces or thrust washers can contribute to 
excessive driveline backlash. 

 Bearing Cups and Cone and Roller Assemblies 

Check bearing cups for rings, scores, galling or excessive wear. Pinion 
cups must be solidly seated. Check for seating by attempting to insert a 0.04 
mm (0.0015 inch) feeler between these cups and the bottoms of their bores. 

When operated in the bearing cups, cone and roller assemblies must turn 
without roughness. Examine the large roller ends for wear. If the original 
blend radius has worn to a sharp edge, the bearing should be replaced. 

If inspection reveals either a worn bearing cup or a worn cone and 
roller assembly, both parts should be replaced to avoid damage.

 Universal Joint Flange, Rear Axle 

Make sure the surfaces of the rear axle universal joint flange (4851) 
have not been damaged in removing the driveshaft (4602) or in removing the 
driveshaft centering socket yoke (4782) from the axle. The end of the rear 
axle universal joint flange that contacts the rear axle drive pinion shaft oil 
slinger (4670), as well as the flat surface of the pinion nut counterbore, 
must be smooth. Polish these surfaces if necessary. Roughness aggravates 
backlash noises and causes wear of the rear axle universal joint flange and 
pinion nut with a loss in pinion bearing preload. 

 Driveshaft Centering Socket Yoke Flange 

Make sure the surfaces of the driveshaft centering socket yoke have not 
been damaged in removing the driveshaft or in removing the driveshaft 
centering socket yoke from the rear axle universal joint flange. The end of the 
driveshaft centering socket yoke that contacts the rear axle universal joint 
flange must be smooth. Polish these surfaces if necessary. 

 Carrier Housing 

Make sure the differential bearing bores are smooth. Remove any nicks 
or burrs from the mounting surfaces of the rear axle housing. 

 Differential Case 

Make sure the differential bearing bores are smooth. Remove any nicks 
or burrs from the mounting surfaces of the differential case (4204).

Make sure that the hubs where the differential bearings (4221) mount 
are smooth. Carefully examine the differential bearing shoulders which may 
have been damaged when the differential bearings were removed. The bearing 
assemblies will fail if they do not seat firmly against the shoulders. Check 
the fit (free rotation) of the differential side gears in their counterbores. 
Make sure that the mating surfaces of the two parts of the case are smooth and 
free of nicks or burrs.

 Traction-Lok® Differential Parts 

 CAUTION: Inspect the clutch plates for uneven or extreme wear. The tanged clutch 
plates must be free from burrs, nicks or scratches which could cause excessive 
or erratic wear to the internally splined clutch plates. The internally 
splined clutch plates should be inspected for condition of the material and 
wear. Replace the plates if their thickness is less than 1.5 mm (0.058 inch) 
or if the material is scored or badly worn. Inspect the plate internal teeth 
for wear. Replace them if excessive wear is evident. 

 Plates should only be replaced as a set. Examine all thrust 
surfaces and hubs for wear. Abnormal wear on these surfaces can contribute to 
axle noise.

ADJUSTMENTS

Driveshaft Runout and Balance

 Driveshaft Balancing 

Vibration or shudder which is noticeable either on fast acceleration, 
when coasting, or when using the engine for braking, may be caused by the rear 
axle housing (4010) being loose on the rear suspension, improper tire balance, 
improper driveline installation or balance. 

If driveshaft components are replaced and shaft vibration is 
encountered after installation, disconnect the driveshaft (4602) and remove the 
driveshaft slip yoke (4841). Rotate the driveshaft slip yoke 180 degrees. Then 
reconnect the driveshaft to the driveshaft slip yoke and reinstall in vehicle. 
If the vibration persists, disconnect the driveshaft at the rear axle 
universal joint flange (4851). Rotate the flange 180 degrees and reconnect the 
driveshaft to the rear axle universal joint flange.

If rotating the driveshaft 180 degrees does not eliminate vibration, 
the shaft may be balanced using the following procedure. 

Raise the vehicle on a hoist.

With the transmission in gear, increase the vehicle speed to maximum 
vibration level. Note and record the speed of this vibration period as a 
baseline speed.

 WARNING: USE CAUTION WHEN CHECKING THE DRIVESHAFT NEAR THE BALANCE WEIGHTS TO 
PREVENT INJURY TO THE HANDS. 

With the transmission in gear, run the vehicle with the driveshaft 
rotating at a speed of 64-80 km/h (40-50 mph). Have an assistant bring a 
crayon, piece of chalk, or colored pencil up until it just barely contacts the 
rear end, center and front end of the driveshaft. The chalk marks will 
indicate the heavy side of the shaft.

[FIGURE: E4238A.gif]

Install two screw-type hose clamps on the driveshaft so that their 
heads are located 180 degrees from the chalk mark, starting at the rear axle 
universal joint flange end of the rear axle universal joint flange. Tighten 
the clamps.

[FIGURE: E4239A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not run the engine on the hoist with the transmission engaged for 
extended periods due to the danger of overheating the engine or transmission. 

Accelerate the vehicle up to the baseline speed. If vibration is still 
evident, rotate the clamps approximately 45 degrees away from each other and 
test for correction of vibration. 

If necessary, continue to rotate the clamps apart in smaller increments 
until the vibration is reduced or eliminated. 

If the vibration is not completely eliminated, repeat the above 
procedure and balance the front end of the driveshaft, checking for 
elimination or reduction of the vibration. 

Remove the vehicle from the hoist and perform a road test.

[FIGURE: E4240A.gif]

 Alternate Procedure 

Road test to evaluate and record road speed at which vibration occurs. 

Raise vehicle on a frame contact hoist. Re-evaluate by starting the 
engine, engaging the transmission and accelerating to the indicated speeds at 
which the vibration was most severe during the road test. Suspending the rear 
axle (4001) makes the driveline more sensitive to vibration. 

Mark one of the driveshaft centering socket yoke mounting bolt holes A, 
and number the rear axle universal joint flange holes 1 through 8, starting 
with the one mating with A. The original position can then be identified as 
A-1. Re-index the shaft 180 degrees to A-5 and road test. If not satisfactory, 
repeat for positions A-3 and A-7 and, if necessary, between the best two of 
the previous four tested until the vibration stops or the best position is 
found.

[FIGURE: AE0144A.gif]

A vehicle is more sensitive to excessive imbalance or runout at the 
rearward end of the driveshaft; therefore, locate the heavy side of the 
driveshaft by using the strobe light and transducer, from Rotunda Electronic 
Strobe Balancer 006-01400 or equivalent as follows. 

Remove rear wheels and tires. 

Reinstall all the lug nuts (1012) in reverse, flat side toward the rear 
disc brake rotor (2C026) to avoid wheel hub bolt imbalance and to prevent rear 
disc brake rotor from dislodging. 

Draw an axial chalk line at any radial location approximately 101.6mm 
(4 inches) long at the rear of the driveshaft. 

[FIGURE: E4241A.gif]

Locate the transducer on the bottom side of the rear axle housing and 
secure it in place. 

[FIGURE: AE0139A.gif]

Run the engine at the worst vibration speed noted and watch the 
position of the chalk line using the strobe light. 

This provides a starting point for the initial location of the clamps. 

Stop the engine and rotate the driveshaft so that the chalk line is in 
the same location as seen under the strobe light. 

Install two stainless steel hose clamps on the driveshaft. Position the 
clamp heads 180 degrees from the transducer and tighten the clamps.

[FIGURE: E9165A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not run the engine on the hoist with the transmission engaged for 
extended periods due to the danger of overheating the engine or transmission. 

Run the engine through the speed range. If no vibration is felt, remove 
the lug nuts, install the wheels and tires and reinstall the lug nuts in the 
correct position and go to Step 9.

However, if any vibration still exists, the combined weight of the two 
hose-clamp heads may be in excess. To reduce this excess weight, rotate the 
clamp heads away from each other approximately 15 degrees (one each way from 
the original position). Run the engine and note if the vibration has been 
reduced.

Continue to rotate the clamp heads apart in smaller angular increments 
until the vehicle feel of balance (vibration) is best. At this point, install 
the wheels and tires and road test the vehicle to determine the actual degree 
of improvement.

If satisfactory improvement has been obtained, proceed to Step 9.

When the balance has been corrected to a satisfactory level, tighten 
the clamps securely. Clean thoroughly with lacquer thinner and spray the 
clamps with a commercially available black paint for a finished appearance.

ADJUSTMENTS

Pinion and Ring Gear Adjustment

Two separate adjustments affect pinion and ring gear tooth contact. 
They are pinion location and backlash. 

Individual differences in matching the rear axle housing (4010) and the 
differential pinion bearings (4630) require the use of shims to locate the 
pinion for correct contact with the ring gear. Refer to Section 05-02A (7.5 
inch ring gear) or Section 05-02B (8.8 inch ring gear) for shim selection 
procedures.

ADJUSTMENTS

Pinion Bearing Preload � Bench Check

The absence of differential bearing preload causes noise as driving 
loads tend to move the gear pattern to the outside (heel) of the ring gear. If 
the preload is not set right, it can move out to the edge and score the gears.

Both the differential pinion bearing and differential bearing preload 
must be checked so the pattern will stay in place under load.

 NOTE: Lower front of axle to perform this check. Refer to Section 05-02A (7.5 
inch ring gear) or Section 05-02B (8.8 inch ring gear). 

Check the pinion bearing preload by putting a Nm 
(lb-in) torque wrench on the pinion nut and measuring the torque effort it 
takes to turn the pinion. Compare the reading with the preload specification 
for used bearings.

 NOTE: The rear axle drive pinion seal (4676) will offer a resistance 
equivalent to 0.056-0.451 Nm (0.5-4.0 lb-in). If the bearings 
are preloaded, a reading higher than 0.056-0.451 Nm (0.5-4.0 
lb-in) on the torque wrench scale must be obtained. If not, there is no preload.

Another indication is some threads protruding from in front of the nut. 
Normally about 2.29-2.54 mm (0.090-0.100 inch) of threads protrude if the 
preload is set properly. If the nut is flush with the end of the stem, chances 
are the preload was not set. Refer to Drive Pinion Shim Selection procedure in 
 Section 05-02A (7.5 inch ring gear) or Section 05-02B (8.8 inch ring gear) for 
resetting the proper preload.

 NOTE: The absence of preload here may indicate that the differential drive 
pinion collapsible spacer (4662) must be replaced if sufficient pinion nut 
torque is not achieved when tightening new pinion nut to desired rotational 
torque.

Tighten the pinion nut, rotating the pinion occasionally to ensure 
proper bearing seating. Take frequent drive pinion bearing torque preload 
readings until the original recorded preload reading is obtained.

If the original recorded preload is lower than specification, tighten 
to specification. If the preload is higher than specification, tighten to 
original reading as recorded.

LUBRICATION

Draining and Filling

Raise vehicle.

Clean all dirt from area of axle housing cover (4033).

Drain rear axle lubricant by removing axle housing cover.

 CAUTION: Make sure machined surfaces on both axle housing cover and rear axle 
housing (4010) are clean before installing the new silicone rubber. Inside of 
rear axle housing must be covered when cleaning the machined surface to 
prevent axle contamination. Tighten the cover bolts in a crosswise pattern to 
ensure uniform draw on axle housing cover. 

 NOTE: Axle housing cover must be installed within 15 minutes of the silicone 
rubber application or new silicone rubber must be applied.

Apply Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M4G92-A or ESE-M4G195-A. Install axle housing cover and 
tighten retaining bolts to 27-37 Nm (20-27 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: AE0140A.gif]

Add Motorcraft Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or -KL or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A until it is 6-14 mm 
(0.250-0.562 inch) below bottom of fill hole. Add 118 ml (4 oz) of Additive 
Friction Modifier C8AZ-19B546-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
EST-M2C118-A to Traction-Lok® axles. Install fill plug and 
tighten to 28-40 Nm (21-30 lb-ft).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Driveshaft 

 NOTE: All driveshaft (4602) assemblies are balanced; therefore, if the 
vehicle is to be undercoated, cover the driveshaft and rear axle shaft 
universal joints (4249) to prevent application of any undercoating material.

The driveshaft, equipped with single cardan universal joints, has the 
following features:

The driveshaft is a tubular shaft used to transfer engine torque from 
the transmission output shaft to the differential in the rear axle housing 
(4010) which, in turn, transmits torque through the halfshafts to the drive 
wheels. 

The driveshaft consists of two single cardan universal joints, a 
driveshaft slip yoke (4841), a welded aluminum tube assembly and driveshaft 
yoke. 

The splined driveshaft slip yoke permits the driveshaft to move forward 
and rearward on the transmission output shaft during drivetrain movement and 
during driveshaft removal and installation.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Universal Joints 

 NOTE: Span measurements are with bearing cups fully seated on spider.

Vehicles are equipped with two different series universal joints which

lubed-for-life design.

equipped with nylon thrust washers, located at each base of the bearing

movement.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Driveshaft, Rear

 Removal 

Drain fuel tank (9002). Refer to Section 10-01 .

Raise vehicle on a frame contact hoist.

Remove fuel tank modification shield and pipe kit (9B007) on forward 
side of fuel tank. 

[FIGURE: E6767C.gif]

 Remove muffler outlet pipe (5255) at muffler (5230). 

[FIGURE: E6769B.gif]

Lower muffler outlet pipe and support with wire. 

[FIGURE: E6770B.gif]

Remove exhaust hanger insulator (5F262) from exhaust pipe hanger stud. 

[FIGURE: E7069C.gif]

Lower exhaust system and remove complete system from vehicle. 

[FIGURE: E8292C.gif]

Remove sub-frame crossmember (5K068) on rear side of fuel tank. 

[FIGURE: E6771D.gif]

Remove fuel tank filler pipe retaining bolt from RH frame rail. 

[FIGURE: E6772C.gif]

 CAUTION: To prevent fuel leakage, use care not to damage fuel tank. 

Place Rotunda High Lift Jack 014-00210 or equivalent under fuel tank. 

[FIGURE: AE0102A.gif]

Remove sub-frame center support member on forward side of fuel tank. 

[FIGURE: E6774D.gif]

Remove fuel tank support straps (9092). Lower fuel tank approximately 
15 cm (6 inches). 

[FIGURE: E6775B.gif]

 NOTE: If original factory mark is not visible on rear axle universal joint 
flange (4851), mark both the rear axle universal joint flange and driveshaft 
centering socket yoke (4782). 

Locate original paint mark on rear axle universal joint flange and mark 
rear driveshaft centering socket yoke in same location. 

[FIGURE: E6976E.gif]

Remove four driveshaft retaining bolts. 

[FIGURE: E6977B.gif]

Separate the driveshaft (4602) from rear axle universal joint flange. 
Pull the driveshaft toward the rear of the vehicle until the driveshaft slip 
yoke (4841) clears the transmission extension housing and seal. Check 
driveshaft and transmission output shaft index during removal. Factory-made 
paint marks are on the end of transmission output shaft and the driveshaft 
front yoke weld. If factory-made paint marks are not visible, mark the 
driveshaft slip yoke in relation to transmission output shaft during removal 
and temporarily install the appropriate plug in the extension housing to 
prevent lubricant leakage. 

[FIGURE: E6978C.gif]

 Installation 

Lubricate the driveshaft slip yoke splines with Premium Long-Life 
Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 
Remove the plug from the transmission extension. Inspect the housing seal for 
damage; replace if required. 

Align driveshaft slip yoke index paint mark with transmission output 
shaft paint mark and install the driveshaft assembly. Do not allow the 
driveshaft slip yoke to bottom on the output shaft with excessive force. 

 NOTE: When installing a new driveshaft, align factory-made yellow paint mark 
at rear of driveshaft tube with factory-made yellow paint mark on outside 
diameter of rear axle universal joint flange. If paint marks are not visible, 
refer to Section 05-00 . 

Align marks on driveshaft centering socket yoke with rear axle 
universal joint flange. Install and tighten four retaining bolts to 95-130 Nm
 (70-95 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6976E.gif]

Raise fuel tank and install fuel tank support straps. Tighten retaining 
bolts to 29-41 Nm (22-30 lb-ft). 

Install fuel tank filler pipe retaining bolt. Tighten retaining bolt to 
2.7-3.7 Nm (24-32 lb-in). 

[FIGURE: E6772C.gif]

Install sub-frame crossmember. Tighten two retaining bolts to 20-30 Nm
 (15-22 lb-ft). 

Install sub-frame center support member on forward side of fuel tank. 
Tighten bolts to 20-30 Nm (15-22 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6774D.gif]

Raise muffler outlet pipe and support with wire. 

[FIGURE: E6770B.gif]

Install muffler and exhaust hanger insulator on hanger studs. 

[FIGURE: E7073C.gif]

Install muffler outlet pipe to muffler. Tighten bolts to 28-40 Nm
 (21-29 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6769B.gif]

Install crossmember on forward side of fuel tank. Tighten bolts to 16-24 Nm
 (12-17 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6767C.gif]

Lower vehicle.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Driveshaft, Single Cardan Universal Joint 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

U-Joint Tool

T74P-4635-C

 Disassembly 

 CAUTION: Under no circumstances is the driveshaft assembly to be clamped in the 
jaws of a vise or similar holding fixture. Denting or localized fracture may 
result, causing driveshaft failure during vehicle operation. 

Place driveshaft (4602) on a suitable work bench. Be careful not to 
damage tube. 

Prior to disassembly, mark the positions of the driveshaft components 
relative to the driveshaft tube. All components must be reassembled in the 
same relationship to maintain proper balance. 

Clamp U-Joint Tool T74P-4635-C in vise. 

[FIGURE: E7585A.gif]

Remove the four snap rings that retain the bearing cups. 

Position the driveshaft slip yoke (4841) in U-Joint Tool T74P-4635-C 
and press out bearing. If bearing cup cannot be pressed all the way out of the 
driveshaft slip yoke, remove it with locking pliers. 

 Tool Usage 

[FIGURE: E7586B.gif]

 Bearing Cup Removal 

[FIGURE: E7587C.gif]

Reposition the driveshaft slip yoke in U-Joint Tool T74P-4635-C 180 
degrees to press on the spider and remove the remaining bearing cup from the 
opposite side. 

Remove driveshaft slip yoke from the spider, clean all foreign matter 
from driveshaft slip yoke. 

Remove the remaining bearing cups and spiders from the driveshaft yoke 
in the same manner. 

Repeat Steps 1 through 8 to remove driveshaft centering socket yoke 
(4782). 

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Universal joint service kits are to be installed as complete assemblies 
only. Do not mix components from other universal joints. 

Start a new bearing cup into the yoke of the driveshaft.

Position new spider in the driveshaft yoke and press the bearing cup 
6.3 mm (1/4 inch) below the driveshaft slip yoke surface using U-Joint Tool 
T74P-4635-C. 

[FIGURE: E7588B.gif]

Remove U-Joint Tool T74P-4635-C and install a new snap ring. 

Start a new bearing cup into the opposite side of the driveshaft yoke. 
Check needles for proper position. 

Position driveshaft in U-Joint Tool T74P-4635-C and press on the 
bearing cup until the opposite bearing cup contacts the snap ring. 

 NOTE: Assemble rear axle shaft universal joint (4249) using the yellow snap 
rings supplied in the kit. If difficulty is encountered with yellow snap 
rings, install the black snap rings supplied in the kit. 

Remove U-Joint Tool T74P-4635-C and install a new snap ring. Check snap 
ring for proper seating. 

[FIGURE: E7589B.gif]

Install the driveshaft slip yoke, remaining bearing cups, spider, and 
snap rings in the same manner. 

Check universal joints (4635) for freedom of movement. If binding has 
resulted from misalignment during assembly, a sharp rap on the driveshaft yoke 
with a brass or plastic hammer will seat bearing needles. Take care to support 
the shaft end and do not strike the bearings during this procedure. Make sure 
rear axle shaft universal joints are free to rotate easily without binding 
before installing driveshaft. 

 Checking Movement 

[FIGURE: E7590B.gif]

 Seating Bearing Cups 

[FIGURE: E7591C.gif]

Repeat Steps 1 through 8 to install driveshaft centering socket yoke.

Section 05-02A: Axle, Integral Carrier � 7.5-Inch Ring Gear

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Description

The rear axle assembly contains the following features:

An integral-type housing hypoid gear design has the centerline of the 
pinion set below the centerline of the ring gear. 

The hypoid differential ring gear and pinion (4209) consists of a 191 
mm (7.5-inch) diameter ring gear and an overhung drive pinion which is 
supported by two opposed tapered roller bearings. 

Differential pinion bearing preload is maintained by a differential 
bearing shim (4067) on the pinion shaft and adjusted by the pinion nut. 

The rear axle housing (4010) assembly consists of a cast-aluminum 
center section and a cast-aluminum rear axle housing cover (4033). 

The axle housing cover uses a silicone sealant rather than a gasket. 

The differential case (4204) is a one-piece design with two openings to 
allow for assembly of internal components and lubricant flow. 

The differential pinion shaft (4211) is retained by a differential 
pinion shaft lock pin (4241) assembled to the differential case. 

The differential case is mounted in the rear axle housing between two 
opposed differential bearings (4221). 

The differential bearings are retained in the carrier by removable 
bearing caps. 

Differential bearing preload and ring gear backlash are adjusted by 
differential bearing shims located between the differential bearing cup (4222) 
and the rear axle housing. 

The halfshafts are held in the differential case by a driveshaft 
bearing retainer circlip (3Z498) that is located on the inboard CV joint stub 
shaft pilot bearing housing inboard CV joint. 

When each halfshaft is installed, the driveshaft bearing retainer 
circlip engages a step in the differential side gear (4236). 

 Rear Axle Assembly

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Anti-Lock � Rear

The rear anti-lock brake system (ABS) components consist of the rear 
brake anti-lock sensor (2C190) and a rear brake anti-lock sensor indicator 
(2C189). 

The rear brake anti-lock sensor is attached to the rear axle housing 
(4010) and is not adjustable. Refer to Section 06-09 for installation and 
removal of rear brake anti-lock sensor.

The rear brake anti-lock sensor indicator is attached to the inner CV 
joint. For removal and installation of rear brake anti-lock sensor indicator, 
refer to Section 05-05 .

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Operation

The rear drive axle operates as follows:

Rear axle drive pinion receives its power from the engine through the 
transmission and driveshaft (4602). 

The pinion gear rotates thedifferential case (4204) by engaging with 
the ring gear which is bolted to the differential case outer flange. 

Inside the differential case, two differential pinion gears (4215) are 
mounted on a differential pinion shaft (4211) which is pinned to the 
differential case. 

These differential pinion gears are engaged with the differential side 
gears (4236) to which the halfshafts are splined. 

As the differential case turns, it rotates the halfshafts and rear 
wheels.

When it is necessary for one wheel and halfshaft to rotate faster than 
the other, the faster turning differential side gear causes the differential 
pinion gears to roll on the slower turning differential side gear. This allows 
differential action between the two halfshafts.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Noise Acceptability 

A gear-driven unit, especially an automotive drive axle, will produce a 
certain amount of noise. Some noise is acceptable and may be audible at 
certain speeds or under various driving conditions, such as on a newly paved 
blacktop road. The slight noise is not detrimental to rear axle operation and 
is normal.

Inboard CV Joint Stub Shaft Pilot Bearing Housing and Inboard CV Joint 
Stub Shaft Pilot Bearing Housing Seal 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Bearing Cup Puller

T77F-1102-A

Impact Slide Hammer

T50T-100-A

Needle Bearing Replacer

T89P-1244-A

Differential Seal Replacer

T89P-4850-A

 Removal 

Remove halfshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-05 . 

 NOTE: If only the inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal 
(4B416) is to be replaced, install Bearing Cup Puller T77F-1102-A in bore and 
position it so tangs on tool firmly engage on inboard cv joint stub shaft 
pilot bearing housing seal.

Install Bearing Cup Puller T77F-1102-A in bore and position it behind 
inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing (4B413) so tangs on tool 
engage on inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing outer race. 

[FIGURE: E6739D.gif]

Remove inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal or 
inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing and inboard cv joint stub 
shaft pilot bearing housing seal with Impact Slide Hammer T50T-100-A threaded 
into Bearing Cup Puller T77F-1102-A as shown. 

[FIGURE: E6740C.gif]

 Installation 

Lubricate new inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing with 
SAE 80W-90 Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or -KL or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A.

[FIGURE: AE0224A.gif]

Install the inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing into 
housing bore using Needle Bearing Replacer T89P-1244-A and Driver Handle 
D81L-4000-A or equivalent. 

[FIGURE: E6743B.gif]

If seal is not pregreased, lubricate lip of inboard cv joint stub shaft 
pilot bearing housing seal with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

[FIGURE: E6742C.gif]

 CAUTION: Installation of the inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing or 
inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal assembly without the 
proper tool may result in an early pilot bearing or inboard cv joint stub 
shaft pilot bearing housing seal failure. If inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot 
bearing housing seal becomes cocked in the bore during installation, remove it 
and install a new one. 

Carefully align the inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing 
seal with the housing bore and install the inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot 
bearing housing seal with Differential Seal Replacer T89P-4850-A and Driver 
Handle D81L-4000-A or equivalent. 

[FIGURE: E6743B.gif]

Install halfshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-05 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Pinion Seal/Universal Joint Flange, Rear Axle

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T78P-4851-A

Companion Flange Remover

T65L-4851-B

Pinion Seal Replacer

T79P-4676-A

 Removal 

 CAUTION: This operation disturbs the pinion bearing preload, and this preload 
must be carefully reset when assembling. 

 NOTE: Replacement of rear axle drive pinion seal (4676) involves removal and 
installation of only the pinion nut and rear axle universal joint flange 
(4851). 

Raise vehicle on a frame contact hoist.

 NOTE: This will allow the rear axle housing (4010) to pivot forward.

Place a screw-type jackstand under rear axle housing. Remove rear axle 
differential rear insulator to axle housing cover retaining bolts and nuts. 

Install rear axle differential rear insulator bolt in lower bolt hole 
as shown. 

[FIGURE: E7056B.gif]

Mark driveshaft centering socket yoke (4782) in relation to rear axle 
universal joint flange. Remove driveshaft retaining bolts. 

[FIGURE: E6760B.gif]

Slide driveshaft (4602) forward and rest on driveshaft center bridge 
support reinforcement (4A315). 

[FIGURE: E6761C.gif]

 WARNING: REAR AXLE HOUSING MUST ALWAYS BE SUPPORTED BY JACKSTAND. 

Remove rear axle differential front lower insulator retaining nuts. 

[FIGURE: E7057B.gif]

Slowly lower rear axle housing to access rear axle universal joint 
flange. 

[FIGURE: E7058D.gif]

Install a Nm (lb-in) torque wrench on the pinion nut. 
Record the torque required to maintain rotation of the pinion through several 
revolutions. 

[FIGURE: E7060B.gif]

 NOTE: If installing a new rear axle universal joint flange, it is not 
necessary to mark the rear axle universal joint flange.

Mark the rear axle universal joint flange in relation to pinion stem so 
that rear axle universal joint flange can be reinstalled in the same position. 

[FIGURE: E7020D.gif]

 While holding rear axle universal joint flange with Companion Flange 
Holding Tool T78P-4851-A, remove pinion nut. 

[FIGURE: E7061E.gif]

 CAUTION: The rear axle universal joint flange must never be hammered on or 
assembled with power tools. 

 NOTE: If required, use Companion Flange Remover T65L-4851-B. 

Remove rear axle universal joint flange. 

[FIGURE: AE0225A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not damage rear axle housing. 

Place a drain pan under therear axle housing. Position screwdriver 
under flange of rear axle drive pinion seal and strike with hammer to wedge 
screwdriver blade between metal flange of rear axle drive pinion seal and rear 
axle housing. 

[FIGURE: E7063C.gif]

 Pry on metal flange of rear axle drive pinion seal. Install gripping 
pliers and strike with hammer until rear axle drive pinion seal is removed. 
Remove rear axle drive pinion shaft oil slinger (4670).

[FIGURE: E7064B.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Check rear axle universal joint flange for burrs. Remove burrs as 
necessary. Make sure surfaces of rear axle universal joint flange have not 
been damaged in removing driveshaft or in removing rear axle universal joint 
flange from pinion. The end of the rear axle universal joint flange that 
contacts the bearing cone as well as the nut counterbore and seal surface must 
be smooth and free of nicks.

Make sure splines on the drive pinion stem are free of burrs. If burrs 
are evident, remove them by using a fine crocus cloth. Working in a rotating 
motion, wipe the pinion clean. Clean flange yoke seal seat surface and install 
rear axle drive pinion seal on Pinion Seal Replacer T79P-4676-A. 

[FIGURE: E7065B.gif]

 CAUTION: Installation without proper tool may result in early seal failure. If 
rear axle drive pinion seal becomes cocked during installation, remove and 
replace with new rear axle drive pinion seal. 

Install rear axle drive pinion seal in rear axle housing. 

[FIGURE: E7026D.gif]

 NOTE: Check rear axle universal joint flange for burrs. Remove burrs as 
necessary. Make sure surfaces of flange have not been damaged in removing 
driveshaft or in removing flange from pinion. The end of the flange that 
contacts the bearing cone as well as the nut counterbore and seal surface must 
be smooth and free of nicks. 

Apply a small amount of SAE 80W-90, Premium Rear Axle Lubricant 
XY-80W90-QL or -KL or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A to 
rear axle universal joint flange splines. 

 CAUTION: The rear axle universal joint flange must never be hammered on or 
assembled with power tools. 

Align mark on rear axle universal joint flange with mark on the pinion 
stem. Install rear axle universal joint flange. 

Install a new pinion nut on pinion stem. Apply a small amount of SAE 
80W-90, Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or -KL or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A on the washer side of nut. 

Hold rear axle universal joint flange with Companion Flange Holding 
Tool T78P-4851-A while tightening pinion nut. Rotate pinion occasionally to 
verify proper differential pinion bearing (4630) seating. 

[FIGURE: E7066B.gif]

Take frequent differential pinion bearing torque preload readings until 
the original reading is obtained. 

[FIGURE: AE0226A.gif]

 NOTE: Refer to Adjustment Torque Specifications . 

If the original recorded preload is less than specification, tighten to 
specification. If the preload is higher than specification, tighten to 
original reading as recorded. 

Never back off the pinion nut to reduce preload. If reduced preload is 
required, a new differential drive pinion collapsible spacer (4662) and pinion 
nut must be installed. 

Using a jackstand, raise and locate rear axle housing on rear axle 
differential front lower insulator bolts. 

[FIGURE: E7059C.gif]

Install rear axle differential front lower insulator nuts. Tighten to 
92-136 Nm (68-100 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E7057B.gif]

Remove rear axle differential rear insulator bolt from pivot position. 

[FIGURE: E7067B.gif]

Install rear axle differential rear insulator bolts in axle housing 
cover mount. Tighten to 108-136 Nm (80-100 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E7068B.gif]

Align marks on driveshaft centering socket yoke and rear axle universal 
joint flange. Install retaining bolts. Tighten to 95-130 Nm 
(70-95 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6760B.gif]

Fill rear axle housing with SAE 80W-90 Premium Rear Axle Lubricant 
XY-80W90-QL or -KL or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A to 6 
mm (1/4 inch) below the bottom of filler hole. 

Install filler plug. Tighten to 20-41 Nm (15-30 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6749B.gif]

Lower vehicle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Cover 

 Removal 

Raise vehicle on a hoist.

Support rear axle housing (4010) and remove rear axle differential rear 
insulator-to-crossmember retaining nuts. 

[FIGURE: E6762C.gif]

Position drain pan under rear axle housing. Remove fill plug with 
3/8-inch flex handle and remove axle housing cover-to-housing retaining bolts. 

[FIGURE: E6748B.gif]

Remove rear axle housing cover (4033). 

[FIGURE: E6745B.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Make sure rear axle housing vent (4022) and vent hose are not plugged. 
When axle housing cover is installed, the open end of vent hose fits into 
middle hole in RH rail of crossmember. 

Clean sealing surfaces and groove in axle housing cover. 

[FIGURE: E6746D.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure machined surfaces on both axle housing cover and rear axle 
housing are clean before installing the new silicone sealant. Inside of axle 
must be covered when cleaning the machined surface to prevent axle 
contamination. 

 NOTE: Axle housing cover assembly must be installed within 15 minutes of 
application of the silicone or new sealant must be applied. 

Apply a continuous bead of Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or -BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESE-M4G195-A or ESB-M4G92-A to groove 
in axle housing cover. 

[FIGURE: AE0211A.gif]

 CAUTION: Tighten the axle housing cover bolts in a crosswise pattern to prevent 
distortion of axle housing cover. 

Position axle housing cover and install retaining bolts.

Place service identification tag in the 12 o'clock position. Tighten to 
27-37 Nm (20-27 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6748B.gif]

Install rear axle differential rear insulator to crossmember nuts. 
Tighten to 108-136 Nm (80-100 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6762C.gif]

Fill rear axle housing with SAE 80W-90; Premium Rear Axle Lubricant 
XY-80W90-QL or -KL or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A to 
6.35 mm (1/4 inch) below the bottom of filler hole. 

Install oil filler plug. Tighten to 20-41 Nm (15-30 
lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6749B.gif]

Lower vehicle.

Axle Housing

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Front Hub Remover/Replacer

T81P-1104-C

Metric Hub Remover Adapters

T83P-1104-BH

Differential Plug

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Do not begin this removal procedure unless the following parts are 
available: 

A new rear axle wheel hub retainer (4B477). 

A new inboard CV joint stub shaft driveshaft bearing retainer circlip 
(3Z498). 

 Once removed, these parts must not be reused during assembly. 
Their torque-holding ability or retention capability is diminished during 
removal. 

 CAUTION: Discard the rear axle wheel hub retainer. It is a torque-prevailing 
design and cannot be reused. 

Remove RH wheel cover (1130). Remove rear axle wheel hub retainer using 
a 36 mm socket. Loosen lug nuts (1012). 

[FIGURE: F5191D.gif]

 CAUTION: A frame contact hoist must be used to avoid damage to the halfshafts 
and halfshaft boots. 

Raise vehicle on a frame contact hoist.

 CAUTION: Some vehicles are equipped with directional tires. Always make sure 
tires are installed in their original positions. 

Remove lug nuts and wheel and tire. 

Remove brake drums (1126) (if equipped). 

 CAUTION: Damage to the sensors may occur if they are not removed before the 
halfshafts. 

Remove RH and LH rear brake anti-lock sensors (2C190). Refer to Section 06-09 . 

[FIGURE: E6989B.gif]

Remove rear suspension arm and bushing bolt. Wire upper suspension arm 
to top of rear shock absorber (18125) so it does not interfere with or damage 
CV joint boot when halfshaft (3A329) is removed. 

 Rear Suspension Arm Disconnected 

[FIGURE: E6751B.gif]

 Rear Suspension Arm Temporary Support 

[FIGURE: F5188B.gif]

 WARNING: FAILURE TO MARK THIS POSITION WILL CAUSE BUSHING WINDUP ON REASSEMBLY 
AND INCORRECT RIDE HEIGHT. THIS WILL CAUSE MISALIGNMENT AND PREMATURE TIRE 
WEAR. 

Using a paint marker, mark the position of the rear suspension arm and 
bushing (5500) in relation to the rear wheel knuckle (5A969) with the bushings 
in the relaxed position. 

[FIGURE: E6752B.gif]

Install Front Hub Remover/Replacer T81P-1104-C with Metric Hub Remover 
Adapters T83P-1104-BH on Hub Adapter T86P-1104-A1 to RH wheel studs as shown. 
Turn wrench counterclockwise until halfshaft is free in rear hub (1109). 

[FIGURE: E6753G.gif]

Remove rear suspension arm and bushing-to-rear suspension arm and 
bushing retaining bolts. 

[FIGURE: E6754C.gif]

Remove rear wheel knuckle assembly from driveshaft and joint assembly. 

[FIGURE: E6755C.gif]

 WARNING: DO NOT STRETCH, TWIST OR KINK BRAKE HOSE ASSEMBLY. 

Carefully rest halfshaft on rear suspension arm and bushing and wire 
rear wheel knuckle to top of rear shock absorber. 

[FIGURE: E6756C.gif]

 NOTE: Inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal (4B416) must be 
replaced whenever the halfshaft is removed. 

Remove RH halfshaft from rear axle housing (4010) using CV Joint 
Remover T89P-3514-A. 

[FIGURE: E7054B.gif]

Remove halfshaft from vehicle. 

[FIGURE: E7055B.gif]

Install Differential Plug T89P-4850-B into rear axle housing to prevent 
lubricant loss. 

[FIGURE: E6759C.gif]

Mark driveshaft centering socket yoke (4782) in relation to rear axle 
universal joint flange (4851). Remove driveshaft retaining bolts. 

[FIGURE: E6760B.gif]

Slide driveshaft (4602) forward and rest on driveshaft center bridge 
support reinforcement (4A315) . 

[FIGURE: E6761C.gif]

With a transmission jack supporting the rear axle housing, remove rear 
axle differential rear insulator-to-crossmember retaining nuts. 

[FIGURE: E6762C.gif]

Remove rear axle differential rear insulator (4B425) from axle housing 
cover (4033). 

[FIGURE: E6763C.gif]

Remove axle front retaining bolts, nuts, bushings and washers. 

[FIGURE: E6764C.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not damage CV joint boot. 

 NOTE: Inboard CV joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal must be replaced 
whenever a halfshaft (CV joint) has been removed from the rear axle housing. 

Remove LH halfshaft (inboard CV joint) from rear axle housing using CV 
Joint Remover T89P-3514-A. Push tool inward (toward rear axle housing). 

[FIGURE: E6765C.gif]

Partially lower rear axle housing. While lowering rear axle housing, 
move to the right and disengage rear axle housing from LH inboard CV joint 
stub shaft. 

[FIGURE: E6766C.gif]

Install Differential Plug T89P-4850-B in LH side of rear axle housing 
and lower rear axle housing from vehicle. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Remove Differential Plug T89P-4850-B from the rear axle housing.

Replace inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal as 
described.

 NOTE: With LH halfshaft in vehicle, install new driveshaft bearing retainer 
circlip as shown. Do not bend or twist circlip. 

Install new driveshaft bearing retainer circlip on LH inboard CV joint 
by pushing new driveshaft bearing retainer circlip into stub shaft groove. 

[FIGURE: E6979B.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not damage inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing (4B413) 
and inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal during halfshaft 
installation and spline alignment. 

Position rear axle housing on transmission jack and partially raise to 
align LH CV joint stub shaft into differential side gear (4236). Lightly 
lubricate LH inboard CV joint stub shaft splines prior to installation. 

[FIGURE: E6766C.gif]

Locate rear axle housing on front mounting bolts and push in CV joint 
until driveshaft bearing retainer circlip seats in axle shaft (4234). 

 NOTE: Bushings must be installed into rear axle housing as shown. 

Install bushings, washers and nuts on rear axle differential front 
lower insulator (4B431). Tighten retaining nuts to 92-136 Nm 
(68-100 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6980B.gif]

Install rear axle differential rear insulator to axle housing cover. 
Tighten nuts and bolts to 108-136 Nm (80-100 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6763C.gif]

Install rear axle differential rear insulator-to-crossmember retaining 
bolts and nuts. Tighten to 165-211 Nm (122-155 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6762C.gif]

Align marks on driveshaft centering socket yoke and rear axle universal 
joint flange. Install retaining bolts. Tighten to 95-130 Nm 
(70-95 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6760B.gif]

Install new driveshaft bearing retainer circlip on RH inboard stub 
shaft by pushing it into stub shaft groove as shown. Do not bend or twist 
circlip. 

[FIGURE: E6981D.gif]

Lightly lubricate the splines with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or 
-K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

[FIGURE: E6984B.gif]

 NOTE: Do not damage the inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing 
seal. The inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal must be 
replaced whenever the halfshaft is removed. 

Carefully align the splines of the stub shaft with the splines in the 
differential side gear. 

[FIGURE: E4314G.gif]

 NOTE: A non-metallic mallet may be used to aid in seating the driveshaft 
bearing retainer circlip into the differential side gear groove. If a mallet 
is necessary, tap only on the outboard CV joint stub shaft. 

Push halfshaft into rear axle housing until driveshaft bearing retainer 
circlip engages into differential side gear. 

[FIGURE: E6985D.gif]

Engage rear wheel knuckle splines with outboard stub shaft splines. 

[FIGURE: E6986C.gif]

Install rear suspension upper arm and bushing bolts and nuts. Align 
paint marks. Tighten bolts to 160-200 Nm (119-147 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6987C.gif]

Install new rear axle wheel hub retainer and pull CV joint into hub as 
far as possible by hand, as shown. 

[FIGURE: E6988B.gif]

Install rear suspension lower arm and bushing retaining bolt and nut. 
Tighten to 160-200 Nm (119-147 lb-ft). 

Install brake drum and new pushnuts. 

Fill rear axle housing with SAE 80W-90 Premium Rear Axle Lubricant 
XY-80W90-QL or -KL or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A. 

Install fill plug. Tighten to 20-41 Nm (15-30 lb-ft). 

Install rear brake anti-lock sensors on each side of rear axle housing. 
Tighten to 19-27 Nm (14-20 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6989B.gif]

Install wheel and tire assembly. Tighten lug nuts to 115-142 Nm
 (85-104 lb-ft). 

Lower vehicle. 

Tighten rear axle wheel hub retainer to 340 Nm (250 
lb-ft). 

Install wheel cover. 

[FIGURE: E6751B.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Axle Disassembly 

 Universal Joint Flange 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T78P-4851-A

 CAUTION: This operation disturbs the pinion bearing preload. This preload must 
be carefully reset when assembling. 

 Removal 

 NOTE: If installing a new rear axle universal joint flange (4851) or 
differential ring gear and pinion (4209), it is not necessary to mark the rear 
axle universal joint flange.

Mark rear axle universal joint flange in relation to the pinion stem. 
Hold the rear axle universal joint flange with the proper tool and remove the 
pinion nut.

[FIGURE: E7020D.gif]

Remove rear axle universal joint flange with Companion Flange Holding 
Tool T78P-4851-A. 

[FIGURE: E7021B.gif]

 Differential Case Removal 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Bench Mounted Holding Fixture

T57L-500-B

Differential Side Bearing Replacer

T57L-4221-A2

Differential Side Bearing Puller

T77F-4220-B1

Step Plate

T81P-4220-A

Remove rear axle housing (4010) as described.

Remove axle housing cover (4033). 

Position rear axle housing in Bench Mounted Holding Fixture T57L-500-B. 

[FIGURE: E7035B.gif]

The arrows face outboard on bearing caps. When assembled, the arrows 
must be pointing in the same direction and bearing caps must be in original 
positions as before removal. 

Mark one differential bearing cap to make sure the caps are installed 
in their original positions during assembly. 

 NOTE: Arrows face outboard on bearing caps. When assembled, the arrows must 
be pointing in the same direction as before removal with bearing caps in 
original positions.

Loosen differential bearing cap bolts and bearing caps. 

[FIGURE: E7036C.gif]

Pry out differential case (4204), differential bearing cups (4222) and 
differential bearing shims (4067) until loose in the bearing caps. Remove 
bearing caps and remove differential case from rear axle housing. 

[FIGURE: E7558B.gif]

 NOTE: If equipped with Traction-Lok® limited slip 
differential, refer to Section 05-02C for Differential Disassembly procedure.

Remove differential pinion shaft lock pin (4241) and differential 
pinion shaft (4211). 

Remove differential side gears (4236), differential pinion gears (4215) 
and differential pinion thrust washers (4230). 

Inspect the differential bearings (4221) and differential bearing cups 
for damage. If damaged, remove the differential bearings using Differential 
Side Bearing Puller T77F-4220-B1 and Step Plate T81P-4220-A. 

[FIGURE: AE0177A.gif]

Using a drift that will bottom in ring gear bolt holes, strike at 
alternate holes around gear. Remove ring gear.

[FIGURE: E6262C.gif]

Install differential bearings using Differential Side Bearing Replacer 
T57L-4221-A2.

[FIGURE: AE0209A.gif]

 Drive Pinion Removal 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Pinion Bearing Cone Remover

T71P-4621-B

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T78P-4851-A

Companion Flange Remover

T65L-4851-B

Remove differential case as described.

Mark rear axle universal joint flange in relation to the pinion stem. 
Hold the rear axle universal joint flange with Companion Flange Holding Tool 
T78P-4851-A and remove the pinion nut. If installing a new differential ring 
gear and pinion, it is not necessary to mark the rear axle universal joint 
flange. 

[FIGURE: E7020D.gif]

Remove rear axle universal joint flange with Companion Flange Holding 
Tool T78P-4851-A. 

[FIGURE: E7021B.gif]

With a soft-faced hammer, drive the differential ring gear and pinion 
out of the rear differential pinion bearing (4630). Remove through the rear of 
the rear axle housing. 

Remove the rear axle drive pinion seal (4676) as described. Remove the 
front differential pinion bearing (4621) from the rear axle housing. 

 Pinion Bearing Cup Removal 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Pinion Bearing Cone Remover

T71P-4621-B

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T78P-4851-A

Using a press and Pinion Bearing Cone Remover T71P-4621-B, remove

[FIGURE: AE0178A.gif]

 NOTE: Measure the drive pinion bearing adjustment shim (4663), which is found

Remove the drive pinion bearing adjustment shim from the drive pinion.

 NOTE: To make sure bearings are properly seated, clean bores before installing

 Differential Case Runout Check 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Differential Side Bearing Replacer

T57L-4221-A2

If the differential ring gear and pinion runout check (performed before 
disassembly) exceeds specification, the condition may be caused by a warped 
ring gear, a damaged differential case or loss of differential bearing 
preload. To determine the cause of excessive runout, proceed as follows: 

With the pinion removed, place differential case/gear subassembly with 
differential bearings and differential bearing cups in rear axle housing. 

[FIGURE: E7041B.gif]

Install a 6.731 mm (0.265-inch) differential bearing shim on the LH 
side of subassembly. 

[FIGURE: AE0039A.gif]

Install the LH bearing cap finger-tight. 

[FIGURE: E7043B.gif]

Install progressively larger differential bearing shims on the RH side 
until the largest differential bearing shim selected can be assembled with a 
slight drag feel. 

[FIGURE: AE0143A.gif]

Install the RH side bearing cap. Install bearing cap bolts. Tighten to 
95-115 Nm (70-84 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: AE0228A.gif]

Rotate the assembly to make sure differential rotates freely. 

[FIGURE: E7502B.gif]

Install Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent. Check 
and note ring gear runout. 

[FIGURE: E7503D.gif]

If the runout is within specification, the original 
out-of-specification runout was caused by insufficient differential bearing 
preload. If the runout exceeds specification, proceed to Step 9. 

Remove differential case from the rear axle housing. 

[FIGURE: E7041B.gif]

Using a drift that will bottom in ring gear bolt holes, strike at 
alternate holes around gear. Remove ring gear.

[FIGURE: E6262C.gif]

Install differential assembly in rear axle housing without ring gear. 

[FIGURE: E7505B.gif]

Check runout of differential case flange with Dial Indicator with 
Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent. If runout is within specification, 
(maximum 0.076 mm, 0.003 inch), install a new differential ring gear and 
pinion. If runout exceeds specification, ring gear is true and concern is due 
to either a damaged differential case or differential bearings. Inspect 
differential bearings. If differential bearings are not damaged, replace both 
differential case and differential bearings. Recheck runout with new parts (
differential case and differential bearings). 

[FIGURE: E7506C.gif]

 NOTE: Press against the differential bearing only. 

Press new differential bearings on differential case hubs using 
Differential Side Bearing Replacer T57L-4221-A2. Install differential assembly 
in carrier without differential ring gear and pinion. 

Check case runout again with new differential bearings. If runout is 
within limits, use new differential bearings for assembly. If runout is still 
excessive, differential case is damaged and should be replaced.

Axle Assembly

 Pinion Bearing Cup Installation

T71P-4616-A

 NOTE: The same differential pinion bearing (4630) used in this procedure must

Place the drive pinion bearing adjustment shims (4663) on the pinion. 
Press the pinion bearing cone and roller assembly until it is firmly seated on 
the pinion with Pinion Bearing Cone Replacer T53T-4621-C. 

[FIGURE: AE0222A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not remove the differential pinion bearings (4621) from the carrier

properly seated. Whenever the differential bearing cups are replaced, the

 Drive Pinion Shim Selection 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Pinion Depth Gauge Set

T79P-4020-A

A selective drive pinion bearing adjustment shim measuring 0.254 mm to 
0.965 mm (0.010 to 0.038 inch) is used between differential pinion bearing and 
differential ring gear and pinion (4209). The drive pinion bearing adjustment 
shim compensates for machining variations in rear axle housing (4010), 
differential ring gear and pinion and differential pinion bearings. The 
correct drive pinion bearing adjustment shim size will locate differential 
ring gear and pinion for proper tooth contact with differential ring gear and 
pinion. Selecting correct drive pinion bearing adjustment shim when installing 
a new gearset can be done by using Pinion Depth Gauge Set T79P-4020-A:

Refer to illustration and assemble the appropriate aligning adapter, 
gauge disc and gauge block to the screw.

 NOTE: The gauge block must be offset to obtain an accurate reading. 

Place rear differential pinion bearing (new, or used if in good 
condition) over aligning disc and insert into rear axle pinion bearing cup 
(4628) of the rear axle housing. Place front differential pinion bearing into 
the bearing cap and assemble the tool handle into screw. Tighten to 2.26 Nm
 (20 lb-in). 

[FIGURE: AE0221A.gif]

Make sure gauge handle adapter screw, aligning adapter, gauge disc and 
gauge block assembly are securely mounted between the front differential 
pinion bearing and rear differential pinion bearing. Check the tool handle 
torque prior to gauging to make sure bearings are properly seated. This can 
affect final drive pinion bearing adjustment shim selection when improperly 
assembled. Clean bearing cups and differential pedestal surfaces thoroughly. 
Apply only light oil film on bearing assemblies prior to gauging. 

Rotate the gauge block several half turns to make sure rollers are 
properly seated in bearing cups. Rotational torque on the gauge assembly 
should be 2.26 Nm (20 lb-in) with new bearings. Final 
position should be approximately 45 degrees across gauge tube to make sure 
gauge block is in-line with gauge tube high point. This area should be used 
for pinion shim selection. Selection of drive pinion bearing adjustment shim 
with gauge block not lined up with tube high point will cause improper drive 
pinion bearing adjustment shim selection and may result in axle noise. 

 NOTE: Drive pinion bearing adjustment shims must be flat. Do not use dirty, 
bent, nicked or mutilated shims as a gauge. 

Use drive pinion bearing adjustment shims as the gauge for shim 
selection. This will minimize errors in attempting to stack feeler gauge stock 
together. It also helps to prevent simple addition errors in calculating 
correct drive pinion bearing adjustment shim thickness. 

 NOTE: The same rear differential pinion bearing used in this procedure must 
be used in final assembly of the axle. 

It is important to feel a slight drag on the drive pinion bearing 
adjustment shim for correct selection. Do not attempt to force the drive 
pinion bearing adjustment shim between the gauge block and the gauge tube. 
This will minimize selection of a drive pinion bearing adjustment shim thicker 
than required which results in a deep tooth contact in final assembly of 
integral axles. 

Place the selected drive pinion bearing adjustment shims on pinion 
shaft and press pinion bearing until firmly seated on shaft. 

[FIGURE: AE0040A.gif]

 CAUTION: Installation without the proper tool may result in early flange yoke

 Universal Joint Flange Installation 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Companion Flange Holding Tool

T78P-4851-A

Apply a small amount of SAE 80W-90; Premium Rear Axle Lubricant 
XY-80W90-QL or -KL or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A to 
rear axle universal joint flange splines. 

 NOTE: If installing a new rear axle universal joint flange (4851), disregard 
the scribe mark on the pinion stem. 

Align mark on rear axle universal joint flange with mark on the pinion 
shaft. 

 CAUTION: The circular rear axle universal joint flange must never be hammered on 
or installed with power tools. 

With drive pinion in place in rear axle housing, install rear axle 
universal joint flange using Companion Flange Replacer TOOL-4858-E or

Install a new pinion nut on pinion shaft (apply a small amount of 
lubricant on the washer side of nut). 

Hold the rear axle universal joint flange with Companion Flange Holding 
Tool T78P-4851-A while tightening the nut. 

[FIGURE: E8295A.gif]

 NOTE: Never back off the pinion nut to reduce preload. If reduced preload is 
required, a new differential drive pinion collapsible spacer and pinion nut 
must be installed. 

Tighten pinion nut. Rotate pinion occasionally to make sure 
differential pinion bearing is properly seated. Take frequent pinion bearing 
torque preload readings until obtaining the original recorded preload reading. 

If the original recorded preload is less than specification, tighten 
used differential pinion bearing to 0.9-1.6 Nm (8-14 lb-in) 
and new differential pinion bearings to 1.8-3.2 Nm (16-29 
lb-in). If the preload is higher than specification, tighten to original 
reading as recorded. 

 Differential Case Installation � Condition 1 

Follow this procedure when only differential ring gear and pinion 
replacement is required and the differential bearing (4221) and differential 
case (4204) do not require replacement. 

Remove the differential caps and bolts. Identify the RH cap, RH 
differential bearing cup and differential bearing shim (4067) to keep these 
components as RH and LH sets. 

Remove the differential case subassembly using the pry bar method. 
Reasonable effort will be required to remove subassembly if preload is within 
specification. If subassembly can be removed by hand, use Differential Case 
Installation � Condition 2 for assembly. 

Replace the differential ring gear and pinion using the differential 
bearing shim components from the original assembly. Select the differential 
bearing shim as described.

 Differential Case Installation � Condition 2 

Follow this procedure when original differential bearing shims are not 
available or when rear axle housing, differential case or differential bearing 
replacement is required. 

With pinion depth set and differential ring gear and pinion installed, 
place the differential case/gear subassembly with differential bearings and 
differential bearing cups in rear axle housing. 

[FIGURE: E7508B.gif]

Install a (6.731 mm) 0.265-inch differential bearing shim on the LH 
side. 

[FIGURE: AE0039A.gif]

Install LH bearing cap finger-tight. 

[FIGURE: E7510B.gif]

Install progressively larger differential bearing shims on the RH side 
until the largest differential bearing shim selected can be assembled with a 
slight drag feel. 

[FIGURE: AE0143A.gif]

Install RH side bearing cap and differential bearing cap bolts. Tighten 
to 95-115 Nm (70-84 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: AE0228A.gif]

Rotate the assembly to make sure differential operates freely. 

[FIGURE: E7511B.gif]

Check ring gear and differential ring gear and pinion backlash. If 
backlash is within specification, go to Step 14. If backlash is not within 
specification, go to Step 10. If zero backlash is measured, proceed with Step 
8. 

[FIGURE: AE0210A.gif]

If a zero backlash condition occurs, add 0.508 mm (0.020 inch) to the 
RH side and subtract 0.508 mm (0.020 inch) from the LH side to allow backlash 
indication.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Inspection Before Disassembly of Carrier 

The differential case (4204) assemblies and differential ring gear and 
pinion (4209) should be inspected before they are removed from the carrier. 
These inspections can help find the cause of the condition and the solution.

Wipe lubricant from internal working parts and inspect parts for wear 
and damage. 

Rotate gears to see if there is any roughness which would indicate worn 
or damaged bearings or gears. 

Check ring gear teeth for signs of scoring, abnormal wear, nicks or 
chips. 

Set up a Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent and 
check ring gear backlash and ring gear backface runout. Refer to Section 05-00 .
