CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Inspection After Disassembly of Carrier

Thoroughly clean all parts. Always use new solvent when cleaning 
bearings. Do not spin dry bearings with compressed air. Oil the bearings 
immediately with SAE 80W-90; Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or -KL or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A to prevent rusting. Inspect 
parts for damage. Clean the inside of rear axle housing (4010) before 
rebuilding. When a scored or chipped gearset is replaced, the rear axle 
housing must be washed thoroughly. Inspections of individual parts are 
described as follows:

 Gears 

Examine differential ring gear and pinion teeth for scoring, excessive 
wear, nicks and chipping. Worn, scored and damaged differential ring gear and 
pinions (4209) cannot be rebuilt to correct a noisy condition. 

Pattern inspection allows the technician to detect gross errors in 
set-up prior to complete assembly. Pattern contact should be within the 
primary area of the ring gear tooth surface, avoiding narrow or hard contact 
with the outer perimeter of tooth (top to root, toe to heel). Pattern 
inspection should be on the drive (pull) side. Correct assembly of drive 
pattern will result in satisfactory coast performance. If gross pattern error 
is detected, with preferred backlash 0.305 to 0.381 mm (0.012 to 0.015 inch), 
check pinion shim selection. 

 Bearing Cups 

Check differential drive pinion bearing cups (4616) for deep scores, 
galling or spalling. If a 0.038-mm (0.0015-inch) feeler gauge can be inserted 
between a differential drive pinion bearing cup and the bottom of its bore at 
any point around the differential drive pinion bearing cup , the differential 
drive pinion bearing cup must be reseated. 

 Universal Joint Flange, Rear Axle 

Make sure surfaces of the rear axle universal joint flange (4851) were 
not damaged when it was removed from the pinion. The end of the rear axle 
universal joint flange that contacts bearing cone as well as the nut 
counterbore and seal surface must be smooth and free of nicks. 

 Cone and Roller Assemblies 

When operated in the differential drive pinion bearing cups, bearing 
rollers must turn without roughness. Examine the rollers for wear (pitting, 
scoring, galling or spalling). If inspection reveals either a damaged 
differential drive pinion bearing cup or a damaged differential pinion bearing 
(4630), replace both parts. 

 Carrier Housing 

Make sure the differential bearing bores are smooth. Remove any nicks 
or burrs from the mounting surfaces of the rear axle housing. 

 Differential Case 

Make sure the hubs where the differential bearings (4221) mount are 
smooth. Carefully examine the differential case bearing shoulders which may 
have been damaged when the differential bearings were removed. The 
differential bearing assemblies will fail if they do not seat firmly against 
the shoulders. Check the fit (free rotation) of the axle shaft (4234) in their 
counterbores.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Description

The rear axle assembly contains the following features: 

An integral-type housing, hypoid gear design. (The centerline of pinion 
set is below centerline of ring gear.)

The hypoid differential ring gear and pinion (4209) consists of a 224 
mm (8.8-inch) diameter ring gear and an overhung drive pinion which is 
supported by two opposed tapered roller bearings. 

Differential pinion bearing preload is maintained by a differential 
drive pinion collapsible spacer (4662) on pinion shaft and adjusted by pinion 
nut. 

The rear axle housing (4010) assembly consists of a nodular iron center 
section and a cast-aluminum axle housing cover (4033).

The axle housing cover uses silicone sealant rather than a gasket. 

The differential case (4204) is a one-piece design with two openings to 
allow for assembly of internal components and lubricant flow. 

The differential pinion shaft (4211) is retained by a threaded 
differential pinion shaft lock pin (4241) assembled to differential case. 

The differential case is mounted in rear axle housing between two 
opposed differential bearings (4221). 

The differential bearings are retained in rear axle housing by 
removable bearing caps. 

Differential pinion bearing preload and ring gear backlash are adjusted 
by differential bearing shims (4067) located between the differential bearing 
cup (4222) and the rear axle housing. 

The halfshafts are held in differential case by a driveshaft bearing 
retainer circlip (3Z498) located on inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing 
housing (4B413). 

When each halfshaft is installed, driveshaft bearing retainer circlip 
engages a step in differential side gear (4236).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Anti-Lock � Rear

Rear anti-lock brake system (ABS) components consist of rear brake 
anti-lock sensor (2C190) and rear brake anti-lock sensor indicator (2C189).

Rear brake anti-lock sensor is attached to rear axle housing (4010) and 
is not adjustable. For installation and removal of rear brake anti-lock 
sensor, refer to Section 06-09 .

Rear brake anti-lock sensor indicator is attached to inboard CV joint 
outer race. For installation and removal of rear brake anti-lock sensor 
indicator, refer to Section 05-05 .

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Operation 

Rear drive axle operates as follows:

Rear axle drive pinion receives its power from the engine through 
transmission and driveshaft (4602).

Pinion gear rotates differential case (4204) by engaging with ring 
gear, which is bolted to differential case outer flange.

Inside differential case, two differential pinion gears (4215) are 
mounted on differential pinion shaft (4211) which is pinned to differential 
case.

These differential pinion shafts are engaged with differential side 
gears (4236), to which halfshafts are splined. 

As differential side gear rotates, it rotates halfshafts and rear wheels.

When it is necessary for one wheel and halfshaft to rotate faster than 
the other, the faster turning differential side gear causes differential 
pinion gears to roll on the slower turning differential side gear to allow 
differential action between the two halfshafts.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Noise Acceptability 

A gear-driven unit, especially an automotive drive axle, will produce a 
certain amount of noise. Some noise is acceptable and may be audible at 
certain speeds or under various driving conditions; for example, on a newly 
paved blacktop road. The slight noise is not detrimental to rear axle 
operation and is normal.

 Removal 

 CAUTION: This operation disturbs pinion bearing preload. This preload must be 
carefully reset when assembling. 

 NOTE: Replacement of rear axle drive pinion seals (4676) involves removal and 
installation of only pinion nut and rear axle universal joint flange (4851). 

Raise vehicle on frame-contact hoist. Refer to Section 00-02 .

 NOTE: This will allow the axle to pivot forward. 

Place screw-type jackstand under rear axle pinion nose. Remove rear 
axle differential rear insulator to axle housing cover retaining bolts and 
nuts. 

Install rear axle differential rear insulator bolt in lower bolt hole 
as shown. 

[FIGURE: E7056B.gif]

Mark driveshaft (4602) in relation to rear axle universal joint flange. 
Remove driveshaft retaining bolts. 

[FIGURE: E6760B.gif]

Slide driveshaft forward and rest on driveshaft center bridge support 
reinforcement (4A315). 

[FIGURE: E6761C.gif]

 WARNING: REAR AXLE HOUSING (4010) MUST ALWAYS BE SUPPORTED BY JACKSTAND. 

Remove rear axle differential front lower insulator retaining nuts. 

[FIGURE: E7057B.gif]

Slowly lower rear axle housing to access rear axle universal joint

[FIGURE: E7058D.gif]

Install Nm (lb-in) torque wrench on pinion nut. Record 
torque required to maintain rotation of pinion through several revolutions. 

[FIGURE: AE0226A.gif]

 NOTE: If installing new rear axle universal joint flange, it is not necessary 
to mark rear axle universal joint flange. 

Mark rear axle universal joint flange in relation to pinion stem so 
rear axle universal joint flange can be reinstalled in same position. 

[FIGURE: E7020D.gif]

While holding rear axle universal joint flange with Companion Flange 
Holding Tool T78P-4851-A, remove pinion nut. 

[FIGURE: E7061E.gif]

 CAUTION: The rear axle universal joint flange must never be hammered on or 
assembled with power tools. 

 NOTE: Use Companion Flange Remover T65L-4851-B or Puller Tool D80L-1002-L or 
equivalent (if required). 

Remove rear axle universal joint flange. 

[FIGURE: AE0225A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not damage rear axle housing. 

 NOTE: Place drain pan under rear axle housing.

Position screwdriver under flange of rear axle drive pinion seal and

[FIGURE: E7063C.gif]

 Pry up on metal flange of rear axle drive pinion seal. Install 
gripping pliers and strike with hammer until pinion seal is removed. Remove 
rear axle drive pinion shaft oil slinger (4670).

[FIGURE: E7064B.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Check rear axle universal joint flange for burrs. Remove burrs as 
necessary. Make sure surfaces of rear axle universal joint flange have not 
been damaged in removing driveshaft or in removing rear axle universal joint 
flange from pinion. The end of the rear axle universal joint flange that 
contacts bearing cone as well as nut counterbore and seal surface must be 
smooth and free of nicks. 

Make sure splines on drive pinion stem are free of burrs. If burrs are 
evident, remove them using a fine crocus cloth. Working in a rotating motion, 
wipe pinion clean. Clean flange yoke seal seat surface and install rear axle 
drive pinion seal on Pinion Seal Replacer T79P-4676-A. 

[FIGURE: E7065B.gif]

 CAUTION: Installation without proper tool may result in early flange yoke seal 
failure. If rear axle drive pinion seal becomes cocked during installation, 
remove and replace with new rear axle drive pinion seal. 

Install rear axle drive pinion seal in rear axle housing. 

[FIGURE: E7026D.gif]

 NOTE: Check rear axle universal joint flange for burrs. Remove burrs as 
necessary. Be sure surfaces of flange have not been damaged in removing 
driveshaft or in removing flange from pinion. The end of rear axle universal 
joint flange that contacts bearing cone as well as nut counterbore and seal 
surface must be smooth and free of nicks. 

Apply a small amount of SAE 80W-90 Premium Rear Axle Lubricant 
XY-80W90-QL or -KL meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A or equivalent to 
rear axle universal joint flange splines. 

 CAUTION: The rear axle universal joint flange must never be hammered on or 
assembled with power tools. 

Align mark on rear axle universal joint flange with mark on pinion 
stem. Install rear axle universal joint flange.

Install new pinion nut on pinion stem. Apply a small amount of SAE 
80W-90 Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or -KL or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A on washer side of nut. 

Hold rear axle universal joint flange with Companion Flange Holding 
Tool T78P-4851-A while tightening pinion nut. Rotate pinion occasionally to 
make sure of proper differential pinion bearing (4630) seating. 

[FIGURE: E7066B.gif]

Take frequent pinion bearing torque preload readings until original 
preload reading is obtained. 

[FIGURE: AE0226A.gif]

 NOTE: Refer to Adjustment Torque Specifications .

If original recorded preload is less than specification tighten used 
differential pinion bearing to 0.9-1.6 Nm (8-14 lb-in) and new 
differential pinion bearing to 1.8-3.2 Nm (16-28 lb-in). If 
preload is higher than specification, tighten to original reading as recorded. 

Never back off pinion nut to reduce preload. If reduced preload is 
required, a new differential drive pinion collapsible spacer (4662) and pinion 
nut must be installed. 

Using a jackstand, raise and locate rear axle housing on rear axle 
differential front lower insulator bolts. 

[FIGURE: E7059C.gif]

Install rear axle differential front lower insulator nuts. Tighten to 
92-136 Nm (68-100 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E7057B.gif]

Remove rear axle differential rear insulator bolt from pivot position. 

[FIGURE: E7067B.gif]

Install rear axle differential rear insulator bolts in axle housing 
cover mount. Tighten to 108-136 Nm (80-100 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E7068B.gif]

Align marks on driveshaft and rear axle universal joint flange. Install 
retaining bolts. Tighten to 95-130 Nm (70-95 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6760B.gif]

Fill rear axle housing with Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or 
-KL meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A or equivalent to 6 mm (1/4 inch) 
below the filler hole. For complete refill of traction-lok axles, add 4 ounces 
of Additive Friction Modifier C8AZ-19B546-A or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification EST-M2C118-A.

Install filler plug. Tighten to 28-40 Nm (21-29 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6749B.gif]

Lower vehicle.

retainer circlip. 

[FIGURE: E6981D.gif]

Lightly lubricate stub shaft splines with Premium Long-Life Grease 
XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B.

[FIGURE: E6984B.gif]

 NOTE: Do not damage the inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing 
seal. The inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal must be 
replaced whenever halfshaft is removed.

Remove differential plug from rear axle housing (RH side). 

[FIGURE: E4314G.gif]

 NOTE: A non-metallic mallet may be used to aid in seating driveshaft bearing 
retainer circlip into axle shaft groove. If a mallet is necessary, tap only on 
outboard CV joint stub shaft. 

With CV joint splines engaged with axle shaft (4234), push rear wheel 
knuckle inward to seat inboard CV joint driveshaft bearing retainer circlip in 
axle shaft. Use care to prevent damage to inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot 
bearing housing seal. 

[FIGURE: E6994B.gif]

Install rear suspension arm and bushing bolts and nuts. 

Align paint marks on rear suspension arm and bushing and knuckle 
bushing. Tighten bolts to 160-200 Nm (118-147 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6995B.gif]

Install rear suspension arm and bushing retaining bolt and nut. Tighten 
to 160-200 Nm (118-147 lb-ft). 

Install rear disc brake rotor and new pushnuts. Refer to Section 06-04 .

[FIGURE: F5192C.gif]

Install rear disc brake caliper over rear disc brake rotor with outer 
brake pad against the rear disc brake rotor braking surface. This will prevent 
pinching the piston boot between the inner rear brake shoe and lining (2200) 
and the piston. Refer to Section 06-04 . 

Install upper and lower disc brake caliper locating pins. Tighten to 
105-135 Nm (78-99 lb-ft). 

Install parking brake rear cable and conduit on the rear disc brake 
caliper. 

[FIGURE: AF0037A.gif]

Install parking brake cable adjustment clip. Refer to Section 06-05 . 

[FIGURE: E8312B.gif]

Install rear brake anti-lock sensor on each side of rear axle housing. 
Tighten to 19-27 Nm (14-20 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6989B.gif]

Fill axle with SAE 80W-90 Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or 
-KL or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A to 6 mm (0.250 inch) 
below filler hose. For traction-lok axles, add 118 ml (4 ounces) of Additive 
Friction Modifier C8AZ-19B546-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
EST-M2C118-A. Install axle filler plug and tighten to 28-40 Nm
 (21-29 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: Some vehicles are equipped with directional tires (note arrows on 
tires) and must be installed in their original positions. 

Install wheel and tire assembly.

 Differential Case Runout Check 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Differential Side Bearing Replacer

T57L-4221-A2

If differential ring gear and pinion runout check (performed before 
disassembly) exceeds specification, condition may be caused by warped ring 
gear, damaged differential case or loss of differential bearing preload. To 
determine the cause of excessive runout, proceed as follows: 

With differential ring gear and pinion removed, place differential 
case/gear subassembly with differential bearing and differential drive pinion 
bearing cup (4616) in rear axle housing. 

[FIGURE: E7041B.gif]

Install 6.731 mm (0.265-inch) differential bearing shim on LH side of 
subassembly. 

[FIGURE: AE0039A.gif]

Install LH bearing cap finger-tight. 

[FIGURE: E7043B.gif]

Install progressively larger differential bearing shims on RH side 
until largest differential bearing shim selected can be assembled with slight 
drag feel. 

[FIGURE: AE0143A.gif]

Install RH side bearing cap. Install bearing cap bolts. Tighten to 
95-115 Nm (70-84 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: AE0228A.gif]

Rotate assembly to make sure differential rotates freely. 

[FIGURE: E7502B.gif]

Install Dial Indicator With Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent. Check 
differential ring gear and pinion runout. 

[FIGURE: E7503D.gif]

If runout is within specification, original out-of-specification runout 
was caused by insufficient differential bearing preload. If runout exceeds 
specification, proceed to Step 9. 

Remove differential case from rear axle housing. 

[FIGURE: E7041B.gif]

Remove rear axle differential gear case bolts. Using drift that will 
bottom in ring gear bolt holes, strike at alternate holes around gear. Remove 
ring gear.

[FIGURE: E6262C.gif]

Install differential assembly in differential case without ring gears. 

[FIGURE: E7505B.gif]

Check runout of differential case flange with Dial Indicator With 
Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent. If runout is within specification 
(maximum 0.076 mm (0.003 inch)), install new differential ring gear. If runout 
exceeds specification, concern is due to either a differential cases or 
differential bearing. Inspect differential bearings. If differential bearings 
are not damaged, replace both differential case and differential bearing. 
Recheck runout with new parts.

[FIGURE: E7506C.gif]

 NOTE: Press against differential bearing only. 

Press new differential bearing on case hubs using Differential Side 
Bearing Replacer T57L-4221-A2 and install differential case in rear axle 
housing without differential ring gear. 

[FIGURE: AE0209A.gif]

Check differential case runout again with differential bearings. If 
runout is now within limits, use differential bearings for assembly. If runout 
is still excessive, differential case is damaged and should be replaced.

A selective drive pinion bearing adjustment shim (4663) (0.254 mm to

(4630) and pinion head. The shim compensates for machining variations in rear 
axle housing (4010), pinion and pinion bearings. The correct shim size will 
locate pinion for proper tooth contact with ring gear. Selecting correct drive

and pinion (4209) can be done by using Pinion Depth Gauge Set T79P-4020-A as 
described.

Refer to following illustration and assemble appropriate aligning

Place differential pinion bearing (new, or used if in good condition) 
over aligning disc and insert into rear axle pinion bearing cup (4628). Place 
front differential pinion bearing into rear axle pinion bearing cup and 
assemble tool handle into screw. Tighten to 2.26 Nm (20 
lb-in). 

[FIGURE: AE0221A.gif]

Make sure gauge handle adapter screw, aligning adapter, gauge disc and 
gauge block assembly are securely mounted between front differential pinion 
bearing and rear differential pinion bearing. Check tool handle torque prior 
to gauging to make sure front and rear differential pinion bearings are 
properly seated. This can affect final shim selection when improperly 
assembled. Clean rear axle pinion bearing cups and differential drive pinion 
bearing cup and differential pedestal surfaces thoroughly. Apply only light 
SAE 10W30 engine oil film on front differential pinion bearing and rear 
differential pinion bearing assemblies prior to gauging. 

Rotate gauge block several half turns to make sure rollers are properly 
seated in rear axle pinion bearing cups and differential drive pinion bearing 
cup. Rotational torque on gauge assembly should be 2.26 Nm 
(20 lb-in) with new differential pinion bearings. Final position should be 
approximately 45 degrees across gauge tube to make sure gauge block is in line 
with gauge tube high point. This area should be used for drive pinion bearing 
adjustment shim selection. Selection of drive pinion bearing adjustment shim 
with gauge block not lined up with tube high point will cause improper drive 
pinion bearing adjustment shim selection and may result in axle noise. 

 NOTE: Drive pinion bearing adjustment shims must be flat. Do not use dirty, 
bent, nicked or mutilated shims as a gauge. 

Use drive pinion bearing adjustment shims as gauge for shim selection. 
This will minimize errors in attempting to stack feeler gauge stock together. 
It also minimizes addition errors in calculating correct drive pinion bearing 
adjustment shim thickness. 

 NOTE: The same differential pinion bearing used in this procedure must be 
used in final assembly of rear axle assembly (4006). 

It is important to feel slight drag on drive pinion bearing adjustment 
shim for correct selection. Do not attempt to force drive pinion bearing 
adjustment shim between gauge block and gauge tube. This will minimize 
selection of shim thicker than required which results in deep tooth contact in 
final assembly of integral axles. 

Place drive pinion bearing adjustment shim on pinion shaft and press 
differential pinion bearing until firmly seated on shaft. 

[FIGURE: AE0040A.gif]

 Differential Case Installation � Condition 1 

Follow this procedure when only differential ring gear and pinion 
replacement is required and differential bearings (4221) and differential case 
(4204) do not require replacement. 

Remove differential caps and bolts. Identify RH cap, RH cup and 
differential bearing shim spacer to keep these components as RH and LH sets. 

Remove differential case subassembly using pry bar method. Reasonable 
effort will be required to remove subassembly if preload is within 
specification range. If subassembly can be removed by hand, use Differential 
Case Installation � Condition 2 as described for assembly. 

Replace differential ring gear and pinion using differential bearing 
shim components from original assembly and select drive pinion bearing 
adjustment shim as described. (Differential bearing shim (4067) may be reused 
with exception of drive pinion bearing adjustment shim which will require 
regauging to specification before assembly). 

Tighten rear axle differential gear case bolt (4216) in criss cross 
pattern. Tighten rear axle differential gear case bolt to 95-115 Nm
 (70-84 lb-ft).

Follow this procedure when original differential bearing shims are not 
available or when rear axle housing, differential case or differential bearing 
replacement is required. 

With pinion depth set and differential ring gear and pinion installed, 
place the differential case/gear subassembly with differential bearings and 
differential bearing cups (4222) in differential case. 

[FIGURE: E7508B.gif]

Install a 6.731 mm (0.265-inch) differential bearing shim on LH side. 

[FIGURE: AE0039A.gif]

Install LH bearing cap finger-tight. 

[FIGURE: E7510B.gif]

Install progressively larger differential bearing shims on the RH side 
until largest differential bearing shim selected can be assembled with slight 
drag. 

[FIGURE: E7511B.gif]

Install RH side bearing cap and differential bearing cap bolts. Tighten 
to 95-115 Nm (70-84 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: AE0228A.gif]

Rotate assembly to make sure differential operates freely. 

[FIGURE: E7511B.gif]

Using Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent, check 
differential ring gear and pinion backlash. If backlash is within 
specification, go to Step 14. If not within specification, go to Step 10. If 
zero backlash is measured, proceed with Step 8.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

The differential case (4204) assembly and differential ring gear and 
pinion (4209) should be inspected before they are removed from the carrier. 
These inspections help find the cause and solution for the condition. 

Wipe lubricant from internal working parts and inspect parts for wear 
or damage.

 Section 05-00 .

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Inspection After Disassembly of Carrier 

Thoroughly clean all parts. Always use new solvent when cleaning 
bearings. Do not spin dry bearings with compressed air. Oil bearings 
immediately with SAE 80W-90 Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or -KL or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A to prevent rusting. Inspect 
parts for damage. Clean inside of rear axle housing (4010) before building. 
When scored or chipped gearset is replaced, rear axle housing must be washed 
thoroughly. Inspections of individual parts are described below. 

 Gears 

Examine differential ring gear and pinion teeth for scoring, excessive 
wear, nicks or chipping. Worn, scored and damaged differential ring gear and 
pinions (4209) cannot be rebuilt to correct noisy condition. 

 Bearing Cups 

Check differential drive pinion bearing cups (4616) for deep scores, 
galling or spalling. If 0.038 mm (0.0015-inch) feeler gauge can be inserted 
between differential drive pinion bearing cup and bottom of its bore at any 
point around the differential drive pinion bearing cup, the differential drive 
pinion bearing cup must be reseated. 

 Universal Joint Flange, Rear Axle 

Make sure surfaces of the rear axle universal joint flange (4851) have 
not been damaged in removing driveshaft (4602) or in removing rear axle 
universal joint flange from differential ring gear and pinion. The end of 
flange that contacts bearing cone as well as nut counterbore and rear axle 
drive pinion seal (4676) must be smooth and free of nicks. 

 Cone and Roller Assemblies 

When operated in differential drive pinion bearing cups, bearing 
rollers must turn without roughness. Examine large end of rollers for wear 
(pitting, scoring, galling or spalling). If inspection reveals either a 
damaged differential drive pinion bearing cup or damaged differential pinion 
bearing (4630), replace both parts. 

 Carrier Housing 

Make sure differential bearing bores are smooth. Remove any nicks or 
burrs from mounting surfaces of rear axle housing.

 Differential Case 

Make sure hubs where differential bearings (4221) mount are smooth. 
Carefully examine differential case bearing shoulders, which may have been 
damaged when differential bearings were removed. The bearing assemblies will 
fail if they do not seat firmly against the shoulders. Check fit (free 
rotation) of the differential bearings in their counterbores.

Section 05-02C: Differential, Traction-Lok Limited Slip � 7.5-Inch Ring Gear

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Description 

 WARNING: TO AVOID INJURY, NEVER RUN THE ENGINE WITH ONE WHEEL OFF THE GROUND, 
SUCH AS WHEN CHANGING A TIRE. THE WHEEL STILL ON THE GROUND COULD CAUSE THE 
VEHICLE TO MOVE. 

 NOTE: Replacement of the Traction-Lok® differential clutch 
pack (4947) on Thunderbird and Cougar independent rear suspension vehicles 
requires removal of the halfshafts and differential carrier.

The Traction-Lok® axle assembly, except for the 
differential case (4204) and its internal components, is identical to the 
conventional axle. 

The Traction-Lok® differential employs two sets of 
differential clutch packs to control differential action. 

The differential side gear mounting distance is controlled by seven 
plates (three steel, four friction) and one rear axle differential clutch shim 
(4A324) by select size to control differential side gear position. 

The plates are stacked on the differential side gear (4236) and are 
housed in the differential case.

Also located in the differential case, between the differential side 
gears, is a one-piece differential clutch spring (4214) which applies a 
pre-loaded initial force to the differential clutch packs. 

Additional clutch capacity is delivered from the differential side 
gear's thrust loads. 

The three steel plates are stacked between the four friction plates and 
are splined to the differential side gear hub. The side gear hub is splined to 
the halfshaft. 

The friction plates are tabbed to the differential case so the 
differential clutch packs are always engaged.

Section 05-02C: Differential, Traction-Lok Limited Slip � 7.5-Inch Ring Gear

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Operation

 CAUTION: Extended use of other than matching size tires on a Traction-Lok®
 rear axle could result in reduction in effectiveness (bias 
torque). This loss of effectiveness does not affect normal driving and should 
not be noticeable to the driver. However, extended usage will reduce the 
ability of the axle to provide added traction on slippery surfaces. 

Differential action is accomplished as follows:

The pressure between the differential clutch plates opposes 
differential action at all times. 

When the vehicle turns a corner, the differential clutch plates slip, 
allowing normal differential action to take place. 

Under adverse weather conditions where one or both wheels may be on a 
low-traction surface such as snow, ice or mud, the friction between the clutch 
plates will transfer a portion of the usable torque to the wheels with the 
most traction. The wheel on ice or snow will have a tendency to operate with 
the opposite wheel in a combined driving effort.

1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 05-02C: Differential, Traction-Lok Limited Slip � 7.5-Inch Ring Gear

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Noise Acceptability 

 NOTE: Vehicles equipped with a Traction-Lok® differential 
may exhibit a slight stick-slip noise on tight turns after extended highway 
driving. This is considered acceptable and has no detrimental effect. 

A gear-driven unit, such as automotive drive axles, will produce a 
certain amount of noise. Some noise is acceptable and may be heard at certain 
speeds or under various driving conditions; for example, on a newly paved 
blacktop road. The slight noise is not detrimental to rear axle operation and 
is normal.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Differential, Traction-Lok Limited Slip

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Gear Rotator

T84P-4205-A

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the differential bearings (4221) from the 
differential case journals unless they are damaged. If the differential 
bearings remain on the differential case (4204) during service, keep them 
clean and free from foreign material. 

Remove and discard 10 rear axle differential gear case bolts (4216), 
retaining ring gear to differential case. 

Remove ring gear by tapping with a soft-faced hammer or press gear from 
differential case. 

Remove differential pinion shaft lock pin (4241) and remove 
differential pinion shaft (4211). 

 WARNING: USE CARE WHEN REMOVING THE DIFFERENTIAL CLUTCH SPRING (4214) BECAUSE OF 
SPRING TENSION. 

With a suitable drift, drive out the S-shaped, pre-loaded differential 
clutch spring. Hold differential clutch spring with pliers and tap 
differential clutch spring until it is removed from the differential case. 

[FIGURE: E5484C.gif]

Using Gear Rotator T84P-4205-A, rotate differential pinion gears (4215) 
until differential pinion gears and differential pinion thrust washers (4230) 
can be removed. 

 Traction-Lok Differential � Disassembly 

[FIGURE: E5485F.gif]

Remove differential side gears (4236), differential clutch packs (4947) 
and rear axle differential clutch shims (4A324) from RH and LH cavities and 
tag them "RH" and "LH."

 NOTE: Do not use cleaning solvents on friction plate surfaces. Wipe clean 
only. 

Clean and inspect all parts for wear or damage. Replace as necessary. 

Adjust clutch pack preload as described.

 Assembly 

Lubricate all parts with Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or -KL 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A. Soak all friction 
plates in Additive Friction Modifier C8AZ-19B546-A or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification EST-M2C118-A for 15 minutes prior to assembly. 

Mount the differential case in a soft-jaw vise and place the 
differential clutch packs and differential side gears in their proper cavities 
in the differential case. 

Place the differential pinion gears and differential pinion thrust 
washers on the differential side gears. 

 Traction-Lok Differential � Assembly 

[FIGURE: E9139A.gif]

Install Gear Rotator T84P-4205-A in the differential case. 

Rotate differential pinion gears until the bores in the differential 
pinion gears are aligned with differential pinion shaft holes in the 
differential case. Remove tool from differential case. 

 NOTE: Inspect the differential clutch spring for damage. 

With a soft-faced hammer, install the S-shaped, pre-loaded differential 
clutch spring in the differential case. If necessary, complete installation of 
S-shaped, pre-loaded differential clutch spring with a brass drift.

[FIGURE: E5484C.gif]

 NOTE: Differential pinion shaft lock pin should be replaced with a new 
differential pinion shaft lock pin. If new differential pinion shaft lock pin 
is not available, coat threads with Stud and Bearing Mount E0AZ-19554-BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G349-A1 and tighten to 20-41 Nm
 (15-30 Lb-Ft).

Clean tapped holes in ring gear with a suitable solvent. If the new 
rear axle differential ring gear bolts (4558) to be used show a green coating 
over approximately 12.7 mm (1/2 inch) of the threaded area, use as is. If not 
coated, apply a small amount of Stud and Bearing Mount E0AZ-19554-BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G349-A1. Tighten to 95-115 Nm
 (70-84 lb-ft). 

To install the differential case and ring gear, refer to Section 05-02A .

Bench Torque Test 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Tool Number

Traction-Lok® Torque Tool

T59L-4204-A

Prior to installation of locking differential into vehicle, perform a 
bench torque check.

 NOTE: The initial breakaway torque should be at least 27 Nm

turning with new differential clutch packs (4947) may fluctuate.

 If torque reading is less than 27 Nm (20 lb-ft), 
check the differential for proper assembly.

Using Gear Rotator T80P-4205-A, rotate the differential pinion gears 
(4215) until the differential pinion gears and differential pinion thrust 
washers (4230) can be removed. 

 Traction-Lok Differential � Disassembly 

[FIGURE: E3961G.gif]

Remove the differential side gears (4236), differential clutch packs 
(4947) and rear axle differential clutch shims (4A324) from the RH and LH 
cavities and tag them "RH" and "LH." 

 NOTE: Do not use cleaning solvents on friction plate surfaces. Wipe clean 
only. 

Clean and inspect all parts for wear or damage. Replace as necessary. 

Adjust clutch pack preload as described.

 Assembly 

Lubricate all parts with Premium Rear Axle Lubricant XY-80W90-QL or -KL 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSP-M2C197-A. Soak all friction 
clutch plates in Additive Friction Modifier C8AZ-19B546-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification EST-M2C118-A for at least 15 minutes prior to 
assembly.

Mount the differential case in a soft-jaw vise and place the 
differential clutch packs and differential side gears in their proper cavities 
in the differential case. 

Place the differential pinion gears and differential pinion thrust 
washers on the differential side gears. 

 Traction-Lok Differential � Assembly 

[FIGURE: E7545E.gif]

Install Gear Rotator T80P-4205-A in the differential case. 

Rotate the differential pinion gears until the bores in the 
differential pinion gears are aligned with the differential pinion shaft holes 
in the differential case. Remove the tool from the differential case. 

 NOTE: Inspect the differential clutch spring for damage.

With a soft-faced hammer, install the S-shaped, pre-loaded differential 
clutch spring in the differential case. If necessary, complete installation of 
S-shaped, pre-loaded differential clutch spring with a brass drift. 

[FIGURE: E5484C.gif]

 NOTE: Differential pinion shaft lock pin should be replaced with a new 
differential pinion shaft lock pin. If new differential pinion shaft lock pin 
is not available, coat threads with Stud and Bearing Mount E0AZ-19554-BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G349-A1 and tighten to 20-40 Nm
 (15-29 lb-ft). 

Install the differential pinion shaft and differential pinion shaft 
lock pin.

Clean the tapped holes in the ring gear with a suitable solvent. If the 
new rear axle differential ring gear bolts (4558) to be used show a green 
coating over approximately 12.7 mm (1/2 inch) of the threaded area, use as is. 
If not coated, apply a small amount of Stud and Bearing Mount E0AZ-19554-BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G349-A1. Tighten to 95-115 Nm
 (70-84 lb-ft). 

To install differential case and ring gear, refer to Section 05-02B .

Section 05-05: Halfshafts, Rear Drive

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Halfshafts, Rear Drive

The rear wheel drive halfshaft system is assembled and installed as 
follows:

Constant velocity (CV) joints at both its inboard (differential) and 
outboard (wheel) ends provide operating smoothness. 

CV joints are connected by an interconnecting shaft which is splined at 
both ends and retained in the inboard and outboard CV joints by driveshaft 
bearing retainer circlips (3Z498).

The inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing (4B413) is 
splined and held in the differential side gear (4236) by a driveshaft bearing 
retainer circlip. 

The outboard rear wheel driveshaft and joint is pressed into the rear 
hub (1109) and secured with a rear axle wheel hub retainer (4B477). 

The CV joints are lubed-for-life with a special CV joint grease and 
require no periodic lubrication. 

The rear axle shaft outer boot (4A331)/rear axle shaft inner boot 
(4L537), however, should be periodically inspected and replaced immediately 
when damage or grease leakage is evident. 

Continued operation would result in CV joint wear and noise due to 
contamination or loss of the CV joint grease. 

Halfshaft removal from the differential is accomplished by applying a 
load to the back face of the inboard CV joint assembly to overcome the 
driveshaft bearing retainer circlip. 

The outboard joint end must be pressed from the rear hub. 

The inboard tripod CV joints can be disassembled and serviced. 

Other than the rear axle cv joint boot (4697), the outboard CV joint is 
serviced only as an assembly with the outboard CV joint/interconnecting shaft.

Rear halfshafts operate as follows:

The primary purpose of the halfshaft is to transmit engine torque from 
the rear axle housing (4010) to the rear wheels. 

CV joints are capable of operating at varying angles and provide a 
means of shaft length changes to allow for vertical suspension (wheel) and 
engine dynamic movement. 

These requirements are satisfied by using CV joints at the inboard 
(differential) end and outboard (wheel) end of the halfshaft. 

A CV joint is a mechanism for transmitting uniform torque and rotary 
motion while operating through its angle range. 

The inboard CV joint is a plunge-type joint which provides for the 
required axial movement to affect shaft length changes. 

The outboard CV joint has a higher angle capability than the inboard CV 
joint to accommodate suspension travel. 

The CV joints and halfshaft assemblies rotate at approximately 
one-third the speed of the driveshaft (4602) and do not contribute to 
rotational vibration disturbances.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Halfshaft Handling 

 CAUTION: Never hold the CV joint and halfshaft assembly by the inboard cv joint 
stub shaft pilot bearing housing (4B413) or outboard joint only. 

Handle all rear drive halfshaft components carefully during halfshaft 
removal and installation and during various component disassembly and assembly 
procedures as described. 

Do not remove inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing by 
pulling on interconnecting shaft. 

The complete halfshaft should be handled by the interconnecting shaft 
to avoid pull-apart and potential damage to the inboard cv joint stub shaft 
pilot bearing housing. 

Do not over-angle CV joints beyond their capacity. 

Make sure ground surfaces and splines are not damaged. 

Do not allow rear axle shaft outer boots (4A331)/rear axle shaft inner 
boots (4L537) to come into contact with sharp edges or hot exhaust components. 

Do not drop assembled halfshafts, as the impact will cut the rear axle 
shaft outer boot/rear axle shaft inner boot from the inside without external 
evidence of damage. 

Never use halfshaft assembly as a lever arm to position other rear end 
components. Always support free end of halfshaft. 

Keep internal CV joint clean and maintain proper grease refill when 
rear axle shaft outer boot/rear axle shaft inner boot is replaced. 

An assembled inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing may be 
damaged if it is over-plunged outward from the joint housing. 

Never use a hammer to remove or install halfshafts.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Traction-Lok Differential 

 WARNING: A VEHICLE EQUIPPED WITH A TRACTION-LOK DIFFERENTIAL WILL ALWAYS HAVE 
BOTH WHEELS DRIVING. IF WHILE THE VEHICLE IS BEING SERVICED ONLY ONE WHEEL IS 
RAISED OFF THE FLOOR, THE WHEEL ON THE FLOOR COULD DRIVE THE VEHICLE OFF THE 
STAND OR JACK. MAKE SURE BOTH REAR WHEELS ARE OFF THE FLOOR.

Wheel and Tire Balancing, Rear

COULD RESULT, CAUSING PERSONAL INJURY AND/OR EXTENSIVE COMPONENT DAMAGE. USE 
OFF-VEHICLE WHEEL AND TIRE BALANCER ONLY.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Undercoating and Rustproofing 

During undercoating and rustproofing procedures, be very careful to 
protect rear axle shaft outer boots (4A331)/rear axle shaft inner boot (4L537) 
from coating materials. Foreign materials on the rubber boot convolutions will 
cause extreme advanced wear.

Halfshaft Assembly 

 Disc Brakes

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Do not begin this procedure unless the following parts are available: 

 new rear axle wheel hub retainer (4B477) (Step 1) 

 new driveshaft bearing retainer circlip (3Z498) 

 new inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal (4B416) 

Once removed, these parts must not be reused during assembly. Their 
torque holding ability or retention capability is diminished during removal.

Remove wheel covers (1130) and remove rear axle wheel hub retainers 
using a 36 mm socket. Loosen lug nuts (1012). 

[FIGURE: F5191D.gif]

 CAUTION: A frame contact hoist must be used to avoid damage to the halfshafts or 
rear axle shaft outer boot (4A331)/rear axle shaft inner boot (4L537). 

Raise vehicle on a frame contact hoist.

Remove lug nuts and remove rear wheel and tire assemblies. 

 CAUTION: Rear brake anti-lock sensors (2C190) must be removed before halfshaft 
removal to prevent damage to the rear brake anti-lock sensors. 

Remove retaining bolt and rear brake anti-lock sensors. 

[FIGURE: E6989B.gif]

Using needle nose pliers, slide parking brake cable adjuster (2B599) 
downward until parking brake rear cable and conduit (2A635) is free. 

[FIGURE: E8311A.gif]

Remove parking brake rear cable and conduit from rear disc brake 
caliper (2552). 

[FIGURE: AF0037A.gif]

Remove upper and lower disc brake caliper locating pins (2B296). 

Remove rear disc brake caliper from rear disc brake rotor (2C026). 
Refer to Section 06-04 . 

 WARNING: EXTREME CARE MUST BE TAKEN NOT TO STRETCH, TWIST OR KINK REAR BRAKE 
HOSE (2282). 

Carefully wire rear disc brake caliper to brake line junction bracket 
as shown. 

[FIGURE: F5187C.gif]

Remove brake rotor pushnuts and remove rear disc brake rotor. 

[FIGURE: E6990B.gif]

Remove upper rear suspension arm and bushing bolt and nuts. 

[FIGURE: E6991B.gif]

Wire rear suspension arm and bushing (5500) to shock absorber (18080) 
so it does not interfere with or damage rear axle cv joint boots (4697) when 
halfshaft is removed. 

[FIGURE: F5188B.gif]

 CAUTION: Failure to mark this position will result in bushing wind-up on 
assembly and incorrect ride height, causing misalignment and premature tire 
wear. 

 NOTE: When rear suspension arm and bushing bolt is removed from the rear 
wheel knuckle (5A969), the lower bushings will return to their relaxed 
positions. 

Using a paint marker, mark the position of the rear suspension arm and 
bushing in relation to the rear wheel knuckle with the lower bushings in their 
relaxed position. 

[FIGURE: F5190B.gif]

 NOTE: Metric adapters (12 mm) make sure the adapters are fully threaded onto 
the hub studs and are positioned opposite the other adapter.

Attach Front Hub Remover/Replacer T81P-1104-C, Metric Hub Remover 
Adapters M12 x 1.5 T83P-1104-BH and Two Stud Adapter T86P-1104-A1 to hub studs 
as shown. With wrench, turn nut counterclockwise while holding wrench on 
threaded rod stationary until halfshaft is free in rear hub (1109). 

[FIGURE: F5189F.gif]

Remove rear suspension arm and bushing retaining bolts. 

[FIGURE: E6992B.gif]

Remove rear wheel knuckle while supporting outboard CV joint and rear 
axle cv joint boot. Carefully rest halfshaft on rear suspension arm and 
bushing. 

[FIGURE: F5193B.gif]

 CAUTION: Extreme care must be taken to prevent damage to the inboard cv joint 
stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal, rear axle housing (4010), rear brake 
anti-lock sensor indicator (2C189) or CV joint and rear axle cv joint boot. 

Insert CV Joint Remover T89P-3514-A between rear axle housing and 
inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing (4B413) and push tool 
outboard until inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing becomes free 
from differential side gear (4236). 

[FIGURE: E6757C.gif]

Remove halfshaft assembly from vehicle. 

[FIGURE: E6758B.gif]

Insert Differential Plug T89P-4850-B into rear axle housing to prevent 
loss of lubricant. 

[FIGURE: E6759C.gif]

 Installation 

Remove Differential Plug T89P-4850-B. 

Replace inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal. Refer 
to Section 05-02A (7.5 Inch Ring Gear) or Section 05-02B (8.8 Inch Ring Gear) 
for procedure. 

 NOTE: To install driveshaft bearing retainer circlip properly, start ends in 
groove and push driveshaft bearing retainer circlip into groove. This will 
prevent overexpanding of the driveshaft bearing retainer circlip. 

Install a new driveshaft bearing retainer circlip on inboard cv joint 
stub shaft pilot bearing housing. 

[FIGURE: E6981D.gif]

Lightly lubricate stub shaft splines with Constant Velocity Joint 
Grease (High Temp) E43Z-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESP-M1C207-A.

[FIGURE: E6984B.gif]

Carefully align splines of inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing 
housing with splines in differential side gear.

[FIGURE: E4314G.gif]

 NOTE: A non-metallic mallet may be used to aid in seating driveshaft bearing 
retainer circlip into differential side gear groove. If a mallet is necessary, 
tap only on the outboard CV joint stub shaft until circlip engages. 

Push halfshaft into differential side gear until driveshaft bearing 
retainer circlip engages with groove in differential side gear. Use care to 
prevent damage to inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing seal. 

[FIGURE: E6985D.gif]

Engage hub splines with outboard CV joint splines.

[FIGURE: F5193B.gif]

Install lower rear suspension arm bolts to rear wheel knuckle. Using 
inboard wrench as a lever, align paint mark on rear suspension arm and bushing 
with mark on rear wheel knuckle/bushing and tighten bolts to 160-200 Nm
 (118-147 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6992B.gif]

Install a new rear axle wheel hub retainer and pull CV joint into rear 
hub as far as possible by hand. 

[FIGURE: E6999C.gif]

Install rear suspension arm and bushing-to-rear wheel knuckle retaining 
bolt and nut. Tighten bolt to 160-200 Nm (118-147 lb-ft). 

Install rear disc brake rotor. Install new rotor pushnuts. 

[FIGURE: F5192C.gif]

Install the rear disc brake caliper to the rear disc brake rotor with 
the outer brake shoe against the braking surface of the rear disc brake 
rotors. This prevents pinching the piston boot between the inner brake shoe 
and the piston. Refer to Section 06-04 . 

Install disc brake caliper locating pin and tighten to 108-135 Nm
 (80-99 lb-ft). 

Install parking brake rear cable and conduit to rear disc brake caliper 
(2553). 

[FIGURE: AF0037A.gif]

Install parking brake cable adjuster. Refer to Section 06-05 . 

[FIGURE: E8312B.gif]

Install rear brake anti-lock sensors. Tighten retaining bolts to 19-27 Nm
 (14-20 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E6989B.gif]

Check axle lube level and fill as necessary. 

Check driveshaft bearing retainer circlip engagement by attempting to 
pull inboard cv joint stub shaft pilot bearing housing from axle. If 
driveshaft bearing retainer circlip is not seated, push CV joint in until 
driveshaft bearing retainer circlip is fully engaged in differential side gear. 

[FIGURE: E7548B.gif]

Install wheel and tire assembly. Tighten lug nuts to 115-142 Nm
 (85-104 lb-ft). 

Lower vehicle. 

Tighten rear axle wheel hub retainer to 340 Nm (250 
lb-ft). 

Install wheel cover.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Master Cylinder, Dual 

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THOROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

The brake master cylinder (2140) contains the following features:

The brake master cylinder has a common plastic hydraulic control unit 
reservoir (2C246) and fluid level indicator combined in one assembly.

The ABS brake master cylinder has a fitting for connecting the 
hydraulic control unit (HCU) supply hose.

The dual hydraulic brake system is a conventional, pedal-actuated 
system with a brake master cylinder, brake pressure control valve (2B091) and 
brake tubes and hoses.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Pressure Control Valve

The brake pressure control valve (2B091) operates as follows:

Thebrake pressure control valve regulates hydraulic pressure in the 
rear brake system.

Vehicles with 3.8L engine and not equipped with anti-lock brakes use two 
brake pressure control valves located in the rear brake outlet ports of brake 
master cylinder (2140).

All others use remote-mounted brake pressure control valves.

When brake pedal (2455) is applied, the full rear brake fluid pressure 
passes through the proportioning valve to the rear brake system until the 
valve's split point is reached.

Above its split point, the proportioning valve begins to reduce the 
hydraulic pressure to the rear brakes.

The reduced pressure creates a balanced braking condition between the 
front and rear wheels to minimize rear wheel skidding during hard braking.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Hydraulic

This vehicle is equipped with a pedal-actuated hydraulic dual brake 
system. The system consists of the following:

power brake booster (2005)

brake master cylinder (2140)

brake pressure control valve (2B091)

brake tubes and brake hoses

The dual hydraulic system is diagonally split with the LH front and RH 
rear making up the secondary circuit and the RH front and LH rear making up 
the primary circuit.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Booster, Power Brake 

The diaphragm-type power brake booster (2005):

is self-contained.

is mounted on the engine side of the dash panel.

uses engine intake manifold vacuum and atmospheric pressure for its 
power.

must be replaced with a new power brake booster if it becomes damaged 
or inoperative.

uses a power brake booster check valve (2365) to provide temporary 
power assist when the vacuum source is reduced.

The power brake booster check valve and grommet are serviced 
separately. The hose is serviced as an assembly with the check valve.

The power brake booster is serviced only as an assembly.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brakes, Front Disc

The front disc brakes consist of the following features:

A hydraulically activated pin slider-type front disc brake caliper 
(2B120) assembly with a 276 mm (10.9 inch) or 294 mm (11.6 inch) full cast, 
vented front disc brake rotor (1125).

Yellow paint is used to match front disc brake rotor with the front hub 
to minimize front brake rotor runout. Replacement front disc brake rotors 
should be match-mounted to front hub as described.

The disc brake caliper has a steel caliper piston (2196) with a piston 
seal and a press-in type dust boot.

The disc brake caliper is attached to the front suspension spindle with 
a front disc brake anchor plate.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brakes, Rear Disc

The rear disc brakes consist of:

vented full cast rear disc brake rotor (2C026).

hydraulically-activated caliper assemblies with integral mechanically 
(cable) operated parking brake mechanism.

Except for the parking brake mechanism, the rear disc brake caliper 
(2553) assembly is similar to the front disc brake caliper (2B120). 

The added parking brake lever on the back of the rear disc brake 
caliper is cable-operated by the parking brake control (2780) which is located 
below the instrument panel. 

The caliper parking brake mechanism is self-adjusting.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brakes, Rear Drum

Rear drum brakes are non-servo, leading/trailing shoe design. The rear 
drum brakes function as follows:

Rear drum brakes use internal, hydraulically actuated, expanding rear 
brake shoe and lining (2200) that are applied against a rotating brake drum 
(1126).

An incremental self-adjuster mechanism is actuated whenever sufficient 
wear occurs.

Brake adjustment takes place in forward or reverse braking. 

All models equipped with rear drum brakes use a 250 mm (9.84 inch) 
diameter brake assembly.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Parking 

The parking brake system functions as follows:

The system is cable-actuated and controlled by an independent, 
foot-operated parking brake control (2780).

The parking brake warning indicator is activated by the parking brake 
control and warns the driver to release the parking brake control before 
driving the vehicle. If indicator remains lighted, brake system service is 
required. 

The foot-operated parking brake control is released by depressing the 
parking brake pedal. A click will be heard signaling release and parking brake 
pedal can be seen returning to the OFF position. Upon returning to the full 
OFF position, the parking brake control will reset itself to lock upon the 
next parking brake pedal application.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Anti-Lock

The ABS is a four-wheel system which prevents wheel lockup by 
automatically modulating the brake pressure during an emergency stop. By 
preventing the wheels from locking, it enables the driver to maintain steering 
control and stop in the shortest possible distance under most conditions.

During normal braking, the ABS and non-ABS brake pedal feel will be the 
same. During ABS operation, a pulsation can be felt in the brake pedal (2455), 
accompanied by a fall and then a rise in the brake pedal height and a clicking 
sound.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Brake System

 Inspection and Verification 

 Road Test 

Perform a road test to compare actual vehicle braking performance with 
the performance standards expected by the driver. The ability of the test 
driver to make valid comparisons and detect performance deficiencies will 
depend on experience. 

The driver should have a thorough knowledge of brake system operation 
and accepted general performance guidelines in order to make good comparisons 
and detect performance concerns.

An experienced brake technician will always establish a route that will 
be used for all brake diagnosis road tests. The road selected will be 
reasonably smooth and level. Gravel or bumpy roads are not suitable because 
the surface does not allow the tires to grip the road equally. Crowned roads 
should be avoided because of the large amount of weight shifted to the low set 
of wheels on this type of road. Once the route is established and consistently 
used, the road surface variable can be eliminated from the test results. 

Before a road test, get a complete description of the customer concerns 
or suspected condition. From the description, the technician's experience will 
allow the technician to match possible causes with symptoms. Certain 
components will be tagged as possible suspects while others will be eliminated 
by the evidence. More importantly, the customer's description can reveal 
unsafe conditions which should be checked or corrected before the road test. 
The description will also help form the basic approach to the road test by 
narrowing the problem to specific components, vehicle speed or conditions. 

Begin the road test with a general brake performance check. Keeping the 
description in mind, test the brakes at different vehicle speeds using both 
light and heavy pedal pressure. To determine if the problem is in the front or 
rear braking system, first use the brake pedal (2455), then use the parking 
brake. If the condition (pull, vibration, pulsation, for example) occurs only 
with the parking brake, the concern is in the rear system. 

If a concern exists, use the Brake System Symptom Chart in order to 
isolate it to a specific sub-system and condition description. From this 
description, a list of possible sources can be used to further narrow the 
cause to a specific component or condition.

Refer to the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual for connector 
numbers cited in the pinpoint tests.

pinpoint tests.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Hydraulic Leak Test

It is possible that all evidence of fluid leakage may have washed off 
if the vehicle has been operated in rain or snow, as brake fluid is water 
soluble. Refill system, bleed, and apply the brake pedals (2455) several 
times. Examine the system to verify that the brake master cylinder reservoir 
is actually dropping. Locate and correct the external leak. If fluid level 
drops and no external leak can be found, check for a master cylinder bore end 
seal leak.

================================================================================
PAGE 2469
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 06-00: Brake System � Service

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Brake System Test Procedure

 Brake Pedal Reserve Check 

Where a low brake pedal (2455) or the feel of a bottomed-out condition 
exists, check for brake pedal reserve. 

Operate engine at idle with the transmission in either PARK or NEUTRAL. 

Depress brake pedal lightly three to four times. 

Allow 15 seconds for vacuum to replenish power brake booster (2005). 

 NOTE: This increased resistance may feel like something has bottomed out. 

Apply brake pedal until it stops moving downward or an increased 
resistance to the brake pedal travel occurs. 

Hold brake pedal in applied position and raise the engine speed to 
approximately 2000 rpm. 

 NOTE: The additional movement of the brake pedal is the result of the 
increased engine manifold vacuum which exerts more force on the power brake 
booster during engine rundown. This means that additional stroke is available 
in the brake master cylinder (2140) and the brake system is not bottoming out 
as a customer may believe. 

Release accelerator pedal and observe that brake pedal moves downward 
as engine returns to idle speed.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Brake Hose 

A flexible brake hose should be replaced if it shows signs of 
softening, cracking or other damage. 

Positioning of front brake hose (2078) to disc brake caliper (2B120) is 
controlled by a self-indexing brass block. When retaining brake hose 
connection to disc brake caliper, tighten bolt to 40-60 Nm 
(30-44 lb-ft). Attach intermediate bracket to front shock absorber (18124) and 
tighten screw to specification. Engage opposite end of front brake hose to 
bracket on body. Install horseshoe-type retaining clip and connect tube to 
front brake hose with tube nut. Inspect position of installed front brake hose 
for clearance to other chassis components. 

Positioning of rear brake hose (2282) is controlled by self-indexing 
end fittings.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Service Precautions 

Grease or any other foreign material must be kept off the brake lining 
surfaces and the braking surfaces of the disc brake rotor. In handling the 
disc brake rotor and disc brake caliper (2B120) assemblies, avoid deformation 
of the disc brake rotor and nicking, scratching or dropping of brake shoe and 
linings. 

During removal and installation of a wheel assembly, exercise care not 
to interfere with the front disc brake rotor shield (2K005) or the bleeder 
screw fitting. 

Never use a twin post hoist to raise a rear wheel drive vehicle with 
independent rear suspension. 

Do not attempt to clean or restore any oil or grease-soaked brake shoes 
and linings. When contaminated brake shoes and linings are found, they must be 
replaced in complete axle sets. 

When replacing disc brake rotors after machining or new part 
replacement, make sure hub surface that contacts the wheel, and the rotor 
surfaces that contact the hub or wheel are free of dirt, rust or other 
contaminants. Apply High Temperature Nickel Anti-Sieze Lubricant F6AZ-9L494-AA 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M12A4-A to hub face. Avoid 
getting lubricant on wheel studs.

Brakes, Drum 

Raise vehicle on hoist. Refer to Section 00-02 .

Removal of dust and dirt from brake drum assemblies should be done by

[FIGURE: H7966A.gif]

Inspect the rear brake shoes and linings (2200) for excessive lining

rivet heads or 1.5 mm (1/16 inch) of the shoe on bonded linings or if the

Prior to replacement of lining, the brake drum diameter should be checked to 
determine that the brake drum braking surface diameter is within specification 
by using the Rotunda Brake Drum Micrometer 104-00046 or equivalent. If the 
braking surface diameter exceeds specification, the brake drum must be 
replaced. 

 Maximum Braking Surface 

[FIGURE: H9043B.gif]

 Maximum Braking Surface Specification 

[FIGURE: H3312C.gif]

Check the condition of rear brake shoe and lining, retracting springs, 
brake shoe hold-down spring (2068) and brake drum for signs of overheating. If 
the brake drum has a slight blue coloring, indicating overheating, the 
retracting and brake shoe hold-down springs should be replaced. Overheated 
brake shoe hold-down springs lose their tension and could cause the new lining 
to wear prematurely if not replaced. If the brake drums are heat-spotted, 
indicating an overheated condition, they should be replaced.

Inspect all other brake parts and replace any that are worn or damaged. 

Inspect the brake drum and if necessary, refinish. The maximum inside 
braking surface diameter is shown on each brake drum. If the maximum inside 
braking surface diameter shown on the brake drum is exceeded either by wear or 
refinishing, the brake drum must be replaced.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Hydraulic System 

An inspection of the brake hydraulic system begins with a fluid level 
check. If the fluid level is below the MAX line in the hydraulic control unit 
reservoir (2C246), add the required amount of fluid. Use High Performance 
DOT-3 Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M6C25-A.

 Brake Master Cylinder 

When in the brake master cylinder area, check the brake tubes and brake 
master cylinder mounting. The brake tubes and attaching nuts must be tight. 
The brake tube fittings must not show any sign of leakage. Tighten the brake 
tubes at the brake master cylinder (2140) to 13-22 Nm (10-16 
lb-ft).

The following conditions are considered normal and are not indications 
that the brake master cylinder is in need of service:

Low fluid level detected without signs of leakage; this condition is 
caused by displacement of fluid from the hydraulic control unit reservoir into 
the disc brake calipers (2B120) to compensate for normal brake wear. Add fluid 
as needed.

A momentary or slight squirt of brake fluid within the hydraulic 
control unit reservoir upon application of the brake pedal (2455); this 
condition is caused by fluid displacement through the brake master cylinder 
reservoir compensating port as the brake master cylinder pistons move forward 
in the bore when the brakes are applied.

Slight turbulence in the brake master cylinder reservoir fluid when the 
brake pedal is released; turbulence occurs as brake fluid returns to the brake 
master cylinder after releasing the brakes.

A trace of brake fluid found on the outside of the power brake booster 
(2005) below the brake master cylinder mounting flange; this condition results 
from the lubricating action of the master cylinder wiping seal.

 Brake Tubing 

Inspect the brake tubes under the vehicle for damage and proper 
routing. Check the hoses connecting the brake tubes to the front disc brake 
calipers to the rear drum brake wheel cylinders or rear disc brake calipers 
(2552) for any signs of damage, cracking or softening. The hose fittings must 
be tight without signs of leakage.

Double wall steel tubing is used throughout the brake system with the 
exception of the front brake hose (2078) at the front wheels and at the rear 
axle housing brake tube connection. 

Always bleed the applicable primary or secondary brake system after 
primary or secondary brake system hose or tube replacement. Bleed the longest 
tube first.

When connecting a tube to a hose, tube connector or brake cylinder, 
tighten the tube fitting nut to specification.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Parking Brake

Check the parking brake rear cable and conduit (2A635) for damage and 
proper routing. If the parking brake rear cable and conduit is damaged, it 
must be replaced. Refer to Section 06-05 .

Check to make sure the parking brake intermediate cable (2A620) is not 
sagging or loose and the tiedown strap is tightened around sub-frame and 
parking brake cable adjuster (2B599).

Operate the parking brake control (2780) and check for conditions that 
may cause binding, groaning or an incomplete release of the parking brake.

Verify the parking brake control lever stroke is five to seven notches 
when applied with a foot pedal force of 445 N (100 lb).

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake Pedal Free Height Measurements 

With the engine running for full power brake operation and the parking 
brake fully released, measure the brake pedal free height. 

Insert a slender, sharp-pointed prod through the carpet and sound 
deadener to the dash panel metal. Measure the distance to the center on top of 
the brake pedal pad. 

If the position of the brake pedal (2455) is not within specification, 
check the brake pedal for missing, worn or damaged bushings or loose retaining 
bolts and replace if required. 

If the brake pedal free height is still out of specification, check the 
brake pedal, power brake booster (2005) or brake master cylinder (2140) to 
make sure the correct parts are installed. Replace the worn or damaged parts 
as necessary.

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake Pedal Travel Measurement 

With engine running and transmission in PARK or NEUTRAL, block wheels 
and release parking brake. 

Install Rotunda Car Gauge 014-R1051 or equivalent and check brake pedal 
travel. 

[FIGURE: H3669F.gif]

Hook a steel measuring tape to the brake pedal (2455). Measure and 
record the distance from the brake pedal free height position to the reference 
point, which is at the six o'clock position on the steering wheel rim. 

With the steel tape still hooked to the brake pedal, depress the brake 
pedal by pressing downward on the brake pedal effort gauge. Apply a 111 N (25 
lb) load to the center of the brake pedal. Maintain the brake pedal load and 
measure the distance from the brake pedal to the fixed reference point on the 
steering wheel rim parallel to the centerline of the steering column. 

The difference between the brake pedal free height and the depressed 
pedal measurement under a 111 N (25 lb) load should be 76.2 mm (3.0 inches) 
maximum. 

If the brake pedal travel is more than the maximum dimension 
specification, make several reverse stops with a forward stop before each. 
Move the vehicle in reverse and then forward for approximately 10 feet; then, 
apply the brakes holding the brake pedal down until the vehicle is completely 
stopped. This will actuate the brake self-adjusters. If these stops do not 
bring the brake pedal travel within specification, make several additional 
forward and reverse stops as described above. 

If the second series of stops does not bring brake pedal travel within 
specification, remove brake drum (1126) and check the brake adjusters to make 
sure they are functioning. Check brake shoe and lining (2001) for wear or 
damage. Service or replace all worn or damaged parts and non-functioning 
adjusters. Adjust the brake shoe lining outside diameter to the approximate 
inside diameter of the brake drum with Brake Adjustment Gauge D81L-1103-A or 
equivalent. Refer to Section 06-02 . 

If all the brake drum adjusters, brake drums and rear brake shoes and 
linings (2200) are functional and brake travel is not within specification, 
check brake pedal assembly for missing or worn bushings or loose attachments.

If the above steps do not bring the brake travel within specification, 
bleed the brake system.

ADJUSTMENTS

Hydraulic Brake Fluid Color 

Hydraulic brake fluid color must conform with the requirements of 
Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 116. Under this standard, brake fluids 
are visually different from other automotive fluids such as transmission, 
power steering and engine oil. 

 NOTE: Brake fluid contaminated with a hydrocarbon/mineral based fluid (power 
steering or transmission fluid) can be detected by an obvious swelling of the 
master cylinder cap gasket. If the swollen brake master cylinder gasket 
condition is present, all brake system rubber parts must be replaced. All 
brake tubes and hoses must be thoroughly flushed with High Performance DOT-3 
Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or equivalent fluid meeting Ford 
Specification ESA-M6C25-A before the vehicle goes back into service.

The color of the fluid in a normal brake system in service can vary 
from its original color for many reasons. Sometimes a brake master cylinder 
(2140) may show significantly different shades of color of fluid between the 
two brake master cylinder reservoir compartments. Color may appear to vary 
between cast steel and die cast aluminum reservoirs. Some of the reasons for 
the apparent difference in color in a system are listed below: 

Fluid discoloration can occur due to heat or aging. 

Difference in fluid color of a two-compartment brake master cylinder 
reservoir can be due to the different operating temperatures or different 
rates of normal oxidation between the two reservoir compartments. 

Fluid discoloration can exist when different brands/shades of brake 
fluid are used in topping off during normal service. 

Fluid discoloration can occur through dissolution of color dye used on 
brake master cylinder internal springs in manufacturer's assembly procedure.

Reinstall the caliper and caliper bracket. Refer to Section 06-03 for 
front disc brakes or Section 06-04 for rear disc brakes.

 Parallelism 

Parallelism is the variations in the thickness of the disc brake rotor. 
If the two rubbing surfaces of the disc brake rotor are not parallel, the disc 
brake rotor may cause excessive brake pedal travel, a pulsating brake pedal or 
noise.

Two methods can be used to check if the two faces of a disc brake rotor 
are parallel. A micrometer can be used to measure the disc brake rotor 
thickness at 12 points approximately 30 degrees apart and 9.5 mm (0.375 inch) 
from the outer edge of the disc brake rotor.

The other method is to measure the disc brake rotor on a precision 
lathe designed for machining disc brake rotors. Attach two dial indicators, 
one on each side of the disc brake rotor, so that the stylus of each indicator 
contacts the rubbing surface, directly opposite each other, approximately 9.5 
mm (0.375 inch) from the outer edge of the disc brake rotor.

Zero both indicators and rotate the disc brake rotor while watching 
both dials. If the total readings of both indicators exceed the specified 
limit for parallelism, the disc brake rotor must be refinished or replaced.

 Refinishing 

All disc brake rotor refinishing must adhere to the rule that equal 
amounts of disc brake rotor stock are removed from each braking surface each 
time a disc brake rotor is refinished. 

The minimum allowable overall disc brake rotor thickness continues to 
be cast on the disc brake rotor and must not be exceeded. 

With a suitable micrometer, measure the overall thickness of the disc 
brake rotor braking surface at four equally-spaced points around the disc 
brake rotor. 

[FIGURE: H10092A.gif]

Using the lowest reading from Step 1, subtract the minimum allowable 
thickness stamped into the disc brake rotor. The difference, if any, 
represents the total amount of material available for machining. A thickness 
reading less than the minimum rear disc brake rotor thickness requires disc 
brake rotor replacement. 

Remove disc brake caliper/rear disc brake caliper (2553). Refer to 
 Section 06-03 (front) or Section 06-04 (rear). Position out of the way. Use S 
hooks provided with Rotunda On-The-Car Lathe 168-00004 or equivalent.

Using concave receiving washers and five lug nuts, secure disc brake 
rotor to the wheel hub. Tighten lug nuts to 115-142 Nm 
(85-104 lb-ft).

Make sure Rotunda On-The-Car Brake Lathe mounting surface is free of 
rust, dirt or other debris. Clean surface with a wire brush.

Check wheel hub endplay. Refer to Section 04-01 (Front) or Section 04-02 (Rear).

Install silencer band on front disc brake rotor (1125)/rear disc brake 
rotor (2C026).

Make sure tool bits are in good condition and installed properly. Refer 
to lathe manufacturer's instructions.

Install Rotunda On-The-Car-Lathe 168-00004 or equivalent following 
manufacturer's instruction.

 Service Limits 

 CAUTION: Never refinish a disc brake rotor to the minimum wear or discard 
thickness. 

Measure the thickness of the disc brake rotor to determine if it is 
within the specification. Refer to Specifications . Disc brake rotor minimum 
(discard) thickness is also cast in the disc brake rotor. Disc brake rotors 
have a minimum thickness dimension (minimum wear thickness or discard 
thickness). This is not the refinishing dimension.

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake Drum

 Out Of Round 

A brake drum (1126) that is out-of-round can cause vehicle vibration 
and brake pedal pulsation when braking. 

Measure the inside diameter of the brake drum using Rotunda Brake Drum 
Micrometer 104-00046 or equivalent. Measure at several points around the 
inside of the brake drum to detect an out-of-round condition. 

To service an out-of-round condition, refer to the following 
Refinishing procedure. 

 Refinishing 

Minor scores on a brake drum can be removed with sandpaper. Do not 
refinish brake drums to remove score marks. A highly polished drum surface can 
cause brake lockup or noise. This polished condition should be removed with 
sandpaper. A brake drum that is out-of-round enough to cause vehicle vibration 
or roughness when braking should be refinished. Remove only enough stock to 
true-up the brake drum. When brake drum maximum inside diameter shown on the 
brake drum is exceeded either through wear or refinishing, the brake drum must 
be replaced. 

Check inside diameter of brake drum with Brake Adjustment Gauge 
D81L-1103-A or Rotunda Brake Drum Micrometer 104-00046 or equivalent. 

After a brake drum is refinished, wipe refinished surface with a cloth 
soaked in clean denatured alcohol. If one brake drum is refinished, the 
opposite brake drum on the same axle should also be refinished to the same 
diameter. 

[FIGURE: H9043B.gif]

 Service Limits 

The maximum inside braking surface diameter is shown on each brake drum 
and also in Specifications. If the maximum inside braking surface diameter 
shown on the brake drum is exceeded either by wear or refinishing, the brake 
drum must be replaced.
