DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake, Parking

The parking brake system is cable-actuated and controlled by an 
independent foot-operated parking brake control which actuates the rear drum 
brakes. 

To apply parking brake, press parking brake control pedal downward. 

To release parking brake, press parking brake control pedal downward 
and allow it to spring upward. 

The parking brake control will release with a click, signaling that the 
parking brake is disengaged. 

After returning to the full OFF position, the parking brake control 
will reset itself to lock upon the next parking brake control application.

A parking brake warning lamp is part of the system, indicating to the 
driver whether the parking brake is applied or released.

Refer to Section 06-05 for service procedures.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brake Drum 

 Removal 

Raise vehicle on hoist. 

Remove wheel cover (1130) and/or nut covers as required. 

Remove tire and wheel assembly. Refer to Section 04-04 . 

Remove drum retainer pushnuts onlug bolt (1107) and remove brake drum 
(1126). 

If the brake drum assembly will not come off for brake service, pry 
rubber plug from backing plate inspection hole. 

Insert a screwdriver and brake tools to disengage brake shoe adjusting 
lever (2A177) and back-off the adjusting screw. 

[FIGURE: H3971E.gif]

 Installation 

If installing new brake drum, completely remove protective coating. 
Lightly sand inner brake drum surface. 

Before installing a brake drum, thoroughly clean all rust, dirt, etc. 
from the drum surface that contacts the hub. 

Adjust brakes as described. 

Install brake drum. Install brake drum retainer pushnuts. Pushnuts 
prevent drum distortion by keeping the drum square to the hub until the wheel 
is installed.

Install tire and wheel assembly. Install wheel cover. Refer to Section 04-04 . 

Lower vehicle.

Wheel Cylinder 

 Removal

Remove brake drum (1126) as described.

 NOTE: Do not let brake fluid contact brake linings or the linings must be

 Installation 

 NOTE: Wipe the ends of the hydraulic hose to remove any foreign matter before 
making connections. 

Position rear wheel cylinder on rear brake backing plate (2212) and 
finger-tighten rear brake tube to rear wheel cylinder.

retaining bolts. Tighten bolts to 12-18 Nm (107-159 lb-in). 

Tighten rear brake line fitting to 14-24 Nm (11-17 
lb-ft) using a tube nut wrench. 

Install and adjust brakes as described. 

Install brake drum as described.

Install wheel and tire assembly. Refer to Section 04-04 .

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Wheel Cylinder 

Rear wheel cylinders (2261) should not be disassembled unless they are 
leaking. Carefully pull lower edges of rear wheel cylinder boots away from 
rear wheel cylinder and note whether interior is wet with brake fluid. 
Excessive fluid indicates leakage past piston cups and a need for rear wheel 
cylinder overhaul. 

A slight amount of fluid is normal and acts as a lubricant for the 
piston. It is not necessary to remove the rear wheel cylinder from the rear 
brake backing plate (2212) to disassemble, inspect, hone and overhaul the rear 
wheel cylinder. Removal is necessary only if the rear wheel cylinder is 
damaged or scored beyond service. 

 Disassembly 

Remove rear brake shoe and lining (2200) assembly as described. 

Disengage rear wheel cylinder boots from retaining grooves in rear 
wheel cylinder casting. Remove each boot and piston from rear wheel cylinder 
as an assembly. 

Remove rear wheel cylinder rubber cups and spring and expander 
assemblies from wheel cylinder bore. 

Discard all rubber parts. 

Remove bleeder screw from rear wheel cylinder. 

Wash all parts in clean denatured alcohol. 

Inspect pistons for scratches, scoring or other damage. Replace if 
necessary. Always replace rubber cups and dust boots. 

Inspect cylinder bore for score marks or rust. If either condition is 
present, cylinder bore must be honed. However, cylinder should not be honed 
more than 0.08 mm (0.003 inch) beyond its original diameter.

Wash rear wheel cylinder with clean denatured alcohol after honing. Dry 
it with compressed air. 

Inspect the bleeder hole to make sure it is free of obstructions.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cleaning

Use Rotunda Automobile Asbestos Brake Drum System with Vacuum 164-R3622 
or equivalent to remove all dust from rear brake backing plate (2212) and 
interior of brake drums (1126).

================================================================================
PAGE 2501
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 06-02: Brakes, Rear Drum

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Inspection 

 Rear Wheel Cylinders 

Rear wheel cylinders (2261) should not be disassembled unless they are 
leaking. Pull back each rear wheel cylinder dust boot as shown and inspect for 
leakage. 

[FIGURE: H9752A.gif]

Excessive fluid at this point indicates leakage past the piston cups. 
Overhaul the rear wheel cylinder. A slight amount of fluid is normally present 
and acts as a lubricant for the pistons. If evidence of leakage is noted, the 
rear wheel cylinder should be disassembled, inspected and overhauled.

Inspect the rear wheel cylinder bore for scratches and pitting. If the 
rear wheel cylinder is pitted or has deep scratches, replace the rear wheel 
cylinder.

 Brake Drums 

Inspect and measure brake drum (1126) with Rotunda Brake Drum 
Micrometer 104-00046 or equivalent. Before making an inspection or 
measurement, remove grease, brake fluid or other contaminants from the brake 
drums using denatured alcohol.

Measure every brake drum with a brake drum micrometer regardless of 
inspection. The brake drum micrometer is set to the drum diameter and measures 
the amount and type of wear. Measure the diameter at various points of 45 
degrees around the circumference and at the bottom of the deepest groove to 
determine if the brake drum requires replacement.

[FIGURE: H9856A.gif]

 Adjuster 

Inspect threads of adjuster assembly for nicks, burrs and freedom of 
movement. If brake shoe adjusting screw socket (2048) is frozen, it must be 
replaced.

 Brake Lining 

Inspect rear brake shoes and linings (2200) for peeling, cracking or 
uneven wear and replace if necessary. Using a micrometer, measure the 
thickness of the remaining lining. If less than 3 mm (0.125 inch) of lining 
remains, the rear brake shoe and lining must be replaced. Replace any lining 
that has been contaminated with oil, grease or brake fluid. Replace linings in 
axle sets only. Never replace just one rear brake shoe and lining of a brake 
assembly. Replace both leading and trailing shoes. Prior to replacement of 
linings, check brake drum diameter to determine if brake drum diameter is 
within specification. If braking surface diameter exceeds specification, brake 
drum must be replaced. 

Check condition of rear brake shoes and linings, retracting spring, 
hold-down springs and brake drum for signs of overheating. If rear brake shoes 
and linings have a slight blue coloring, this indicates overheating and 
retracting. Replace the hold-down springs. If not replaced, overheated springs 
lose their tension and could allow new lining to drag and wear prematurely. 

[FIGURE: H7966A.gif]

 Springs 

Check springs for:

spread or collapsed coils.

twisted, bent or damaged shanks.

discoloration, which indicates brake overheating. Overheated springs 
lose some of their tension and should be replaced.

[FIGURE: H5326B.gif]

 Brake Backing Plate 

Inspect the brake shoe and lining contact pads (where therear brake 
shoes and linings rest).

Deep grooves in the brake shoe and lining contact pads could restrict 
brake shoe and lining movement.

If grooves exist, hand-sand the brake shoe and lining contact pads.

If the grooves are still present after hand sanding, the rear brake 
backing plate (2212) must be replaced. Any attempt to remove the grooves by 
grinding may result in improper brake shoe and lining to brake drum contact.

Inspect all other brake parts and replace any that are worn or damaged.

Section 06-02: Brakes, Rear Drum

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake Shoe and Lining 

 Drums Removed 

The rear brakes are automatically adjusted while driving the vehicle. 
Manual brake adjustment is required only after the rear brake shoes and 
linings (2200) have been replaced, or if the adjuster has malfunctioned and 
has been repaired or replaced. Perform the manual adjustment with the brake 
drum (1126) removed, using Brake Adjustment Gauge D81L-1103-A or equivalent 
and the procedure described below.

When adjusting the rear brake shoes and linings, check the front 
parking brake cable and conduit and parking brake rear cable and conduit for 
proper adjustment. For parking brake service, refer to Section 06-05 .

Apply a small quantity of Silicone Brake Caliper Grease and Dielectric 
Compound D7AZ-19A331-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M1C171-A 
to points where the shoes contact the rear brake backing plate (2212). Do not 
get lubricant on linings. 

Determine inside diameter of the brake drum braking surface using Brake 
Adjustment Gauge D81L-1103-A or equivalent. 

 Brake Adjustment 

[FIGURE: H9751A.gif]

Adjust the brake shoe and lining diameter to fit the gauge. Line up the 
rear brake shoes and linings vertically so the flats on the bottom of the rear 
brake shoes and linings are aligned approximately 1.5 mm (0.05 inch) above the 
bottom of the brake shoe and lining abutment plate before setting the gauge 
diameter. Hold automatic brake shoe adjusting lever (2A177) out of engagement 
while rotating adjusting screw. If necessary, lubricate. Make sure adjusting 
screw rotates freely. 

Rotate Brake Adjustment Gauge D81L-1103-A or equivalent around rear 
brake shoe and lining to make sure of proper setting. 

Install brake drum as described. Install tire and wheel assembly. Refer 
to Section 04-04 . 

Install the wheel cover (1130) and nut covers as required. 

After rear brake shoes and linings have been properly adjusted, check 
operation of brakes by making several stops from varying forward speeds.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brakes System, Disc 

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THOROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

 NOTE: Brake friction materials inherently generate noise and heat to 
dissipate energy. As a result, occasional squeal is possible, and it is 
aggravated by severe environmental conditions such as cold, heat, rain, snow, 
salt, mud and other conditions. 

Disc brakes are standard on all vehicles. Two sizes of pin slider 
calipers are used:

276 mm (10.87 inch) is used with 15 inch wheels.

294 mm (11.57 inch) is used with 16 inch wheels.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Rotor 

The front disc brake rotor (1125): 

is 276 mm (10.87 inch) in diameter on 15 inch wheel vehicles.

is 294 mm (11.57 inch) in diameter on 16 inch wheel vehicles.

is a ventilated full cast design, using non-directional cooling fins. 

mounts to the wheel hub (1104). 

is serviced with the disc brake caliper (2B120) and front disc brake 
caliper anchor plate (2B292) removed.

Section 06-03: Brake, Front Disc

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Caliper 

Two types of disc brake calipers (2B120), matched to rotor size and 
determined by wheel size are used.

Front disc brakes use a pin slider-type disc brake caliper assembly 
with either a 276 mm (10.87 inch) or 294 mm (11.57 inch) full cast front disc 
brake rotor (1125). 

The disc brake caliper has a caliper piston (2196) with a piston seal 
and a press-in type dust boot. 

The disc brake caliper assembly used with 15 inch wheels is retained to 
the front disc brake caliper anchor plate (2B292) with one brake caliper bolt 
(2W303) and one disc brake caliper locating pin (2B296) contained in the 
anchor plate.

The disc brake caliper assembly used with 16 inch wheels is retained to 
the front disc brake caliper anchor plate with two brake pin retainers.

The front disc brake caliper anchor plate is attached to the front 
wheel spindle (3105) by two M12 X 1.75 X 30 mm bolts. Using longer bolts will 
damage the front disc brake rotor. 

Rubber insulators isolate the disc brake caliper locating pins from 
direct contact with the disc brake caliper. 

The brake hose inlet port thread size is M10 X 1.5.

Section 06-03: Brake, Front Disc

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Shoe and Linings

The brake shoes and linings (2001) are interchangeable, side to side 
and inboard to outboard. 

The brake shoes and linings for vehicles with 15 inch wheels use a 
pressure sensitive insulator material for noise suppression. Remove the 
protective paper from this insulator before installing new brake shoe and 
lining assemblies.

Vehicles with 16 inch wheels use a clip-on shoe and lining insulator to 
prevent noise.

The flanges on both inner and outer brake shoe and lining assemblies 
slide on machined surfaces of the front disc brake caliper anchor plate 
(2B292).

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Service Precautions 

Grease or any other foreign material must be kept off lining surfaces 
and braking surfaces of front disc brake rotor (1125), and external surfaces of 
wheel hub (1104) during service operation. In handling front disc brake rotor 
and disc brake caliper (2B120) assemblies, avoid deformation, nicking or 
scratching of brake shoes and linings (2001) and front disc brake rotor. 

If a caliper piston (2196) is removed for any reason, piston seal and 
dust boot must be replaced. 

During removal and installation of a wheel assembly, exercise care not 
to interfere with or damage front disc brake rotor shield (2K005), or the 
caliper bleed screw.

Do not attempt to clean or restore any oil- or grease-soaked brake 
shoes and linings. When contaminated, brake shoes and linings must be replaced 
in complete axle sets and front disc brake rotor surfaces wiped clean. 

The LH and RH disc brake calipers must be installed on the correct side 
of the vehicle to be sure bleed screw is in the topmost position for proper 
purging of air from the front brake system during bleeding.

Caliper 

 Removal

Remove wheel and tire assembly. Use care to avoid damage to or

Mark disc brake caliper (2B120) assembly to make sure it will be

Remove hollow bolt that retains front brake hose (2078) to disc brake 
caliper. Remove front brake hose from disc brake caliper and plug hose. It is 
not necessary to remove the front brake hose from the disc brake caliper if the 
brake shoe and lining (2001) or front disc brake rotor (1125) is to be serviced.

Remove the one brake caliper bolt (2W303). For 16 inch wheel vehicles

 Installation

through washers and fitting. Tighten bolt to 40-60 Nm (30-44 
lb-ft).

Always reinstall rubber bleeder screw cap after bleeding.

Vehicle Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or DOT-3 equivalent meeting Ford 
Specification ESA-M6C25-A and DOT 3.

rotor runout, which will speed up the development of brake roughness, shudder 
and vibration.

 Lug Nut Sockets 164-R0303 or equivalent on 1/2 inch drive air impact wrench 
or use torque wrench to tighten lug nuts to 115-142 Nm 
(85-104 lb-ft). 

Lower vehicle. 

Pump brake pedal (2455) prior to moving vehicle to position brake shoes 
and linings. Refill the brake master cylinder with High Performance DOT-3 
Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or DOT-3 equivalent meeting Ford 
Specification ESA-M6C25-A and DOT 3 as required.

Road test vehicle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brake Shoe and Lining 

 Removal 

Refer to the illustration under Caliper Installation . 

Remove brake master cylinder cap and check fluid level in brake master 
cylinder reservoir (2K478). Remove brake fluid until brake master cylinder 
reservoir is half full. Discard removed fluid. 

Raise vehicle on hoist. For additional information refer to Section 00-02 .

Remove wheel and tire assembly. Use care to avoid damage or 
interference with front disc brake rotor shield (2K005) or wheel cylinder 
bleeder screw (2208). 

Measure runout and brake disc thickness. For additional
information refer to Section 06-00 .

 NOTE: It is not necessary to disconnect hydraulic connections to
install a new brake shoe and lining (2001).

For 15 inch wheels � Remove front disc brake caliper bolt 
(2W303) from disc brake caliper (2B120).

For 16 inch wheels � Remove upper and lower brake pin retainer from 
disc brake caliper.

For 15 inch wheels � rotate disc brake caliper up and 
away from front disc brake caliper anchor plate (2B292) and front brake disc 
(1125) pivoting on the disc brake caliper locating pin (2B296).

Support the disc brake caliper assembly in a manner that will not 
stretch or damage the front brake hose (2078). Be sure shoe and linings stay 
in the front disc brake caliper anchor plate.

Remove outer and inner brake shoe and lining assembly from front disc 
brake caliper anchor plate.

Inspect both front brake disc braking surfaces. Minor scoring or 
buildup of brake shoe and lining material does not require machining or 
installation of new front brake disc. Remove glaze from both front brake 
disc braking surfaces by hand-sanding with garnet paper 100A (medium-grit) or 
aluminum oxide 150-J (medium). 

Inspect piston boot and caliper pin boots for damage and
install new components as necessary. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Metal or sharp objects cannot come into direct contact with wheel 
cylinder piston surface or damage will result. 

Use a 10 cm (4 inch) C-clamp and wood block 70 mm x 25 mm (2-3/4 inches 
x 1 inch) and approximately 19 mm (3/4 inch) thick to seat caliper piston 
(2196) in its bore. This must be done to provide clearance for disc brake 
caliper assembly to fit over front disc brake rotor during installation. 

[FIGURE: AH0262A.gif]

 NOTE: Front disc brake caliper casting for 15 inch wheels allows brake shoe 
hold-down spring (2068) to be installed one way only. RH and LH brake shoe 
hold-down springs are identical but installed in opposite directions. 

Clean front disc brake caliper legs and brake shoe and lining abutments 
as necessary. Make sure disc brake pad anti-rattle clip (2B164) is seated in 
caliper lining inspection opening. Disc brake pad anti-rattle clip must be 
installed from lining side. 

For disc brake caliper used with 15 inch wheels, peel protective paper 
from insulator on the brake shoe and lining assembly. The insulator will be 
black after the paper has been removed. This pressure-sensitive adhesive 
insulator functions to reduce noise. Care should be exercised to avoid 
contamination on the adhesive surface prior to installing the brake shoe and 
lining in the disc brake caliper assembly.

Brake shoe and lining for disc brake calipers used on 16 inch wheels 
use a clip-on insulator.

Engage the brake shoes and linings in the front disc brake caliper 
anchor plate.

Inspect disc brake caliper/front disc brake caliper anchor plate 
assembly and install and rotate disc brake caliper over the brake shoe and 
lining nested in the front disc brake caliper anchor plate.

For 15 inch wheels � rotate disc brake caliper into 
position and reinstall the brake caliper bolt. Tighten to 81 Nm
 (60 lb-ft).

For 16 inch wheels � tighten upper and lower brake pin 
retainers to 35 Nm (26 lb-ft). Make sure caliper slides freely.

Install wheel and tire assembly. Tighten lug nuts (1012) to 115-142 Nm
 (85-104 lb-ft). 

Lower vehicle. 

Pump brake pedal (2455) prior to moving vehicle to position brake shoes 
and linings. Refill the brake master cylinder (2140) with High Performance 
DOT-3 Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or DOT-3 equivalent meeting Ford 
Specification ESA-M6C26-A and DOT 3 as required.

Road test vehicle.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Rotor 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Handle the front disc brake rotor (1125) and disc brake caliper (2B120) 
assemblies in such a way as to avoid damage to the front disc brake rotor and 
nicking, scratching, dropping or contamination of the brake shoe and lining 
(2001). 

Remove the wheel and tire assembly. Be careful to avoid damage to or 
interference with the wheel cylinder bleeder screw (2208) and front disc brake 
rotor shield (2K004). 

Remove two bolts retaining front disc brake caliper anchor plate 
(2B292) to front wheel spindle (3105).

Remove the disc brake caliper/front disc brake caliper anchor plate 
assembly from the front wheel spindle and the front disc brake rotor. 

Note front disc brake rotor to wheel hub (1104) position. Mark on one 
lug bolt (1107) should line up with mark on front disc brake rotor hat section 
at one wheel hub bolt location. This provides lowest front disc brake rotor 
runout location. If marks are not visible, put mark on lug bolt and area 
adjacent on front disc brake rotor. 

 NOTE: If the disc brake caliper does not require servicing, it is not 
necessary to disconnect the front brake hose (2078). 

Position the disc brake caliper out of the way, and support it with a 
wire to avoid damaging the disc brake caliper or stretching the front brake 
hose. 

Insert a clean cardboard spacer between the brake shoes and linings to 
prevent the inner brake shoe and lining from coming out of the disc brake 
caliper and being damaged by falling on the floor. 

 NOTE: If excessive force must be used during front disc brake rotor removal, 
the front disc brake rotor should be checked for lateral runout prior to 
installation. 

Remove front disc brake rotor assembly from wheel hub. 

If additional force is required to remove front disc brake rotor, apply 
Rust Penetrant and Inhibitor F2AZ-19A501-A or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C56-A on both front disc brake rotor/hub mating surfaces. 
First, strike front disc brake rotor between studs with a plastic hammer. If 
this does not work, attach 2-3-Jaw Puller D80L-1013-A or equivalent and remove 
front disc brake rotor. 

 Installation 

If the front disc brake rotor is being replaced, remove the protective 
coating from the new front disc brake rotor with Metal Brake Parts Cleaner 
F3AZ-19579-SA or equivalent. Clean the wheel hubs mounting surface of rust, 
scale or dirt.

If the front disc brake rotor is not being replaced, clean the hub 
mounting surface of the front disc brake rotor as well as the wheel hubs 
mounting surface for rust, scale or dirt. Contamination will not allow front 
disc brake rotor to sit flat to the hub surface. Apply High Temperature Nickel 
Anti-Sieze Lubricant F6AZ-9G494-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESE-M12A4-A to the backside of rotor hat section facing the hub.

Install the front disc brake rotor assembly on the wheel hub indexing 
stud to rotor stud previously marked.

Install two push-on nuts at non-adjacent positions to retain the indexed 
front disc brake rotor to the wheel hub.

Install the disc brake caliper/front disc brake caliper anchor plate 
assembly on the front wheel spindle using new bolts, hand start and tighten to 
130 Nm (96 lb-ft) for 15 inch wheels. For 16 inch wheel 
vehicles tighten to 119 Nm (87 lb-ft).

 CAUTION: Failure to tighten lug nuts (1012) in a star pattern may result in high 
rotor runout, which will speed up the development of brake roughness, shudder 
and vibration. 

Install wheel and tire assembly using Rotunda Accutorq®
 Lug Nut Sockets 164-R0303 or equivalent on 1/2 inch drive air impact wrench 
or use torque wrench to tighten lug nuts to 115-142 Nm 
(85-104 lb-ft).

PAGE 2517

Section 06-03: Brake, Front Disc

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Rotor Shield 

 Removal 

Remove the disc brake caliper (2B120) and the front disc brake rotor 
(1125) assembly as described. It is not necessary to disconnect hydraulic 
connections. 

Remove the three rivets retaining the front disc brake rotor shield 
(2K005) to the front wheel spindle (3105) by punching out the mandrel located 
in the center of the rivet. Using a chisel, cut off rivet at front wheel 
spindle and punch out rivet remaining in hole. Remove the front disc brake 
rotor shield.

 Installation 

Position the front disc brake rotor shield on the mounting bracket. 
Install the rivets using Heavy Duty Riveter D80L-23200-A or equivalent. Do not 
attempt to bend or adjust the front disc brake rotor shield. 

Install front disc brake rotor assembly and disc brake caliper as 
described.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Caliper 

 Single Piston 

 Disassembly 

 CAUTION: Use layers of shop towels to cushion possible impact of the caliper 
piston (2196) against the front disc brake caliper iron when caliper piston 
comes out of the piston bore. Do not use a screwdriver or similar tool to pry 
caliper piston out of the bore, as damage to the caliper piston may result. If 
the caliper piston is seized and cannot be forced from the disc brake caliper 
(2B120), tap lightly around the piston while applying air pressure. Use care 
because the caliper piston can develop considerable force from pressure 
buildup. 

Remove disc brake caliper/front disc brake caliper anchor plate (2B292) 
assembly as described. 

Disconnect disc brake caliper from hydraulic system, and blow out the 
caliper piston using Rubber-Tipped Air Gun D93L-7000-A or equivalent. 

Remove the dust boot from the disc brake caliper assembly. 

[FIGURE: H1574G.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

�

Fiber Block 

2

�

Cloth 

3

2196

Caliper Piston

4

D93L-7000-A

Rubber-Tipped Air Gun

5

2B120

Disc Brake Caliper

Remove the rubber piston seal from the caliper piston and discard. 

 Assembly 

 NOTE: When assembling disc brake caliper, examine caliper piston for surface 
irregularities, pitting, scoring, wear or corrosion of the chrome plated 
surface. Replace caliper piston if damaged. Be sure to clean foreign material 
from caliper bore piston surfaces and lubricate with High Performance DOT-3 
Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or DOT-3 equivalent meeting Ford 
Specification ESA-M6C26-A and DOT-3 before inserting piston into disc brake 
caliper. 

Install new piston seal and dust boot.

Start caliper piston into bore by hand to assure correct alignment.

When installing caliper piston back into bore, use wood block or 
another flat stock, like an old brake shoe and lining (2001) assembly, between 
C-clamp and caliper piston. Do not apply C-clamp directly to wheel cylinder 
piston surface. This can damage caliper piston. Make sure caliper piston is 
not cocked. 

Make sure dust boot is tight in boot groove on caliper piston and in 
disc brake caliper. 

Install disc brake caliper assembly as described.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Caliper

 CAUTION: Do not submerge large end of disc brake caliper (2B120) in solvent. 
This side contains a permanently lubricated sealed bearing assembly that is 
not serviceable. 

Clean all metal parts with isopropyl alcohol. Then, clean out and dry 
grooves and passageways with compressed air. Make sure front disc brake bore 
and component parts are clean. 

Visually check disc brake caliper. If disc brake caliper is leaking, it 
should be serviced or replaced. If a seal is leaking, disc brake caliper must 
be disassembled and new seals and dust boot installed. If a caliper piston 
(2196) is seized in the bore, a new disc brake caliper is required. 

Check the cylinder bore and caliper piston for damage or excessive 
wear. Replace the caliper piston if it is pitted, scored, corroded or the 
plating is worn off.

Inspect caliper slide pins for ripped or torn boot seals. Lubricate the 
slide pins with Silicone Brake Caliper Grease and Dielectric Compound 
D7AZ-19A331-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M1C171-A.

================================================================================
PAGE 2521
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 06-03: Brake, Front Disc

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Brake Shoe and Linings

Inspect brake shoe and lining (2001) for excessive wear or damage. If 
lining is worn to within 3 mm (0.118 inch) of shoe, replace all four brake 
shoe and lining assemblies (complete axle set). 

Replace any brake shoe and lining that has been contaminated with oil, 
grease or brake fluid. Inspect for and correct any source of contamination. 
Replace linings in complete axle sets.

================================================================================
PAGE 2522
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 06-03: Brake, Front Disc

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Rotor

Brake pulsation (brake roughness) that is present during brake 
application is caused by either foreign material build-up or contamination on 
the rotor brake surface or uneven lateral runout. To check lateral runout, 
refer to Section 06-00 .

If there is a foreign material build-up or contamination found on front 
disc brake rotor (1125) or lining surfaces, hand-sand linings and front disc 
brake rotors. 

If brake pulsation (brake roughness) is present, attempt stopping 
vehicle with transmission in the NEUTRAL position. If the pulsation 
(roughness) is gone, the drivetrain should be inspected. If pulsation 
(roughness) remains, stop vehicle from 48 km/h (30 mph) using parking brake 
control (2780). If pulsation remains, inspect rear brakes. If pulsation is 
gone, inspect front brakes.

ADJUSTMENTS

Rotor and Brake Shoe and Lining Hand Sanding

 NOTE: Minor scoring or buildup of lining material does not require machining 
or replacement of front disc brake rotor (1125).

Remove glaze from both rotor braking surfaces by hand-sanding with 
garnet paper 100A (medium-grit) or aluminum oxide 150J (medium).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brakes, Rear Disc

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THOROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

 NOTE: Brake friction materials inherently generate noise and heat in order to 
dissipate energy. As a result, occasional squeal is possible, which may be 
aggravated by severe environmental conditions such as cold, heat, rain, snow, 
salt, mud and other conditions.

The rear disc brakes consist of:

ventilated full cast rear disc brake rotors (2C026)

hydraulically activated rear disc brake calipers (2553) with integral 
cable-operated parking brake mechanisms

The rear disc brake caliper is similar to front disc brake caliper 
(2B120), except for parking brake mechanism.

The parking brake mechanism in caliper is self-adjusting.

================================================================================

================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 06-04: Brakes, Rear Disc

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Rotor 

The rear disc brake rotors (2C026) are ventilated and full-cast.

Ventilation is provided by fins between the braking surfaces that cause 
rear disc brake rotor to act as an air pump. 

The rear disc brake rotor is retained to rear hub (1109) in same manner 
as rear brake drum.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Caliper 

The rear disc brake caliper (2553) assembly consists of:

caliper housing with single rear disc brake piston and adjuster (2B588) 
and parking brake mechanism

inner and outer rear brake shoes and linings (2200)

rear disc support bracket (2B511)

two lubricated disc brake caliper locating pins (2B296) that position 
rear disc brake piston and adjuster relative to rear disc support bracket. 

rubber slide pin boot seals that prevent lubrication washout and 
corrosion of disc brake caliper locating pins.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Service Precautions 

Observe the following precautions when servicing the rear disc brake 
system.

Keep grease or any other foreign material off brake shoe and lining 
surfaces, braking surfaces of rear disc brake rotor (2C026) and external 
surfaces of rear hub (1109) during service operation. In handling rear disc 
brake rotor and caliper assemblies, avoid deformation, nicking, scratching or 
dropping of rear brake shoes and linings (2200) and rear disc brake rotor. 

If a rear disc brake piston and adjuster (2B588) is removed for any 
reason, replace piston seal and dust boot. Be careful not to damage rear disc 
brake piston and adjuster; protect it from contact with any metal or 
sharp-edged objects. 

During removal and installation of wheel assembly, be careful not to 
interfere with, or damage rear wheel disc brake shield (2C028), if equipped, 
or bleeder screw. 

Do not use twin post hoist when lifting rear wheel drive vehicle with 
independent rear suspension. Refer to Section 00-02 .

Do not attempt to clean or restore any oil or grease-soaked rear brake 
shoes and linings. When contaminated linings are found, replace rear brake 
shoes and linings in complete axle sets and wipe rear disc brake rotor braking 
surfaces clean. 

Before installing rear disc brake rotor, thoroughly clean all rust and 
dirt from hub surface that contacts rotor, rotor surface that contacts hub and 
the rotor surface that contacts wheel. Contamination will keep rear disc brake 
rotor from sitting flat on the hub surface. Apply High Temperature Nickel 
Anti-Sieze Lubricant F6AZ-9G494-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESE-M12A4-A to the backside of the rotor hat section facing the hub.

Install LH and RH rear disc brake calipers (2553) on correct side of 
vehicle to be sure bleeder screw is in topmost position for proper purging of 
air from rear brake system during bleeding. 

After any service, pump brake pedal (2455) before moving vehicle to 
obtain firm brake pedal.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Rotor 

 Removal 

Remove rear disc brake caliper (2553) assembly as described. If service 
to rear disc brake caliper assembly is not necessary, do not disconnect rear 
wheel brake hose (2A442) from rear disc brake caliper in this operation. 
Support rear disc brake caliper assembly with wire hook or other means, so 
rear wheel brake hose is not stretched or twisted. 

Remove two bolts that retain rear disc support bracket (2B511) to rear 
wheel knuckle (5A968). Remove rear disc support bracket and rear brake shoes 
and linings (2200). 

Remove two push-on nuts retaining rear disc brake rotor (2C026) to rear 
hub (1109). Remove the rear disc brake rotor from the rear hub. 

 Installation 

If rear disc brake rotor is being replaced, remove protective coating 
from new rear disc brake rotor with Metal Brake Parts Cleaner 
(non-chlorinated) F5AZ-2C410-AA or equivalent. Before installing brake rotor, 
thoroughly clean all rust and dirt from hub and rotor surface. Contamination 
will keep rear disc brake rotor from sitting flat on the hub surface.

Apply High Temperature Nickel Anti-Sieze Lubricant F6AZ-9G494-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M12A4-A to backside of rotor hat 
section facing the hub.

Install rear disc brake rotors on rear hub flange. Install rear disc 
rotor push on retaining nuts at two non-adjacent places securely. 

Install rear disc support bracket as described. 

Install inner and outer rear brake shoes and linings. 

Install rear disc brake caliper assembly as described.

Support Bracket 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Do not remove rear disc support bracket (2B511) unless rear disc brake 
rotor (2C026) is to be removed. 

Remove rear disc brake caliper (2553) as described. If service to rear 
disc brake caliper is not necessary, do not disconnect rear wheel brake hose 
(2A442) from rear disc brake caliper in this operation. Support rear disc 
brake caliper with wire hook or other means, so rear wheel brake hose is not

D7AZ-19A331-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M1C171-A to inside

disc brake caliper locating pin (2B296). 

Install the rear disc brake caliper/rear disc support bracket assembly 
to the rear wheel knuckle (5A969). Install new bolts and tighten to 98-132 Nm
 (73-97 lb-ft). 

Install the rear disc brake caliper assembly as described.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Caliper

Clean all metal parts with isopropyl alcohol. Use clean, dry compressed 
air to clean out and dry grooves and passages. Make sure caliper bore and 
component parts are completely free of any foreign material. 

Inspect caliper bores for damage or excessive wear. If piston is 
pitted, scored or plating is worn off, replace piston assembly.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Control Assemblies 

 Cable Actuated Rear Wheel Parking Brake 

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THOROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

The parking brake system is cable-actuated and controlled by an 
independent foot-operated parking brake control (2780) which actuates the rear 
drum brakes or, if equipped, the rear disc brake caliper (2552).

To apply parking brake, press parking brake control pedal downward.

When the parking brake is engaged, the brake warning indicator 
illuminates to signal the driver that the parking brake is applied.

To release parking brake, press parking brake control pedal downward 
and allow it to spring upward. 

The parking brake control will release with a click, the brake warning 
indicator will turn off, signaling that the parking brake is disengaged. 

After returning to the full OFF position, the parking brake control 
will reset itself to lock upon the next parking brake control application.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Brake System, Parking

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's concern by operating the parking brake system to 
duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply: 

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged parking brake control.

Binding/damaged parking brake cables.

Loose/sagging parking brake cables.

Parking brake warning indicator switch.

If inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required. 

If the concerns remain after the inspection, determine the symptoms and 
go to the Symptom Chart. 

 Symptom Chart � Parking Brake System 

 Symptom Chart � Parking Brake System 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Binding/damaged parking brake cables.

Binding/damaged parking brake cables. 

Damaged parking brake control.

GO to Pinpoint Test B .

 Pinpoint Tests

 Did parking brakes apply?

GO to A2 .

Actuate parking brake control as described in Test Step A1 . 

 Did parking brake control actuate?

Yes

No

system. 

REPLACE parking brake control. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system. 

PINPOINT TEST B: PARKING BRAKE WILL NOT RELEASE

 B1 CHECK PARKING BRAKE CONTROL 

Raise vehicle on a hoist with parking brake fully applied.

Release parking brake by pressing on parking brake pedal until click is 
heard. 

 Did parking brake release?

Yes

No

ADJUST cable as described. SERVICE as required. 

GO to B2 .

Move gearshift lever to NEUTRAL position. 

Rotate rear wheels by hand. 

 Did rear wheels turn freely?

Yes

No

REPLACE parking brake control. RESTORE vehicle. RETEST system. 

GO to B3 .

 B3 CHECK FRONT PARKING BRAKE CABLE 

Disconnect front parking brake cable and conduit. Refer to Removal 
and Installation . 

Rotate rear wheels by hand. 

 Did rear wheels turn freely?

Yes

No

REPLACE front parking brake cable and conduit as described. RESTORE 
vehicle. RETEST system. 

GO to B4 .

 B4 CHECK INTERMEDIATE CABLE 

Disconnect parking brake intermediate cable as described. 

Rotate rear wheels by hand. 

 Did rear wheels turn freely?

Yes

No

system. 

GO to B5 .

Disconnect parking brake cables one at a time.

 Did wheel turn freely?

Yes

No

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Control

 Removal 

Raise vehicle.

Remove cable tension as described under Adjustments. 

Lower vehicle. 

Disconnect wiring connection from parking brake signal switch and 
bracket (15A851).

Remove cowl side trim panel (02345). 

Remove front parking brake cable and conduit end from clevis at parking 
brake control (2780). 

Remove conduit snap-in fitting from foot parking brake control using a 
13 mm 12-point box-end wrench to press retaining prongs. 

Remove three bolts retaining parking brake control to cowl side trim 
panel. 

Remove bolt retaining foot parking brake control to instrument panel 
(04320). 

Remove foot parking brake control from vehicle. 

 Installation 

Position parking brake control in vehicle. 

Fit front parking brake cable and conduit (2853) through its mounting 
hole and press pronged retainer in place. Make sure prongs are securely locked 
in place. Connect the cable end fitting to clevis at foot parking brake 
control. 

Install retaining bolts to cowl side trim panel and instrument panel. 
Tighten bolts to 23-35 Nm (17-25 lb-ft). 

Connect wiring connector to parking brake signal switch and bracket. 

Install cowl side trim panel. 

Raise vehicle. Check parking brake operation and adjust as described. 

Lower vehicle.

Cable and Conduit

 Removal

 Intermediate

 Installation

parking brake intermediate cable or parking brake cable adjuster.

Route parking brake intermediate cable through clip on rear suspension 
arm and bushing and secure snap-in retainer into brake rear brake backing 
plate by pushing retainer fully until prongs are secure. 

Connect rear parking brake cable and conduit end to parking brake lever. 

Connect parking brake lever to parking brake cable adjuster or parking 
brake intermediate cable at cable connector. 

Adjust cable tension as described under Adjustments and lower vehicle. 

 Rear Disc 

 Removal

ADJUSTMENTS

Cable Adjustment

Apply parking brake control (2780) fully with 445 N (100 lb) foot pedal 
effort. Release parking brake control. Repeat application and release. 

Place the transmission in NEUTRAL. Raise the vehicle on hoist. 

With parking brake control in OFF position, grasp tensioner around 
housing. Using a tool similar to the one shown, hook the end into the rounded 
end of clip between clip and housing. Unlock clip by pulling downward with the 
tool and support tensioner. The tensioner spring will take up cable slack and 
preload cables. While holding tensioner, lock the clip by pushing up on bottom 
of clip. If clip does not slide up, move assembly slightly to align closest 
groove on adjuster rod to the clip. 

 Parking Brake Cable Adjustment Tool 

[FIGURE: H7382B.gif]

Examine tensioner for remaining cable take-up capability. If none is 
present, check all cables, parking brake control and brackets for possible 
damage or deflection. Replace damaged parts and tension system by using 
Initial Installation Adjustment procedure. 

 Initial Installation Adjustment 

Install parking brake control, tensioner and all cables with routing 
clips. Connect all cables together with tensioner. (Be sure to install correct 
adjuster for rear brake usage.) 

Place the transmission in NEUTRAL. Raise the vehicle on hoist.

With parking brake control in OFF position, grasp tensioner around 
housing. Using a tool similar to the one shown, hook the end into the rounded 
end of clip between clip and housing. Unlock clip by pulling downward with the 
tool and support tensioner. The tensioner spring will take up cable slack and 
preload cables. While holding tensioner, lock the clip by pushing up on bottom 
of clip. If clip does not slide up, move assembly slightly to align closest 
groove on adjuster rod to the clip. 

Apply parking brake control fully with 445 N (100 lb) foot pedal 
effort. Release parking brake control. Repeat application and release. 

Repeat Step 3 to take up any additional slack.

ADJUSTMENTS

Cable Tension, Release 

Fully release the parking brake. 

Raise vehicle on axle-type hoist. 

Removal of cable tension requires two people to disengage and reload 
the tensioner. One person unlocks the tensioner by pulling downward on the 
clip. While the clip is disengaged, the second person fully applies the 
parking brake control (2780) to the last notch position. The tensioner spring 
will compress, allowing cable slack to return. Next, lock the tensioner by 
pushing up on the clip. Make sure locking lever is secure by rotating it 
toward threaded rod. Wrap tape or wire around the locking lever and threaded 
rod to prevent any accidental release.

Section 06-06: Brake System, Hydraulic

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THOROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

This vehicle is equipped with a pedal-actuated dual brake system. The 
system consists of the following: 

power brake booster (2005)

brake master cylinder (2140)

brake pressure control valves (2B091)

front disc brake caliper (2B120) assemblies

rear disc brake calipers (2553)

rear wheel cylinders (2261) (rear drum brakes)

brake tubes and hoses

anti-lock brake system (ABS) components

Both hydraulic brake systems are diagonally split with the LH front and 
RH rear making up one circuit and the RH front and LH rear making up the other 
circuit.

================================================================================
PAGE 2558
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 06-06: Brake System, Hydraulic

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Master Cylinder 

The brake master cylinder (2140) is a dual-piston type. The brake 
master cylinder operates as follows:

When the brake pedal (2455) is depressed, pressure is applied by 
mechanical linkage to the primary and secondary pistons.

Brake master cylinder pistons apply hydraulic pressure to the two 
opposed hydraulic circuits.

The brake master cylinder consists of the following:

hydraulic control unit reservoir (2C246)

primary and secondary pistons

brake master cylinder body

fitting connecting the brake master cylinder reservoir (2K478) to the 
hydraulic control unit reservoir on ABS hydraulic control unit reservoir

integral fluid level connector

 Dual Hydraulic Brake System 

The dual hydraulic brake system is a conventional pedal actuated system.

The system consists of the following:

brake master cylinder

brake pressure control valve (2B091)

brake tubes and hoses

Hydraulic brake line routing is LH front to RH rear and RH front to LH 
rear.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Control Valves and Pressure Switch

The brake pressure control valve assembly consists of twin brake 
proportioning valves which proportion the pressure to both rear brakes 
individually. On vehicles equipped with 3.8L engine, without ABS, brake 
pressure control valves (2B091) are installed into the brake master cylinder 
(2140). 

The brake pressure control valve operates as follows:

When the brake pedal (2455) is applied, the full rear brake fluid 
pressure passes through the non-ABS proportioning valves to the rear brake 
system until the valve split point is reached. 

Above its split point, the proportioning valves begin to reduce the 
additional hydraulic pressure to the rear brakes, creating a balanced braking 
condition between the front and rear wheels.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Anti-Lock 

The ABS is a four-wheel system which prevents wheel lock-up by 
automatically modulating the brake pressure during an emergency stop. By not 
locking the wheels, it enables the driver to maintain steering control and to 
stop in the shortest possible distance under most conditions.

Refer to Section 06-09 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brake Pedal and Bracket

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Disconnect the stoplight switch wire connector from the stoplight 
switch (13480). 

Loosen the three pedal support bracket retaining nuts at the dash panel 
(01610).

Loosen pedal support bracket (01508) to instrument panel retaining bolt.

Remove the push rod retainer and brake master cylinder push rod spacer 
(2B129).

Slide the stoplight switch outboard along the brake pedal pin just far 
enough for the outer hole of the switch frame to clear the pin. Remove the 
stoplight switch by sliding it off the pin.

Remove the brake master cylinder push rod bushing (2474) from the push 
rod. 

Remove brake pedal (2455).

 Installation 

Apply a coating of clean engine oil meeting Ford specification 
WSS-M2C910-A1 to the brake master cylinder push rod bushing. Locate brake 
master cylinder push rod bushings and brake master cylinder push rod spacer in 
the brake pedal hub. 

Position brake pedal onto brake booster studs that come through the 
dash panel. Make sure the brake pedal can swing freely while not being too 
loose side-to-side. If there is too much free play side-to-side, increase 
locknut torque. The brake pedal must continue to swing freely. Replace brake 
pedal if it cannot swing freely.

Install the master cylinder push rod and the brake master cylinder push 
rod bushing on the brake pedal pin. The large diameter portion of brake master 
cylinder push rod bushing must not be between the push rod and pedal arm. 

Position the stoplight switch so it straddles the push rod with the 
slot on the pedal pin and the switch outer frame hole just clearing the pin. 

Slide the stoplight switch onto the pin and push rod. Slide the 
assembly toward the brake pedal arm.

Install the brake master cylinder push rod spacer and the push rod 
retainer. Lock the retainer securely. 

Tighten the three pedal support retaining nuts to 21-29 Nm
 (16-21 lb-ft). Tighten pedal support bracket to instrument 
panel retaining bolt to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

Connect the stoplight switch wire to the stoplight switch. 

Connect the battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brake Master Cylinder 

 Removal 

Apply the brake pedal (2455) several times to exhaust all vacuum in the 
system. 

Disconnect the brake warning indicator switch connector. 

Remove brake tubes from primary and secondary outlet ports of brake 
master cylinder (2140). 

For vehicles with ABS, disconnect hydraulic control unit (HCU) supply 
hose at hydraulic control unit reservoir (2C246) and secure in a position to 
prevent loss of brake fluid. 

Remove two nuts retaining brake master cylinder to power brake booster 
assembly. 

Slide brake master cylinder forward and upward from vehicle. 

 Installation 

ABS-equipped vehicles-install a new seal in groove in brake master 
cylinder mounting face. 

[FIGURE: H8060C.gif]

Position brake master cylinder as an assembly on studs on power brake 
booster assembly. 

Install retaining nuts. Tighten retaining nuts to 21-29 Nm
 (16-21 lb-ft). 

Install primary and secondary brake tubes to master cylinder outlet 
ports. Tighten to 21-29 Nm (16-21 lb-ft). 

For vehicles with ABS, connect HCU supply hose to brake master cylinder 
reservoir fitting and secure with hose clamp. 

Connect brake warning indicator switch connector. 

Fill brake master cylinder with specified brake fluid to MAX line or 
4.0 mm (0.16 inch) below MAX line on hydraulic control unit reservoir. Use 
High Performance DOT-3 Motor Vehicle brake fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or equivalent 
fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A, DOT 3. 

Bleed brake system as described.

Operate brakes several times; then check for external hydraulic leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brake Master Cylinder Reservoir 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Whenever the hydraulic control unit reservoir (2C246) is removed from 
the brake master cylinder (2140), the hydraulic control unit reservoir must be 
replaced and new grommets must be installed. 

Disconnect fluid level indicator switch. 

Remove anti-lock reservoir cap (2C251) from hydraulic control unit 
reservoir.

For 3.8L non-ABS vehicles, use needle-nose pliers and remove float from 
hydraulic control unit reservoir. 

Remove brake fluid from hydraulic control unit reservoir. 

On vehicles with ABS, disconnect the HCU supply hose from the brake 
master cylinder reservoir fitting and secure in a position to prevent loss of 
brake fluid. 

Remove primary reservoir port from master cylinder by prying upward 
with rod or long screwdriver. For vehicles with ABS, simultaneously pry the 
brake master cylinder reservoir retaining leg off the pin. 

Remove secondary brake master cylinder reservoir port in same manner 
and discard complete hydraulic control unit reservoir as an assembly. 

Remove grommets from brake master cylinder. 

 Installation 

Coat inside of grommets with clean brake fluid and press into brake 
master cylinder. 

Coat reservoir ports with clean brake fluid and press replacement 
hydraulic control unit reservoir as an assembly into grommets. For 3.8L 
non-ABS vehicles, use needle-nose pliers to install float intohydraulic 
control unit reservoir. For vehicles with other than the 3.8L non-ABS, 
assemble reservoir retaining legs on pins while pressing reservoir ports into 
grommets. 

For vehicles with ABS, connect HCU supply hose to reservoir fitting and 
secure with hose clamp. 

Connect fluid level indicator switch. 

Fill hydraulic control unit reservoir with specified brake fluid to MAX 
line or 4.0 mm (0.16 inch) below MAX line. Use High Performance DOT-3 Motor 
Vehicle brake fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or equivalent fluid meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M6C25-A, DOT 3. 

Check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Brake Pressure Control Valve 

 3.8L Engine With ABS and 4.6L Engine 

 NOTE: The brake pressure control valve assembly is serviced only as an 
assembly. 

With ABS, a remote proportioning valve is used. 

 Removal 

Disconnect the brake inlet tubes and the rear tubes from the brake 
pressure control valve (2B091).

Remove the screw that retains the brake pressure control valve as an 
assembly on the frame. Remove the assembly from the vehicle. 

 Installation

Tighten the tube nut to 14-24 Nm (11-17 lb-ft). 

Bleed the brake system as described.

 3.8L Engine Without ABS 

 Removal 

Disconnect brake tube from the brake pressure control valve.

Remove brake pressure control valve from the brake master cylinder 
(2140). 

 Installation 

Install the brake pressure control valve into the brake master cylinder. 

Connect brake tube to the brake pressure control valve.

Bleed brake system as described.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Hydraulic System Bleeding 

When any part of the hydraulic system has been disconnected for service 
or replacement, air may enter the system causing a spongy pedal action. Bleed 
the hydraulic system after it has been properly connected to make sure all air 
is expelled. 

 Brake Master Cylinder Bleeding 

When a new brake master cylinder (2140) has been installed or the brake 
system emptied or partially emptied, fluid may not flow from the bleeder 
screws during normal bleeding. It may be necessary to prime the system using 
the following procedure:

 CAUTION: Brake fluid is harmful to painted and plastic surfaces. If brake fluid 
is spilled onto a painted or plastic surface, immediately wash it with water. 

Use a tubing wrench to remove the brake tubes from the master cylinder. 

Install short brake tubes in the brake master cylinder and position 
them so that they point back into the reservoir and the ends of the pipes are 
submerged in brake fluid. 

Fill the reservoir with new High Performance DOT-3 Motor Vehicle Brake 
Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A, DOT 
3. 

Cover the reservoir with a clean shop towel.

Pump the brakes until clear, bubble-free fluid comes out of both brake 
tubes.

Remove the short brake tubes and reinstall the ones from the vehicle. 

Bleed each brake tube at the brake master cylinder using the following 
procedure:

Have an assistant pump the brake pedal (2455) 10 times and then hold 
firm pressure on the brake pedal.

Loosen the front brake tube fitting with a tubing wrench until a stream 
of brake fluid comes out. Have your assistant maintain pressure on the brake 
pedal until the brake tube fitting is tightened again. 

Repeat this operation until clear, bubble-free fluid comes out from 
around the tubing fitting. 

Repeat this bleeding operation at the rear brake tube fitting. 

If any of the brake tubes or calipers have been removed, it may be 
helpful to prime the system by gravity bleeding it. This should be done after 
the brake master cylinder is primed and bled. 

To prime the brake system:

Fill the hydraulic control unit reservoir (2C246) with new High 
Performance DOT-3 Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A, DOT 3. 

Loosen both rear caliper bleeder screws and leave them open until clear 
brake fluid flows out. Be sure to check the reservoir fluid level often and 
not let it run dry.

Tighten the bleeder screws. 

One at a time, loosen the front caliper bleeder screws. Leave the 
bleeder screws open until clear fluid flows out. Be sure to check the 
reservoir level often and not let it run dry. 

Tighten the bleeder screws to 7-9 Nm (62-79 lb-in).

After the brake master cylinder has been primed, the lines bled at the 
brake master cylinder and the brake system primed, normal brake system 
bleeding can resume at each wheel.

 Manual Bleeding 

The primary right front and left rear and secondary left front and 
right rear hydraulic brake systems are individual systems and are bled 
separately. Bleed the longest line first on the individual system being 
serviced. During the complete bleeding operation, DO NOT allow the hydraulic 
control unit reservoir to run dry. Keep the hydraulic control unit reservoir 
filled with High Performance DOT-3 Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or 
equivalent fluid meeting Ford specification ESA-M6C25-A, DOT 3. Never reuse 
brake fluid that has been drained from the hydraulic system or has been 
allowed to stand in an open container for an extended period of time.

 NOTE: On vehicles which have the brake master cylinder mounted at an angle, 
bleeding may be better performed if the vehicle is positioned so the brake 
master cylinder is horizontal. 

To bleed the brake system, position a suitable box wrench on the 
bleeder fitting on the rear brake assembly wheel cylinder. Attach a rubber 
drain tube to the wheel cylinder bleeder screw (2208). The end of the tube 
should fit snugly around the wheel cylinder bleeder screw. 

Submerge the free end of the tube in a container partially filled with 
clean brake fluid and loosen the wheel cylinder bleeder screw approximately 
three-quarter turn. 

Have an assistant push the brake pedal down slowly through its full 
travel. Close the wheel cylinder bleeder screw, then return the brake pedal to 
full-release position. Repeat this operation until air bubbles cease to appear 
at the submerged end of the bleeder tube. 

When the fluid is completely free of air bubbles, secure the wheel 
cylinder bleeder screw and remove the bleeder tube. 

Repeat this procedure at the brake assembly on the opposite side. 
Refill the hydraulic control unit reservoir after each wheel cylinder is bled 
and install the brake master cylinder filler cap (2162) and gasket. Make sure 
the diaphragm-type gasket is properly positioned in the brake master cylinder 
filler cap. When the bleeding operation is completed, the fluid level should 
be at the MAX line or 4.0 mm (0.16 inch) below MAX line.

Repeat Steps 1 through 5 on the system not yet bled.

After disc brake service, make sure the disc brake pistons are returned 
to their normal positions and the brake shoe and lining assemblies are 
properly seated. This is accomplished by applying the brake pedal several 
times until normal pedal travel is established. 

Check pedal feel. If brake pedal feels spongy, repeat bleed procedure. 

 Pressure Bleeding 

 CAUTION: Never exceed 344 kPa (50 psi) pressure to prevent system damage. 

For pressure bleeding, use a bladder-type bleeder tank only, such as 
Rotunda Brake Bleeder 104-00064 or equivalent. 

Bleed the longest lines first. The bleeder tank should contain enough 
new brake fluid to complete the bleeding operation. Use High Performance DOT-3 
Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid C6AZ-19542-AB or equivalent fluid meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M6C25-A, DOT 3. Never reuse brake fluid that has been 
drained from the hydraulic system. The tank should be charged with 
approximately 69-206 kPa (10-30 psi) of air pressure. 

Clean all dirt from the brake master cylinder filler cap. 

Remove the brake master cylinder filler cap. Fill the hydraulic control 
unit reservoir with the specified brake fluid. Install the pressure bleeder 
adapter tool to the brake master cylinder and attach the bleeder tank hose to 
the fitting on the adapter. Master cylinder pressure bleeder adapter tools can 
be obtained from various manufacturers. Follow the instructions of the 
manufacturer to install the adapter. 

Use a suitable box wrench on the wheel cylinder bleeder screw at the 
right rear brake assembly. Attach a bleeder tube snugly around the wheel 
cylinder bleeder screw. 

Open the valve on the bleeder tank to admit pressurized brake fluid 
into the master cylinder.

Submerge the free end of the tube in a container partially filled with 
clean brake fluid and loosen the wheel cylinder bleeder screw.

When air bubbles cease to appear in the fluid at the submerged end of 
the bleeder tube, close thewheel cylinder bleeder screw. Remove the tube. 
Replace rubber dust cap on wheel cylinder bleeder screw. 

Attach a bleeder tube and repeat Steps 4, 5 and 6 at the left front 
brake assembly.

Repeat Steps 3 through 7 on the system not yet bled.

When the bleeding operation is completed, close the bleeder tank valve 
and remove the tank hose from the adapter fitting. 

After disc brake service, make sure disc brake pistons are returned to 
their normal positions and the brake shoe and lining assemblies are properly 
seated. This is accomplished by applying the brake pedal several times until 
normal pedal travel is established. 

Check pedal feel. If brake pedal feels spongy, repeat bleed procedure.

 Anti-Lock Brake System Bleeding 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Anti-Lock Brake Adapter

T90P-50-ALA

The anti-lock brake system must be bled in two steps: 

 NOTE: The brake master cylinder and anti-lock brake hydraulic control bracket 
(2C304) must be bled using Anti-Lock Brake Adapter T90P-50-ALA. If this 
procedure is not followed, air will be trapped in the anti-lock brake 
hydraulic control bracket , which will eventually lead to a spongy brake pedal. 

To bleed the brake master cylinder and anti-lock brake control module, 
disconnect the anti-lock brake wiring (2C054) from the anti-lock brake control 
module and install the anti-lock brake adapter to the wire harness anti-lock 
brake wiring.

Place bleed/harness switch in bleed position. 

Turn ignition to ON position. At this point, the red OFF indicator 
should turn on. 

Push motor button on adapter down. This starts the pump motor. The red 
OFF indicator will turn off and the green ON indicator will turn on. The pump 
motor will run for 60 seconds once the motor button is pushed. If the pump 
motor is to be turned off for any reason before this 60 seconds have elapsed, 
push the abort button and the pump motor will turn off. 

After 20 seconds of pump motor operation, push and hold the valve 
button down. Hold valve button for 20 seconds, then release. 

The pump motor (2C256) will continue to run for an additional 20 
seconds. 

The brake lines can be bled in the conventional manner. 

Bleed in the following sequence: 

RH rear

LH front

LH rear

RH front

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Brake Master Cylinder

 CAUTION: Blistering or swelling indicates contamination of brake fluid by a 
petroleum-based solvent or oil. In that case, all rubber components in the 
brake hydraulic system must be inspected and replaced, and the entire system 
must be flushed with clean brake fluid to prevent recontamination. Replace the

front brake caliper seals

rubber front brake tube (2264)/front brake hose (2078)

rear wheel cylinder seals

rubber rear wheel brake hoses (2A442)

brake pressure control valves (2B091)

primary and secondary piston assemblies

reservoir seals

brake master cylinder filler caps (2162)

Wash brake master cylinder body.

 NOTE: The aluminum body of the brake master cylinder (2140) is anodized. Some 
signs of bore wear on the anodized surface, as evidenced by lighter areas of 
the anodized surface, are normal and not detrimental. 

 CAUTION: Honing of the bore on aluminum brake master cylinder is not recommended 
as the anodic coating and hardness could be removed. 

Inspect seals on primary and secondary piston assemblies for cuts, 
nicks, scratches or signs of wear, and for presence of any blistering or 
swelling. 

Inspect master cylinder bore for pitting, corrosion or heavy wear. 
Heavy wear is characterized by scoring or galling of metal.

Brake Booster to Master Cylinder Push Rod

A push rod which is too long will prevent the master cylinder piston 
from completely releasing hydraulic pressure and will cause brakes to drag. 

A push rod which is too short will increase brake pedal travel and will

 Removal 

 NOTE: When the battery (10655) has been disconnected or reconnected, some 
abnormal drive symptoms may occur while the powertrain control module (PCM) 
(12A650) relearns its adaptive strategy. The vehicle may need to be driven 18 
km (11 miles) or more to relearn the strategy.

Disconnect manifold vacuum hose from power brake booster check valve 
(2365). 

Remove two nuts retaining brake master cylinder (2140) to power brake 
booster (2005) assembly and remove brake master cylinder from power brake 
booster.

switch wiring connector from stoplight switch (13480). Remove hairpin retainer 
and outer nylon washer from pedal pin. Slide the stoplight switch off the

switch. Be careful not to damage stoplight switch.

and the brake master cylinder push rod bushing (2474) off the brake pedal pin. 

Inside the engine compartment, move power brake booster forward until 
the booster studs clear the dash panel. Rotate front of power brake booster

clear.

ADJUSTMENTS

Power Brake Booster to Master Cylinder Push Rod

 All Except 3.8 Liter Without ABS 

The vacuum booster push rod (output rod) is not adjustable. The push 
rod length is set during assembly. A properly set push rod that remains within 
the power brake booster (2005) after it was assembled in production should not 
require service. 

A power brake booster suspected of having an improperly set push rod 
length will indicate either of the following: 

A push rod which is too long will prevent brake master cylinder piston 
from completely releasing hydraulic pressure and cause brakes to drag. 

A push rod which is too short will increase brake pedal travel and 
cause a clunk or groaning noise from the power brake booster. 

 3.8L Without ABS 

The power brake boosters have an adjustable push rod (output rod) which 
is used to compensate for dimensional variations in an assembled power brake 
booster. The push rod length is adjusted after each power brake booster has 
been assembled in production. A properly adjusted push rod that remains 
assembled to the power brake booster with which it was matched in production 
should not require a service adjustment.

A power brake booster that is suspected of having an improper push rod 
length will indicate either of the following: 

A push rod that is too long will prevent brake master cylinder piston 
from completely releasing hydraulic pressure and eventually cause brakes to 
drag. 

A push rod that is too short will increase brake pedal travel and cause 
a groaning noise from power brake booster. 

[FIGURE: H3305D.gif]

If necessary, the push rod length of a power brake booster can be 
verified with a push rod gauge by using the following procedure: 

 CAUTION: The brake master cylinder (2140) must be supported to prevent damage to 
the brake tubes. 

Without disconnecting the brake tubes, disconnect the brake master 
cylinder and move it away from the power brake booster. 

 CAUTION: Do not adjust push rod length too long or brake drag could result. 

With engine running, gauge and adjust push rod length. A force of 
approximately 22 N (5 lb) applied to push rod with the gauge will make sure 
push rod is seated within the power brake booster. 

[FIGURE: H3987C.gif]

Install brake master cylinder on power brake booster. Gradually 
alternate tightening retaining nuts to 21-29 Nm (16-21 
lb-ft). Refer to Section 06-06 .

With engine idling and the master cylinder reservoir cover removed, 
observe the fluid surface in reservoirs when brake pedal is applied rapidly. 
Some fluid movement should occur in the forward reservoir. If fluid surface 
movement did not occur, the push rod is adjusted too long and procedure must 
be repeated to prevent eventual brake drag.

Section 06-09: Brake System, Anti-Lock

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake System, Anti-Lock

 WARNING: BRAKE FLUID CONTAINS POLYGLYCOL ETHERS AND POLYGLYCOLS. AVOID CONTACT 
WITH EYES. WASH HANDS THOROUGHLY AFTER HANDLING. IF BRAKE FLUID CONTACTS EYES, 
FLUSH EYES WITH RUNNING WATER FOR 15 MINUTES. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION IF 
IRRITATION PERSISTS. IF TAKEN INTERNALLY, DRINK WATER AND INDUCE VOMITING. GET 
MEDICAL ATTENTION IMMEDIATELY. 

Thunderbird and Cougar have a 4-wheel, anti-lock brake system (ABS) as 
an option. The system operates as follows: 

The ABS system prevents wheel lockup by automatically modulating the 
brake pressure during an emergency stop. 

By not locking the wheels, the driver can maintain steering control and 
stop the vehicle in the shortest possible distance under most conditions. 

The brake pedal force required to engage the ABS function may vary with 
the road surface conditions. A dry surface requires a higher force, while a 
slippery surface requires much less force. 

During anti-lock operation, the driver will sense a pulsation in the 
brake pedal (2455), accompanied by a slight up and down movement in the brake 
pedal height and a clicking sound. The pedal effort and pedal feel during 
normal braking are similar to that of a conventional power brake system.

The anti-lock brake system consists of the following major components: 

power brake booster (2005) and brake master cylinder (2140) assembly

brake pressure control valve (2B091) assembly 

anti-lock brake hydraulic control unit (HCU) 

anti-lock brake control module

two front brake anti-lock sensors (2C204) and two rear brake anti-lock 
sensors (2C190)

anti-lock brake pedal sensor switch (2C309)

Anti-lock brake system operates as follows:

When the brakes are applied, fluid is forced from the brake master 
cylinder outlet ports to the anti-lock brake hydraulic control (HCU) inlet 
ports. This pressure is transmitted through four normally open solenoid valves 
contained inside the HCU, then through the outlet ports of the HCU to each 
wheel. 

The primary (rear) circuit of the brake master cylinder feeds the right 
front and left rear brakes. 

The secondary (front) circuit of the brake master cylinder feeds the 
left front and right rear brakes. 

If the anti-lock brake control module senses a wheel is about to lock, 
based on sensor data, it closes the normally open solenoid valve for that 
circuit. This prevents any more fluid from entering that circuit. 

The anti-lock brake control module then looks at the brake anti-lock 
sensor signal from the affected wheel again. 

If that wheel is still decelerating, it opens the normally closed 
solenoid valve for that circuit. This dumps any pressure trapped between the 
normally open valve and the brake back to the hydraulic control unit reservoir 
(2C246). 

Once the affected wheel comes back up to speed, the anti-lock brake 
control module returns the valves to their normal condition allowing fluid to 
flow to the affected brake. 

The anti-lock brake control module monitors the electromechanical 
components of the system. 

Malfunction of the anti-lock brake system will cause the anti-lock 
brake control module to shut off or inhibit the system. However, normal power 
assisted braking remains. 

Malfunctions are indicated by either of two warning indicators inside 
the vehicle. 

Loss of hydraulic fluid in the HCU brake master cylinder reservoir 
(2K478) will disable the anti-lock system. 

The 4-wheel anti-lock brake system is self-monitoring. When the 
ignition switch is placed in the RUN position, the anti-lock brake control 
module will perform a preliminary self-check on the anti-lock electrical 
system indicated by a three to four second illumination of the amber check 
anti-lock brake indicator in the instrument cluster (10849). 

During vehicle operation, including normal and anti-lock braking, the 
anti-lock brake control module monitors all electrical anti-lock functions and 
some hydraulic operations. 

Each time the vehicle is driven, and reaches approximately 30 km/h (19 
mph) the anti-lock brake control module turns on the pump motor (2C256) for 
approximately one-half second. At this time a mechanical noise may be heard. 
This is a normal function of the self-check by the anti-lock brake control 
module.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Traction Control 

Traction control is offered as an option on vehicles equipped with ABS. 
It is designed to control wheel spin when accelerating on slippery surfaces.

The traction control system operates as follows: 

During acceleration, if one or both rear wheels lose traction and begin 
to spin, the traction control system will rapidly apply and release the 
appropriate rear brake to reduce wheel spin and add traction.

The traction control system monitors brake usage to prevent brake 
overheating. 

If the traction control system is turned off by the anti-lock brake 
control module to prevent the rear brakes from overheating, the indicator lamp 
in the traction control ON/OFF switch will be illuminated. This will not 
affect the anti-lock operation. The traction control system operates at 
vehicle speeds up to approximately 55 km/h (34 mph). For more information, 
refer to Section 06-10 .
