ADJUSTMENTS

Exhaust System Alignment

A misaligned exhaust system is usually indicated by vibration, 
grounding, rattling, or binding of system components. Often the associated 
noise is hard to distinguish from other chassis noises. Look for broken or 
loose clamps and brackets. Replace or tighten as necessary. It is important 
that exhaust clearances and alignment be maintained.

Perform the following procedures to align the system.

Loosen the attaching hardware, clamp and the pipe support brackets.

Align the exhaust system, beginning at the front of the vehicle to 
establish maximum clearance.

 NOTE: Tighten the flange nuts and the exhaust manifold nuts evenly and 
alternately.

Tighten all attachments.

 NOTE: Three way catalytic converters (TWC) (5E212), dual converter Y pipe 
(5F250), muffler inlet pipe, muffler (5230), brackets, clamps and insulators 
should be replaced if they are worn or become badly corroded. Do not attempt 
to service these parts.

Start the engine and check the exhaust system for leaks.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel System Service

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE OR CARRY LIGHTED TOBACCO OR OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN 
WORKING ON OR NEAR ANY FUEL-RELATED COMPONENT. HIGHLY FLAMMABLE MIXTURES ARE 
ALWAYS PRESENT AND MAY BE IGNITED, RESULTING IN POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY. 

When servicing the fuel system, observe the following information: 

All engines use a closed-type positive crankcase ventilation system and 
an exhaust emission system to control engine emissions within Government 
specifications. 

To maintain the required exhaust emission levels the fuel system must 
be kept in good operating condition. 

The fuel system must be adjusted to specifications listed in the 
applicable Section of the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Manual. 

This section covers Diagnosis, Cleaning and Inspection procedures 
related directly to the fuel system. 

Always refer to the Master Parts Catalog for parts usage and 
interchangeability before replacing a component part of the fuel system.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Engine Air Cleaner 

Clean the air cleaner body and the cover with a solvent or compressed 
air. Wipe the air cleaner body and cover dry if a solvent is used. Inspect the 
air cleaner body and cover for distortion or damage at the gasket mating 
surfaces. Replace cover or body if they are damaged beyond service.

================================================================================
PAGE 2722
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 10-00: Fuel System � Service

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Cleaner Element

 CAUTION: Cleaning the air cleaner element (ACL element) (9601) is not 
recommended. Cleaning the air cleaner element will result in restricted airflow. 

Visually inspect the air cleaner element for signs of dust or dirt 
leaking through holes in the filter media or past the sealing edges. Place a 
light on the bottom (clean side) of the air cleaner element and look through 
the filter media at the light. Even the smallest hole is cause for 
replacement. 

Also check the air cleaner element for deformed seals or brittle spots 
that could fail under engine operation and cause a hole. Discoloration only is 
not a cause for replacement. 

Refer to Section 03-12 for Removal and Installation procedures of the 
air cleaner element.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Idle Air Control (IAC) Valve 

 CAUTION: Do not use Carburetor Tune-Up Cleaner D9AZ-19579-BA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P9-A or any other type solvent or damage to 
the valve internal components may result. 

The idle air control valve (IAC valve) (9F715) cannot be cleaned. The 
idle air control valve must be replaced. 

Refer to Section 03-14 for Removal and Installation procedures of the 
idle air control valve.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Injected Engines 

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE, CARRY LIGHTED TOBACCO OR AN OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN 
WORKING ON OR NEAR ANY FUEL-RELATED COMPONENT. HIGHLY FLAMMABLE MIXTURES ARE 
ALWAYS PRESENT AND MAY BE IGNITED, POSSIBLY RESULTING IN PERSONAL INJURY. 

 WARNING: THE FUEL TUBES LEADING FROM THE FUEL TANK (9002) TO THE ENGINE ARE 
UNDER PRESSURE DURING VEHICLE OPERATION. WHEN FUEL-INJECTED ENGINES ARE TURNED 
OFF, THE FUEL IN THE FUEL TUBES REMAINS PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME 
TO PROVIDE QUICK START-UPS. SPECIAL PROCEDURES FOR SERVICING THESE PRESSURIZED 
FUEL SYSTEMS ARE OUTLINED IN THIS SECTION. THESE PROCEDURES SHOULD BE FOLLOWED 
TO PREVENT ACCIDENTAL SPRAYING OF FUEL, CAUSING PERSONAL INJURY OR A FIRE 
HAZARD. 

Fuel-injected engines have the following characteristics:

An electric fuel pump is part of the fuel pump (FP) module. The fuel 
pump provides high-pressure fuel to fuel injectors.

The fuel pump (FP) module is located inside the fuel tank. 

The supply line, which delivers fuel from the fuel tank to the engine, 
is under pressure during vehicle operation. 

A return tube delivers excess fuel from the engine to the fuel tank. 

When fuel-injected engines are turned off, the fuel in the fuel supply 
tubes remains pressurized for long periods to provide quick start-ups. 

Procedures for servicing a pressurized fuel system are described in 
this section.

================================================================================
PAGE 2729
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 10-01: Fuel Tank, Filters, Tubes and Electric Fuel Pump Module

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tank and Fuel Tank Filler Pipe 

The fuel tank (9002) holds approximately 68.1 liters (18 gallons) of 
usable fuel. A restricted fuel tank filler pipe (9034) with a restricted fuel 
filler opening functions as follows: 

The opening in the fuel tank filler pipe allows only non-leaded fuel 
nozzles to be inserted. The restrictor consists of a narrow opening in the 
fuel tank filler pipe covered by a spring steel trap door. 

The smaller nozzle will fit through the narrow opening and push the 
trap door aside, allowing normal filling. Leaded fuel nozzles will not fit 
through the narrow opening. 

Restricted fuel tank filler pipes are manufactured as an assembly and 
must be serviced by removal and replacement with a new fuel tank filler pipe. 

Fuel tank filler pipes are not to be modified in any way. 

Fill limiting is accomplished through the shape of the vent fittings in 
the fuel tank. The fill limiting system is designed to permit an approximate 
10-12 percent fuel tank volume air space when the fuel tank is filled to 
capacity. This air space provides for thermal expansion of fuel as well as 
being an aid to the in-fuel tank vapor vent system. 

[FIGURE: V4564D.gif]

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tank Filler Cap

 WARNING: FUEL TANK (9002) MAY BE PRESSURIZED. TO REMOVE FUEL TANK FILLER CAP 
(9030), ROTATE FUEL TANK FILLER CAP OVER ONE HALF TURN COUNTERCLOCKWISE. IF 
FUEL TANK FILLER CAP IS VENTING FUEL OR A HISSING SOUND IS HEARD, WAIT UNTIL 
CONDITION STOPS BEFORE CONTINUING TO TURN FUEL TANK FILLER CAP. IF THESE 
PRECAUTIONS ARE NOT FOLLOWED, FUEL MAY SPRAY AND CAUSE PERSONAL INJURY. 

The fuel tank filler cap has the following characteristics:

A vacuum relief valve allows air into the fuel tank to replace the fuel 
as it is used. The valve opens after a vacuum of -3.4 kPa (-0.5 psi). 

A pressure valve acts as a backup pressure relief valve if the venting 
system is overpressurized or restricted. The pressure relief range is 
11.1-14.4 kPa (1.6-2.1 psi). 

Damage to the fuel tank filler cap or contamination that stops the 
pressure vacuum valve from working may result in deformation of the fuel tank. 
Care should always be taken to use a proper fuel tank filler cap in good 
working order. 

The fuel tank filler cap is a threaded screw-on with a pre-vent feature 
that allows the fuel tank to vent for the first three-quarter turn before 
unthreading. 

Fuel tank filler caps are attached to the vehicle with a strap using 
the fuel tank filler pipe-to-housing screw at the three to four o'clock 
position. 

The fuel tank filler cap provides vacuum relief functions and should be 
replaced with the proper pressure/vacuum relief fuel tank filler cap to 
prevent possible system malfunction. 

The fuel tank filler cap is fitted with a torque-limiting ratchet to 
ease in removal.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Vapor Valve

Fuel vapor in the fuel tank (9002) is vented to the evaporative 
emissions canister (EVAP canister) (9D653) through the evaporative emission 
valve (9B593) mounted in a rubber grommet at a central location in the upper 
surface of the fuel tank.

A vapor space between the fuel level and the fuel tank upper surface is 
combined with a small orifice and float shut-off valve in the evaporative 
emission valve to prevent liquid fuel from passing to the evaporative 
emissions canister.

The vapor space also allows for thermal expansion of the fuel.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Pump Module

The fuel system has the following characteristics:

It uses a high-pressure in-fuel tank mounted electric fuel pump.

The fuel pump module is a combined assembly with a fuel gauge sender.

Is mounted with its inlet at the bottom of the reservoir in the 
polyethylene fuel tank (9002).

Is designed to increase fuel pump operation during extreme vehicle 
maneuvers and steep climbs with low fuel levels.

The high-pressure fuel pump on the 3.8L and 4.6L (2V) engines can 
supply 95 liters (25.1 gal) of fuel per hour at a working pressure of 269.0 
kPa (39 psi) at 13.2V.

The fuel pump has an internal check valve to maintain pressure in the 
system after the engine is shut down.

The fuel pump also has an internal release valve to provide protection 
from too much pressure if fuel flow becomes clogged in the fuel filter (9155), 
the fuel line is damaged, or other factors.

Overpressure is limited to 850 kPa (123 psi) and reduced fuel flow will 
result if the pressure relief valve is activated.

The fuel pump is protected at its inlet by a nylon fuel filter element 
(9365) which filters contaminants which could plug or damage fuel pump 
components.

The fuel filter element simultaneously allows passage of small 
quantities of water which may accumulate within the fuel tank reservoir.

The electrical system has a fuel pump control relay controlled by the 
powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650) which provides power to the fuel pump 
module through an inertia fuel shutoff switch (IFS switch) (9341) that is 
normally closed.

The electrical system provides power to the fuel pump module through 
two relays:

fuel pump power relay 

PCM power relay 

The current path depends on operating conditions.

When the ignition switch is OFF, contacts of both relays are open.

When the ignition switch is first turned to RUN, the PCM power relay 
energizes and closes its contacts.

Power is sent to the fuel pump relay and a timing device in the 
powertrain control module.

The fuel pump module runs through the contacts of the fuel pump relay.

If ignition switch is not turned to START, the timing device in the 
powertrain control module will open ground Circuit 57 after about a second.

Opening the ground circuit deenergizes the fuel pump relay, which opens 
its contacts and de-energizes the fuel pump.

The circuitry provides pre-pressurization of the fuel system.

When the ignition switch is turned to START, the powertrain control 
module operates the fuel pump relay to provide fuel while cranking.

After the engine starts and the ignition switch is in RUN, power to the 
fuel pump is again supplied through the fuel pump relay. The powertrain 
control module senses engine speed and shuts the fuel pump OFF by opening the 
ground circuit to the fuel pump relay when the engine stops or is below 120 rpm.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Inertia Fuel Shutoff (IFS) Switch

 WARNING: DO NOT RESET THE INERTIA FUEL SHUTOFF SWITCH (IFS SWITCH) (9341) UNTIL 
THE COMPLETE FUEL SYSTEM HAS BEEN INSPECTED FOR LEAKS OR POSSIBLE PERSONAL 
INJURY OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE MAY OCCUR. 

In the event of a collision, the electrical contacts in the inertia 
fuel shutoff switch open and the fuel pump automatically shuts off.

the fuel pump will shut off even if the engine does not stop running, 
the engine, however, will stop a few seconds after the fuel pump stops. 

it is not possible to restart the engine until the inertia fuel shutoff 
switch is manually reset.

The inertia fuel shutoff switch is located in the LH side lower back 
panel in the luggage compartment. 

 NOTE: In the reset position, the button can be pressed an additional 1.59 mm 
(0.0625 inch) against a spring. This is a normal condition.

To reset the inertia fuel shutoff switch, press button on top of 
inertia fuel shutoff switch.

 Installation 

 NOTE: If fuel pump module has been removed, the fuel pump mounting gasket 
(9417) must be replaced.

Before proceeding, check fuel pump module area for leaks. If necessary, 
tighten with Fuel Tank Sender Wrench T74P-9275-A. Refer to Fuel Pump Module 
Removal and Installation procedures as described.

Make sure evaporative emission valve (9B593) is properly installed on 
the fuel tank top. 

Connect all required fuel tube, fuel return tube, vapor vent and 
electrical connections which will be inaccessible after the fuel tank is 
installed. 

Replace or install all body-mounted fuel tank shields. 

Check the hoses and wiring mounted on the fuel tank top to make sure 
they are correctly routed and will not be pinched between the fuel tank and 
rear floor pan (11215) or driveshaft. 

 NOTE: If required, tape hoses and wiring to fuel tank top to verify they are 
correctly routed and will not be pinched between fuel tank and body.

Place fuel tank in its proper position underbody.

Lubricate the fuel tank to filler pipe hose with water-base tire 
mounting lubricant. Install the fuel tank onto the fuel tank to filler pipe 
hose; then bring the fuel tank into final position. Tighten fuel tank to 
filler pipe hose clamps to 2.7-3.7 Nm (24-32 lb-in).

 CAUTION: Make sure the fuel vent hose is positioned above the vent retainer and 
not contacting the driveshaft. 

Bring fuel tank support straps around the fuel tank and start the 
retaining bolts. Align fuel tank with the fuel tank support straps and rear 
floor pan.

Tighten the fuel tank support straps retaining bolts to 30-40 Nm
 (22-29 lb-ft). 

Reconnect the fuel hoses and tubes which were disconnected. Make sure 
that the fuel supply, fuel return (if present) and vapor vent connections are 
made correctly. Trace the various tubes to the engine and refer to the 
applicable system illustrations to make sure the proper tubes are connected. 

 CAUTION: Make sure that fuel tank shield is installed or possible damage to the 
fuel tank may occur. 

Install exhaust system. Refer to Section 09-00 . 

Lower vehicle.

Install fuel filler neck to body bolt. Tighten to 2.7-3.7 Nm
 (24-32 lb-in).

Replace fuel drained from fuel tank as described in Fuel Filling.

Check all connections for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Filter(s)

 In-Tank 

 Removal 

Remove fuel tank (9002) as described.

Remove fuel pump module as described.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

 In-Line 

 Removal 

 WARNING: BECAUSE OF THE COMBUSTION CHARACTERISTICS OF GASOLINE, ALWAYS USE 
EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING AND INSTALLING ANY FUEL SYSTEM COMPONENT OR 
PERSONAL INJURY OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE MAY OCCUR. 

Relieve fuel system pressure as described under Fuel System Pressure 
Relief. 

Raise vehicle on hoist.

Remove the push connect fittings at both ends of the fuel filter (9155) 
as described. Install new retainer clips in each push connect fitting. 

Remove fuel filter from fuel filter bracket (9A335) by loosening worm 
gear clamp. Note the direction of the flow arrow as installed in the fuel 
filter to make sure proper direction of fuel flow through replacement fuel 
filter. 

 Installation 

Install the fuel filter into the fuel filter bracket, ensuring the 
proper direction of flow. 

Tighten worm gear clamp to 1.7-2.8 Nm (15-24 lb-in). 

Install the push connect fittings onto the fuel filter as described. 

Lower vehicle.

Start engine and inspect for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Pump Module

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Fuel Pressure Gauge

T80L-9974-B

Fuel Tank Sender Wrench

T74P-9275-A

 Removal 

Place vehicle on hoist; do not raise. 

Install Fuel Pressure Gauge T80L-9974-B and relieve fuel system 
pressure as described. Refer to Service Procedures, Fuel System Pressure Relief .

Drain fuel from fuel tank (9002) as described. 

Raise vehicle on hoist.

Remove the exhaust system as required. Refer to Section 09-00 . 

 NOTE: The plastic fuel tube connections are on top of the fuel tank and are 
inaccessible. The fuel tank must be lowered to gain access to the connections. 

Disconnect fuel hoses and tubes. Disconnect one end of the vapor 
crossover hose at the rear over the driveshaft (4602). Disconnect fuel tank to 
filler pipe hose (9047). 

Place a safety support under the fuel tank. Remove the bolts from the 
fuel tank support straps (9092). Take care not to deform the fuel tank or fuel 
tank support straps. This will avoid affecting fuel tank capacity or fuel 
pick-up. 

Lower the fuel tank and disconnect the rear fuel supply return and 
vapor tube (9S278) and electrical connector from the fuel pump module, if 
required. Refer to Push Connect Fittings Removal, if so equipped. 

Move fuel tank to bench.

Remove any dirt that has accumulated around the fuel tank sending unit 
retaining flange so that it will not enter the fuel tank during removal and 
installation. 

Turn the fuel pump locking retainer ring (9C385) counterclockwise using 
Fuel Tank Sender Wrench T74P-9275-A and remove fuel pump locking retainer ring. 

Remove fuel pump module. 

Remove fuel pump mounting gasket (9417) and discard. 

 Installation 

Clean the fuel pump module retaining flange, fuel tank mounting surface 
and fuel pump mounting gasket groove. 

Apply a light coating of Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or XG-1-K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B on a new fuel pump mounting 
gasket to hold it in place during assembly and install in fuel pump mounting 
gasket groove. 

Install fuel pump module carefully to make sure that fuel filter 
element (9365) is not damaged. Make sure locating keys are in keyways and fuel 
pump mounting gasket remains in groove. 

Hold fuel pump module in place and install fuel pump locking retainer 
ring finger-tight. Make sure that all locking tabs are under fuel pump module 
locking retainer ring tabs. 

Secure the fuel pump module by rotating the fuel pump locking retainer 
ring clockwise using Fuel Tank Sender Wrench T74P-9275-A until fuel pump 
locking retainer ring stops against stop. 

Move fuel tank from bench to vehicle.

 CAUTION: Make sure that fuel tank heat shields (9A032) are installed and are 
positioned correctly or possible damage to the fuel tank may occur. 

Install fuel tank in vehicle as described.

Lower vehicle. 

Install a minimum of 38 liters (10 gal) of fuel and check for leaks. 

Install Fuel Pressure Gauge T80L-9974-B on the fuel pressure relief 
valve (9H321). Turn ignition switch from OFF to ON position for three seconds. 
Turn ignition switch for three seconds repeatedly (5 to 10 times) until 
pressure gauge shows at least 241 kPa (35 psi). Check for leaks at fittings. 

Remove pressure gauge, start engine and re-check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel and Vapor Return Tubes

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY TUBES ON VEHICLES WITH FUEL INJECTED ENGINES WILL REMAIN 
PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. THE PRESSURE MUST 
BE RELIEVED BEFORE SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM. REFER TO FUEL 
SYSTEM PRESSURE RELIEF . 

 CAUTION: Ford-approved nylon fuel tubing is made from material which has been 
tested and proven to be acceptable for use with commercially available fuels. 
It is also resistant to most environmental conditions. Avoid using alternate 
tubing materials as this could pose a hazard in service. 

 CAUTION: Nylon fuel tube must not be repaired using hose and hose clamps. Should 
the plastic tubes, push connect fittings or steel tube ends become damaged and 
leak, approved service parts shown in the illustration must be used to service 
the fuel tubes. 

 CAUTION: The plastic fuel tubes can be damaged by torches, welding sparks, 
grinding and other operations which involve heat and high temperatures. If any 
repair or service operation will be used which involves heat and high 
temperatures, locate all fuel system components, especially the plastic fuel 
tubes, to make sure they are not damaged. It is recommended that the plastic 
fuel tubes be removed from the vehicle if a torch or high heat producing 
equipment is to be used for service in the following areas: 

 exhaust or suspension components in proximity to fuel 
tubes 

 floorpan under vehicle and inside the passenger 
compartment (RH side) 

 rocker panel (RH side) 

 underbody frames, rails and crossmembers (RH side) 

 dash panel, under vehicle or inside the passenger 
compartment (lower RH side) 

 front or rear wheel house/fender apron (RH side) 

The nylon fuel tubes are of a two-piece (front and rear) design. The 
front fuel supply return and vapor tube (9S286) and rear fuel supply return 
and vapor tube (9S278) are joined together in the area of the fuel filter 
(9155). They are located under the body, below front passenger seat. 

 Front Fuel Tube Assembly 

 Removal 

Relieve fuel system pressure as described. Refer to Service Procedures, Fuel System Pressure Relief 
.

On 4.6L engine, release fuel tube clip (9A317) located on dash and 
release spring lock coupling as described.

Remove tethers which secure the spring lock coupling retainer clips to 
the fuel tubes. 

Disconnect spring lock couplings from fuel injection supply manifold 
(9F792) and fuel filter outlet. 

Raise vehicle.

Remove RH front fender liner. 

Remove two screws attaching the plastic retainer/shield to the front 
side rear member (10535). 

Disconnect front fuel supply return and vapor tube by disconnecting the 
push connect at the fuel filter outlet. 

Disconnect front fuel supply return and vapor tube from the rear fuel 
supply return and vapor tube by disconnecting the push connect fittings 
located rearward of the fuel filter. 

Disconnect vapor tube from evaporative emissions canister (EVAP 
canister) (9D653) and remove two retaining clips in the RH front fender apron 
(16054). 

The front fuel supply return and vapor tube can now be removed from the 
vehicle by pulling the front fuel supply return and vapor tube out through the 
front fender apron opening. 

 Installation 

Feed front fuel supply return and vapor tube through the front fender 
apron opening. 

Connect front fuel supply return and vapor tube to evaporative 
emissions canister and install two retaining clips in the front fender apron.

Connect front fuel supply return and vapor tube to rear fuel supply 
return and vapor tube by connecting the push connect fittings located rearward 
of fuel filter. 

Connect front fuel supply return and vapor tube push connect fitting to 
fuel filter outlet. 

Install plastic retainer/shield to the front side rear member with two 
screws. 

Install front fender liner. 

On 4.6L engine connect spring lock coupling as described.

Lower vehicle.

Connect spring lock couplings to fuel injection supply manifold. 

Install tethers and retainer clips removed in Step 4 of the Removal 
procedure. 

 Fill fuel tank (9002), start engine and check for leaks.

 Rear Fuel Tube Assembly 

 Removal 

Relieve fuel system pressure as described. Refer to Service Procedures, Fuel System Pressure Relief 
.

Drain fuel from fuel tank as described.

of the fuel tank.

Disconnect rear fuel supply return and vapor tube from front fuel

Connect rear fuel supply return and vapor tube to front fuel supply 
return and vapor tube by connecting the push connect fittings located rearward 
of the fuel filter.

Fill fuel tank, start engine and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Push Connect Fittings

 Steel 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Fuel Line Disconnect Tool 5/16 Inch (Part of T90T-9550-S)

T90T-9550-B

Fuel Line Disconnect Tool 3/8 Inch (Part of T90T-9550-S)

T90T-9550-C

 Removal 

 NOTE: This fitting consists of a body, spacers, O-rings and a retaining clip. 
The clip locks the fitting onto the fuel or vapor tube depending on application.

Inspect visible internal portion of fitting for dirt accumulation. If 
more than a light coating of dust is present, clean the fitting before 
disassembly. 

 NOTE: If necessary, drain fuel tank (9002) as described. 

Some adhesion between the seals in the fitting and the tubes will occur 
with time. To separate, twist the fitting on the tube, then push and pull the 
fitting until it moves freely on the tube. 

 NOTE: Some fuel tubes have a secondary bead which aligns with the outer 
surface of the clip. These beads can make tool insertion difficult. 

To disengage the tube from the fitting, snap the Fuel Line Disconnect 
Tool T90T-9550-B (5/16 inch) and T90T-9550-C (3/8 inch) (Part of Fuel Line 
Disconnect Tool Set T90T-9550-S) with either tab on the fuel line to be 
disconnected. 

Push the disconnect tool into the connector to release the internal 
locking fingers. 

[FIGURE: V7615A.gif]

 NOTE: Only moderate effort is required if the tube has been properly 
disengaged. Use hands only.

Separate fuel or vapor tube from the connector. Remove disconnect tool. 

[FIGURE: V7616A.gif]

After disassembly, inspect and clean the tube end sealing surface. Tube 
end should be free of scratches and corrosion as they result in path for fuel 
or vapor leakage. Inspect the inside of the fitting for any internal parts 
such as O-rings and spacers that may have been dislodged from the fitting. 
Replace any damaged connector. 

 Installation 

Install new connector/hose tube assembly if damage was found. 

Before installing fitting on the tube, wipe tube end with a clean 
cloth. Inspect the inside of the fitting to make sure it is free of dirt 
and/or obstructions. 

To install the fitting onto the tube, align the fitting and tube 
axially and push the fitting onto the tube end. When the fitting is engaged, a 
definite click will be heard. Pull on fitting to make sure it is fully 
engaged. Applying a light coat of engine oil to the tube end will ease 
assembly. 

 Hairpin Clip Fittings 

 Removal 

 NOTE: If necessary, drain fuel tank as described. 

Inspect visible internal portion of fitting for dirt accumulation. If 
more than a light coating of dust is present, clean the fitting before 
disassembly. 

 NOTE: Push connect fittings are designed with a retaining clip. The fittings 
used with 9.5 mm and 7.9 mm (3/8 and 5/16 inch) diameter tubing use a 
hairpin-type clip. Clips should be replaced whenever a connector is removed.

Some adhesion between the seals in the fitting and the tubing will 
occur with time. To separate, twist the fitting on the tube, then push and 
pull the fitting until it moves freely on the tube. 

 CAUTION: Do not use any tools. The use of tools may cause a deformity in clip 
components which may cause fuel leaks. 

Remove hairpin-type clip from fitting by first bending and breaking the 
shipping tab. Next, (USING HANDS ONLY) spread the two clip legs about 3.2 mm 
(0.125 inch) each to disengage the body and push the legs into the fitting. 
Complete removal is accomplished by LIGHTLY pulling from the triangular end of 
the clip and working it clear of the tube and fitting. 

 NOTE: On 90-degree elbow connectors, excessive side loading could break the 
connector body. 

Grasp the fitting and hose assembly and pull in an axial direction to 
remove the fitting from the steel tube. 

After disassembly, inspect and clean tube end sealing surface. Tube end 
should be free of scratches and corrosion as they result in a path for fuel or 
vapor leakage. Inspect inside of fitting for any internal parts such as O-ring 
and spacer that may have been dislodged from the fitting. Replace damaged 
connector; do not repair it.

 Installation 

Install a new connector hose assembly if connector was found to be

and/or obstructions. Apply a light coat of engine oil meeting Ford

axially and push the fitting onto the tube end. When the fitting is engaged, a 
definite click will be heard. Pull on fitting to make sure it is fully 
engaged.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring Lock Coupling

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE, CARRY LIGHTED TOBACCO OR AN OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN 
WORKING ON OR NEAR ANY FUEL-RELATED COMPONENT. HIGHLY FLAMMABLE MIXTURES ARE 
ALWAYS PRESENT AND MAY BE IGNITED, RESULTING IN POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY. 

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY LINES ON VEHICLES EQUIPPED WITH FUEL INJECTED ENGINES 
REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. FUEL SYSTEM 
PRESSURE MUST BE RELIEVED PRIOR TO FUEL SYSTEM SERVICE TO PREVENT POSSIBLE

 Removal

[FIGURE: V10147A.gif]

[FIGURE: V10148A.gif]

release the female fitting from the garter spring.

[FIGURE: V10149A.gif]

Pull the coupling male and female fittings apart.

[FIGURE: V10150A.gif]

Remove the Spring Lock Coupling Disconnect Tool from the disconnected 
spring lock coupling.

[FIGURE: V10151A.gif]

 NOTE: Inspect coupling for missing or damaged O-rings. If either O-ring is 
damaged both O-rings must be replaced. Replace O-rings or garter springs with 
appropriate replacement parts only. 

Clean fittings with solvent.

[FIGURE: V10156A.gif]

[FIGURE: AV0219A.gif]

Insert male fitting into female fitting and push together until garter 
spring is engaged.

[FIGURE: V10153A.gif]

Pull on fittings to make sure coupling engagement.

Install clip to spring lock coupling.

[FIGURE: V10154B.gif]

Make sure clip is correctly installed.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fuel Tanks 

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY TUBES ON VEHICLES EQUIPPED WITH FUEL INJECTED ENGINES WILL 
REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. THE 
PRESSURE MUST BE RELIEVED BEFORE SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM OR PERSONAL INJURY 
OR DAMAGE TO VEHICLE MAY OCCUR. REFER TO FUEL SYSTEM PRESSURE RELIEF . 

 CAUTION: Polyethylenefuel tanks (9002) are not repairable including all portions 
of the fuel tank body and plastic fittings attached to it. There is no 
acceptable repair procedure that meets new fuel tank standards. Fuel tank 
replacement is the only acceptable service. 

 CAUTION: Take care not to let steam-cleaning tubing touch plastic as it will 
damage/distort the fuel tank. Do not direct steam jet at one spot on the 
plastic fuel tank for a prolonged period as it may damage/distort the fuel 
tank. 

 NOTE: Plastic fuel tanks may be steam-cleaned using standard procedures. 

If required, steam clean fuel tank.

After cleaning, allow fuel tank to thoroughly air-dry.

Section 10-01: Fuel Tank, Filters, Tubes and Electric Fuel Pump Module

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Fuel System � Pressurized

 CAUTION: Ford-approved nylon fuel tubing is made from material which has been 
tested and proven to be acceptable for use with commercially available fuels. 
It is also resistant to most environmental conditions. Avoid using alternate 
tubing materials as this could pose a hazard in service. 

 CAUTION: Nylon fuel tube must not be repaired using hose and hose clamps. Should 
the plastic tubes, push connect fittings or steel tube ends become damaged and 
leak, approved service parts shown in the illustration must be used to service 
the fuel tubes. 

Vehicles equipped with nylon fuel tubes and push connect fittings have 
three types of service that can be performed to the fuel lines: replacing 
nylon tubing (splicing nylon-to-nylon), replacing push connector fittings and 
replacing damaged push connect tube end. 

 Fuel Tube Service Parts 

[FIGURE: V4491D.gif]

 Fuel Tubes, Steel 

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY TUBES ON VEHICLES EQUIPPED WITH FUEL INJECTED ENGINES WILL 
REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. THE 
PRESSURE MUST BE RELIEVED BEFORE SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM OR PERSONAL INJURY 
OR DAMAGE TO VEHICLE MAY OCCUR. REFER TO FUEL SYSTEM PRESSURE RELIEF . 

The tubes attached to the vehicle underbody may be serviced and 
repaired. The metal underbody tubes must be cut and formed out of rolls of 
fuel system service tubing available at the dealerships. 

A damaged section of tubing can be cut out of the existing line and 
replaced by a comparable service tubing section, spliced into the tube by 
means of threaded fasteners and connectors. 

All replacement hoses MUST be serviced as assemblies. Refer to push 
connect fitting installation for connecting procedure. Bulk fuel hose must not 
be used to service tubing in high-pressure fuel systems. 

 Removal 

Drain the fuel from the fuel tank (9002) as described.

Disconnect the line(s) at the fuel tank and at the engine. Remove the 
lines from the holding clips along the underbody. Remove all damaged hoses and 
tube sections. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: After disassembly of the flareless fitting joint, such as at the fuel 
hose-to-fuel line connection, the flareless fitting can be reassembled. To 
reassemble, reconnect the threaded fitting and seat the ferrule to be 
finger-tight. When the ferrule is seated, draw the nut up approximately 
one-sixth to one-third of a turn with a wrench to complete the tightening 
operation. 

Cut a new section of tubing to approximately the same length as the 
section to be replaced, allowing for the threaded connectors/fasteners. 

Bend the tube section to conform to the contour of the original tube. 

Square the ends of the cut tubing with a file. Remove burrs. Blow out 
any particles with compressed air. 

Position the tubes in the underbody clips. Do not tighten at this time. 

[FIGURE: V8607A.gif]

Assemble the fitting by sliding the nut over the tubing with threaded 
(open) end out. 

 CAUTION: Make sure that ferrule is assembled correctly before installing it on 
tube. 

Slide the ferrule on the tubing with the cutting edge out; the large 
head end should be inside of the nut. 

Lubricate the ferrule and the threads on the fasteners with clean 
engine oil meeting Ford specification WSS-M2C910-A1.

Bottom the tube in the fitting and tighten the nut until the ferrule 
just grips the tube. When the tube can no longer be turned by hand, the 
ferrule has started to grip the tube. 

After the ferrule grips the tube, tighten the nut one full turn. 

Tighten the fuel tube to the underbody clips in order to secure the 
fuel tubes. 

Fill the fuel tank and check for leaks. 

 Fuel and Vapor Return Tubes 

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY TUBES ON VEHICLES EQUIPPED WITH FUEL INJECTED ENGINES WILL 
REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. THE 
PRESSURE MUST BE RELIEVED BEFORE SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM OR PERSONAL INJURY 
OR DAMAGE TO VEHICLE MAY OCCUR. REFER TO FUEL SYSTEM PRESSURE RELIEF . 

Fuel injection systems are equipped with an electric fuel pump that 
provides fuel to the engine at higher pressure than conventional fuel systems. 
Refer to Fuel Pump Module for service. A fuel return system is also provided. 
All fuel hose/tube connections are made with push connect fittings and all 
hoses are serviced as assemblies. 

All replacement hoses MUST be serviced as assemblies. Refer to Push 
Connect Fittings installation for connecting procedure. Bulk fuel hose must not 
be used to service tubing in high-pressure fuel systems. 

 Splicing Nylon to Nylon 

Relieve fuel system pressure as described in Fuel System 
Pressure Relief . 

Drain fuel tank as described if necessary. 

Cut a section of service tubing (type 11 or 12 nylon available in 1/4 
and 5/16-inch sizes) to the same length as the damaged section of tubing. 

 CAUTION: Do not use any heating method except hot water to repair nylon tubing. 
Temperatures above 100°C (212°F) cause the 
nylon to soften and will not seal on the barbed connectors. Replacing nylon 
line in the engine compartment requires heat protective Hypalon hose. 

 NOTE: To make hand-insertion of the barbed connectors into the nylon easier, 
the tube end must be soaked in a cup of boiling water for one minute 
immediately before pushing the barbs into the nylon. The 5/16-inch barbed 
connector is used for splicing 5/16-inch non EFI and 5/16-inch EFI tubing. 

Select the proper (1/4 or 5/16-inch) barbed connectors for completing 
the splice. Two connectors are required for each splice.

Push Connectors, Nylon

 NOTE: Damaged push connectors must be discarded and replaced with new push

Cut out a section of the original tube to the same length as the nylon 
tube attached to the new push connector. 

 CAUTION: Do not use any heating method except hot water to repair nylon tubing. 
Temperatures above 100°C (212°F) cause the

line in the engine compartment requires heat protective Hypalon hose. 

 NOTE: To make hand insertion of barbed connectors into the nylon easier, the 
tube end must be soaked in a cup of boiling water for one minute immediately

illustration following Step 4, Splicing Nylon to Nylon procedure for all

Section 10-02: Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

The throttle is controlled by an accelerator cable (9A758) and an
accelerator pedal and shaft (9725). The following should be noted when 
servicing the system:

The accelerator pedal and shaft should travel smoothly from an idle to 
wide open throttle (WOT) position. 

Hesitation on return and/or prevention of return to idle position must 
not occur throughout the total travel of the accelerator pedal and shaft. 

Surrounding components such as wiring, hoses, sound insulator and floor 
covering must not contact the sliding inner member of the accelerator cable or 
the accelerator pedal and shaft. 

The sliding inner member accelerator cable should not be lubricated and 
it is not serviceable.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

shaft (9725) to duplicate the condition.

Visually inspect the accelerator pedal and shaft,accelerator cable 
(9A758) and accelerator cable bracket (9723) for obvious damage and 
interference.

Correct any obvious concerns, such as pedal interference from floor 
mats or obvious damage to accelerator cable.

If concern(s) remain after inspection, determine the conditions and go 
to Symptom Chart.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Accelerator Cable 

 Removal and Installation 

Using a suitable tool, push the accelerator pedal nylon bushing out of 
the accelerator pedal and shaft arm. 

Remove accelerator cable housing from dash panel (01610) by removing 
two screws retaining accelerator cable housing to dash panel and pushing 
outward from inside passenger compartment. 

Remove speed control actuator cable (9A825), if equipped. Refer to 
 Section 10-03 . 

On the 3.8L engine, remove the throttle body lever snow shield.

Disconnect the accelerator cable (9A758) at the throttle body lever by 
inserting a screwdriver between the accelerator cable and the throttle body 
lever and giving a twist. 

Remove the accelerator cable housing to accelerator cable mounting 
bracket retaining bolt. 

On 3.8L engine, remove accelerator cable from accelerator cable 
retainer (9E728) on upper intake manifold brace. 

Refer to Diagnosis and Testing for diagnosis of 
the Accelerator Pedal and Shaft (9725) after the disconnection of the accelerator cable from the 
throttle body lever. Disconnect speed control actuator cable from the 
accelerator cable, if equipped. 

To install, reverse Removal procedure and make sure accelerator cable 
movement is not restricted. Tighten accelerator cable to accelerator cable 
mounting bracket retaining bolt to 5-7 Nm (45-61 lb-in). On 
3.8L engine, tighten throttle body lever snow shield nut to 3.4-4.8 Nm
 (31-42 lb-in).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Accelerator Pedal and Shaft

 Removal and Installation 

Using a suitable tool, push the accelerator cable nylon bushing out of 
the accelerator pedal and shaft arm. 

Remove the two nuts retaining accelerator pedal and shaft (9725) to the 
floor. 

To install, reverse Removal procedure. Tighten accelerator pedal and 
shaft nuts to 15-20 Nm (12-14 lb-ft) and make sure 
accelerator pedal and shaft moves without restrictions.

Section 10-03: Speed Control System � Electronic

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Speed Control System

The speed control system consists of the following:

speed control servo (9C735)

speed control actuator cable (9A825)

vehicle speed sensor (VSS) (9E731)

horn relay and bracket (13853)

speed control actuator switch (9C888)

stoplight switch (13480)

deactivator switch (Part of 2B091)

brake pressure control valve (2B091)

air bag sliding contact

The system operates independently of engine vacuum, therefore no vacuum 
lines are required.

The speed control servo:

is mounted under the LH front fender (16005), forward of the wheel.

connects to the throttle linkage with a speed control cable.

integrates system electronics, eliminating the need for any other speed 
control electronic modules. 

The speed control actuator switch assembly is mounted in the steering 
wheel (3600). It consists of: 

LH switches (ON, OFF).

RH switches (RESUME, SET, ACCEL, COAST).

necessary wiring.

[FIGURE: L8770A.gif]

The vehicle speed sensor (VSS):

is mounted to the transmission. 

is a magnetic pickup driven by a gear which is driven by the 
transmission. 

sends a signal to the speed control servo proportional to vehicle speed.

The air bag sliding contact:

is located at the center of steering wheel.

transfers electrical signals from the steering column wiring to the 
following components:

driver side air bag module (043B13).

horn blow switch (13A875).

speed control actuator switch.

The stoplight switch:

is a normally open switch that closes when the brake pedal (2455) is 
applied.

sends an electrical signal to the speed control servo when closed and 
disengages speed control system. 

returns to its open position when the brake pedal is released.

Refer to Section 17-01 for additional information.

The deactivator switch:

is a normally closed switch. 

replaces the speed control dump valve (9C727) as a redundant safety 
feature in the system.

Under normal conditions, when the brake pedal is applied, an electrical 
(brake on/off) signal from the stop lamp circuit to the speed control servo 
will disengage the system. 

Under increased brake pedal efforts (36-67 N [8-15 
lbs] engine running), the deactivator switch will open and remove power to the 
speed control servo, releasing the throttle from servo control.

The deactivator switch is located on the brake pedal support assembly.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Speed Control Actuator Switch Assembly

 Removal 

 WARNING: THE POSITIVE BATTERY CABLE MUST BE DISCONNECTED BEFORE ANY AIR BAG 
COMPONENT IS SERVICED. 

 WARNING: THE ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT NECESSARY FOR SYSTEM DEPLOYMENT IS POWERED 
DIRECTLY FROM THE BATTERY AND BACKUP POWER SUPPLY. TO AVOID ACCIDENTAL 
DEPLOYMENT AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY, THE BATTERY POSITIVE CABLE MUST BE 
DISCONNECTED FOR ONE MINUTE TO DE-ENERGIZE THE BACKUP POWER SUPPLY PRIOR TO 
SERVICING OR REPLACING ANY SYSTEM COMPONENTS. 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 . 

Disconnect positive battery cable and wait one minute for backup power 
supply to deplete its stored energy. Refer to Section 01-20B . 

Remove two back cover plugs. Remove two screw and washer assemblies 
retaining driver side air bag module (043B13) to steering wheel (3600). 

Disconnect air bag electrical connector from air bag sliding contact 
connector. 

[FIGURE: G7687B.gif]

 WARNING: PLACE AIR BAG MODULE ON BENCH WITH TRIM COVER FACING UP. 

Remove driver side air bag module from steering wheel. 

[FIGURE: L8313C.gif]

Disconnect speed control wire harness. Disconnect horn switch wire.

Remove four retaining screws from speed control actuator switch (9C888).

Carefully pry away RH side of steering wheel back cover to allow enough 
clearance to remove RH side speed control switch wiring from steering wheel. 
Repeat on the LH side and remove speed control actuator switch.

 Speed Control Switch Wire Removal 

[FIGURE: L8712A.gif]

 Speed Control Switch Removal 

[FIGURE: L8314A.gif]

 Installation 

Carefully pry away RH side of the steering wheel back cover to allow 
enough clearance to insert RH side of the speed control switch wiring into 
steering wheel. Repeat on LH side.

Position speed control actuator switch onto steering wheel and install 
four Phillips-head screws. 

 CAUTION: Make sure wires are positioned so no interference is encountered when 
installing air bag module. 

Connect all harness connectors and route wiring in steering wheel 
cavity. Install wire organizer. 

Position driver side air bag module on steering wheel and connect air 
bag sliding contact (14A664). 

Install driver side air bag module on steering wheel and install two 
screw and washer assemblies. Tighten to 10.2-13.8 Nm (91-122 
lb-in). 

Install two back cover plugs. 

Re-connect positive battery cable. 

Re-connect battery ground cable.

Check operation of speed control actuator switch.

Prove out air bag system. Refer to Section 01-20B .

Speed Control Servo

 Removal 

Disconnect speed control cable fitting from throttle body (9E926) by 
pulling lever arm up and off.

 Section 01-02 .

Remove two screws retaining speed control servo to vehicle. 

Lower vehicle. 

Remove speed control cable cap from speed control servo by pressing cap 
locking arm and rotating speed control cable cap counterclockwise. 

 Speed Control Servo Assembly 

[FIGURE: L8303C.gif]

[FIGURE: L8713B.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Stoplight Switch

 Removal 

 NOTE: Locking tab on connector must be lifted before connector can be removed. 

Disconnect the wire harness at the connector from the stoplight switch 
(13480). 

 NOTE: Since the stoplight switch side plate nearest the brake pedal (2455) is 
slotted, it is not necessary to remove the brake master cylinder push rod and 
one spacer washer from the brake pedal pin. 

Remove the hairpin retainer, slide the stoplight switch, the push rod 
and the nylon washers and bushing away from the brake pedal, and remove the 
stoplight switch by sliding the stoplight switch up/down. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not substitute other types of pin retainers. Replace only with 
production hairpin retainer. 

Position stoplight switch so that the U-shaped side is nearest the 
brake pedal and directly over/under the pin. Then slide stoplight switch 
up/down trapping the master cylinder push rod and blade bushing between the 
stoplight switch sideplates. Push stoplight switch and push rod assembly 
firmly toward brake pedal arm. Assemble outside white plastic washer to pin 
and install hairpin retainer to trap whole assembly. 

 NOTE: Stoplight switch wire harness must have sufficient length to travel 
with switch during full stroke of brake pedal. If wire length is insufficient, 
reroute harness or service as required. 

Assemble the wire harness connector to the stoplight switch and install 
the wires in the retaining clip. 

Check stoplight switch for proper operation.

Actuator Cable

Section 11-00: Steering System � Service

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

 Steering Gear Model 

Steering gears are identified by a dot matrix identification tag on the 
gear housing. Dot matrix tags contain information as shown in the 
illustration. The dot matrix is located on the gear housing between the sector 
cover and valve housing. An identification tag with the same information is 
optional.

[FIGURE: G7151C.gif]

The power steering pump (3A674) has a service identification tag to 
identify assemblies for service purposes. 

[FIGURE: AG0072A.gif]

 Power Steering Pump 

The CIII power steering pump has the following features:

It is a belt driven, vane-type power steering pump.

It is mounted directly to the engine block by four retaining bolts. 

An electronic variable orifice (EVO) power steering control valve 
actuator (3783) is connected to the pump body to control speed sensitive power 
steering assist. 

The electrical connector and casing are able to swivel. This is normal 
and does not indicate a loose power steering control valve actuator assembly. 

The power steering oil reservoir (3A697) for the power steering fluid 
is mounted on the LH apron. 

An identification tag attached to the power steering pump indicates the 
model number and bar code. Refer to these when a new power steering pump is 
required. 

[FIGURE: G5874D.gif]

The power steering pump is serviced as an assembly. If any service is 
required, the entire power steering pump assembly must be replaced. 

The only exception is if the power steering control valve actuator or 
connector on the power steering pump assembly is found to be damaged; then 
replace the power steering control valve actuator only. 

In the event of an electrical circuit malfunction, such as circuit 
open, shorted, or electronic variable orifice (EVO) control module failure, 
the power steering control valve actuator will provide full power steering 
assist during such failure modes. 

Continued operation under such conditions may cause excessively high 
power steering fluid temperature and damage the steering components.

Electrical Schematics

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 43,

and connector information.

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's concerns by operating the steering system to 
duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if any of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

If the concern(s) remain after the inspection, perform the EVO Steering Diagnosis 
 procedure 
(vehicles without computer controlled suspension) using 
the Super Star II as described. Retrieve Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) and 
go to the Symptom Charts.

 Symptom Chart � EVO Diagnosis

connector numbers cited in the pinpoint tests.

Use Rotunda Inductive Dwell Tach-Volt Ohmmeter 164-R0254 or equivalent 
as necessary.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

EVO Steering Diagnosis

 Using the Super Star II Tester 

The Thinderbird, Couger without air suspension is equipped 
with a stand alone EVO steering control module. This control module is 
diagnosed using Rotunda Super Star II Tester 007-0041B or equivalent.

The test connector used to communicate with the EVO control module is 
located on the RH side of the luggage compartment.

 Entering EVO Diagnostics 

When the tester is connected, the engine is started and the HOLD/TEST 
button is latched down, the EVO controller will respond by sending a code 20 
to the Star Tester which represents "Diagnostics mode entered." If diagnostic 
trouble code (DTC) 20 is not displayed, go to Pinpoint Test A.

Once this mode is entered, the EVO control module will continuously 
cycle through a menu of five tests. The EVO control module will scroll through 
these tests waiting eight seconds before proceeding to the next test. If at 
any time in the eight-second period the Star Tester line is toggled high by 
unlatching the HOLD/TEST button for at least one second but less than eight, 
then toggled back low by relatching the HOLD/TEST button, the EVO control 
module will enter and run that selected test. If the HOLD/TEST button is 
unlatched for the entire eight seconds in between any of the tests, the EVO 
control module will exit diagnostic mode and resume operation in its normal 
operating state.

If power is removed at any time while the EVO control module is in 
diagnostic mode, the EVO control module will exit diagnostic mode and resume 
operation in its normal operating state when power is reapplied.

The sequence and definition of the five tests that the service 
technician can perform are as follows:

 Reading the Fault Codes 

The first item on the menu the EVO control module will output to the 
Star Tester is DTC 21. This represents asking the service technician whether 
he/she would like to "Read fault codes?" stored in memory. If the service 
technician releases the HOLD/TEST button for one second, then latches the 
HOLD/TEST down again within eight seconds after receiving DTC 21, the EVO 
control module will enter this test, output the fault DTCs stored in memory 
and complete this test by outputting DTC 22 to the Star Tester which signals 
end of test.

 Clearing the Fault Codes 

The second item on the menu the EVO control module will output to the 
Star Tester is DTC 23. This represents asking the service technician whether 
he/she would like to "Clear fault codes?" stored in memory. If the service 
technician releases the HOLD/TEST button for one second, then latches the 
HOLD/TEST button down again within eight seconds after receiving DTC 23, the 
EVO control module will enter this test, clear the fault DTCs and complete 
this test by outputting DTC 24 to the Star Tester which means DTCs cleared.

 Actuator Output Circuit Test 

The third item on the menu the EVO control module will output to the 
Star Tester is DTC 25. This represents asking the service technician whether 
he/she would like to "Perform actuator test?". If the service technician 
releases the HOLD/TEST button for one second, then latches the HOLD/TEST 
button down again within eight seconds after receiving DTC 25, the EVO control 
module will enter this self-test and automatically test for the actuator 
faults. If faults exist, the control module will store the appropriate codes 
in memory, output these codes to the Star Tester and complete this test by 
outputting DTC 22 to the Star Tester which signals end of test. If no faults 
exist, the control module will complete this test by outputting DTC 26 to the 
Star Tester which represents "Test passed."

 Steering Wheel Sensor Test 

The fourth item on the menu the EVO control module will output to the 
Star Tester is DTC 32. This represents asking the service technician whether 
he/she would like to "Perform steering wheel sensor test?". If the service 
technician releases the HOLD/TEST button for one second, then latches the 
HOLD/TEST button down again within eight seconds after receiving DTC 32, the 
EVO control module will enter this test. Once this test has been entered and 
with vehicle speed 0, the control module will wait 30 seconds for the 
service technician to rotate the steering wheel at least 40 degrees in one 
direction only. If the steering wheel rotation is not detected within this 
time, the control module will store DTC 33 in memory and complete this test by 
outputting DTC 33 to the Star Tester which represents "Steering wheel rotation 
not detected". If the steering wheel sensor hardware is operating properly, 
the control module will complete this test by outputting DTC 26 to the Star 
Tester which means "Test passed." If DTC 33 is received, go to DTC 33.

 Vehicle Speed Sensor Test 

 NOTE: Before entering this test, the vehicle drive wheels must be raised off 
the floor.

The final item on the menu the EVO control module will output to the 
Star Tester is DTC 34. This represents asking the service technician whether 
he/she would like to "Perform vehicle speed sensor test?". If the service 
technician releases the HOLD/TEST button for one second, then latches the 
HOLD/TEST button down again within eight seconds after receiving DTC 34, the 
EVO control module will enter this test. Once this test has been entered and 
with steering wheel rotation rate = 0, the control module will wait 30 seconds 
for the service technician to make the vehicle speed go above 24 km/h (15 
mph). If a vehicle speed of greater than 24 km/h (15 mph) is not detected 
within this time, the control module will store DTC 35 in memory and complete 
this test by outputting DTC 35 to the Star Tester which represents "Vehicle 
speed greater than 15 mph not detected." If the vehicle speed sensor hardware 
is operating properly, the control module will complete this test by 
outputting DTC 26 to the Star Tester which means "Test passed." If DTC 35 is 
received, GO to DTC 35.

After completion of this test, the EVO control module will go back to 
test No. 1 and continuously cycle through the menu of tests until the service 
technician either unlatches the HOLD/TEST button until the control module 
exits this mode or removes power to the EVO control module by turning the 
ignition switch OFF.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Preliminary Procedures 

Make the following preliminary checks before disassembling power 
steering:

 Air Bleeding 

If bubbles are present in the power steering fluid, bleed the system as 
follows: 

Fill the power steering pump reservoir (3E764) with MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent.

Run the engine until the fluid reaches normal operating temperature of 74°
-79°C (165°-175°
F). 

 CAUTION: Do not hold the steering wheel in the far left or right position for 
more than 5 seconds or damage to power steering pump (3A674) may result. 

Turn the steering wheel (3600) all the way to the left and right 
several times. 

Check the fluid level and add fluid as necessary. 

If air is still trapped in the system, refer to Purging 
Power Steering System of Air as described. 

 Fluid Level 

Run the engine until the fluid reaches normal operating temperature of 74°
-79°C (165°-175°
F). 

Turn the steering wheel all the way to the left and right several 
times. Turn the engine off. 

 NOTE: Do not overfill the power steering oil reservoir (3A697). 

Check the fluid level in the power steering oil reservoir. If the level 
is low, add MERCON® Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid 
or equivalent.

 Pump Belt 

Replace broken, glazed or worn drive belt (8620). Refer to Section 03-05 .

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Turning Effort Check

 Power Steering 

Make sure front wheels are properly aligned and tire pressure is 
correct before checking turning effort. 

Park vehicle on dry concrete and set the parking brake. 

Idle the engine for two or three minutes. Turn the steering wheel to 
the left and right several times to warm the fluid to 43°-49°
C (110°-120°F). 

With the engine running, attach a pull scale to the rim of the steering 
wheel. Starting with the road wheels in straight-ahead position, measure the 
pull required to turn steering wheel the one complete revolution in each 
direction. Refer to Static Steering Wheel Turning 
Effort table in Specifications.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

External Leakage

When looking for leaks, use this procedure to pinpoint the exact cause 
and location to avoid misdiagnosis:

Check for overfilled power steering oil reservoir (3A697).

Wipe suspected area dry.

Check for power steering pump overflow and aeration.

Check for exact source. Example: oil may be running down from another 
area (for example, engine) and drip may not be leak source.

 CAUTION: Do not hold the steering wheel against a stop for more than five 
seconds at a time as damage to power steering pump (3A674) may result. 

Cycle the steering wheel from stop-to-stop 10 times and check for 
leaks. The small boot clamp on the tie-rod should be loosened to free the boot 
end which allows movement of the boot to check for leakage.

Some leaks are high-pressure leaks and may require holding steering 
wheel against stops to seep out.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Pump Flow and Pressure Tests 

Before performing the pump flow and pressure test, complete the 
following checks for conditions which could cause loss of power assist. Take 
corrective action if necessary. 

Check power steering oil reservoir (3A697) for proper fluid level. 

Check tires for correct air pressure. 

Check power steering pump (3A674) for correct model and vehicle 
application. 

Check for correct size power steering pump pulley (3A733) forpower 
steering pump and engine. 

Check entire system for damage. Replace parts as necessary. 

If the above items are correct or have been corrected and the loss of 
assist still exists, test the power steering pump flow and pressure to 
determine whether the trouble is in the pump, rack and pinion steering gear or 
hoses. 

 Test Equipment 

Engine tachometer

Thermometer: -17.8° to 148.9°C (0°
 to 300°F)

Rotunda Power Steering System Analyzer 014-00207 or equivalent

Set of adapter fittings 

The test procedure used in conjunction with the Rotunda Power Steering 
System Analyzer 014-00207 or equivalent provides a method for checking the 
complete power steering system. The analyzer can be used on integral or 
non-integral power steering systems to determine the cause of hard steering or 
lack of assist concerns. The analyzer provides readouts for the following: 

system back pressure

power steering pump flow

steering gear internal leakage

power steering pump relief pressure

The interpretation of the above readouts will determine which of the 
following conditions or components are the cause of the concern: 

restriction in hoses or fittings

sticking gear valve

inefficient pump cam pack

sticking relief valve

binding in suspension

 Test Procedure 

To connect the analyzer into the steering system, remove the pressure 
fitting from the power steering pump and connect it into the appropriate 
adapter of the analyzer. 

Thread the other adapter of the analyzer into the pump. 

Connect the analyzer to the adapters. Tighten both connections to 20 Nm
 (15 lb-ft) maximum. 

Add MERCON® Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or 
equivalent to the power steering pump if required. Start the engine and run it 
for approximately two minutes at idle.

 System Back-Pressure 

If pressure is above 1034 kPa (150 psi), check hoses for restrictions.

If pressure recorded is above maximum specification listed, the power 
steering control valve actuator (3783) in the power steering pump should be 
replaced. Refer to Section 11-02 .

 Minimum Pump Flow 

If the flow drops to level lower than the value in the power steering 
pump specification chart, replace the power steering pump. Refer to Section 11-02 . 

If flow exceeds the maximum free flow specified in the chart, the power 
steering control valve actuator in the power steering pump should be removed. 
Refer to Section 11-02 .

 Relief Pressure Test 

If flow is below 6 liters/minute (1.6 gallons/minute), the power 
steering pump may require service. At this point continue diagnosis.

 Internal Leakage Test 

If pressure does not reach maximum output or flow does not drop below 
1.9 liters/minute (0.5 gallons/minute) excessive internal leakage is 
occurring. Replace power steering pump. Refer to Section 11-02 .

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Steering Wheel Free Play

With the wheels in the straight ahead position, gently turn steering 
wheel the to the left and right to check free play. Free play should be 
between 0 and 30 mm (0 and 1.18 inches). If the free play exceeds this limit, 
either the steering joints are worn or the backlash of the power rack and 
pinion steering gear is excessive.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Purging Power Steering System of Air 

 NOTE: If the air is not purged from the power steering system correctly, a 
second customer concern or pump failure could result. This condition can only 
occur on vehicles that have had steering component service.

A whine noise heard from the power steering pump may be caused by air 
in the system.

The power steering system must be purged of air whenever any of the 
following services are performed:

All power steering noise complaints with evidence of aerated fluid on 
pre-delivery vehicles only, prior to any component service

Replacement of any power steering system component (for example, gear, 
hose)

 Fluid Level Top-Off Procedure 

Check and fill power steering oil reservoir (3A697) to dipstick FULL 
COLD or power steering pump reservoir (3E764) center mark with MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent.

Disable ignition by disconnecting the ignition coil wire. 

Crank engine 30 seconds, check fluid level and add if required.

 NOTE: Do not hold steering wheel on stops.

Crank engine 30 seconds while cycling lock to lock.

Check fluid level and add fluid if required.

 Air Purge With Vacuum External Source Procedure 

Tightly insert the rubber stopper of the air evacuator assembly into 
power steering oil reservoir or power steering pump reservoir.

Reconnect connection used to disable ignition. Start vehicle.

Apply 20-25 in-Hg (68-85 kPa) maximum vacuum for minimum of three 
minutes at idle; maintain maximum vacuum with vacuum source.

Release vacuum and remove vacuum source.

Add fluid to power steering oil reservoir full warm mark or power 
steering pump reservoircenter mark.

Reinstall vacuum source and apply 20-25 in-Hg (68-85 kPa) vacuum.

 NOTE: Do not hold steering wheel on stops.

Cycle steering wheel from lock to lock every 30 seconds for 
approximately five minutes.

Shut engine off, release vacuum and remove vacuum source.

Add fluid if necessary, install dipstick or reservoir cap.

 NOTE: Do not hold steering wheel on stops.

Start engine and cycle steering wheel from lock to lock every 30 
seconds for approximately five minutes.

Check for oil leaks at all connections.

In severe cases it may be necessary to repeat air purge with vacuum 
source procedure.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Start-Up Procedure After Power Steering Pump or Gear Service 

After engine start up, follow these steps to eliminate excessive 
steering system noise due to air trapped in the system during service: 

Disconnect the ignition coil wire and raise front wheels off floor.

Fill the power steering oil reservoir (3A697) with MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent.

Crank the engine with the starter motor and add MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent until the level remains 
constant. 

 NOTE: Front wheels must be off the floor during lock-to-lock rotation of the 
steering wheel. 

While cranking the engine, rotate the steering wheel from lock-to-lock. 

Check the fluid level and add MERCON® Multi-Purpose 
(ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent if necessary. 

Connect the ignition coil wire. 

Start the engine and allow it to run for several minutes. 

Rotate steering wheel from lock-to-lock. 

Turn off the engine and check the fluid level. Add MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent.

Purge system of air as described, if air is still present.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Fill Procedure

This procedure is recommended whenever the power steering pump (3A674) 
or power rack and pinion steering gear is removed, serviced and installed into 
the power steering hydraulic system. 

 Materials Required 

A vacuum pump with gauge, capable of pulling 101 kPa (30 in-Hg) such as 
Rotunda Vacuum Source 014-R1054 or equivalent.

A No. 7 stopper cap or a special power steering pump cap assembly with 
a tee connection, shutoff valves and a power steering pump reservoir (3E764).

 Preparation 

Assemble the vacuum fill system.

Install the vacuum fill system on the vehicle. If thepower steering 
short rack (3L547) or power steering pump has been changed or flushed, allow 
old fluid to drain from the system.

Tighten all steering system and vacuum fill connections.

 Initial Fill 

Install the cap on the power steering pump fill neck or rubber stopper 
on power steering oil reservoir (3A697).

Open valve No. 1 and allow the power steering fluid to bleed through 
the tee fitting. Close valve No. 1 after bleeding.

Pour enough MERCON® Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission 
Fluid or equivalent in thepower steering pump reservoir to exceed the amount 
required for filling the system.

Close all valves.

Open valves No. 2 and No. 3. Start the vacuum pump. Operate the pump 
until a gauge reading of 84-101 kPa (25-30 in-Hg) is obtained.

Close valve No. 3, and shut off the vacuum pump. Watch the gauge for 
approximately 30 seconds. If the vacuum reading drops more than 3 kPa (1 
in-Hg), there is a leak in the power steering or filling system that must be 
corrected.

Start the vacuum pump. Open valve No. 3. Operate the pump until a gauge 
reading of 84-101 kPa (25-30 in-Hg) is obtained.

Close valve No. 2, and shut off the pump. Open valve No. 1 to fill the 
steering system with fluid. The power steering pump reservoir should be 
elevated higher than the power steering pump and power steering oil reservoir.

When fluid stops draining from power steering pump reservoir, close 
valve No. 1 and remove cap or rubber stopper.

 Final Fill 

Adjust fluid level in power steering oil reservoir to correct level. 
There will be a slight drop in the level when the engine is first started and 
the steering wheel is cycled.

Operate the engine at an idle for 15 minutes, then inspect for leaks. 
It will not be necessary to devac the system unless there is evidence of air 
in the power steering pump that could cause noise or affect performance.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Steering Pump, Power 

 Procedure No. 1 

 NOTE: The replacement power steering pump (3A674) must be primed with MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent prior 
to installation. 

Remove the fitting from the pressure port and pour power steering fluid 
into the pressure port with the port facing upward to maximize the amount of 
fluid added to the power steering pump. Turn the power steering pump 
driveshaft slowly during this procedure to allow more fluid to enter the power 
steering pump. 

Mount the power steering pump to the vehicle in a manner that does not 
allow the fluid to escape from the power steering pump. 

Connect the hoses to the power steering pump and power steering pump 
reservoir (3E764). 

Fill the power steering pump reservoir to the proper indicator level. 

Start the engine and slowly make stop-to-stop turns to purge air from 
the system. 

Stop the engine and add additional fluid to the power steering pump 
reservoir to the proper level. 

 Procedure No. 2 

When the unprimed replacement power steering pump has been mounted to 
the engine:

Connect the hoses to the power steering pump and power steering pump 
reservoir.

Fill the power steering pump reservoir to the proper indicator level. 

Raise the front of the vehicle until both front wheels are off the 
ground.

Start the engine and slowly make stop-to-stop turns to purge air from 
the system. 

Stop the engine and add additional fluid to the power steering pump 
reservoir to the proper indicator level. 

Lower front of vehicle and check power steering system for proper 
operation.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Steering Pump, Power

 Flushing 

If contamination is found in the power rack and pinion steering gear, 
flush the power steering system as follows: 

Make sure all other hoses are connected, then disconnect the power 
steering pressure hose (3A719) at the power steering short rack (3L547). 

Place the power steering pressure hose in a container. 

Fill the power steering oil reservoir (3A697) with MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent.

Disconnect the ignition coil wire. 

While adding approximately 1.9 liter (0.5 gal) of fluid, turn ignition 
switch to the START position, and crank the engine with the starter motor. As 
soon as all fluid has been added, turn the ignition switch to the OFF 
position. 

Connect the power steering pressure hose at the power rack and pinion 
steering gear. 

Check the fluid level. 

Crank the engine with the starter motor and add fluid until the level 
remains constant. 

Lower vehicle and connect the ignition coil wire. 

Start the engine and turn the steering wheel from lock-to-lock to expel 
any air trapped in the system. This will restore normal steering action. 

 Cleaning 

Clean exterior power steering pump (3A674).

 Inspection 

 NOTE: The only serviceable components on the power steering pump are the EVO 
power steering control valve actuator and the pressure hose tube nut 
(connector assembly). If the power steering pump needs service, replace power 
steering pump assembly with service assembly.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Steering Gear

 Cleaning 

Use a clean bench and tools.

Clean exterior of the power rack and pinion steering gear with solvent. 
If necessary, drain off excessive hydraulic fluid.

Handle the parts carefully to avoid nicks, burrs, scratches and dirt. 
Do not use solvent on seals.

 Inspection 

Inspect power rack and pinion steering gear for:

worn steering gear insulator (3C716).

cracks.

torn bellows.

worn or damaged front wheel spindle tie rods (3280).

 Flushing 

Always flush the power rack and pinion steering gear when replacing the 
power steering pump (3A674) due to fluid contamination. 

Remove the power steering pump and power steering pump pulley (3A733) 
and service the power steering pump as required. 

 NOTE: Connect only the power steering pressure hose (3A719). 

Install the power steering pump pulley on the serviced power steering 
pump. Install the power steering pump. Flush the power steering pressure hose 
before installing. 

Place the power steering return hose (3A713) from the power rack and 
pinion steering gear in a container and plug the power steering reservoir pump 
hose (3691). 

Fill the power steering oil reservoir (3A697) or power steering pump 
reservoir (3E764) with MERCON® Multi-Purpose (ATF) 
Transmission Fluid or equivalent.

Disconnect ignition coil and raise the front wheels off the ground.

While adding approximately 1.9 liters (0.5 gallons) of MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent, turn 
the ignition switch to the START position and crank the engine with the 
starter motor while turning the steering wheel from left to right. 

When all the fluid has been added, turn ignition switch to the OFF 
position and connect ignition coil wire. 

Remove the plug from the power steering reservoir pump hose and connect 
the power steering reservoir pump hose to the power steering oil reservoir. 

Check the fluid level. Add MERCON® Multi-Purpose 
(ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent. Do not overfill the power steering oil 
reservoir or power steering pump reservoir. 

Lower the vehicle. 

Turn the steering wheel from lock-to-lock without hitting the stops to 
expel any trapped air.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering System, Power

The power steering system uses a belt-driven power steering pump 
(3A674) to provide hydraulic pressure to the power rack and pinion steering 
gear. The power rack and pinion steering gear uses integral valving that 
directs power steering pump flow and controls pressure as required to reduce 
steering effort.

================================================================================
PAGE 2805
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering, Power � Variable Assist 

 4.6L Engine 

The electronic variable orifice (EVO) system is designed to vary the 
flow from the power steering pump (3A674) as a function of vehicle speed and 
steering wheel rate of rotation, giving a form of variable assist. 

The system provides full power steering assist at low vehicle speed for 
light parking effort. 

The system provides minimum assist at high speed for good road feel and 
directional stability. 

Full assist is returned during evasive maneuvers.
