DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Pump � CII 

 3.8L Engine 

 CAUTION: Always use the model codes on the tag when requesting a new power 
steering pump (3A674). 

 NOTE: The power steering pump is serviced as an assembly. If any service is 
required, the entire power steering pump must be replaced.

The Ford Model CII power steering pump has the following features:

It is a belt-driven 10-slipper type power steering pump with a 
fiberglass-filled nylon power steering oil reservoir (3A697). 

The power steering oil reservoir is retained to the rear side of the 
aluminum power steering pump housing (3A643) .

The pump body is encased within the power steering pump housing and 
power steering oil reservoir. 

The power steering pump design incorporates a pump pressure fitting 
that allows the power steering pressure hose (3A719) to swivel. 

A pressure-sensitive identification tag is attached to the power 
steering oil reservoir body. This tag indicates the basic model number (HBC) 
and the suffix. 

The power steering pump service identification tag identifies the power 
steering pump for service purposes.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Pump � CIII 

 4.6L Engine 

 CAUTION: Always use the model codes on the tag when requesting a new power

 NOTE: The power steering pump is serviced as an assembly. If any service is 
required, the entire power steering pump must be replaced. The only exception 
is if the EVO actuator or connector on the power steering pump is found to be 
damaged; then replace the power steering control valve actuator (3783) only. 

The CIII power steering pump is a belt-driven, vane-type pump mounted 
directly to the engine block by four retaining bolts.

The EVO power steering control valve actuator is connected to the pump 
body to provide variable power assist. 

The electrical connector and casing are able to swivel. This is normal 
and does not indicate a loose actuator assembly.

The power steering pump reservoir (3E764) for the power steering fluid 
is mounted to the LH engine coil bracket.

An identification tag attached to the power steering pump indicates the 
model number and bar code. Refer to these when service parts are required.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Gear

 NOTE: The power rack and pinion steering gear is serviced as a power steering

1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

System Components

The electronic variable orifice (EVO) system consists of: 

the EVO actuator assembly, attached to the CIII power steering pump 
(3A674). 

steering wheel rotation sensor, attached to lower steering column tube 
(3514). 

vehicle speed sensor (VSS) (9E731), located on transmission. 

data link connector (14489) , located in upper left glove compartment 
(06010) on Thunderbird LX and Cougar LS models. 

On vehicles with 4.6L engine, the module is behind the glove 
compartment mounted to the A/C evaporator housing. 

 EVO Power Steering Control Valve Actuator 

 NOTE: In the event of an electrical circuit malfunction such as circuits 
open/shorted or control module failure, the actuator will provide full power 
steering assist.

The EVO power steering control valve actuator (3783) generates a 
differential pressure, dependent on flow and current input. 

This differential pressure is used to control the spool valve in the 
power steering pump. 

On the CIII power steering pump, the power steering control valve 
actuator bolts directly to the housing. 

The power steering control valve actuator regulates the hydraulic flow 
and when combined with a current controlling device, yields a variable assist 
power steering system. 

[FIGURE: G5192C.gif]

 Steering Wheel Rotation Sensor 

An optical steering sensor (photo-cell), mounted on the steering 
column, is used to establish the rate of the steering wheel rotation. 

When the steering wheel rotation rate reaches 15 rpm, the output 
current to the power steering control valve actuator begins to reduce, 
providing additional power steering assist. 

Once the steering wheel rotation rate reaches 100 rpm, the output 
current to the power steering control valve actuator reaches zero and full 
power steering assist is provided. 

After the steering wheel rotation rate drops below 15 rpm, the output 
current returns to the amount of current regulated by the vehicle speed sensor 
input within one second. 

[FIGURE: G5191B.gif]

 Vehicle Speed Sensor 

The vehicle speed sensor, also used for shock damping control, is 
located on the transmission and is used to establish the vehicle speed. 

The output current to the power steering control valve actuator is a 
function of the vehicle speed and the steering wheel rotation rate with 
vehicle speed as the primary input to the control module.

When the vehicle speed is 8 km/h (5 mph) or less, the power steering 
control valve actuator output current is 0 mA and full power steering assist 
is provided. 

As the vehicle speed increases, the current increases. 

Conversely, as vehicle speeds decrease, the current decreases at 
approximately a linear rate. 

[FIGURE: K6267D.gif]

 Data Link Connector 

The data link connector is used for diagnostics with Rotunda Super Star 
II Tester 007-0041B. Refer to Section 11-00 .

 Control Module 

The control module contains a microprocessor which analyzes the vehicle 
speed sensor input and the steering wheel rotation sensor input continuously. 
With this information, the microprocessor controls the power steering control 
valve actuator, thereby regulating the fluid flow from the power steering pump. 

At low vehicle speeds of 8 km/h (5 mph) or less, the actuator valve is 
controlled to provide full power steering pump flow for full power steering 
assist. 

At higher vehicle speeds, the power steering is controlled to reduce 
power steering pump flow and to reduce the power steering assist. 

For evasive maneuvering at high speeds (steering wheel rotation rate 
greater than 15 rpm), the power steering control valve actuator is controlled 
to increase the power steering pump flow, thereby increasing power steering 
assist.

EVO is designed to provide full assist in the event of a component 
failure or system malfunction.

[FIGURE: G8547A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hydraulic Operation

================================================================================
PAGE 2814
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Rotary Valve 

The rotary design control valve uses relative rotational motion of the 
power steering gear input shaft and control (3D517) to the valve sleeve to 
direct fluid flow. 

When the steering wheel is turned, resistance of the wheels and the 
weight of the vehicle cause a torsion bar in the gear to twist. 

This twist changes the position of the valve spool and sleeve ports, 
directing fluid under pressure to the appropriate end of the power cylinder. 

The difference in pressure forces on the piston helps move the steering 
gear rack to assist turning effort. 

The piston is attached directly to the steering gear rack and the 
steering gear housing (3548) functions as the power cylinder. 

The fluid in the opposite end of the power cylinder is forced to the 
control valve and back to the power steering pump reservoir (3E764). 

When the driver stops applying steering effort, the valve is forced 
back to a centered position by the torsion bar. 

When this occurs, pressure is equalized on both sides of the piston and 
the front wheels tend to return to a straight-ahead position.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Tie Rod End

 Steering Gear Installed 

 Removal 

Raise vehicle on hoist.

Remove and discard the cotter pin and nut from the worn tie rod end 
(3A130). 

Disconnect tie rod end from front wheel spindle (3105) using Tie Rod 
End Remover TOOL-3290-D or equivalent. 

Holding the tie rod end with a wrench, loosen the tie rod end jam nut. 

Note the depth to which the tie rod end was located by using the jam 
nut as a marker. Grip the tie rod end with a pair of suitable pliers and 
remove the tie rod end. 

 Installation 

Clean the tie rod end threads. 

Thread the tie rod end to the same depth as the removed tie rod end. 

Place the tie rod end into the front wheel knuckle (3K185). Make sure 
front wheels are in the straight-ahead position.

Install a new nut on the tie rod end. Tighten the nut to 53-73 Nm
 (40-53 lb-ft) and continue tightening the nut to align the 
next castellation of the nut with the cotter pin hole in the stud. Install a 
new cotter pin. 

Set toe to specification. Refer to Section 04-00 . Tighten the jam nut 
to 48-68 Nm (36-50 lb-ft).

Pressure will damage the internal thrust areas. 

Hold the small hex head and rotate the tool nut counterclockwise to 
remove the power steering pump pulley (3A733). 

 CII Power Steering Pump Tools 

[FIGURE: G3353D.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not apply in and out pressure on the shaft. Pressure will damage the 
internal thrust areas. 

Place the power steering pump pulley on the power steering pump shaft 
and install Steering Pump Pulley Replacer T65P-3A733-C. The small diameter 
threads on the tool should be fully engaged in the power steering pump shaft. 

Hold the power steering pump (3A674) and rotate the tool nut clockwise 
to install the power steering pump pulley on the shaft. The power steering 
pump pulley face must be flush within 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) of the end of the 
power steering pump shaft.

Remove the tool. Install drive belt. Refer to Section 03-05 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Steering Pump, Power

 CII 3.8L Engines 

 Removal 

To remove the power steering fluid from the power steering pump 
reservoir (3E764) disconnect the power steering return hose (3A713) at the oil 
pan flange reinforcement (6A674) and drain the fluid into a container. 

Remove the power steering pressure hose (3A719) from the power steering 
oil reservoir fitting. 

Do not remove the fitting from the power steering pump (3A674).

Remove the mounting bracket. Disconnect the drive belt (8620) from the 
power steering pump pulley (3A733) and remove the power steering pump. 

For fixed-pump system on 3.8L engines, remove the drive belt from the 
power steering pump pulley. Remove the power steering pump pulley as described. 

Remove power steering pump. 

 Installation 

Prior to power steering pump installation, remove the shipping tube nut 
from the pressure fitting (if equipped). 

Place the power steering pump on the mounting bracket and install the 
bolts at the front of the power steering pump. Tighten to 40-62 Nm
 (30-45 lb-ft). 

Install the power steering pump pulley as described. 

Install drive belt. Refer to Section 03-05 . 

 CAUTION: Do not overtighten this fitting. Swivel or end play of the fitting is 
normal and does not indicate a loose fitting. Overtightening the tube nut can 
collapse the tube nut wall, resulting in a leak and requiring replacement of 
the entire power steering pressure hose. Use a tube-nut wrench to tighten tube 
nut. Use of an open-end wrench to tighten the nut can deform the tube nut hex 
which may result in improper torque and may make further servicing of the 
system difficult. 

Install the power steering pressure hose to the power steering pump 
fitting. Tighten the tube nut with a tube nut wrench rather than with an 
open-end wrench. Tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft). 

Connect the power steering return hose to the power steering pump and 
tighten the clamp. 

Fill the power steering oil reservoir (3A697) with MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent. 
Refer to Section 11-00 . 

Check for leaks and check the fluid level. Add fluid if necessary. 

 CIII � 4.6L Engine 

 Removal 

To remove the power steering fluid from the power steering pump 
reservoir, disconnect the power steering return hose at the cooler return tube 
connection and drain the fluid into a container. 

Remove the power steering pressure hose from the power steering pump 
outlet and drain the fluid into a container. 

Disconnect the drive belt from the power steering pump pulley, remove 
four retaining bolts and remove the power steering pump and power steering 
pump pulley. 

Remove power steering pump pulley from power steering pump as described. 

 Installation 

Prior to power steering pump installation, remove the shipping tube nut 
from housing (if equipped). 

Install power steering pump pulley to power steering pump as described. 

Place the power steering pump on the mounting bosses of engine block 
and install the bolts at the side of the power steering pump. Tighten to 20-30 Nm
 (15-22 lb-ft). 

Install drive belt. Refer to Section 03-05 . 

Install the power steering pressure hose to the power steering pump 
fitting. Tighten the tube nut with a tube nut wrench rather than with an 
open-end wrench. Tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft). 

Swivel or end play of the power steering pressure hose tube end is 
normal and does not indicate a loose fitting. 

Connect the power steering return hose to the cooler return tube and 
reposition the hose clamp to power steering pump inlet fitting. 

Fill the power steering pump reservoir with MERCON® 
Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent. Refer to Section 11-00 .

Check for leaks and check the fluid level. Add fluid if necessary.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Reservoir, Power Steering Pump � CII

Take the following precautions when servicing the power steering oil 
reservoir (3A697): 

Use a clean work bench and tools. 

Plug the inlet and outlet openings of the power steering pump (3A674) 
with plugs or masking tape. 

Thoroughly clean the exterior of the power steering pump with solvent. 

 Removal 

Remove oil pan flange reinforcement (6A674) and power steering pump 
pulley (3A733) as described. 

Place the power steering pump in a bench vise with soft jaws and remove 
the power steering pump valve outlet fitting (3D654), power steering pump 
valve (3A561) and power steering pump flow control valve spring (3D586). 
Discard all seals. 

 Power Steering Pump Valve 

[FIGURE: G4067C.gif]

 O-Ring Removal 

[FIGURE: G2568D.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not hammer on the power steering oil reservoir or damage to power 
steering oil reservoir will occur. 

Remove the nylonpower steering oil reservoir by twisting side-to-side 
and lifting. 

 Reservoir Removal 

[FIGURE: G2569D.gif]

 Power Steering Oil Reservoir 

[FIGURE: G4068B.gif]

Discard O-ring seal on power steering pump housing (3A643).

[FIGURE: G4069B.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not twist the O-ring seal as it will stick, grab, bind or leak. 

Install a new O-ring seal on the power steering pump housing.

Apply petroleum jelly to the reservoir O-ring seal and the inside edge 
of the power steering oil reservoir. 

Place the power steering oil reservoir over the power steering pump and 
align the outlet fitting hole in the power steering oil reservoir with the 
hole in the power steering pump housing.

 CAUTION: If the valve is cocked, it may become stuck in the power steering pump 
housing. Do not force the valve forward. Forcing the valve may shear off metal 
and carry the metal chips into the valve bore. 

Place new O-ring seals on the power steering pump valve outlet fitting. 
. Install the power steering pump flow control valve spring, power steering 
pump valve and power steering pump valve outlet fitting into the power 
steering oil reservoir and power steering pump housing. Tighten the fitting to 
34-46 Nm (26-33 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: G4070B.gif]

Install oil pan flange reinforcement and power steering pump pulley as 
described.

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Steering Gear � 3.8L Engine 

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle. For additional information, refer to
 Section 00-02 .

Remove the front wheel assemblies. For additional information,
refer to Section 04-04 . 

Remove the cotter pins and castle nuts from the outer tie-rod
ends. 

Separate the tie-rod ends from the steering knuckles, using
Tie-Rod End Remover TOOL-3290-D, or equivalent. 

Remove the engine splash shield by disconnecting the pushpin
retainers. 

Remove the left stabilizer bracket retaining bolts from the
subframe. Position the sway bar forward, to gain the necessary
clearance for removal of the steering gear fitting.

Drain the steering fluid.

Disconnect and plug the steering return hose at the hose clamp,
near the steering gear. 

Disconnect and plug the steering pressure hose at steering gear
elbow, located on the steering gear.

Remove the steering shaft retaining bolt from the bottom side
of the flex coupling and separate the shaft from the steering gear. 

Remove the rack-to-subframe bolts and nuts. Lower the steering
gear to access the pressure line elbow at the steering rack. Remove
the elbow, then remove the steering gear. 

Remove the return line fitting from the steering gear (if
equipped). Remove the O-Rings from the pressure line fitting, the
return line fitting, and the pressure line in the vehicle. 

 Installation 

[FIGURE: G5890B.gif]

Using Rotunda Seal Expanders D9OP-3517-A2 and D9OP-3517-A3,
install O-ring seals on the steering pressure line in the vehicle,
the pressure line fitting, and the return line fitting. Install the
return line fitting to the steering gear. Tighten the fitting to 37 Nm
 (27 lb-ft).

 CAUTION: Make sure the fitting is above the frame access hole prior to
installing the fitting into the steering gear. (If the fitting is
not above the access hole, the steering gear will not position up into
place). 

Position the steering gear into place. Allow the steering gear
to drop far enough to install the pressure line elbow fitting. 
Tighten the fitting to 37 Nm (27 lb-ft).

Install the steering gear retainers and tighten them to 165 Nm (122 lb-ft). 

Install the steering pressure line fitting to the elbow
fitting. Tighten the line fitting to 37 Nm (27 lb-ft). 

Connect the steering return hose to the steering gear fitting
and position the clamp in place.

Position the steering shaft to the steering gear and install
the retaining bolt. Tighten the bolt to 49 Nm (36
lb-ft). 

Position the left stabilizer bar bracket and install the two
retaining bolts to the subframe. Tighten the bolts to 62 Nm 
(46 lb-ft). 

Position the engine splash shield and install the pushpin
retainers. 

Install the outer tie-rod ends to the front steering knuckles. 
Install the castle nuts to each of the tie-rods. Tighten the nuts to
63 Nm (46 lb-ft). Continue to tighten the nuts
until they line up with the holes in the tie-rod end studs. Install
new cotter pins. 

Install the front wheel assemblies. For additional
information, refer to Section 04-04 . 

Lower the vehicle. 

Fill the system and check for leaks. For additional
information, refer to Section 11-00 .

Check the toe setting and adjust it if necessary. For
additional information, refer to Section 04-00 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Steering Gear � 4.6L Engine 

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle. For additional information, refer to
 Section 00-02 .

Remove the front wheel/tire assemblies. For additional information,
refer to Section 04-04 . 

Remove the cotter pins from the left and right outer tie-rod
ends. Remove the castle nuts from each of the tie-rods. 

Separate the tie-rod ends from the left and right front wheel knuckles, using
Tie-Rod End Remover TOOL-3290-D, or equivalent. 

Remove the engine splash shield by disconnecting six pushpin
retainers. 

Position a drain pan.

Remove the engine oil filter to gain access to the power
steering gear fittings.

Remove the power steering pressure hose bracket retaining bolt
at the subframe. Disconnect and plug the pressure hose at the
steering gear. 

Disconnect and plug the power steering return hose at the hose
clamp near the steering gear.

Drain the power steering fluid. 

Remove the drain pan. 

Remove the steering shaft retaining bolt at the bottom side of
the flex coupling and separate the shaft from the steering gear.

Remove the steering rack-to-subframe bolts and nuts. Remove the
power steering gear from the vehicle.

Remove the return line fitting and O-Ring from the steering
gear (if required). 

 Installation 

[FIGURE: G5890B.gif]

Install a new Teflon O-ring to the fitting and install the
return line to the steering gear. Tighten the fitting 37 Nm (27 lb-ft).

Position the steering gear. Install the retaining bolts and
nuts. Tighten the bolts to 165 Nm (122 lb-ft).

Install a new Teflon O-ring on the power steering pressure line
fitting. Install the line to the steering gear. Tighten the fitting to
37 Nm (27 lb-ft). 

Install the pressure hose bracket and retaining bolt. Tighten the
bolt to 10 Nm (89 lb-in). 

Connect the power steering return hose to the steering gear
fitting. Position the clamp in place.

Position the steering shaft to the steering gear and install
the retaining bolt. Tighten the bolt to 49 Nm (36
lb-ft). 

Clean the O-ring surface on the engine and the oil filter. 
Lubricate the oil filter O-ring and install the filter. 

Position the engine splash shield and install the six pushpin
retainers. 

Install the outer tie-rod ends to both front wheel knuckles and 
install the castle nuts to the tie-rod ends. Tighten the nuts to 63 Nm (46 lb-ft). Install new cotter pins. 

Install the front wheel/tire assemblies. For additional
information, refer to Section 04-04 . 

Lower the vehicle. 

Partially fill the engine with oil. 

Fill and leak check the power steering system. 

Check the toe setting and adjust it if necessary. For
additional information, refer to Section 04-00 .

Quick Connect Power Steering Fitting 

 Seal Replacement 

If a leak occurs between the tubing and tube nut, replace the power 
steering pressure hose (3A719)/power steering return hose (3A713). If a leak 
occurs between the tube nut and the pump outlet, replace the Teflon®
 seal. 

[FIGURE: G5788B.gif]

The following procedure should be used: 

Check fitting to determine whether leak is between tube and tube nut or 
between tube nut and power steering pump outlet. 

 CAUTION: DO NOT overtighten. 

If leak is between tube nut and power steering pump outlet, check that 
nut is tightened to 57-73 Nm (43-53 lb-ft). 

If leak continues or if leak is between tube and tube nut, remove power 
steering pressure hose/power steering return hose. 

Unscrew tube nut and inspect plastic seal washer. Always replace 
plastic seal washer (388898-S) when power steering pressure hose/power 
steering return hose is removed. To facilitate assembly of new plastic seal 
washer, a tapered shaft such as a Teflon® Seal Replacer Set 
D90P-3517-A or equivalent may be required to stretch washer so it may be 
slipped over tube nut threads. 

[FIGURE: G5890B.gif]

The rubber O-ring cannot be serviced with this design. If leak is due 
to the O-ring, replace the power steering pressure hose/power steering return 
hose. 

Connect tube nut and tighten to 57-73 Nm (43-53 lb-ft). 

The quick connect fitting may disengage if not fully assembled, if the 
snap ring is missing, or if the tube nut or the hose end is not machined 
properly. 

If the fitting disengages, replace the power steering pressure hose/
power steering return hose. The fitting is fully engaged only when the power 
steering pressure hose/power steering return hose will not pull out. To test 
for positive engagement, the system should be properly filled, the engine 
started and the steering wheel cycled from lock-to-lock. Service power 
steering pressure hose/power steering return hose have tube nuts, snap rings 
and O-rings already attached.

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hoses, Pressure and Return

 Hose Fittings, Pressure and Return Lines at Steering Gear and Pump 

If a leak occurs between the tubing and tube nut, replace thepower 
steering pressure hose (3A719)/power steering return hose (3A713). If a leak 
occurs between the power steering pressure hose nut and the aluminum power 
rack and pinion steering gear or power steering pump valve outlet fitting 
(3D654), replace the Teflon® seal.

 Seal Replacement 

The following procedure should be used:

Check steering gear housing fitting andpower steering pump valve outlet 
fitting to determine which fitting is leaking and whether leak is between 
power steering return hose and power steering pressure hose nut or between 
power steering pressure hose nut and steering gear housing (3548) or power 
steering pump valve outlet fitting.

 CAUTION: DO NOT overtighten. 

If leak is between power steering pressure hose nut andsteering gear 
housing or power steering pump valve outlet fitting, check to make sure nuts 
are tightened to 57-73 Nm (43-53 lb-ft) at power steering 
pump (3A674) and 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft) at power rack and 
pinion steering gear.

If a leak continues or if leak is between power steering pressure hose 
or power steering return hose and power steering pressure hose and power 
steering return hose nut, remove hose.

Unscrew power steering pressure hose or power steering return hose nut 
and inspect Teflon® seal. Always replace Teflon®
 seal (388897-S) at power steering pressure hose or power 
steering return hose, Teflon ® seal at gear, and pump outlet 
power steering return hose or power steering return hose Teflon®
 seal (388898-S) when power steering pressure hose or power 
steering return hose is removed. To facilitate assembly of new Teflon®
 seal, a tapered shaft may be required to stretch seal so 
it may be slipped overpower steering pressure hose or power steering return 
hose nut threads.

The rubber O-ring cannot be serviced with this design. If leak is due 
to O-ring, replace power steering pressure hose or power steering return hose.

Connect tube nuts and tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 
lb-ft) at power rack and pinion steering gear and 57-73 Nm 
(43-53 lb-ft) at the power steering pump. Install plastic strap to attachpower 
steering pressure hose and power steering return hose to LH turn transfer line.

The quick connect fittings may disengage in the following cases:

if not fully assembled

if snap ring is missing

if female port in power rack and pinion steering gear, tube nut or 
power steering pressure hose or power steering return hose end is not machined 
properly

If the steering gear housing fitting or power steering pump valve 
outlet fitting disengages, check for a snap ring in the tube before assembling 
the steering gear housing fitting or power steering pump valve outlet fitting. 
The steering gear housing fitting or power steering pump valve outlet fitting 
is fully engaged only when the power steering pressure hose bottoms in the 
port and will not pull out. To test for positive engagement, fill the system 
properly, start the engine and cycle the steering wheel from lock-to-lock. If 
power steering pressure hose still does not engage, replace the power steering 
pressure hose. Service power steering pressure hoses have tube nuts, snap 
rings and O-rings already attached.

 Hoses, Pressure � 3.8L Engine 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 . 

Remove steering gear mounting bolts and lower power rack and pinion 
steering gear to gain access to hoses.

Remove power steering fitting atpower steering pump.

Remove plasticpower steering hose clip (3E523) onrear sub-frame (5R003) 
to secure power steering left turn pressure hose (3A714).

Remove intermediate fitting at pressure hose connection point near 
power rack and pinion steering gear.

Remove power steering left turn pressure hose.

Remove power steering pressure hose fitting at power rack and pinion 
steering gear. 

Remove power steering pressure hose.

 Installation 

Position power steering pressure hose at power rack and pinion steering 
gear.

Install power steering pressure hose fitting at power rack and pinion 
steering gear. Tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

Position power steering left turn pressure hose in originally installed 
position.

Connect power steering pressure hose and power steering left turn 
pressure hose at intermediate connection point at power rack and pinion 
steering gear. Tighten to 14-20 Nm (11-14 lb-ft).

Secure power steering left turn pressure hose to rear sub-frame with 
power steering hose clip.

Install power steering left turn pressure hose to fitting at power 
steering pump. Tighten to 57-73 Nm (43-53 lb-ft).

Position power rack and pinion steering gear and install steering gear 
mounting bolts. Tighten to 135-195 Nm (100-143 lb-ft). 

Connect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 . 

Fill the power steering pump reservoir (3E764) with MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent. 
Refer to Section 11-00 . 

 Hoses, Pressure � 4.6L Engine 

 Removal 

Disconnect steering column intermediate shaft coupling (3A525).

Remove steering gear mounting bolts and lower power rack and pinion 
steering gear to gain access to hoses.

Remove bracket retaining screw atpower steering pump.

pressure hose at intermediate connection point at power rack and pinion 
steering gear. Tighten to 14-20 Nm (11-14 lb-ft).

lower radiator support. Tighten to 19-25 Nm (14-18 lb-ft).

Secure power steering left turn pressure hose with two retaining screws 
onrear sub-frame. Tighten to 9-12 Nm (80-106 lb-in).

Install power steering left turn pressure hose to fitting at power 
steering pump. Tighten to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

Secure power steering left turn pressure hose to power steering pump 
with bracket and retaining screw. Tighten to 9-12 Nm (80-106 
lb-in).

Position power rack and pinion steering gear and install steering gear 
mounting bolts. Tighten to 135-195 Nm (100-143 lb-ft). 

Connect steering column intermediate shaft coupling.

Fill the power steering pump reservoir with MERCON® 
Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent. Refer to Section 11-00 .

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Tie Rod and Bellows 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Bench Mounted Holding Fixture

T57L-500-B

 Disassembly 

Remove power rack and pinion steering gear as described. 

Install two long bolts and washers through the steering gear insulators 
(3C716) and attach to Bench Mounted Holding Fixture T57L-500-B. 

Loosen the jam nuts on the outer ends of the front wheel spindle tie 
rods (3280) adjacent to the tie rod ends (3A130) and remove the tie rod ends 
and jam nuts. 

Remove the four inner/outer steering gear boot clamps (3C650) retaining 
the bellows to the steering gear housing and the front wheel spindle tie rods. 
Discard the inner/outer steering gear boot clamps if damaged or excessively 
corroded. 

 CAUTION: Use care not to damage the bellows, as internal damage to front wheel 
spindle tie rod may result. 

Remove the front suspension steering ball stud dust seal (3332) along 
with the power steering gear rack tube (3K762). 

Remove power rack and pinion steering gear from the holding fixture and 
lay on the bench before proceeding. This prevents steering gear teeth damage 
from steering gear input shaft twisting when removing the front wheel spindle 
tie rods. 

Position steering gear input shaft so that several steering gear input 
shaft teeth are exposed. Hold steering gear rack with an adjustable wrench on 
the end teeth only, while loosening front wheel spindle tie rods with nut 
wrench. 

 Assembly 

Turn power rack and pinion against or near left stop and hold steering 
gear rack with adjustable wrench. Tighten each front wheel spindle tie rod 
assembly separately using nut wrench to 90-110 Nm (67-81 
lb-ft). 

Install front suspension steering ball stud dust seal and power 
steering gear rack tube. Install clamps retaining front suspension steering 
ball stud dust seal to the steering gear housing (3548) and tighten to 2.3-3.4 Nm
 (20-30 lb-in). Position front suspension steering ball 
stud dust seal , power steering gear rack tube and clamps as shown. 

[FIGURE: AG0083B.gif]

Install new steering gear boot clamps clamps retaining front suspension 
steering ball stud dust seal to tie rod ends tie rod ends.

Install the jam nuts on the front wheel spindle tie rods. 

Apply Silicone Brake Caliper Grease and Dielectric Compound 
D7AZ-19A331-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M1C171-A to tie rod 
end threads. 

Install tie rod ends on the front wheel spindle tie rod.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Steering Gear

The power rack and pinion steering gear is cleaned as follows:

Use a clean work bench and tools.

Clean the exterior of the power rack and pinion steering gear with 
solvent. If necessary, drain off excess hydraulic fluid. 

Handle the parts carefully to avoid nicks, burrs, scratches and dirt. 
Do not use solvent on seals.

================================================================================
PAGE 2835
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

System Flushing

Always flush power rack and pinion steering gear when replacing power 
steering pump (3A674) due to fluid contamination.

Disconnect power steering return hose (3A713) at power steering pump 
and place end in a container. Plug power steering return hose nipple on power 
steering oil reservoir (3A697).

Fill power steering oil reservoir with MERCON® 
Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent.

Disconnect ignition coil wire and raise front wheels off floor.

While adding approximately 1.9 liters (0.5 gal) of MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent, turn 
ignition switch to START position (using the ignition key) and crank engine 
with starter motor while turning steering wheel from lock-to-lock.

When all MERCON® Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission 
Fluid or equivalent has been added, turn ignition switch to OFF position and 
connect ignition coil wire.

Remove plug from the power steering return hose nipple. Attach power 
steering return hose to nipple. Tighten hose clamp to 1-2 Nm 
(9-17 lb-in).

 CAUTION: Do not overfillpower steering oil reservoir. 

Check fluid level. Add MERCON® Multi-Purpose (ATF) 
Transmission Fluid or equivalent if necessary.

Lower vehicle.

Start engine and turn steering wheel slowly from lock-to-lock several 
times. Check fluid level and adjust as required.

================================================================================
PAGE 2836
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Pump Flushing 

If contamination is found in the power rack and pinion steering gear, 
flush the power steering system as follows: 

Make sure all other hoses are connected, then disconnect the power 
steering pressure hose (3A719) at the power rack and pinion steering gear. 

Place the power steering pressure hose in a container. 

Fill the power steering oil reservoir (3A697) with MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent.

Disconnect the ignition coil wire. 

While adding approximately 1.9 liters (0.5 gallon) of MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent, turn 
ignition switch to the START position and crank the engine with the starter 
motor. As soon as all fluid has been added, turn the ignition switch to the 
OFF position. 

Attach the power steering pressure hose at the power rack and pinion 
steering gear. 

Check the fluid level. 

Crank the engine with the starter motor and add MERCON®
 Multi-Purpose (ATF) Transmission Fluid or equivalent until the level remains 
constant. 

Lower vehicle and connect the ignition coil wire. 

Start the engine and turn the steering wheel from lock-to-lock to expel 
any air trapped in the system. This will restore normal steering action.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Column

 NOTE: All fasteners are important because they affect the performance of 
vital parts and systems. Their failure could result in major service expenses. 
They must be replaced with fasteners of the same part number if replacement 
becomes necessary. Do not use a replacement part of lesser quality or 
substitute design. Torque values must be used as specified during assembly to 
maintain proper functioning of these parts. 

The steering column is:

of modular construction. 

features easy-to-service electrical switches.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fixed and Tilt Columns

The Thunderbird/Cougar is not equipped with a fixed steering column.

Tilt steering columns are equipped with a tilt mechanism that allows 
the steering wheel angle to be adjusted.

A tilt lever is located on the LH side of the steering column 
underneath the multi-function switch (13K359). 

When the tilt lever is pulled toward the driver, thesteering wheel 
(3600) can be adjusted to one of five angles.

When the tilt lever is released, the steering column is locked into 
position.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Steering Wheel with Air Bag

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Steering Wheel Puller

T67L-3600-A

 Removal 

Center front wheels to the straight-ahead position.

 WARNING: THE BACKUP POWER SUPPLY MUST BE DISCONNECTED BEFORE ANY AIR BAG 
COMPONENT IS SERVICED. FAILURE TO DO SO MAY RESULT IN PERSONAL INJURY. 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove two steering wheel spoke covers (3L518). Remove two air bag 
module retaining screws. 

Disconnect air bag wire harness from driver side air bag module 
(043B13), and remove driver side air bag module from steering wheel (3600). 

[FIGURE: G7687B.gif]

Disconnect speed control wire harness from steering wheel. 

Remove steering wheel retaining bolt. 

Install Steering Wheel Puller T67L-3600-A and remove steering wheel. 
Route air bag sliding contact assembly wire harness through steering wheel as 
steering wheel is lifted off steering column shaft assembly. 

[FIGURE: G7688A.gif]

 Installation 

Make sure the front wheels are in the straight-ahead position. 

 CAUTION: Be sure wiring does not get trapped between steering wheel and air bag 
sliding contact (14A664) or damage to air bag sliding contact wiring may 
occur. 

Route air bag sliding contact wire harness through steering wheel 
opening at the three o'clock position and position steering wheel on steering 
column shaft assembly. The steering wheel and steering column shaft assembly 
alignment marks should be aligned. Make sure air bag sliding contact wire is 
not pinched. 

Install new steering wheel retaining bolt and tighten to 31-48 Nm
 (23-35 lb-ft). 

Connect speed control wire harness to steering wheel and snap connector 
assembly into steering wheel clip. 

Connect air bag wire harness to driver side air bag module and install 
module to steering wheel. Tighten air bag module retaining screws to 10-14 Nm
 (89-123 lb-in). 

Connect positive battery cable and battery ground cable. Refer to 
 Section 14-01 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Sliding Contact, Air Bag 

 Removal 

Make sure front wheels are in the straight-ahead position and steering 
column shaft alignment mark is at the 12 o'clock position. 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 . 

Remove steering wheel (3600) as described.

Remove instrument panel steering column cover (04459) and lower 
steering column shroud (3530). 

Disconnect air bag sliding contact wire harness. 

Apply two strips of tape across air bag sliding contact assembly stator 
and rotor to prevent accidental rotation. 

Remove ignition switch lock cylinder (11582) and remove key warning 
buzzer wire. 

Detach main wiring mating connectors down steering column assembly side. 

Remove three air bag sliding contact retaining screws and pull air bag 
sliding contact (14A664) off steering column shaft assembly. 

[FIGURE: G5789B.gif]

 Installation 

Make sure front wheels are in the straight-ahead position and steering 
column shaft assembly alignment mark is at the 12 o'clock position. 

 NOTE: If a new air bag sliding contact is being installed, remove the plastic 
lock mechanism after air bag sliding contact is secured to steering column 
shaft assembly.

Align air bag sliding contact assembly to steering column shaft 
assembly and mounting bosses and slide air bag sliding contact onto the 
steering column shaft assembly. 

Install three retaining screws. Tighten screws to 2-3 Nm
 (18-26 lb-in). Remove tape strips. 

Route air bag sliding contact assembly wires down column assembly and 
connect to wire harness. 

Install ignition key warning switch terminal and wire (11A128) into 
steering column lock cylinder housing (3511). 

Install main wiring connectors down steering column assembly. 

Install lower steering column shroud and instrument panel steering 
column cover. 

Install ignition switch lock cylinder. 

Install steering wheel as described.

Connect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Verify air bag warning indicator.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Ignition Switch Lock Cylinder

 Lock Cylinder Functional 

 Removal 

The following procedure applies to vehicles that have functional 
ignition switch lock cylinders (11582). Lock cylinder keys are available for 
these vehicles, or the lock cylinder key numbers are known and the proper key 
can be made. 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Turn ignition switch lock cylinder to RUN position. 

Place a 3.17 mm (0.125-inch) diameter wire pin or small drift punch in 
hole in steering column shroud (3530) under ignition switch lock cylinder. 
Depress retaining pin while pulling out on ignition switch lock cylinder to 
remove it from steering column lock cylinder housing (3511). 

 Installation 

Install ignition switch lock cylinder by turning it to RUN position and 
depressing retaining pin. Insert ignition switch lock cylinder into steering 
column lock cylinder housing. Make sure ignition switch lock cylinder is fully 
seated and aligned in interlocking washer before turning key to OFF position. 
This will permit cylinder retaining pin to extend into steering column lock 
cylinder housing hole. 

Rotate ignition switch lock cylinder, using lock cylinder key, to make 
sure switch works in all positions. 

Connect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

[FIGURE: J3104B.gif]

 Lock Cylinder Non-Functional 

The following procedure applies to vehicles in which the ignition 
switch lock cylinder is inoperative and the ignition switch lock cylinder 
cannot be rotated due to a lost or broken lock cylinder key, unknown key 
number, or an ignition switch cap that has been damaged or broken to the 
extent the key cannot be rotated. 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove steering wheel (3600). 

Working through the access hole in the lower steering column shroud, 
use a small pilot punch to center punch the retaining pin and then drill out 
with a 1/8 inch diameter drill. 

Using channel lock pliers or vise grip pliers, twist ignition switch 
cap or bezel until it separates from ignition switch lock cylinder. 

Using a 3/8-inch diameter drill, drill down middle of key slot 
approximately 44 mm (1.75 inch) until ignition switch lock cylinder breaks 
loose from breakaway base of ignition switch lock cylinder. Remove lock 
cylinder and drill shavings from steering column lock cylinder housing. 

Remove bearing retainer (3C610), steering column lock housing bearing 
(3E700), ignition switch lock cylinder and steering column lock gear (3E717). 
Thoroughly clean all drill shavings and other foreign materials from casting. 

Carefully inspect steering column lock cylinder housing for damage from 
the above operation. If damage is apparent, steering column lock cylinder 
housing must be replaced. 

 Installation 

Replace steering column lock cylinder housing, if damaged. 

Install steering column lock housing bearing and bearing retainer as 
described.

Install trim and electrical parts. 

Install new ignition switch lock cylinder as described.

Install steering wheel as described.

Connect battery ground cable. 

Check ignition switch lock cylinder operation.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Steering Column

Check for side play of the steering column shaft assembly in the 
steering column bearing (3517) at the steering wheel end of the column. Any 
detectable side play can adversely affect steering control. If in excess of 
0.75 mm (0.03 inch), serious bearing wear is indicated, and the steering 
column assembly should be replaced.

ADJUSTMENTS

Transmission Range Indicator

 Functional Test 

To determine if transmission shift cable is properly set:

Stop the engine and apply the parking brake.

Place transmission gearshift lever to the D (overdrive) position.

Push button on handle and holding the gearshift lever (7210) in this 
position, move it slightly fore and aft. A slight resistance will be felt as 
the gearshift lever is moved up and down.

Position the gearshift lever at the position where the least amount of 
resistance is felt. This is the center of the transmission detent.

Let go of button. It should seat directly in the lever detent. If it 
does not, the shift cable requires adjustment. Refer to Section 07-05 .

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Multi-Function Switch

The multi-function switch (13K359), mounted to the lock cylinder 
housing, unifies the following functions: 

windshield washer/wiper

headlamp flash-to-pass and high beam

turn signal

The multi-function switch, located on the LH side of the upper steering 
column, operates in the following manner: 

Ignition switch must be in the RUN position to operate turn signals for 
a full turn. 

Move the turn signal lever to the end-of-travel position for the turn 
desired. 

The turn indicator cancel cam (13318) will cancel the turn signal when 
the turn is completed.

The lane change feature operates as follows: 

Move and hold the turn signal lever to the first stop position when 
changing lanes. 

Release the lever and it will return to its normal position when the 
lane change maneuver is completed.

The headlamp dimmer switch and the flash-to-pass feature operate in the 
following manner: 

Select high beam by pushing the lever away from the driver to the STOP 
position. 

To change the headlamp beam back, pull lever toward driver until the 
switch is in the central position. 

To operate the flash-to-pass feature, pull the lever gently toward the 
driver. When the lever is released, it will return to the LO beam position. 

If driving without headlamps on, use of the flash-to-pass feature will 
turn on the high beams until the turn signal lever is released. 

If the headlamps are turned on, the low and high beams will be on until 
the turn signal lever is released. 

 NOTE: Excessive force used to hold the turn signal lever in the flash-to-pass 
function followed by quick release may result in incorrect selection of high 
beam. The driver must be cautioned to avoid this condition. 

The wiper switch, located in the knob at the end of the multi-function 
switch, operates in the following manner: 

Ignition switch must be in the RUN position. 

The wiper settings include:

LO (fixed low speed)

HI (fixed high speed)

INT (interval)

OFF

The positions are selected by rotating the knob actuator. 

When interval position is selected, the time between wiper cycles will 
decrease as the knob is rotated away from OFF position and will increase as 
the knob is rotated toward OFF position. 

The time interval between wipes will vary depending on the knob's 
position from OFF position.

The washer switch, located at the end of the multi-function switch, 
operates in the following manner: 

Ignition switch must be in the RUN position. 

To actuate the washer housing, push the end of the turn signal lever 
toward the steering column.

Release the switch to turn off the washer. 

The windshield wiper blades (17528) will continue to operate for a few 
wipes and then automatically return to the previous wiper speed setting (OFF, 
LO, HI, INT). 

Washer operation is available in all positions of wiper operation 
(including OFF).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Turn Signal Switch

The turn signal switch is incorporated into the multi-function switch 
(13K359).

The turn signal system consists of:

the electronic indicator flasher (13350).

the multi-function switch.

the turn signal miniature bulb (13465).

circuit wiring and circuit protection.

Power is supplied to the electronic indicator flasher through fuse 
panel junction. This fuse is hot in RUN. The electronic lamp (13550) is 
connected to the turn signal switch of the multi-function switch. Ground is 
provided to the electronic lamp and the turn signal miniature bulb through 
Circuit 57 (BK).

With the multi-function switch in the RH position, power is supplied to 
the RH front turn signal miniature bulb and the RH turn indicator in the 
instrument cluster (10849) and to the RH rear turn signal miniature bulb.

With the multi-function switch in the LH position, power is supplied to 
the LH front turn signal miniature bulb and the LH turn indicator in the 
instrument cluster and to the LH rear turn signal miniature bulb.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ignition Switch 

The ignition switch (11572) has the following features: 

It is mounted on the steering actuator housing (3F723). 

It is controlled by the ignition switch lock cylinder (11582) through a 
pin that is part of the ignition switch. 

The ignition switch lock cylinder also controls the mechanism that 
provides a positive lock for the transmission and the steering system. 

The locking mechanism is located in the ignition switch lock cylinder 
housing (22074) at the upper end of the steering column. 

The ignition switch lock cylinder positions are the following:

ACC

LOCK 

OFF

RUN

START

The position of the ignition switch determines transmission and 
steering system operation as follows:

The lock cylinder key can be removed from the ignition switch lock 
cylinder only when the transmission range selector lever is in PARK position 
and the key is in LOCK position. 

The ACC position operates while the steering and transmission remain 
locked. 

Turning the key to OFF position shuts off the engine without locking 
the steering or transmission systems.

 Blade Type 

The ignition switch has blade-type terminals that engage with one 
multiple connector. The multiple connector is secured to the ignition switch 
by integral locking fingers. 

A push-button steering wheel lock mechanism is used on models equipped 
with the floor-mounted shift system. This button, on the LH side of the 
steering column tube (3514), must be pushed in before the ignition key can be 
removed.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hazard Flasher Switch 

 NOTE: The turn signal system is deactivated when the hazard flasher system is 
on and turn signal lever motion does not affect the hazard flasher system. 

The hazard flasher system operates in the following manner:

The hazard flasher system operates with the ignition switch (11572) in 
any position including OFF and LOCK. 

All turn signal lamps can be made to flash simultaneously by pressing 
and releasing the hazard actuation knob located on the top part of the 
steering column. 

The hazard flasher switch is identified by a "double triangle" symbol. 

The actuator will move out or away from the steering column to the ON 
position. 

To turn the hazard flasher system off, push then release the knob. The 
actuator should remain in or toward the steering column in the OFF position.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake Shift Interlock Switch

A brake/shift interlock mechanism is used to prevent shifting the 
transmission out of the PARK position unless the brake pedal is applied. The 
system consists of the following components: 

an actuator assembly attached to the key interlock assembly 

necessary wiring 

The system operates as follows: 

The actuator is energized when the ignition switch is turned to the RUN 
position. 

This locks the shifter in the PARK position. 

When the brake pedal (2455) is applied and the stoplight switch (13480) 
is activated, the brake shift lock actuator is deactivated and the gearshift 
lever (7210) can be moved out of the PARK position. 

The ignition/shifter interlock cable (3F719) locks the transmission 
range selector lever in the PARK position when the ignition switch is in the 
LOCK position. 

It also requires the gearshift lever to be in the PARK position to turn 
the ignition switch to the LOCK position. 

Refer to Section 07-05 for Diagnosis and Testing.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Multi-Function Switch

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Tilt column to lowest position and remove key release lever (3F527). 

Remove ignition switch lock cylinder (11582).

Remove shroud screws and remove upper steering column shroud (3530) and 
lower steering column shroud. 

Remove two self-tapping screws retaining multi-function switch (13K359) 
to steering column casting. Disengage multi-function switch from casting. 

Disconnect the two electrical connectors. 

 Installation 

Install two electrical connectors to full engagement. 

Align mounting holes in multi-function switch with corresponding holes 
in steering column casting. Install two self-tapping screws, making sure to 
start screws in the previously tapped holes. Tighten to 2-3 Nm
 (18-26 lb-in). 

Install upper steering column shroud and lower steering column shroud. 

Install ignition switch lock cylinder. 

Install key release lever. 

Connect battery ground cable. Refer to Section 14-01 .

Check steering column and multi-function switch for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Ignition Switch

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable (14301). Refer to Section 14-01 .

Remove the upper steering column shroud (3530)by removing the 
self-tapping screws. 

Remove four bolts retaining lower steering column shroud and remove 
lower steering column shroud.

Remove lock screw and disconnect the ignition switch electrical 
connector. 

Rotate the ignition switch lock cylinder (11582) to the RUN position. 

Remove the two screws retaining ignition switch (11572). 

Disengage the ignition switch from the actuator. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: A new replacement ignition switch assembly will be set in the RUN 
position as received. 

Adjust the ignition switch by sliding the carrier to the ignition 
switch RUN position. 

Check to make sure that the ignition switch lock cylinder is in the RUN 
position. The RUN position is achieved by rotating the ignition switch lock 
cylinder approximately 90 degrees from the LOCK position.

BASIC PRINCIPLES

Air Conditioning

Vehicle air conditioning is the cooling or refrigeration of the air in 
the passenger compartment. Refrigeration is accomplished by making practical 
use of three laws of nature. These laws of nature and their practical 
application are as follows:

heat transfer

latent heat of vaporization

effect of pressure on boiling or condensation

================================================================================
PAGE 2878
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 12-00: Climate Control System � Service

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

BASIC PRINCIPLES

Heat Transfer 

The principles of heat transfer are:

that heat always flows from hot to cold. 

that the rate of heat transfer will increase as the difference in 
temperature between two objects increases. 

that the mass of an object remains the same regardless of its heat 
content. 

For example, heat flows from a pan of hot water to the cooler air 
around it. 

[FIGURE: M4725A.gif]

Cold objects have less heat than hot objects of the same mass. To make 
an object colder, remove heat; to make it hotter, add heat. 

[FIGURE: M4726A.gif]

In order to determine the amount of heat that transfers from one 
substance to another, a definite standard of measurement called the British 
Thermal Unit (BTU) is used. One BTU is the amount of heat required to raise 
the temperature of 0.45 kg (1.0 lb) of water 0.55°C (1.0°
F). For example, 180 BTUs of heat must be: 

added to 0.45 kg (1.0 lb) of water to increase its temperature from 0°
C (32°F) to 100°C (212°
F). 

removed from 0.45 kg (1.0 lb) of water to decrease its temperature from 
100°C (212°F) to 0°C (32°
F).

================================================================================
PAGE 2879
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 12-00: Climate Control System � Service

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

BASIC PRINCIPLES

Latent Heat of Vaporization 

Everything is composed of matter, and matter exists in one of these 
states:

solid

liquid

vapor

When a liquid boils (changes to a vapor), it absorbs heat without 
raising the temperature of the resulting vapor. When the vapor condenses 
(changes back to a liquid), it gives off heat without lowering the temperature 
of the resulting liquid.

[FIGURE: M4727A.gif]

For example, 0.45 kg (1.0 lb) of water, still liquid but at a 
temperature of 100°C (212°F): 

will absorb 970 BTUs of heat in changing to a vapor. 

will remain at 100°C (212°F) even 
after changing to a vapor. 

absorbs more than five times the amount of heat when changing to a 
vapor than it can as just a liquid.

[FIGURE: M4728A.gif]

Conversely, the vapor will give off 970 BTUs in condensing back to 
water. 

[FIGURE: M4729A.gif]

This absorption of heat with no change in temperature is known as the 
latent heat of vaporization and is the basic principle of all refrigeration 
systems. 

For a liquid to be a good refrigerant, it must:

absorb heat when vaporizing. 

have a boiling point lower than the substance to be cooled. 

Refrigerant R-134a is the liquid most commonly used in automotive air 
conditioning systems because it boils at -26°C (-15°
F) in an open container. This is well below passenger 
compartment temperatures and, in vaporizing, will absorb tremendous amounts of 
heat without getting any warmer itself.

================================================================================
PAGE 2880
================================================================================
1997 Thunderbird/Cougar

Section 12-00: Climate Control System � Service

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

BASIC PRINCIPLES

Effect of Pressure on Boiling or Condensation 

Changing the pressure on a liquid or vapor changes the boiling point. 
Increasing pressure increases the boiling point, while decreasing pressure 
decreases the boiling point.

[FIGURE: M4730A.gif]

Another effect of compression is an increase in temperature even though 
heat has not been added. For example, if refrigerant R-134a vapor is 
compressed from 206 kPa (30 psi) to 1206 kPa (175 psi) the vapor temperature 
will increase from 0°C (32°F) to 54°
C (130°F) and the boiling/condensation 
point will also increase. 

[FIGURE: M4731A.gif]

It is important to understand that the effect of higher pressure:

does not involve any increase in the heat contained in the vapor. 

causes the refrigerant to condense into a liquid at this new higher 
temperature when heat is removed.

As the heat leaves the refrigerant, it condenses back to a liquid 
without changing temperature. This is latent heat of vaporization in reverse: 

The heat that the refrigerant absorbed in changing from a liquid to a 
vapor is being removed.

The refrigerant is changing back to a liquid. 

Because this change is happening at a higher pressure, the temperature 
is also higher. However, the basic principle is the same � the 
temperature of the refrigerant will not decrease until all of the 
vapor has condensed into liquid. 

It may seem difficult to understand how heat can be transferred from a 
comparatively cooler vehicle passenger compartment to the hot outside air. The 
answer lies in the difference between the refrigerant pressure that exists in 
the A/C evaporator core (19860) and the pressure that exists in the A/C 
condenser core (19712):

In the A/C evaporator core, the compressor suction reduces the pressure 
and the boiling point below the temperature of the passenger compartment. 
Thus, heat transfers from the passenger compartment to the boiling 
refrigerant. 

In the A/C condenser core, the A/C compressor (19703) raises the 
condensation point above the temperature of the outside air. Thus, the heat 
transfers from the condensing refrigerant to the outside air. 

The A/C evaporator core orifice (19D990) and the A/C compressor simply 
create pressure conditions that permit the laws of nature to function.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Safety Precautions 

The refrigerant used in this refrigerant system is HFC-134a, which is a 
hydrofluorocarbon refrigerant. 

HFC-134a, also known as R-134a, is non-corrosive and non-flammable. 

HFC-134a is heavier than air. 

Although it is classified as a safe refrigerant, certain precautions 
must be observed to protect the system component and the technician.

Use only HFC-134a refrigerant. Due to environmental concerns, when the 
air conditioning system is drained, the refrigerant should be collected using 
refrigerant recovery/recycling equipment meeting Society of Automotive 
Engineers (SAE) requirements J1990 and J2210. 

HFC-134a must never be removed without the appropriate equipment or 
released into the atmosphere. 

Use of a recovery machine dedicated for HFC-134a is necessary to reduce 
the possibility of oil and refrigerant contamination concerns. 

Refer to the instructions provided by the equipment manufacturer when 
recovering refrigerant or charging the air conditioning system. 

Avoid breathing A/C refrigerant and lubricant vapor or mist. 

If accidental system discharge occurs, ventilate the work area before 
resuming service.

Liquid HFC-134a, at normal atmospheric pressures and temperatures, 
evaporates so quickly it has the tendency to freeze anything it contacts; 
therefore: 

Extreme care must be taken to prevent any liquid refrigerant from 
coming in contact with the skin, especially the eyes.

Wear proper safety gloves and safety goggles at all times when handling 
liquid refrigerant. 

If any liquid refrigerant gets into the eyes or on the skin, 
immediately flush affected area with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes, 
remove contaminated clothing and shoes, and call a physician. 

Refrigerant HFC-134a is always under pressure. Because the system is 
tightly sealed, heat applied to any part could cause pressure to build up 
excessively. 

To avoid an explosion, keep away from open flames, glowing metal 
surfaces, blow torch, steam cleaning and welding. 

HFC-134a will decompose at high temperatures.

Make sure that containers are never heated to over 52°
C (125°F). Containers should be stored and installed in 
accordance with all state and local ordinances.

When charging HFC-134a into the refrigerant system, always charge from 
the gas phase. If the liquid phase is used for charging, liquid HFC-134a will 
enter the system and damage the A/C compressor (19703).

Refrigerant HFC-134a should not be mixed with air for leak testing or 
for any other purpose above atmospheric pressure. HFC-134a is combustible when 
mixed with high concentrations of air and higher pressures.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Service Precautions 

Never open or loosen a connection before evacuating the refrigerant 
from the system with a recycling machine such as the Rotunda Mobile Recycling 
Center 023-00150 or equivalent. 

When loosening a connection after recovery, allow it to leak off before 
opening the fitting if any residual pressure is evident.

A system which has been opened to replace a component or one which has 
discharged through leakage must be evacuated before charging.

Immediately after disconnecting a component from the system, seal the 
open fittings with a cap or plug.

Before disconnecting a component from the system, thoroughly clean the 
outside of the fittings.

Do not remove sealing caps from a replacement component until ready to 
install.

Refrigerant oil will absorb moisture from the atmosphere if left 
uncapped. Do not open an oil container until ready to use and install cap 
immediately after using. Store oil only in a clean, moisture-free container.

Before connecting an open fitting, always install a new O-ring seal. 
Coat fitting and O-ring seal with specified refrigerant oil before connecting.

When installing a refrigerant line, avoid sharp bends. Position line 
away from exhaust or any sharp edges which may damage the line.

Tighten fittings only to specified torque. Do not overtighten.

When disconnecting a threaded fitting, use a wrench on both halves of 
the fitting to prevent twisting of refrigerant lines or tubes.

Do not open a refrigerant system or uncap a replacement component 
unless it is as close as possible to room temperature. This will prevent 
condensation from forming inside a component which is cooler than surrounding 
air.

Keep service tools and work area clean. Avoid contamination of a 
refrigerant system through careless work habits.

Whenever components in the engine compartment or instrument panel areas 
are being serviced, the battery ground cable (14301) must be disconnected to 
eliminate the possibility of electrical shorts, burned wiring and fires. 
Extreme care must be exercised when performing any electrical test where the 
battery (10655) must be connected to operate the system. Refer to Section 14-01 .

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Refrigerant System Operation

 Refrigerant Flow 

During stabilized (A/C system shutdown) conditions, refrigerant system 
pressures are equalized on both the high and low sides of the refrigerant 
system.

When an A/C, mix or defrost function is selected and the vehicle 
requires cooling, the system operates as follows: 

The A/C clutch field coil (2987) is energized and the A/C clutch (2884) 
is pulled into contact with the belt-driven A/C clutch pulley (2E884). 

The A/C clutch then rotates the compressor shaft. 

When the A/C compressor shaft is rotated, the refrigerant vapors from 
the suction side of the refrigerant system are compressed into a decreasingly 
smaller area, increasing the refrigerant vapor pressure and also raising the 
refrigerant vapor temperature. 

The high-pressure and high-temperature A/C compressor discharge 
refrigerant vapor is released into the A/C condenser core assembly through the 
A/C manifold and tube (19D734). 

In the A/C condenser core (19712), high pressure refrigerant vapor 
condenses into a high pressure liquid when heat is removed from the 
refrigerant vapor by outside air passing over A/C condenser core fins and 
tubing. 

High pressure liquid refrigerant from the bottom of the A/C condenser 
core enters inlet side of the A/C evaporator core orifice (19D990). 

Refrigerant pressure is reduced in the A/C evaporator core (19860) as a 
result of the flow restriction produced by the A/C evaporator core orifice and 
the A/C compressor suction. 

As passenger compartment or outside airflow passes over the plate/fin 
sections of the A/C evaporator core, the refrigerant inside absorbs the heat 
and changes into a vapor. 

A/C compressor suction draws the vaporized refrigerant and oil mixture 
into the suction accumulator/drier (19C836) where the heavier oil-laden vapors 
fall to the bottom and the lighter vapors and oil mixture continue their path 
to the A/C compressor (19703) through the A/C manifold and tube.

 Refrigerant Systems 

Thunderbird and Cougar vehicles offer the R-134a A/C system.

The R-134a system uses a non-chlorofluorocarbon (non-CFC) based 
refrigerant R-134a. 

R-134a is a hydrofluorocarbon (HFC)-based refrigerant.

The A/C refrigerant system is a clutch cycling orifice tube type. The 
system components are as follows:

A/C compressor

A/C clutch 

A/C condenser core

A/C evaporator core

suction accumulator/drier

necessary connecting refrigerant lines

System operation is controlled by the following:

A/C evaporator core orifice

A/C cycling switch (19E561)

A/C compressor pressure relief valve (19D644)

A/C pressure cut-off switch (19D594)

The refrigerant system incorporates an A/C compressor controlled by an 
A/C cycling switch. 

The A/C cycling switch:

senses A/C evaporator core pressure to control A/C compressor operation.

uses this method of compressor control to stop compressor operation 
during ambient temperatures below approximately 10°C (50°
F) and to prevent A/C evaporator core from icing during 
normal system operation.

An A/C compressor pressure relief valve is installed in the A/C 
manifold and tube to protect the refrigerant system against excessive 
refrigerant pressures.

Operation of the A/C clutch is dependent on signals from the powertrain 
control module (PCM) (12A650). The system is programmed to interrupt 
compressor operation when certain conditions exist. The A/C clutch can be shut 
off (or kept off) for several seconds:

at engine start-up.

at high engine speeds.

during acceleration.

when the engine coolant temperature exceeds a predetermined temperature.

during low engine idle conditions (approximately 200 rpm below idle 
specifications).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Compressor and A/C Clutch Assemblies 

The FS-10 A/C compressor (19703) has the following characteristics:

The FS-10 is a swashplate design, 10-cylinder aluminum A/C compressor 
using the tangential design mount with a displacement of 170 cc (10.4 cubic 
inches).

Lubricated by a charge of Motorcraft YN-12b refrigerant oil or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSH-M1C231-B in the refrigerant system.

A one-piece lip-type seal (replaceable from the front of the A/C 
compressor) is used to seal it at the shaft opening in the assembly. 

Five double-acting pistons, positioned axially around the compressor 
shaft, operate within the cylinder assembly. The pistons are started by a 
swashplate that is pressed on the compressor shaft. 

The swashplate changes the rotating action of the shaft to provide a 
reciprocating force to each of the five pistons. This driving force is 
applied, through shoes, to the midpoint of each of the double-end pistons. 

Reed-type discharge valves are assembled on the valve plate.

The valve plate is located with the suction reed valve between the 
cylinder assembly and the head at each end of the A/C compressor. 

The heads are connected to each other by gas-tight passageways through 
the cylinder assembly which directs the refrigerant gas to the suction and 
discharge ports located in the rear head. 

The magnetic A/C clutch (2884) has the following characteristics:

It drives the compressor shaft.

When battery positive voltage (B+) is applied to the A/C clutch field 
coil (2987), the clutch disc and hub assembly (which is solidly coupled to the 
compressor shaft) is drawn rearward by magnetic force toward the A/C clutch 
pulley (2E884) (which rotates freely on the compressor front head casting). 

The magnetic force locks the clutch disc and hub assembly and the A/C 
clutch pulley together as one unit. 

The clutch disc and hub assembly then turns the A/C clutch pulley 
causing the compressor shaft to rotate. 

When voltage is removed from the A/C clutch field coil, springs in the 
clutch disc and hub assembly move the clutch disc and hub assembly away from 
the A/C clutch pulley.

The clutch disc and hub assembly and compressor shaft stop rotating.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Refrigerant System Protection

 A/C Compressor Pressure Relief Valve 

An A/C compressor pressure relief valve (19D644) has been incorporated 
in the compressor's A/C manifold and tube (19D734) to:

relieve unusually high refrigerant system discharge pressure buildups, 
3103 kPa (450 psi) and above.

prevent damage to the A/C compressor (19703) and other system 
components. 

avoid total refrigerant loss by closing after the excessive pressure 
has been relieved.

 A/C Pressure Cut-Off Switch 

An A/C pressure cut-off switch (19D594) is used on all vehicles to 
interrupt operation of the A/C compressor in the event of high system 
discharge pressures.

The A/C pressure cut-off switch is located in the discharge line 
between the A/C compressor and theA/C condenser core (19712). 

 Dual Function 

The A/C pressure cut-off switch has two sets of contacts. One 
electrical contact is normally closed.

When compressor head pressure rises to 2860-3068 kPa (415-445 psi), the 
contacts open and the compressor operation is shut off.

When head pressure drops to 1517-1930 kPa (220-280 psi), the contacts 
again close and allow operation of the A/C compressor.

Shutting down compressor operation prior to the pressure relief valve 
set point 3103 kPa (450 psi) makes sure refrigerant is contained in the A/C 
system.

The switch contains a second set of electrical contacts used for 
high-speed fan control which are normally open.

When discharge line pressure reaches 1965-2172 kPa (285-315 psi), these 
contacts close and engage the high-speed fan control. 

When pressure drops to approximately 1896 kPa (275 psi), the contacts 
again open and the high-speed fan control is disengaged.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Refrigerant Line Connectors

 Spring Lock Coupling 

The spring lock coupling is a refrigerant line coupling held together 
by a garter spring inside a circular cage. 

When the coupling is connected together, the flared end of the female 
fitting slips behind the garter spring inside the cage of the male fitting. 

The garter spring and cage then prevent the flared end of the female 
fitting from pulling out of the cage. 

Two O-ring seals are used to seal between the two halves of the 
coupling. 

These O-ring seals are green in color and are made of special material. 

Use only the green O-ring seals listed in the Ford Master Parts Catalog 
for the spring lock coupling.

A plastic indicator ring is used on the evaporator core spring lock 
couplings to indicate, during vehicle assembly, that the coupling is 
connected. Once the coupling is connected, the indicator ring is no longer 
necessary but remains captive by the coupling near the cage opening. 

The indicator ring may also be used during service operations to 
indicate connection of the coupling.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Evaporator Core Orifice

 NOTE: The A/C evaporator core orifice (19D990) should be replaced whenever an 
A/C compressor (19703) is replaced.

The A/C evaporator core orifice has the following characteristics:

is color coded orange

has a diameter of 1.46 mm (0.058 inch)

is located in the condenser to evaporator tube (19835).

has filter screens located on the inlet and outlet ends of the tube body

The A/C evaporator core orifice assembly is the restriction in the 
refrigerant circuit that creates the pressure drop necessary for cooling by 
metering the flow of liquid refrigerant into the A/C evaporator core (19860), 
reducing the pressure. 

Operation is as follows:

The temperature of the A/C evaporator core is controlled by sensing the 
pressure within the A/C evaporator core with the A/C cycling switch (19E561). 

The A/C cycling switch controls compressor operation as necessary to 
maintain the pressure in the A/C evaporator core within specified limits. 

The inlet filter screen acts as a strainer for the liquid refrigerant 
flowing through the A/C evaporator core orifice. 

O-ring seals on the A/C evaporator core orifice prevent the 
high-pressure liquid refrigerant from bypassing the A/C evaporator core 
orifice. 

Adjustment or service cannot be made to the A/C evaporator core orifice 
assembly. It must be replaced as a unit. 

The condenser to evaporator tube must be replaced, or an Orifice Tube 
Replacement Kit E5VY-19D695-A or equivalent installed, if replacement of the 
A/C evaporator core orifice is necessary.
