DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps, Backup

The back-up lamp system consists of:

the back-up lamp bulb in the rear panel reflector (13A565).

the transmission range (TR) sensor. 

circuit wiring and circuit protection.

Power is supplied to the transmission range (TR) sensor through fuse

the transmission range (TR) sensor closes and power is provided to the 
backup lamp bulbs.

ground is provided to the backup lamp bulbs through Circuit 57 (BK).

Turn Signal and Hazard Lamps

The turn signal system consists of:

turn signal miniature bulb (13465).

circuit wiring and circuit protection.

The electronic indicator flasher is:

supplied by Circuit 385 (W/R).

connected to the turn signal switch portion of the multi-function

provided ground on Circuit 57 (BK).

with the multi-function switch in the right turn position, power is

in the instrument cluster and the RH rear turn signal miniature bulb.

with the multi-function switch in the left turn position, power is 
supplied to the LH front turn signal miniature bulb, the left turn indicator 
in the instrument cluster and the LH rear turn signal miniature bulb.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hazard Flasher Switch

The hazard flasher switch: 

is part of the multi-function switch (13K359).

is located on top of the steering column forward of the steering wheel 
(3600).

cycles smoothly from OFF to ON by pressing and releasing the switch top.

produces an audible click when switching.

extends further above the steering column in the ON position than it 
does in OFF.

when switched on, simultaneously flashes.

both front turn signal lamps.

both rear turn signal lamps.

both turn signal indicator lamps.

Headlamp Switch

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Stoplight Switch

 Removal 

 NOTE: Locking tab on connector must be lifted before connector can be removed. 

Disconnect the wire harness connector from the stoplight switch (13480). 

Remove the hairpin retainer, slide the stoplight switch, power brake 
booster (2005), and the nylon washers and brake master cylinder push rod 
bushing (2474) away from the brake pedal (2455).

 NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the power brake booster push rod and 
brake master cylinder push rod spacer (2B129) from the brake pedal arm pin, 
because the stoplight switch side plate is slotted.

Remove the stoplight switch by sliding it up and down. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not substitute other types of pin retainers. Replace only with 
production hairpin retainer. 

Position stoplight switch so the U-shaped side is nearest the brake 
pedal and directly over/under the pin. Then slide stoplight switch up/down, 
trapping the master cylinder push rod and brake master cylinder push rod 
bushing between the stoplight switch sideplates. Push stoplight switch and 
push rod assembly firmly toward brake pedal arm. Assemble outside white 
plastic washer to pin and install hairpin retainer to trap whole assembly. 

 NOTE: Stoplight switch wire harness must have sufficient length to travel with 
stoplight switch during full stroke of brake pedal. If wire length is 
insufficient, reroute harness or service as required. 

Assemble the wire harness connector to the stoplight switch and install 
the wires in the retaining clip. 

Check stoplight switch for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Headlamp Bulb

 Removal 

 WARNING: THE REPLACEABLE HALOGEN HEADLAMP BULB CONTAINS GAS UNDER PRESSURE. THE 
HALOGEN HEADLAMP BULB MAY SHATTER IF THE GLASS ENVELOPE IS SCRATCHED OR THE 
HALOGEN HEADLAMP BULB IS DROPPED. HANDLE BULB CAREFULLY. GRASP HALOGEN 
HEADLAMP BULB ONLY BY ITS PLASTIC BASE. AVOID TOUCHING GLASS ENVELOPE. KEEP 
HALOGEN HEADLAMP BULB OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. 

 NOTE: A correctly aimed headlamp (13008) normally need not be re-aimed after 
installation of this headlamp bulb and retainer (13N021). A burned out 
headlamp bulb should not be removed from the headlamp until just before a 
replacement headlamp bulb and retainer is to be installed. Removal of a 
headlamp bulb for an extended period of time may allow contaminants (dust, 
moisture, smoke) to enter the headlamp and affect the performance of the 
headlamp. When servicing the headlamp bulb and retainer, energize the headlamp 
bulb only while it is contained within the headlamp body.

Turn headlamp switch (11654) to the OFF position. 

Lift the hood and find the bulb in the headlamp socket.

Remove the electrical connector from the bulb by grasping the wire with 
a quick pull rearward.

Remove the headlamp bulb retainer (13N019) by turning it 1/8 of a turn 
to free it from the socket. Then slide the ring off the plastic base. Keep the 
headlamp bulb retainer to hold the new bulb in place.

 Installation 

With the flat side of the bulb's plastic base facing upward, insert the 
glass end of the bulb into the socket. Turn the bulb left or right to line up 
the grooves in the plastic base with the tabs in the socket. When the grooves 
are aligned, push the bulb into the socket until the plastic base contacts the 
rear of the socket.

Slip the headlamp bulb retainer over the plastic base until it contacts 
the rear of the socket. Lock the headlamp bulb retainer into the socket by 
rotating it clockwise until you feel a stop.

Push the electrical connector into the rear of the plastic base until 
it snaps, locking it into position.

Turn the headlamps on and make sure that they work properly. If the 
headlamp was correctly aimed before replacement, you should not need to adjust 
it.

Close hood.

ADJUSTMENTS

Headlamp 

Perform headlamp aim adjustments with Rotunda Headlight Aiming Kit 
196-00050 or equivalent. To aim the aerodynamically styled headlamps (13008), 
the adjustable aimer adapters provided in the kit must be used. Adjustment 
aimer adapter positions are moulded into the bottom edge of the headlamps.

Set and lock the adjustable adapters, attach each adapter to its 
mechanical aimer and aim headlamps per latest instructions in the kit. All 
headlamp adjustments should be made with a half-full fuel tank (9002), plus or 
minus one gallon, the vehicle unloaded, the luggage compartment empty (except 
for the spare tire and jacking equipment) and recommended pressure in all the 
tires. 

The equipment in Rotunda Headlight Aiming Kit 196-00050 or equivalent 
can be calibrated to accommodate a slight slope in the floor, making it usable 
almost any place in the garage. However, area must be reasonably flat.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamp, Dome/Map Combination 

 Lamp Assembly � Without Roof Sliding Panel 

The two map lamps are located on each side of the interior lamp (13776). 

The map lamps are operated independently of the interior lamp by two 
switches located on interior lamp. 

The interior lamp is illuminated by turning the instrument panel lamp 
dimmer control (10E846) to the detented UP position. 

The interior lamp also illuminates when the doors are opened (lamp 
switch (13713) in the pillar). 

 Lamp Assembly � With Roof Sliding Panel 

The interior lamp contains two lamps which function as door interior 
lamps when the doors are open. 

The map lamps are adjustable.

These interior lamps also function as map interior lamps when the front 
doors (20124) are closed and the rocker switch is activated.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps, Courtesy 

 Rear Quarter Trim Panel 

Interior lamps (13776) are mounted in the rear quarter trim panels. 
These lamps illuminate whenever the courtesy lamps are activated.

 Foot 

Foot lamps:

are located beneath the front passenger instrument panel.

illuminate in response to the courtesy lamp switches.

 Console 

One interior lamp is located in the front of the console panel 
(045A36). This interior lamp is independently operated by a switch also in the 
console panel. 

 Luggage Compartment 

The luggage compartment lamp housing contains a mercury switch that 
closes the lamp circuit when the luggage compartment door (40110) is opened. 

It is mounted near the center of the luggage compartment door. 

 Glove Compartment 

The glove compartment lamp system consists of: 

a glove compartment lamp switch and wire (14413) and miniature bulb 
(13466) assembly. 

circuit wiring and circuit protection. 

Power is provided to the glove compartment lamp switch and wire through 
Circuit 705 (LG/O). Opening the glove compartment door (06024) closes the 
switch which provides power to the glove compartment lamp switch and wire. The 
glove compartment lamp switch and wire is grounded to the sheet metal in the 
instrument panel (04320). 

 Vanity Mirrors 

The vanity mirror lamp system consists of:

a switch and miniature bulb assembly in each inside visor (04100). 

circuit wiring and circuit protection. 

Power is provided to the vanity mirror lamp switches through Circuit 54 
(LG/Y). Turning on the switch in the inside visor provides power to the lamps 
(13550).

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Illuminated Entry 

The illuminated entry system assists vehicle entry during the hours of 
darkness by illuminating the interior lamps (13776). 

On vehicles equipped with the electronic door lock control system, 
illuminated entry is a function of the electronic door lock control processor 
(14B001). If any concerns are encountered, refer to Section 01-14B .

The system is activated by raising the outside driver door handle 
(22404).

Electrical operation is as follows:

An illuminated entry switch mounted on the front door latch (21812) 
closes, grounding a circuit to the electronic door lock control processor or 
the integrated lamp control module as equipped.

The vehicle interior lamps turn ON.

This will remain ON for approximately 25 seconds, then automatically 
turn OFF. 

During this 25-second period, the system can be deactivated by turning 
the ignition switch to either RUN or ACC position. 

Opening the doors from the inside of the vehicle will not activate the 
system. 

If the outside door handle is held up so that the illuminated entry 
switch is continuously closed, the system will operate as normal and turn off 
after 25 seconds. 

At the completion of this cycle, if the door handle is still in the 
raised position, the system will remain OFF and it will be impossible to 
activate the system from the other door handle until the raised door handle is 
returned to its normal position. 

This logic circuitry prevents battery discharge should the outside door 
handle be intentionally propped up or becomes jammed.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bulb

 Removal 

Remove lens cover, if equipped, as described. 

Remove miniature bulb (13466) by one of the following methods:

For twist-in miniature bulbs, gently grasp the miniature bulb, push 
lightly while turning counterclockwise and remove the miniature bulb. 

For pressure-fit miniature bulbs, gently grasp miniature bulb, pull the 
miniature bulb straight out of contacts. If miniature bulb gives resistance, 
use a screwdriver under one edge for leverage. 

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Switch, Courtesy Lamp 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Retention of lamp switch (13713) to the wiring connector is by one of 
three tabs positioned 120 degrees apart on the lamp switch. If, when the lamp 
switch is disconnected from the wiring connector, the engaged locking tab 
breaks off, the lamp switch must be rotated 120 degrees to engage a new tab. 
When all three tabs have been broken, the lamp switch must be replaced. 

Unscrew the hex sleeve nut from the pillar. 

Extract the lamp switch and pull the wiring connector off the lamp 
switch.

 Installation 

To install the lamp switch in the pillar, pull the wiring connector and 
wiring through the courtesy lamp switch mounting hole in the pillar. 

Connect the lamp switch to the connector. 

Twist wiring and lamp switch four turns counterclockwise. 

Push the wiring and connector back through the mounting hole and screw 
the lamp switch into the pillar until it is seated. 

Close and open front door (20124) to make sure the interior lamp 
(13776) is operating properly.

Section 17-04: Lamps, Daytime Running

1997 Thunderbird, Cougar Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Daytime Running Lamp (DRL) System

 WARNING: DAYTIME RUNNING LAMPS CONTROL (15A272) GETS VERY HOT DURING OPERATION. 
BE SURE DAYTIME RUNNING LAMPS CONTROL HAS COOLED BEFORE HANDLING IT OR 
PERSONAL INJURY MAY OCCUR. 

 NOTE: If vehicle is equipped with an autolamp system, the DRL system is 
active until the autolamp turns on the headlamps (13008).

The daytime running lamp (DRL) system is designed to turn the high beam 
headlamps ON, with a reduced light output and without illuminating the high 
beam indicator in the instrument cluster (10849), when the following 
conditions are met:

The ignition switch is in RUN.

The parking brake is fully released.

The headlamp switch (11654) is in OFF or PARK.

The DRL system is required by the Canadian government for vehicles sold 
in Canada. 

The DRL system uses a daytime running lamps control and bracket 
assembly located on the LH fender apron.

The wiring is connected to the headlamp dash panel junction wire 
(14290) and routed through a hole on the horizontal surface in front of 
battery (10653). 

The DRL output:

consists of rapidly pulsating short bursts of power which cannot be 
measured using most multimeters.

cannot be adjusted.

Lamps, Daytime Running

 Electrical Schematics 

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 97 , Daytime Running Lamps for schematic and connector information. 

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's concern by following these steps:

Turn ignition switch OFF.

Turn headlamp switch (11654) to HEAD.

Check low beam headlamp operation. 

Turn high beam headlamp ON with dimmer switch.

Check high beam operation.

Check high beam indicator located in instrument cluster for proper 
operation.

Turn high beam headlamps OFF.

Turn low beam headlamps OFF. Refer to Section 17-01 to service headlamp 
concerns before checking daytime running lamps control (15A272).

Check daytime running lamps system operation:

Turn ignition switch to RUN.

Check for high beam headlamps ON at reduced intensity.

Inspect to determine if one of the following electrical concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Open instrument panel RUN Fuse (5A).

Open instrument panel CLUSTER Fuse (5A).

Circuitry open/shorted.

Open power distribution box fuse 1 (15A)

identified, service as required.

and go to the Symptom Chart.
